indication_long: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glyce...

flattened_sections.indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) not adequately controlled on diet and exercise alone, or who are already treated with the combination of vildagliptin and metformin HCl, as separate tabs. In combination with other antidiabetic drugs (e.g. insulin).
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosage. Max 100 mg vildagliptin daily. Adults ≥18 yrs - Inadequately controlled on vildagliptin monotherapy: Initially 50 mg/500 mg twice daily, gradually titrated based on therapeutic response; on metformin monotherapy: Initially 50 mg/500 mg, 50 mg/850 mg, or 50 mg/1,000 mg twice daily; Switching from combination therapy of vildagliptin + metformin as separate tabs: 50 mg/500 mg, 50 mg/850 mg, or 50 mg/1,000 mg based on dose of vildagliptin or metformin already being taken; Naive patients: Initially 50 mg/500 mg once daily, gradually titrated to max 50 mg/1,000 mg twice daily based on therapeutic response; Combination with SU or insulin: 50 mg vidagliptin twice daily and metformin dose already being taken. Renal impairment – GFR 60-89 mL/min: Max 3,000 mg/day metformin and max 100 mg/day vildagliptin; 45-59 mL/min: Initially ≤1,000 mg with max 2,000 mg/day metformin and max 50 mg/day vildagliptin; 30-44 mL/min: Initially ≤500 mg with max 1,000 mg/day metformin and max 50 mg/day vildagliptin. If no adequate strength of vildagliptin + metformin (Galvusmet) is available, individual components should be used instead of fixed dose. Taken with meals.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 mL/min). CHF. Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis or diabetic ketoacidosis, with or without coma).
flattened_sections.precautions: Not for type 1 DM or diabetic ketoacidosis. Not recommended in patients with hepatic impairment (e.g. pre-treatment ALT or AST >2.5x ULN) and NYHA functional class IV. Patients with risk factors for lactic acidosis or hypoglycemia, excessive alcohol intake, previously controlled DM developing laboratory abnormalities. Perform liver function tests prior to initiation and during 1<sup>st</sup> yr of therapy at 3-month intervals and periodically thereafter. Monitor renal function before treatment initiation and regularly thereafter. Concomitant use of drugs that may affect renal function. Discontinue if AST or ALT increase ≥3x ULN; jaundice or other signs suggestive of liver dysfunction developed; dehydration; prior to or at time of imaging or surgical procedures until renal function has been re-evaluated or resumption of oral nutrition, 48 hrs after and found stable; hypoxic states; temporary withheld in case loss of glycemic control. Decrease serum vit B<sub>12</sub>. Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, nausea, gastroesophageal reflux disease, diarrhea, flatulence, chills, decreased blood glucose; dizziness, tremor, asthenia, hypoglycemia, hyperhidrosis; decreased appetite, vomiting, abdominal pain.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Nifedipine, glyburide, ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine, COX-2 inhibitors, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics (e.g. thiazide and loop), corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid drugs, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, CCBs, isoniazid.
flattened_sections.packaging: Film-coated tablet 50 mg/500 mg (P34.75), 50 mg/850 mg (P34.75), 50 mg/1,000 mg (P34.75).

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of acute deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and/or pulmonary embolism (PE) and prevention of related deaths. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism and reduction of vascular mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation; venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients who have undergone major orthopedic surgery; recurrent DVT and/or PE and related deaths.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - Primary Prevention of VTE in patients who have undergone major orthopedic surgery: 220 mg once daily; moderate renal impairment: 150 mg once daily (2 caps of 75 mg); following knee or hip replacement surgery: Initially 1 cap of 110 mg (mild to moderate renal impairment: 75 mg) within 1-4 hrs of completed surgery, continued with 2 caps of 110 mg (mild to moderate renal impairment: 2 caps of 75 mg) once daily for 10 days (knee replacement surgery) or 28 -35 days (hip replacement surgery) total. For both surgeries, if hemostasis is not secured, delay initiation of treatment. If treatment is not started on the day of surgery, initiate with 2 caps once daily. Prevention of stroke, systemic embolism, and reduction of vascular mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation: 150 mg or 110 mg (elderly ≥80 yrs or with ≥1 of risk factors of bleeding) 2x daily for life -long. Assess renal function in patients with CrCl 30-50 mL/min at least once a yr. Treatment of acute DVT and/or PE and prevention of related death: 150 mg 2x daily following parenteral anticoagulant for ≥5 days, continued to max 6 months. Prevention of recurrent DVT and/or PE and related death: 150 mg 2x daily, may continue for life-long depending on individual patient risk.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Hemorrhagic manifestations, bleeding diathesis, spontaneous or pharmacological impairment of hemostasis. Organ lesions at risk of clinically significant bleeding including hemorrhagic stroke within the last 6 months. Concomitant treatment with systemic ketoconazole. Prosthetic heart valve replacement.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with recent biopsy or major trauma and receiving treatments liable to increase the hemorrhagic risk, bacterial endocarditis, renal insufficiency, spinal/epidural anesthesia and lumbar puncture. Concomitant use with dronedarone. May cause false positive INR elevations. Discontinue treatment if acute renal failure develops; ≥24 hrs prior surgical interventions. Assess renal function prior and during treatment and certain clinical situations when renal function is suspected to decline or deteriorate (e.g. hypovolemia, dehydration, comedications, etc.). Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly >75 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Bleeding or signs of bleeding, e.g. anemia and wound discharge. Abnormal hepatic function.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Unfractionated heparins and heparin derivatives, LMW heparins, fondaparinux, desirudin, thrombolytics, glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor antagonists, clopidogrel, ticlopidine, dextran, sulfinpyrazone, vit K antagonists, aspirin. P-gp inhibitors (e.g. amiodarone, verapamil, quinidine, systemic ketoconazole, dronedarone, ticagrelor, clarithromycin) and inducers.

indication_long: Tab: Treatment of gonococcal infection...

flattened_sections.indications: Tab: Treatment of gonococcal infections, otitis media, pyelonephritis, upper and lower respiratory tract, urinary tract (UTI), and skin and soft tissue infections. IM/IV: Community-acquired pneumonia, upper UTI, intra-abdominal, gynecological, and skin and soft tissue infections. Prophylaxis to reduce the risk of infections following abdominal surgery.
flattened_sections.dose: Tab: 375-750 mg twice a day. Uncomplicated gonorrhea: 2.25 g with probenecid 1 g. IM/IV - Adults: 3-12 g depending on severity of infection, divided into equal single doses every 6-8 hrs. Administer by deep IM injection or slow IV injection over at least 10-15 mins, or IV infusion over 15-30 mins in greater dilutions; Childn weighing ≥40 kg: Adult dose; >2 yrs, newborn (>2nd week of living), toddlers: 150 mg/kg/day (equiv to 100 mg/kg/day ampicillin + 50 mg/kg/day sulbactam) IV given in 3 or 4 divided doses; Newborn (1st week of living): 75 mg/kg daily (equiv to 50 mg/kg/day ampicillin + 25 mg/kg/day sulbactam) in 2 divided doses. Acute pelvic inflammatory disease: 3 g (equiv to 2 g ampicillin + 1 g sulbactam) every 6 hrs in conjunction with doxycycline. Prophylaxis of surgical infections: 1.5-3 g injection given at the induction of anesthesia. Renal impairment - CrCl >30 mL/min: 6-8 hrs dose intervals; 15-30 mL/min: 12 hrs dose intervals; 5-14 mL/min: 24 hrs dose intervals; <5 mL/min: 48 hrs dose intervals.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with mononucleosis, superinfections with mycotic or bacterial pathogens. Hepatic, renal and hematopoietic dysfunction. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms during prolonged use. May reduce effects of oral contraceptives. Antibiotic-associated colitis. Neonates and infants. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B. IM/IV: Concomitant use of oral contraceptives. Patients on controlled sodium diet.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, meteorism, diarrhea. Anaphylactic shock, GI distress, blood dyscrasias, abnormal hepatic function, and jaundice. IM/IV: Pain at injection site, phlebitis (IV).
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Warfarin and methotrexate. Estrogen-containing oral contraceptives, probenecid, allopurinol, aminoglycosides. Aspirin, indomethacin, phenylbutazone, tetracyclines, erythromycin, sulfonamides, chloramphenicol, anticoagulants. May result in false positive values of glucosuria.
flattened_sections.packaging: Film-coated tablet 750 mg. Powder for injection (IM/IV) 500 mg/250 mg (P450.24), 1 g/500 mg (P739.76).

flattened_sections.indications: Management of hypertension (HTN), alone or in combination with other antihypertensives; left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction (MI). Prophylaxis for angina pectoris. Treatment of symptomatic, stable, chronic heart failure in combination with diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and digitalis.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosing. HTN: Initially 12.5 mg once a day or in 2 divided doses, then 25 mg once a day or in 2 divided doses, thereafter; dose may be increased at intervals of at least 2 weeks to max 50 mg once a day or in 2 divided doses. Angina pectoris: 12.5 mg twice daily for the first 2 days, followed by 25 mg twice daily; dose may be increased at intervals of at least 2 weeks to max 50 mg twice daily. Elderly: Max 50 mg/day in 2 divided doses. Symptomatic, stable chronic heart failure: 3.125 mg twice daily for 2 weeks; if tolerated increase to 6.25 mg twice daily, then 12.5 mg twice daily, then max 25 mg twice daily at intervals not less than 2 weeks. Mild to moderate heart failure in patients >85 kg: Max 50 mg twice daily. Mild to moderate heart failure in patients < 85 kg or patients with severe heart failure: Max 25 mg twice daily. Left ventricular dysfunction following MI: Initially 6.25 mg, then increase to 6.25 mg twice daily and maintain for 3-10 days. If tolerated, increase to 12.5 mg twice daily, then max 25 mg twice daily, at intervals of 3-10 days. Decrease dose to 3.125 mg twice daily if not tolerated. Start carvedilol between day 3 and day 21 after MI as patients should receive an ACE inhibitor for at least 48 hrs, given at stable dose during at least the preceding 24 hrs.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Unstable/decompensated heart failure, hepatic impairment, marked fluid retention or overload requiring IV inotropic support, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place), severe bradycardia, sick sinus syndrome, severe hypotension, cardiogenic shock, metabolic acidosis. History of bronchospasm, asthma, or other obstructive lung disorders.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt discontinuation. May mask manifestations of hypoglycemia and hyperthyroidism i.e. tachycardia. Use with caution during anesthesia and major surgery; in combination with digitalis glycosides. Patients with bronchospastic disease, pheochromocytoma, PVD, Prinzmetal’s variant angina, Raynaud’s phenomenon, history of anaphylaxis and psoriasis. Decrease of lacrimation; wearing of contact lenses. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Asthenia, allergy, fatigue, fever, hypovolemia, malaise, edema, flu syndrome, pain in extremities. Undesirable effects on CV, GI, hematologic, metabolic and nutritional, musculoskeletal, nervous, male reproductive, respiratory, skin, appendages, and urogenital systems. Abnormal or blurred vision, eye irritation, tinnitus, decreased lacrimation and hearing. Latent DM and inhibition of blood glucose counterregulation.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CYP2D6 inhibitors, MAOIs, reserpine, clonidine, ciclosporin, digoxin, rifampicin, CCBs, insulin, oral hypoglycemics, amiodarone, anesthesia, and other antihypertensives.

Used as bronchodilator in the management of reversible airways obstruction, as in asthma and in some patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
flattened_sections.dose: Syr: Adults: 5-10 mL. Max 80 mL/day. Childn ≥12 yrs: 5-10 mL to be cautiously increased to max 60 mL/day; 6-12 yrs: 5 mL; 2-6 yrs: 2.5-5 mL. Elderly: 5 mL to be cautiously adjusted to 20 mL if necessary. All doses to be taken 3-4x daily. MDI: Adults - Immediate relief: 1-2 puffs; Chronic or preventive treatment: 2 puffs 3-4x a day; Relief of effort-induced bronchitis: 2 puffs before starting activity. Childn - Immediate relief or before effort: 1 puff; Chronic or preventive treatment: 1 puff 3-4x a day, may be increased to 2 puffs when necessary. Take at fixed intervals. Complete the treatment. Soln for Inhalation: Adults and childn >12 yrs: 2.5-5 mL 4x daily. In adults, max dose of 40 mg/day for the treatment of severe airway obstruction may be given under strict medical supervision in the hospital. Childn < 12 yrs: 1.25-2.5 mL every 4-6 hrs if needed. Use with a nebulizer and inhale over 5-15 mins. Soln for Nebulization: Initially 2.5 mg, may be increased to 5 mg. May be repeated up to 4x daily. For faster delivery time, this may be used undiluted. If prolonged delivery time is desired, dilution with an equal amount of 0.9% sodium chloride soln may be done. Used with a nebulizer, taken by inhalation over 5-15 mins.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Thyrotoxicosis. Not used for threatened abortion during the 1<sup>st</sup> and 2<sup>nd</sup> trimesters of pregnancy. Syr: Concomitant use of non-selective beta-blockers e.g. propranolol. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: HTN, hyperthyroidism or DM, patients with CV diseases (e.g. IHD, tachycardia, occlusive vascular disorders), angina pectoris. Not indicated for the prevention of premature labor associated with toxemia of pregnancy or antepartum hemorrhage. Adjustment of dose and frequency of administration should only be done upon medical advice. Syr: Patients with thyrotoxicosis. Monitor potassium levels in patients taking corticosteroids, diuretics, xanthines, and under digoxin therapy. MDI: Patients with impaired heart and/or vascular system, hyperactivity of the thyroid gland, enlarged prostate, history of spasms. Pregnancy and lactation. Soln for Inhalation: Not to be injected or administered orally, myocardial insufficiency, arrhythmias, susceptibility to QT-interval prolongation, closed-angle glaucoma; undergoing anesthesia with cyclopropane, halothane or other halogenated anesthetics. Monitor plasma potassium concentrations. Soln for Nebulization: Patients with convulsive disorders and hypokalemia. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.

flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Beta-blockers, disopyramide, quinidine, phenothiazine or procainamide. Corticosteroids, aminophylline, or xanthines. Syr: Diuretics and digoxin.

flattened_sections.dose: Monotherapy - 1st 3 administrations: 60 mg/m2 BSA once weekly; Subsequent administrations: Increase to 80 mg/m2 once weekly; for patients whose neutrophil count dropped once below 500/mm3 or more than once to between 500-1,000/mm3 during the 1st 3 administrations, adjust dose. flattened_sections.indications: Schizophrenia in adolescents 13-17 yrs and as acute and maintenance treatment in adults. Bipolar mania: Short-term treatment of acute manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in childn and adolescents 10-17 yrs as monotherapy or in adults in combination with lithium or valproate; treatment of moderate to severe manic episodes associated with bipolar disorders in adults. Conduct and other disruptive behavior disorders: Short-term symptomatic treatment (up to 6 weeks) of conduct and other disruptive behavior disorders in childn (>5 yrs), adolescents and adults with subaverage intellectual functioning or mental retardation, or average IQ. Irritability associated with autistic disorders in childn and adolescents 5-16 yrs.
flattened_sections.dose: Schizophrenia - Adults: 2 mg once or twice daily, increase in increments of 1-2 mg/day to recommended dose of 4-8 mg/day; Adolescents 13-17 yrs: 0.5 mg once daily, either in the morning or evening, adjust in increments of 0.5-1 mg/day to recommended dose of 3 mg/day. Bipolar mania - Adults: 2-3 mg once daily, increase in increments of 1 mg/day to recommended dose of 1-6 mg/day; Childn 10-17 yrs: 0.5 mg once daily, either in the morning or evening, adjust at intervals of not <24 hrs in increments of 0.5-1 mg/day to recommended dose of 2.5 mg/day. Conduct and other disruptive behavior disorders in childn and adolescents 5-18 yrs - BW ≥50 kg: Initially, 0.5 mg/day. Optimum dose: 1 mg/day. <50 kg: Initially, 0.25 mg once a day. Optimum dose: 0.5 mg/day. Autism: Individualized dosing. Adolescents and childn 5-16 yrs and BW ≥20 kg: 0.5 mg/day, may be increased on day 4 by 0.5 mg; <20 kg: 0.25 mg/day, may be increased on day 4 by 0.25 mg. Maintain recommended dose for minimum of 14 days, consider dose increase at ≥2-week intervals in increments of 0.25 mg for patients <20 kg or 0.5 mg in patients ≥20 kg; Elderly or debilitated patients, patients with severe hepatic or renal impairment, patients either predisposed to hypotension or in whom hypotension would pose a risk: 0.5 mg daily, may be increased in increments of not >0.5 mg twice daily, an increase dose of >1.5 mg should occur at intervals of ≥1 week.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Elderly with dementia-related psychosis, NMS, risk of tardive dyskinesia, presence of risk factors for VTE. Patients with history of seizures and other conditions that lower seizure threshold, cardiac arrhythmias, and in patients with congenital long QT syndrome or using drugs known to prolong QT interval, Parkinson’s disease or dementia with Lewy bodies. Possibility of suicide attempt in high-risk patients. Orthostatic hypotension, hyperglycemia and pre-existing DM, weight gain, pre-existing hyperprolactinemia and in patients with possible prolactin-dependent tumors. Esophageal dysmotility and aspiration, aspiration pneumonia, may mask signs and symptoms of overdosage of certain drugs or of conditions e.g. intestinal obstruction, Reye’s syndrome and brain tumor due to antiemetic effect, disruption of body temp regulation. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: NMS, tardive dyskinesia, orthostatic hypotension associated with dizziness, tachycardia, syncope, hyperglycemia, weight gain, hyperprolactinemia, priapism, leukopenia, neutropenia and agranulocytosis, dysphagia, hyperthermia or hypothermia. Somnolence, increased appetite, fatigue, rhinitis, URTI, vomiting, cough, urinary incontinence, increased salivation, constipation, fever, Parkinsonism, EPS, dystonia, abdominal pain, anxiety, nausea, dizziness, dry mouth, tremor, rash, akathisia and dyspepsia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Paliperidone, furosemide, centrally acting drugs (e.g. opiates, antihistamines, benzodiazepines) and alcohol, antihypertensives, levodopa and dopamine agonists, cimetidine, ranitidine, CYP2D6 inhibitors e.g. fluoxetine, paroxetine, quinidine. CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. verapamil. Carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin, phenobarbital. Clozapine.

flattened_sections.indications: Antihistamine: Relief of symptoms associated with seasonal, perennial, vasomotor rhinitis; for mild, uncomplicated allergic skin manifestations of urticaria and angioedema; dermatographism; as adjunct in anaphylactic reactions; allergic conjunctivitis due to foods; amelioration of allergic reactions to blood or plasma. Antiparkinsonism: Parkinsonism (including drug-induced) in elderly unable to tolerate more potent agents; mild cases of parkinsonism (including drug-induced) in other age groups; other cases of parkinsonism (including drug-induced) in combination with centrally acting anticholinergic agents. Nighttime sleep aid: Short-term management of insomnia. Antitussive: Relief of cough caused by minor throat and bronchial irritation e.g. due to common colds, inhaled irritants, or allergy. Antiemetic or motion sickness: Prevention and treatment of nausea, vomiting, and/or dizziness associated with motion sickness.
flattened_sections.dose: Cap - Antihistamine, antiparkinsonism: 1 cap every 6 hrs. Max 300 g/day (antihistamine); Antitussive: 1 cap every 8 hrs. flattened_sections.dose: Routine reversal: 4 mg/kg if recovery has reached at least 1-2 post-tetanic counts (PTC); 2 mg/kg if spontaneous recovery has occurred up to the reappearance of T2 following rocuronium or vecuronium-induced blockade. Immediate reversal of rocuronium-induced blockade: 16 mg/kg, administered 3 mins after bolus dose of rocuronium bromide 1.2 mg/kg. All doses administered as single IV bolus injection, given rapidly within 10 secs. Routine reversal - Childn and adolescent >2 yrs: 4 mg/kg if recovery peaked 1-2 PTC; 2 mg/kg or at reappearance of T2. Re-administration of rocuronium or vecuronium after sugammadex: 2 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg sugammadex at routine reversal required at least 5 mins waiting time for 1.2 mg/kg rocuronium; 2 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg sugammadex at routine reversal requires at least 4 hrs waiting for 0.6 mg/kg rocuronium or 0.1 mg/kg vecuronium to be administered. 16 mg/kg sugammadex at immediate reversal requires at least 24 hrs waiting time for 0.6 mg/kg rocuronium or 0.1 mg/kg vecuronium to be administered.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment, including those requiring dialysis (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Reversal of block induced by nonsteroidal neuromuscular blocking agents and steroidal neuromuscular blocking agents other than rocuronium and vecuronium. Immediate reversal in childn and adolescents. Infants.
flattened_sections.precautions: Monitor respiratory function during recovery. Monitor coagulation parameters in patients with known coagulopathies or taking anticoagulants. Recurrence of neuromuscular blockade. If rocuronium re-administration is required, 24-hr waiting time is recommended. Occurrence of light anesthesia, in rare instances marked bradycardia. Use in ICU. Not to be used for reversal of block induced by nonsteroidal neuromuscular blockers (e.g. succinylcholine, benzylisoquinolinium compounds) other than rocuronium. Severe renal impairment. Delayed recovery time in CV disease, elderly, or edematous state. Hepatic impairment. Patients on controlled sodium diet. History of pulmonary complications. Pregnancy and lactation.

Procedural complications (e.g. coughing, tachycardia, bradycardia, movement, and increased heart rate). Recurrence of neuromuscular blockade. Hypersensitivity reactions (e.g. flushing, urticaria, erythematous rash, hypotension, tachycardia, swelling of tongue or pharynx, bronchospasm, pulmonary obstructive events).

All doses administered as single IV bolus injection, given rapidly within 10 secs. Routine reversal - Childn and adolescent >2 yrs: 4 mg/kg if recovery peaked 1-2 PTC; 2 mg/kg or at reappearance of T2. Re-administration of rocuronium or vecuronium after sugammadex: 2 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg sugammadex at routine reversal required at least 5 mins waiting time for 1.2 mg/kg rocuronium; 2 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg sugammadex at routine reversal requires at least 4 hrs waiting for 0.6 mg/kg rocuronium or 0.1 mg/kg vecuronium to be administered. 16 mg/kg sugammadex at immediate reversal requires at least 24 hrs waiting time for 0.6 mg/kg rocuronium or 0.1 mg/kg vecuronium to be administered.

Infants.

Not to be used for reversal of block induced by nonsteroidal neuromuscular blockers (e.g. succinylcholine, benzylisoquinolinium compounds) other than rocuronium. Severe renal impairment. Delayed recovery time in CV disease, elderly, or edematous state. Hepatic impairment. Patients on controlled sodium diet. History of pulmonary complications. Pregnancy and lactation.

indication_long: Treatment of symptomatic and tachycardiac sup...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of symptomatic and tachycardiac supraventricular arrhythmias requiring treatment. e.g. supraventricular tachycardia associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. Tab: A-V-junctional tachycardia, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, severe symptomatic tachycardiac ventricular arrhythmias. Patients who were not prescribed with or do not respond to other antiarrhythmics. IV infusion: For severe rhythm disorders (e.g. supraventricular rhythm disorders, ventricular rhythm disorder) and patients with rhythm disorders requiring rapid response or where oral administration is not possible.
flattened_sections.dose: Tab - Adults - Saturation dose: 600 mg/day given in 3 divided doses for 8-10 days; doses up to 1,200 mg/day (in 6 divided doses) may be necessary in some cases. Maintenance dose: 200 mg for 5 days/week. In some cases, 200-600 mg/day are required during long-term therapy. Childn: Dosage should be adjusted to BSA or BW. IV infusion - Infusion regimen for the first 24 hrs - Loading infusion: Initial rapid infusion phase: 150 mg (3 mL) over 10 mins at a rate of 15 mg/min. Slow infusion phase: 360 mg over 6 hrs at a rate of 1 mg/min. Maintenance infusion: 540 mg over 18 hrs at a rate of 0.5 mg/min. After the first 24 hrs, continue a maintenance infusion rate of 0.5 mg/min. Breakthrough episodes of ventricular fibrillation or hemodynamically unstable ventricular tachycardia: 150 mg for over 10 mins of supplemental amiodarone infusion. Administer through a central venous catheter.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Sinus bradycardia, SA heart block, sinoauricular and nodal conduction delay (e.g. sick sinus syndrome, 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block, bi- and tri-fascicular if no pacemaker is used), thyropathy, preexisting QT prolongation, hypokalemia, circulatory collapse, severe arterial hypotension, and iodine allergy. Concomitant use with MAOIs and drugs that may induce torsades de pointes. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Pulmonary toxicity. Severe inflammatory pneumopathy, increased liver enzymes, cholestatic icterus or hepatomegaly, ECG changes, dyspnea or non-productive cough may develop. Discontinue if bradycardia or sinus node arrest occurs. May interfere with radioiodine uptake. Photosensitization; avoid exposure to sun. Perform thyroid function test before therapy. Patients with personal or family history of thyroid disorders. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hyperthyroidism/hypothyroidism, extrapyramidal tremors, nightmares, dyssomnia, cornea verticillata, impaired vision, atypical pneumonia, nausea, vomiting, constipation, isolated elevation of serum transaminases, acute hepatitis, photosensitisation, eczema, and muscle weakness. Hypotension, asystole/cardiac arrest/electromechanical dissociation (EMD), cardiogenic shock, CHF, bradycardia, ventricular tachycardia, AV block, and liver function test abnormalities.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: HIV protease inhibitors, loratadine, cimetidine, trazodone, ciclosporin, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, antihypertensives, anticoagulants, clopidogrel, antibiotics, fentanyl, lidocaine, dextromethorphan, St. John’s Wort, grapefruit juice. Drugs affecting QT interval, digoxin, antiarrhythmics. Cholestyramine, phenytoin, vincamine, sultopride, sparfloxacin, erythromycin IV, pentamidine. Agents that cause hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia. Methotrexate. Tab: Sofosbuvir and other antivirals for HCV. IV infusion - Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, cefamandole, cefazolin, mezlocillin, sodium bicarbonate, heparin.
flattened_sections.packaging: Tablet 200 mg (P56.21). Solution for IV infusion 50 mg/mL x 3 mL (P267.10).

indication_long: 60 mg: Prevention of thrombotic events...

flattened_sections.indications: 60 mg: Prevention of thrombotic events (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction (MI), and stroke) in patients with history of MI (≥1 yr ago), high risk of developing a thrombotic event; coronary artery disease (CAD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) who have undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). 90 mg: Prevention of thrombotic events in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) (unstable angina, ST-elevation myocardial infarction [STEMI]) including patients managed medically and with PCI or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Prevention of stroke in patients with acute ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA).
flattened_sections.dose: History of MI (≥1 yr ago) and CAD with type 2 DM (have undergone PCI): 60 mg 2x daily. Long-term treatment is recommended. ACS: Initially 180 mg (2 tabs of 90 mg) once daily, then 90 mg 2x daily for ≥1 yr unless discontinued. After 1 yr, continue with 60 mg 2x daily without interruption. Acute ischemic stroke or TIA: Initially 180 mg (2 tabs of 90 mg) once daily, then 90 mg 2x daily for 30 days. Use with maintenance dose of aspirin 75-150 mg daily for ACS, acute ischemic stroke, or TIA. 60 mg 2x daily may be started regardless of previous antiplatelet regimen and if lapse in therapy occurred or not. Discontinue current antiplatelet therapy before initiating treatment with low-dose aspirin at the next scheduled dose. Switching from other antiplatelet: Administer first dose 24 hrs after last dose of other antiplatelet. Tabs may be crushed, mixed in half a glass of water, and drunk immediately for patients unable to swallow tabs whole. Mixture can also be administered via a nasogastric tube.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active pathological bleeding. History of intracranial hemorrhage. Severe hepatic impairment.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment; increased risk of bleeding (e.g. with propensity to bleed, co-administration with drugs that increase risk of bleeding (e.g. NSAIDs, oral anticoagulants, and/or fibrinolytics) within 24 hrs of treatment; therapy of >1 yr in patients with prior ischemic stroke; increased risk of bradycardic events (e.g. patients without peacemaker who have sick sinus syndrome, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree of AV block, bradycardic-related syncope, ACS, where ischemia and concomitant drugs reducing heart rate or affecting cardiac conduction). May induce bradyarrhythmic events; dyspnea; central sleep apnea (e.g. Cheyne-Stokes respiration); thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura; false negative results in platelet function test for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Premature discontinuation can increase risk of CV death, MI, or stroke due to underlying disease. Platelet transfusion and desmopressin are not effective in managing bleeding. Antifibrinolytic (e.g. aminocaproic acid or tranexamic acid) and/or recombinant factor VIIa therapy may augment hemostasis. Avoid co-administration with >300 mg aspirin or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir, atazanavir). brand_info.title: Indications
brand_info.content: 60 mg: Prevention of thrombotic events (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction (MI), and stroke) in patients with history of MI (≥1 yr ago), high risk of developing a thrombotic event; coronary artery disease (CAD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) who have undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). 90 mg: Prevention of thrombotic events in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) (unstable angina, ST-elevation myocardial infarction [STEMI]) including patients managed medically and with PCI or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Prevention of stroke in patients with acute ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA).

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: History of MI (≥1 yr ago) and CAD with type 2 DM (have undergone PCI): 60 mg 2x daily. Long-term treatment is recommended. ACS: Initially 180 mg (2 tabs of 90 mg) once daily, then 90 mg 2x daily for ≥1 yr unless discontinued. After 1 yr, continue with 60 mg 2x daily without interruption. Acute ischemic stroke or TIA: Initially 180 mg (2 tabs of 90 mg) once daily, then 90 mg 2x daily for 30 days. Use with maintenance dose of aspirin 75-150 mg daily for ACS, acute ischemic stroke, or TIA. 60 mg 2x daily may be started regardless of previous antiplatelet regimen and if lapse in therapy occurred or not. Discontinue current antiplatelet therapy before initiating treatment with low-dose aspirin at the next scheduled dose. Switching from other antiplatelet: Administer first dose 24 hrs after last dose of other antiplatelet. Tabs may be crushed, mixed in half a glass of water, and drunk immediately for patients unable to swallow tabs whole. Mixture can also be administered via a nasogastric tube.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Active pathological bleeding. History of intracranial hemorrhage. Severe hepatic impairment.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment; increased risk of bleeding (e.g. with propensity to bleed, co-administration with drugs that increase risk of bleeding (e.g. NSAIDs, oral anticoagulants, and/or fibrinolytics) within 24 hrs of treatment; therapy of >1 yr in patients with prior ischemic stroke; increased risk of bradycardic events (e.g. patients without peacemaker who have sick sinus syndrome, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree of AV block, bradycardic-related syncope, ACS, where ischemia and concomitant drugs reducing heart rate or affecting cardiac conduction). May induce bradyarrhythmic events; dyspnea; central sleep apnea (e.g. Cheyne-Stokes respiration); thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura; false negative results in platelet function test for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Premature discontinuation can increase risk of CV death, MI, or stroke due to underlying disease. Platelet transfusion and desmopressin are not effective in managing bleeding. Antifibrinolytic (e.g. aminocaproic acid or tranexamic acid) and/or recombinant factor VIIa therapy may augment hemostasis. Avoid co-administration with >300 mg aspirin or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir, atazanavir). Discontinue 5 days prior to elective surgery where antiplatelet effect is not desired. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.

Adjuvant treatment of patients with operable,...

flattened_sections.indications: Adjuvant treatment of patients with operable, node-positive breast cancer in combination with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. Treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer in patients who have not previously received cytotoxic chemotherapy in combination with doxorubicin, or after failure of anthracycline or alkylating agent-containing chemotherapy as monotherapy or in combination with capecitabine; metastatic breast cancer whose tumors overexpress HER2 and without prior chemotherapy in combination with trastuzumab. Treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after failure of prior chemotherapy as monotherapy; unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC without prior chemotherapy in combination with cisplatin; metastatic ovarian cancer after failure of 1<sup>st</sup> line or subsequent therapy; androgen-independent (hormone-refractory) metastatic prostate cancer in combination with prednisone or prednisolone; metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma, including adenocarcinoma of gastroesophageal junction without prior chemotherapy in combination with cisplatin and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU); recurrent and/or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN) after failure of previous chemotherapy as monotherapy. Induction treatment for locally advanced SCCHN in combination with cisplatin and 5-FU.
flattened_sections.dose: Premedicate all patients with oral corticosteroids (e.g. dexamethasone) 16 mg/day (i.e. 8 mg twice daily) for 5 days starting 1 day before docetaxel administration. Adjuvant treatment of operable node-positive and negative breast cancer: 75 mg/m2 after doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 and cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2 every 3 weeks for 6 cycles. Locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after failure of prior chemotherapy - Monotherapy: 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks. Combination therapy: 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks with doxorubicin 50 mg/m2. HER2 overexpressing breast cancer - Combination therapy: 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks with trastuzumab administered weekly. Locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after failure of prior anthracycline-containing chemotherapy - Combination therapy: 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks combined with capecitabine 1,250 mg/m2 twice a day for 2 weeks followed by 1-week rest period. NSCLC - After failure of prior platinum-based chemotherapy: 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks as single agent. Patients who have not previously received chemotherapy: 75 mg/m2 immediately followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2 over 30-60 mins every 3 weeks. Prostate cancer: 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks. Administer oral prednisone/prednisolone 5 mg twice a day continuously from day 1 and through each cycle. Premedicate with oral dexamethasone 8 mg at 12, 3, and 1 hr before docetaxel infusion. Gastric cancer: 75 mg/m2 followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2 as 1- to 3-hr IV infusion (both on day 1). Starting at the end of cisplatin infusion give 5-fluorouracil 750 mg/m2 per day as a 24-hr continuous infusion for 5 days. Repeat treatment every 3 weeks. SCCHN – Induction chemotherapy followed by radiotherapy: 75 mg/m2 followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2 IV over 1 hr (day 1) followed by 5-FU 750 mg/m2 per day as continuous IV infusion for 5 days (day 1-5) initiated after cisplatin infusion. Regimen is administered every 3 weeks for 4 cycles. Radiotherapy should be received after completion of chemotherapy. Induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy: 75 mg/m2 followed by cisplatin 100 mg/m2 as a 30-180 min IV infusion (day 1) followed by 5-FU 1,000 mg/m2 per day as continuous IV infusion for 4 days (days 1-4). Regimen is administered every 3 weeks for 3 cycles. Chemoradiotherapy should be received after chemotherapy.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to docetaxel or polysorbate 80. Neutrophil counts <1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>. Patients under disulfiram treatment; with severe liver impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Abnormal liver function. Patients with bilirubin >ULN, AST and/or ALT >1.5x ULN concomitant with AP >2.5x ULN; severe fluid retention; at risk for treatment-related acute myeloid leukemia. Possible irreversible infertility (men). Elderly. Childn <16 yrs. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia. GI effects. CV effects. Fluid retention. Dermatologic effects. Neurologic, hepatic, musculoskeletal, respiratory, ophthalmic, and otic effects.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Ciclosporin, terfenadine, ketoconazole, erythromycin, troleandomycin, doxorubicin, vinorelbine, vinblastine, and nifedipine. Dexamethasone, phenobarbital, and clofibrate. Topotecan. Trastuzumab, carboplatin.
flattened_sections.packaging: Concentrate solution for IV infusion 20 mg/0.5 mL (P6,787.45), 80 mg/2 mL (P25,374.68).

flattened_sections.indications: Palliative treatment of stage 3 or 4 advanced local carcinoma of the ovary after surgical resection, in combination with cisplatin; management of metastatic carcinoma of the ovary after failure of 1<sup>st</sup> line or subsequent chemotherapy; advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in patients who are not candidates for potentially curative surgery and/or radiation. Palliative treatment of advanced or refractory AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma in patients who have failed prior liposomal anthracycline therapy. Treatment of metastatic carcinoma of the breast after failure of combination therapy or relapse within 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy. For initial treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with an anthracycline in patients for whom anthracycline therapy is suitable, or with trastuzumab in patients who over-express HER-2 at a 3+ level and for whom anthracycline is not suitable.
flattened_sections.dose: Premedicate all patients with corticosteroids (e.g. oral dexamethasone), antihistamines (e.g. IV diphenhydramine), and H2 antagonists (e.g. IV cimetidine or ranitidine) prior to paclitaxel administration. Ovarian cancer - Primary treatment: 135 mg/m2 administered over 24 hrs, followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2, every 3 weeks. Alternatively, 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2, every 3 weeks. Secondary treatment after failure of 1st line or subsequent chemotherapy: 135 or 175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs every 3 weeks. Palliative treatment of advanced NSCLC: 175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hours, followed by a platinum compound, with a 3-week interval between courses; 135 mg/m2 administered over 24 hrs followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2, given every 3 weeks; or 175mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs followed by cisplatin 80 mg/m2, given every 3 weeks. Breast cancer - Adjuvant treatment of node-positive breast cancer: 175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks for 4 courses administered sequentially to doxorubicin-containing combination therapy. Treatment of breast cancer after failure of initial chemotherapy for metastatic disease or relapse within 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy: 175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks. HER-2 overexpressing breast cancer: 175 mg/m2 over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks for 6 cycles. Administer trastuzumab 2 mg/kg IV once a week until progression of disease after an initial loading dose of 4 mg/kg. AIDS-related Kaposi’s sacrcoma: 135 mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks. Alternatively, 100 mg/m2 over 3 hrs, every 2 weeks (dose intensify 45-50 mg/m2 per week).
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. History of hypersensitivity to products containing polyoxyethylated castor oil (cremophor EL). Patients with solid tumors who have baseline neutrophil count <1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>; AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma with neutrophil count <1,000 cells/mm<sup>3</sup> and those with concurrent, serious, uncontrolled infections; hepatic dysfunction, alcoholism, and epilepsy. Childn. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Undiluted paclitaxel should not come in contact with PVC equipment or devices. Contains ethyl alcohol. Narrow therapeutic index. Patients with preexisting or at risk for bone marrow suppression, severe cardiac conduction abnormalities, peripheral neuropathy. Risk for embryotoxicity and mutagenicity. Vaccine administration. Postpone oral poliovirus vaccine in people in close contact with patients undergoing paclitaxel therapy. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Women of childbearing potential. brand_info.content: Palliative treatment of stage 3 or 4 advanced local carcinoma of the ovary after surgical resection, in combination with cisplatin; management of metastatic carcinoma of the ovary after failure of 1<sup>st</sup> line or subsequent chemotherapy; advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in patients who are not candidates for potentially curative surgery and/or radiation. Palliative treatment of advanced or refractory AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma in patients who have failed prior liposomal anthracycline therapy. Treatment of metastatic carcinoma of the breast after failure of combination therapy or relapse within 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy. For initial treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with an anthracycline in patients for whom anthracycline therapy is suitable, or with trastuzumab in patients who over-express HER-2 at a 3+ level and for whom anthracycline is not suitable.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: Premedicate all patients with corticosteroids (e.g. oral dexamethasone), antihistamines (e.g. IV diphenhydramine), and H2 antagonists (e.g. IV cimetidine or ranitidine) prior to paclitaxel administration. Ovarian cancer - Primary treatment: 135 mg/m2 administered over 24 hrs, followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2, every 3 weeks. Alternatively, 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2, every 3 weeks. Secondary treatment after failure of 1st line or subsequent chemotherapy: 135 or 175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs every 3 weeks. Palliative treatment of advanced NSCLC: 175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hours, followed by a platinum compound, with a 3-week interval between courses; 135 mg/m2 administered over 24 hrs followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2, given every 3 weeks; or 175mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs followed by cisplatin 80 mg/m2, given every 3 weeks. Breast cancer - Adjuvant treatment of node-positive breast cancer: 175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks for 4 courses administered sequentially to doxorubicin-containing combination therapy. Treatment of breast cancer after failure of initial chemotherapy for metastatic disease or relapse within 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy: 175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks. HER-2 overexpressing breast cancer: 175 mg/m2 over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks for 6 cycles. Administer trastuzumab 2 mg/kg IV once a week until progression of disease after an initial loading dose of 4 mg/kg. AIDS-related Kaposi’s sacrcoma: 135 mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks. Alternatively, 100 mg/m2 over 3 hrs, every 2 weeks (dose intensify 45-50 mg/m2 per week).

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. History of hypersensitivity to products containing polyoxyethylated castor oil (cremophor EL). Childn. Pregnancy.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Undiluted paclitaxel should not come in contact with PVC equipment or devices. Contains ethyl alcohol. Narrow therapeutic index. Patients with preexisting or at risk for bone marrow suppression, severe cardiac conduction abnormalities, peripheral neuropathy. Risk for embryotoxicity and mutagenicity. Vaccine administration. Postpone oral poliovirus vaccine in people in close contact with patients undergoing paclitaxel therapy. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Women of childbearing potential. flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of advanced colorectal cancer in combination with infusional 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and leucovorin; adjuvant treatment of stage III colon cancer in patients who have undergone complete resection of the primary tumor.
flattened_sections.dose: Administer before fluoropyrimidines. Antiemetics should be given before and after therapy with oxaliplatin. Treatment of patients with advanced colorectal cancer - Day 1: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 (as IV infusion diluted in 250-500 mL of 5% dextrose soln) and leucovorin 200 mg/m2 (by IV infusion in 5% dextrose soln), both given over 120 mins at the same time in different bags using a Y-line, followed by 5-FU 400 mg/m2 by IV bolus given over 2-4 mins, followed by 5-FU 600 mg/m2 (diluted in 500 mL 5% dextrose soln) as a 22-hr continuous IV infusion. Day 2: Leucovorin 200 mg/m2 in IV infusion over 120 mins, followed by 5-FU 400 mg/m2 by IV bolus over 2-4 mins, followed by 5-FU 600 mg/m2 diluted in 500 mL 5% dextrose solution as a 22-hr continuous IV infusion. Treatment may be repeated every 2 weeks. Adjuvant treatment in patients with stage III colon cancer after complete resection of primary tumor: Recommended for a total of 6 months (i.e. 12 cycles), given every 2 weeks according to the dose schedule described for the treatment of advanced colorectal cancer. Postpone next dose until hematological values return to acceptable levels (neutrophils ≥1.5x109/L and platelets ≥75x109/L).
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to oxaliplatin or other platinum compounds (cisplatin, carboplatin). Patients with peripheral sensory neuropathy with functional impairment prior to first course; severe impairment renal function (CrCl <30 mL/min); myelosuppression prior to starting first course with baseline neutrophils <1.5x10<sup>9</sup>/L and/or platelet count < 75x10<sup>9</sup>/L. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid cold foods and drinks and cover skin before cold exposure during and within 48 hrs after administration. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Fertility impairment. Elderly. Childn. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Acute and peripheral neuropathies, sensory disturbance, pulmonary fibrosis, hematologic effects, GI effects, dermatologic reactions, hepatotoxicity (elevation of transaminases, alkaline phosphatase), renal toxicity (creatinine elevation), musculoskeletal effects, thromboembolism.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Nephrotoxic drugs; antineoplastic drugs (irinotecan, topotecan); protein-bound drugs (erythromycin, salicylate, sodium valproate, granisetron, paclitaxel); drugs affecting CYP450 enzymes. Incompatibilities: Sodium chloride or other chloride-containing solutions, aluminum, alkaline compounds or media.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) and stable mild and moderate congestive heart failure (CHF) in addition to standard therapies in elderly patients.
flattened_sections.dose: HTN - Adults: 5 mg once daily. In combination with HCTZ: 5 mg plus HCTZ 12.5-25 mg. Elderly >65 yrs: Initially 2.5 mg daily. May be increased to 5 mg daily. CHF: Initially 1.25 mg once daily, increase at interval of 1-2 weeks based on patient's tolerability to 2.5, 5, and 10 mg once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Liver insufficiency or impairment. Acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock or episodes of heart failure decompensation. Sick sinus syndrome including SA block; 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> degree heart block (without a pacemaker); history of bronchospasm and bronchial asthma; untreated pheochromocytoma; metabolic acidosis; bradycardia (HR <60 bpm); hypotension (systolic BP <90 mmHg); severe peripheral circulatory disturbances.
flattened_sections.precautions: Concomitant use with anesthetics. Untreated CHF, IHD. Peripheral circulatory disorders (Raynaud's disease or syndrome, intermittent claudication); 1st degree heart block; Prinzmetal's angina. DM, hyperthyroidism, COPD, history of psoriasis. Increased sensitivity to allergens and severity of anaphylactic reactions. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Severe renal impairment. Galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn and adolescents. Elderly >75 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, dizziness, paresthesia, dyspnea, constipation, nausea, diarrhea, tiredness, edema, bradycardia.

indication_long: 20 mg: Treatment of hyperlipidemia, in...

flattened_sections.indications: 20 mg: Treatment of hyperlipidemia, including hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia (type IIa or IIb hyperlipoproteinemia), hypertriglyceridemia (type IV) and dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III). Adjunctive therapy in homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia and used for primary prophylaxis of cardiovascular (CV) events. 40 mg: Prevention of CV disease. In patients with type 2 diabetes – reduce risk of myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke. In patients with coronary heart disease – reduce risk of non-fatal MI, fatal and non-fatal stroke, revascularization procedures, hospitalization for congestive heart failure, angina. Adjunct to diet in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous familial and non-familial) and mixed dyslipidemia (Fredrickson types IIa and IIb); patients with elevated serum triglyceride levels (Fredrickson type IV). Treatment of patients with primary dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson type III) who do not respond adequately to diet. Adjunct to other lipid-lowering treatments (e.g. LDL apheresis) in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Adjunct to diet in boys and postmenarchal girls (10-17 yrs) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia if after adequate trial of diet therapy in the following findings are present – LDL-C remains ≥190 mg/dL or ≤160 mg/dL), and there is a positive family history of premature CV disease, or ≥2 CV disease risk factors are present in the child.
flattened_sections.dose: Initially 10-20 mg/day. For patients who require large reduction in LDL-C: Initially 40 mg. May be adjusted at intervals of 4 weeks up to max 80 mg/day. Childn and adolescents (10-17 yrs) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: Initially 10 mg/day, adjust according to response to max 20 mg/day. Patients taking ciclosporin: Max 10 mg/day; clarithromycin: Initially 10 mg. Max 20 mg/day; itraconazole: Initially 10 mg. Max 40 mg/day; ritonavir-boosted lopinavir or ritonavir-boosted saquinavir: Doses >20 mg/day should be used with caution.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistently raised serum aminotransferase concentrations. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Predisposing factors for myopathy. Elderly ≥65 yrs. Pregnancy Risk: Category X. 20 mg: Effects on growth and sexual development of childn. Patients with porphyria. Fetal sterol synthesis. 40 mg: History of renal impairment. Patients with recent stroke or TIA. Patients with diffuse myalgias, muscle tenderness or weakness, and/or marked CPK elevation. Liver function abnormalities.
flattened_sections.side_effects: 20 mg: GI disturbances. 40 mg: Nasopharyngitis, arthralgia, diarrhea, pain in extremities, and UTI.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Ciclosporin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, HIV-protease inhibitors, nefazodone, amiodarone, and verapamil. Erythromycin and other macrolides. Rifampicin, oral anticoagulants, fibric acid derivatives (e.g. fibrates, gemfibrozil), nicotinic acid, and esomeprazole. Grapefruit juice. 20 mg: CCBs and PPIs. 40 mg: Digoxin, oral contraceptives (e.g. norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol), and colchicine.

flattened_sections.indications: Management of treatment-resistant schizophrenia. For reducing risk of recurrent suicidal behavior or schizoaffective disorder who are considered to be at chronic risk for reexperiencing suicidal behavior. For psychotic disorders occurring during the course of Parkinson’s disease, in cases where standard treatment has failed.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosage. Treatment-resistant schizophrenia - Initial dose: 12.5 mg once or twice daily on the 1st day, continue with daily dosage increments of 25-50 mg/day to achieve target dose of 300-450 mg/day by the end of 2 weeks. Subsequent dose increments not >100 mg made once or twice weekly; Therapeutic dose: 300-450 mg/day in divided doses (may be divided unevenly, larger portion at bedtime). Max 900 mg/day; Maintenance dose: Carefully down titrate after achieving max therapeutic benefit. Treatment should be maintained for at least 6 months. If dose is <200 mg, give once a day in the evening. Discontinuation therapy: Gradual dose reduction over a 1- to 2-week period. Psychotic disorders occurring during the course of Parkinson's disease where standard treatment has failed - Initial dose: 12.5 mg in the evening. Subsequent dose increments by 12.5 mg with max 2 increments/week up to max 50 mg; Mean effective dose: 25-37.5 mg/day, increase by increments of 12.5 mg/week up to max 100 mg/day; Ending therapy: Gradual dose reduction by 12.5 mg over a period of at least 1 week (preferably 2 weeks). Patients with history of seizures or suffering from renal or CV disorders: 12.5 mg once daily on the 1st day, increase dose slowly and in small increments. Elderly: 12.5 mg once daily on the 1st day, with subsequent dose increments of 25 mg/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Myeloproliferative disorders, uncontrolled epilepsy, paralytic ileus, history of clozapine-induced agranulocytosis or severe granulocytopenia, unable to undergo regular blood tests, history of toxic or idiosyncratic granulocytopenia or agranulocytosis, impaired bone marrow function, alcoholic and other toxic psychoses, drug intoxication, comatose conditions, circulatory collapse and/or CNS depression of any cause, severe renal or cardiac disorders, liver disease.
flattened_sections.precautions: Risk of agranulocytosis, fatal myocarditis, history of seizures or other predisposing factors. Concomitant use with benzodiazepines or other psychotropic drug. Not for dementia-related psychosis. CV and/or pulmonary disease, DM, recurrences of NMS, tardive dyskinesia (particularly in elderly women), transient temp elevations >38<sup>o</sup>C with peak incidence within the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 weeks of treatment. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Fever, chills, hypothermia, fatigue, weakness; central and autonomic nervous systems, CV, GI, endocrine and metabolic, hepatic, respiratory, genitourinary/reproductive, hemic and lymphatic system, dermatologic and sensitivity, and musculoskeletal effects; visual disturbance, narrow-angle glaucoma, mydriasis, eyelid and ear disorder, bloodshot eyes, nystagmus, periorbital edema, numb/sore tongue, bitter taste, nosebleed.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Bone marrow suppressants, sulfonamides, pyrazolone analgesics, azapropazone, penicillamine, cytotoxic agents and long-acting depot injection of antipsychotics. Ritonavir, benzodiazepines, alcohol, antihistamines, MAOIs, CNS depressants including narcotics, anticholinergics, antihypertensives, type 1C antiarrhythmics, highly protein-bound drugs, TCAs and antimuscarinics, caffeine, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, sertraline, venlafaxine, ciprofloxacin and amprenavir, omeprazole, rifampicin, lithium, phenytoin, cimetidine, citalopram, erythromycin, nicotine.

flattened_sections.dose: Blastomycosis, histoplasmosis: 200 mg (2 caps) once daily, may be increased by 100 mg increments up to max 400 mg daily. Doses >200 mg/day should be given in 2 divided doses. Duration of treatment: Minimum of 3 months until active fungal infection have subsided. Onychomycosis - Toenails with or without finger involvement: 200 mg (2 caps) once daily for 12 consecutive weeks. Fingernails only: 2 treatment pulses, each consisting of 200 mg (2 caps) twice daily for 1 week. Pulses are separated by a 3-week period without itraconazole. Tinea versicolor: 2 caps once daily for 7 days. Tinea corporis, tinea cruris: 1 cap once daily for 2 weeks. Dermatomycosis of palms and soles (tinea manus, tinea pedis): 1 cap once daily for 4 weeks. flattened_sections.precautions: Renal and hepatic impairment. Perform liver function testing and discontinue treatment if patients develop signs of liver dysfunction. Transient or permanent hearing loss. Should not be used interchangeably with itraconazole oral solution.

Patients with severe coronary insufficiency, recent MI, conduction disturbances, mild to moderate bradyarrhythmia, cerebrovascular disease, cerebral or peripheral perfusion disorders, polyneuropathy, depression, chronic renal failure, Reynaud’s disease, thromboangiitis obliterans or constipation. May cause decreased lacrimation and dryness of eyes. Off-label use for ADHD, concomitantly with methylphenidate. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. flattened_sections.dose: IV infusion over 30 mins but not more than 60 mins and not more frequent than once a week. Adults - Ovarian cancer: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle; carboplatin should be administered after, on day 1 consistent with a target AUC of 4 mg/mL/min. Breast cancer: Gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle; paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 administered on day 1 over approximately 3 hrs as IV infusion before the administration of gemcitabine. NSCLC – Monotherapy: 1,000 mg/m2 repeated once a week for 3 weeks, followed by a 1-week rest period. The 4-week cycle is then repeated. Combination therapy - 3-week schedule: Gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle; cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV administered on day 1 after gemcitabine infusion. 4-week schedule: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 21-day cycle; cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV administered on day 1 after gemcitabine infusion. Pancreatic cancer: 1,000 mg/m2 repeated once a week for up to 7 weeks, followed by a 1-week rest period. Subsequent cycles should consist of injection once a week for 3 consecutive weeks out of every 4 weeks. Bladder cancer – Monotherapy: 1,250 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle. This 4-week cycle is then repeated. Combination therapy: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle; cisplatin 70 mg/m2 administered on day 1 following gemcitabine or day 2 of each 28-day cycle. This 4-week cycle is then repeated.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

indication_long: Menace of abortion or prevention or recurrent...

flattened_sections.indications: Menace of abortion or prevention or recurrent spontaneous abortions due to diagnosed luteal phase defect; preterm delivery. Oral cap: Treatment of disorders associated with progesterone deficit e.g. pre-menstrual syndrome (PMS), menstrual irregularity, benign breast disease, pre-menopause; infertility caused by luteal phase defect. Adjunct to estrogen therapy in the treatment of menopause. Vaginal cap: During In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) cycles.
flattened_sections.dose: Threatened abortion or prevention of LPD-related recurrent spontaneous abortions: 200-400 mg in 2 divided doses, taken up until gestation week 12. Oral cap - usually 200-300 mg daily as a single or in 2 doses (i.e. 200 mg in the evening at bedtime and 100 mg in the morning, if needed). Luteal phase defect (PMS, menstrual irregularity, pre-menopause, benign breast disease): Administered for 10 days/menstrual cycle, usually from cycle days 17-26. Menopause (as adjunct to estrogen): Given during last 2 weeks of the treatment sequence, followed by 1-week suspension of all HRT. Threatened pre-term delivery: 400 mg every 6-8 hrs, followed by a maintenance dose (e.g. 3 x 200 mg/day) taken up until gestation week 36. Vaginal cap - usually 200 mg daily as a single dose or in 2 divided doses, taken in the morning and evening. To be inserted deep into vagina with or without applicator. Partial luteal phase defect (dysovulation, irregular menstrual cycles): 200 mg for 10 days/menstrual cycle, usually from cycle days 17-26. Infertility associated with total luteal phase defect (oocyte donation): Initially 100 mg on days 13-14 of the transfer cycle, then 100 mg in the morning and evening on cycle days 15-25. From cycle day 26, in the event of conception, increase dose in weekly increments of 100 mg/day up to max 600 mg given in 3 divided doses. Dose is maintained up until day 60. Luteal phase supplementation during IVF: Initiate treatment in the evening of the transfer at a rate of 600 mg given in 3 divided doses (morning, noon, evening). Threatened pre-term delivery: 200-300 mg 2-3x a day for 3 days, followed by a maintenance dose of 100-200 mg/day until suppression of contraction.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe changes in hepatic function.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not a contraceptive. Shortened menstrual cycle and/or bleeding may occur if treatment is initiated too early, i.e. before cycle day 15. Patients with uterine bleeding, history of thrombophlebitis. Suspend treatment if eye disorder (e.g. vision loss, diplopia, vascular lesions of the retina), VTE or thrombotic events regardless of territory, or severe headache develops. Administration of progesterone during HRT involving estrogens over a minimum of 12 days/cycle is strongly recommended in non-hysterectomized women. May cause a reduction in glucose tolerance, which increases the need for insulin and other antidiabetics in diabetic patients. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Lactation. Vaginal cap: Contains soya lecithin.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Altered menstrual cycles, amenorrhea, intermenstrual bleeding, headache. Vaginal cap: Local irritation.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Barbiturates, antiepileptics (e.g. phenytoin), rifampicin, phenylbutazone, spironolactone, griseofulvin; antibiotics (e.g. ampicillin, tetracycline).
flattened_sections.packaging: Oral softgel capsule 100 mg (P38.00), 200 mg (P73.75). Vaginal softgel capsule 200 mg (P73.75).

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: Adults and adolescents: 0.5 to 1 mg/kg BW daily in 2 divided doses for 15-20 weeks. Max: 2 mg/kg/day. Maintenance treatment to be adjusted within the range of 0.1 to 1 mg/kg/day. Usual treatment duration: 16 weeks. Take with meals.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Hepatic or renal insufficiency. Hypervitaminosis A. Patients with excessively elevated blood lipid values. Blood donation by patients during and within 1 month of isotretinoin to women of childbearing potential should be avoided. Pregnancy and lactation.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Concurrent administration of other keratolytic or exfoliative anti-acne agents. Radiation therapy with UV light. Avoid exposure to sun. Monitor liver function. Patients with history of depression; diabetes, obesity, alcoholism, disturbances of lipid metabolism, psychiatric disorders. Dental problems. Avoid dermabrasion and wax epilation during and 5-6 months after treatment. Vision impairment may develop. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Use of androgen progestational contraceptives should be avoided. Pregnancy Risk: Category X.

flattened_sections.indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) when both linagliptin and metformin are appropriate. Patients inadequately controlled on metformin alone or those already being treated and well-controlled with separate tabs of linagliptin and metformin. In combination with a sulfonylurea or an SGLT2 inhibitor (triple combination therapy) in patients inadequately controlled on max tolerated dose of metformin and a sulfonylurea or an SGLT2 inhibitor.  Add-on to insulin in patients inadequately controlled with insulin and metformin alone.
flattened_sections.dose: Linagliptin 2.5 mg and metformin 500 mg, 850 mg, or 1 g 2x daily. Individualized dose.Max 5 mg/2 g daily. Patients currently not treated with metformin: Initially 2.5 mg/500 mg 2x daily. Inadequately controlled on max tolerated dose of metformin monotherapy: Initially 2.5 mg linagliptin 2x daily with dose of metformin already being taken. Switching from co-administration to fixed-dose combination: Initiate treatment at the doses already being taken. Inadequately controlled on dual combination therapy with max tolerated dose of metformin and a sulfonylurea or insulin: 2.5 mg linagliptin 2x daily with dose of metformin already being taken. Lower dose of sulfonylurea or insulin when combined with therapy. Renal impairment: No dose adjustment for linagliptin; GFR 60-89 mL/min: Max 3 g metformin daily, may reduce in relation to declining renal function; 45-59 mL/min: Max 2 g metformin daily (starting dose: most ½ max dose); 30-44 mL/min: Max 1 g metformin daily (starting dose: most ½ max dose). Taken with meals.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Any type of acute metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis).  Diabetic pre-coma. Severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min or eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Acute conditions with the potential to alter renal function (e.g. dehydration, severe infection, shock, IV iodinated contrast agents). Diseases which may cause tissue hypoxia, especially acute disease or worsening of chronic disease (e.g. decompensated heart failure, respiratory failure, recent MI, shock). Hepatic impairment. Acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not for type 1 DM. Pancreatitis, hypoglycemia, bullous pemphigoid. Coadministration with sulfonylureas or insulin. Inform patients of risk of lactic acidosis (e.g. acidotic dyspnea, abdominal pain,  muscle cramps, asthenia, hypothermia followed by coma). Discontinue if dehydration and symptoms of lactic acidosis occurs; prior to or at the time of the imaging procedure or surgery under general, spinal or epidural anesthesia until ≥48 hrs after, provided that renal function has been re-evaluated and found to be stable. Assess GFR prior initiation of treatment and regularly after. Monitor vit B<sub>12</sub> levels periodically. May be used with regular monitoring of cardiac and renal function in patients with stable chronic heart failure.  Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs. Planning pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nasopharyngitis, lactic acidosis, decreased vit B<sub>12</sub>, hypoglycemia, taste disturbance, cough,  decreased appetite, diarrhea, constipation (combination with insulin), nausea, pancreatitis, vomiting,  pruritus, abdominal pain, mouth ulceration, abnormal liver function test, hepatitis, bullous pemphigoid,  pruritus, erythema, rash, increased lipase and amylase.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Alcohol, iodinated contrast agents, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists and diuretics, verapamil, cimetidine, dolutegravir, ranolazine, trimethoprim, vandetanib, crizotinib, olaparib.

Pregnancy and lactation.

flattened_sections.indications: Initial therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM), in whom diet and exercise do not provide adequate glycemic control. Adjunct to diet and exercise in patients with inadequately controlled type 2 DM: (1) on metformin or sitagliptin (alone or in combination); (2) as part of triple combination therapy with a sulfonylurea; (3) as part of triple combination therapy with a PPAR-gamma agonist (e.g. thiazolidinedione); or (4) in combination with insulin.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosage. Single tab once daily with meals, preferably in the evening. Tabs must not be split, broken, crushed, or chewed before swallowing. Type 2 DM inadequately controlled with diet and exercise: 100 mg/1 g, titrate gradually to reduce GI side effects. Max 2 g of metformin. Patients with inadequately controlled type 2 DM on metformin monotherapy: 100 mg sitagliptin + metformin (current dose); On sitagliptin monotherapy: 100 mg/1 g. As part of combination therapy with a sulfonylurea or a thiazolidinedione or insulin: 100 mg total daily dose of sitagliptin. May require lower doses to reduce risks of sulfonylurea-induced hypoglycemia. Consider the patient's level of glycemic control and current metformin dose in determining the starting dose of metformin. Patients switching from co-administration of sitagliptin and metformin as separate tabs: Initiate previously prescribed dose of sitagliptin and metformin.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), acute or chronic metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis with or without coma, and radiologic studies involving IV administration of iodinated contrast materials. Patients with an eGFR ≥30-< 45 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>.
flattened_sections.precautions: Pancreatitis, liver disease, hypoxic states, surgical procedures, alcohol intake. Hypoglycemia in combination with sulfonylureas or insulin. Lactic acidosis in the elderly and in patients with significant renal insufficiency, impaired hepatic function. Monitor renal function before initiation of therapy. Discontinue if bullous pemphigoid or hypersensitivity reactions occur. Concomitant use of cationic drugs eliminated by renal tubular secretion. Discontinue at the time of or prior to iodinated contrast imaging in patients with eGFR ≥30-< 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, history of liver disease, alcoholism, heart failure, or those who will be administered intra-arterial iodinated contrast. Re-evaluate eGFR 48 hrs after the imaging procedure and restart Janumet if renal function is acceptable. Decreased vit B12 levels. Patients susceptible to hypoglycemia (e.g. elderly, debilitated, or malnourished; adrenal or pituitary insufficiency, alcohol intoxication, taking adrenergic blockers). Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, headache, pemphigoid, hypoglycemia, abdominal pain, pancreatitis.

flattened_sections.indications: Short-term treatment of active duodenal ulcer, active benign gastric ulcer, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) with or without esophagitis. Maintenance therapy of duodenal ulcer after healing of an active ulcer and GERD. Treatment of pathological hypersecretory conditions (e.g. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, multiple endocrine adenomas). IV/IM: For hospitalized patients with pathological hypersecretory conditions or intractable ulcers. Short-term treatment when oral medication is not feasible; of upper gastrointestinal bleeding due to esophagitis.
flattened_sections.dose: Tab - Ulcer – Adults: 40 mg once daily at bedtime or 20 mg twice daily for 4-8 weeks; Maintenance: 20 mg/day at bedtime; Childn 1-16 yrs: Initially 0.5 mg/kg/day as single dose at night or in 2 divided dose. Max 40 mg/day. GERD – Adults: 20 mg twice daily (morning and bedtime) for 6-12 weeks. Max 40 mg twice daily if there is esophageal erosion or ulceration; Childn 1-16 yrs: 0.5 mg/kg twice daily. Max 40 mg twice daily. Pathological hypersecretory conditions: 20 mg every 6 hrs, increased as necessary and continued as long as it is clinically indicated; doses up to 800 mg/day have been used. IM/IV - Administered via slow IV injection for ≥2 mins, slow IV infusion for 15-30 mins, or IM injection. Adults: 20 mg every 12 hrs. Childn 1-16 yrs: Initially 0.25 mg/kg every 12 hrs. Max 40 mg/day. Patients with renal impairment: Reduce dose by 50% or prolong dosing to 36-48 hrs. Patients undergoing dialysis: Reduce dose by 50%. Tabs should be administered at the end of dialysis session or later.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with renal impairment; duodenal and benign gastric ulcer. Risk of CAP or hospital-acquired pneumonia. Gastric malignancy should be excluded prior to therapy initiation. Monitor blood count and liver function during prolonged high-dose therapy. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Constipation, diarrhea, dizziness, headache.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Antacids, atazanavir, ketoconazole, itraconazole, probenecid, sucralfate.
flattened_sections.packaging: Film-coated tablet 20 mg (P23.01). Powder for IM/IV injection 20 mg (P204.33).

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of malignant gliomas e.g. glioblastoma multiforme and anaplastic astrocytoma, and malignant melanoma.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults with newly diagnosed glioblastoma multiforme: Concomitant 75 mg/m2 once daily for 42 days with focal radiotherapy, monotherapy 4 weeks after completing concomitant phase, administered for up to 6 cycles of monotherapy treatment. Cycle 1: 150 mg/m2 once daily for 5 days followed by 23 days without treatment; Cycle 2: Escalate dose to 200 mg/m2 once daily, once escalated, the dose remains at 200 mg/m2 once daily for the 1st 5 days of each subsequent cycle except if toxicity occurs. Adults and childn ≥3 yrs with recurrent or progressive malignant glioma: Treatment cycle is 28 days. Patients previously untreated with chemotherapy: 200 mg/m2 once daily for the 1st 5 days followed by 23-day treatment interruption; Patients previously treated with chemotherapy: 150 mg/m2 once daily, may be increased in the 2nd cycle to 200 mg/m2 once daily for 5 days if there is no hematological toxicity.
flattened_sections.precautions: May experience myelosuppression. Prior to dosing, patients must have absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥1.5 x 109/L and platelet count ≥100 x 109/L. CBC should be obtained on day 22 (21 days after 1st dosing) or within 48 hrs of that day, and weekly until ANC is above 1.5 x 109/L and platelet count exceeds 100 x 109/L. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, headache, fatigue, myelosuppression. May induce hypercoagulability.
