flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of patients with metastatic breast cancer resistant to both paclitaxel and an anthracycline-containing chemotherapy regimen. May also be used in combination with docetaxel for the treatment of metastatic breast cancer in patients who have failed to respond to, or recurred or relapsed during or following anthracycline-containing chemotherapy. When used alone as an adjuvant therapy following the complete resection of primary tumor in patients with stage III colon cancer when monotherapy with fluoropyrimidine is preferred.
flattened_sections.dose: Monotherapy: 1,250 mg/m2 twice daily orally for 2 weeks followed by 1 week rest period in 3-week cycle. Adjuvant treatment recommended for total of 6 months (8 cycles). In combination with docetaxel: 1,250 mg/m2 twice daily for 2 weeks followed by 1-week rest period, combined with docetaxel at 75 mg/m2 as 1-hr infusion every 3 weeks.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to 5-fluorouracil.
flattened_sections.precautions: Hand-and-foot syndrome (palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia or chemotherapy-induced acral erythema). MI, angina dysrhythmias, cardiogenic shock, sudden death and ECG changes in patients with history of CHD. Hepatic dysfunction, hyperbilirubinemia, fertility impairment. Childn <18 yrs. Elderly ≥80 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Altered coagulation parameters and/or bleeding with coumarin-derivative anticoagulants. Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, constipation, dyspepsia, fatigue, myalgia.

indication_long: 1st-line chemotherapy in ovarian c...

flattened_sections.indications: 1<sup>st</sup>-line chemotherapy in ovarian cancer for the treatment of advanced disease or a residual disease >1 cm after the initial laparotomy, in combination with cisplatin and as 2<sup>nd</sup>-line in the treatment of metastatic carcinoma of ovary after failure of standard platinum-based therapy. Adjuvant treatment in node-positive breast carcinoma following anthracycline and cyclophosphamide therapy. Initial treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer either in combination with an anthracycline, or in combination with trastuzumab in patients over-express HER-2 at 3+ level for whom an anthracycline is not suitable. Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma who have failed prior liposomal anthracycline therapy.
flattened_sections.dose: 1st-line treatment of ovarian cancer: 175 mg/m2 IV infusion over 3 hrs or 135 mg/m2 IV infusion over 24 hrs followed by 75 mg/m2 cisplatin, therapy repeated at 3-weeks intervals. 2nd-line treatment of ovarian cancer: 175 mg/m2 over 3 hrs with 3 weeks interval between courses. 1st-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma in combination with doxorubicin (50 mg/m2): Recommended dose 220 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs, with a 3-week interval between courses, should be given 24 hrs after doxorubicin. 1st-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma in combination with trastuzumab: Recommended dose 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs with a 3-week interval between courses, infusion may be started the day following the 1st dose of trastuzumab or immediately after subsequent doses of trastuzumab. 2nd-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma: 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs with 3-week intervals between courses. Advanced NSCLC: 175 mg/m2 over 3 hrs, followed by 80 mg/m2 of cisplatin with 3-week intervals between courses. AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma: Recommended dose 100 mg/m2 3 hrs IV infusion every 2 weeks.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Hypersensitivity. Patients must be pre-treated with corticosteroids, antihistamines and H2-antagonists. Impaired hepatic function. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Bone marrow suppression, peripheral neuropathy.
flattened_sections.packaging: Solution for IV infusion 6 mg/mL x 5 mL, 16.7 mL, 50 mL.

flattened_sections.precautions: Not for prevention of relapse after curative operation. flattened_sections.indications: Tab: 20 mg – Adults: Prevention of NSAID-induced gastroduodenal ulcers in patients at risk with a need for continuous NSAID treatment. Adults and adolescents ≥12 yrs: Symptomatic improvement (e.g. heartburn, acid regurgitation, pain in swallowing) and healing of mild reflux esophagitis; long-term management and prevention of relapse in reflux esophagitis. Childn 5-11 yrs: Treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux esophagitis. 40 mg – Adults: Treatment of moderate and severe reflux esophagitis, gastric and duodenal ulcer, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other pathological hypersecretory conditions, and in combination with 2 appropriate antibiotics for eradication of H. pylori in patients with peptic ulcers to reduce recurrence of duodenal and gastric ulcer. Childn 5-17 yrs: Treatment of reflux esophagitis. IV: Treatment of duodenal ulcer, gastric ulcer, moderate and severe reflux esophagitis, bleeding peptic ulcer (and prevention of re-bleeding), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other conditions associated with pathological overproduction of gastric acid. Prophylaxis of acute bleeding stress ulcer.
flattened_sections.dose: Taken 1 hr before breakfast. Tab - Adults - Prevention of NSAID-induced gastroduodenal ulcers: 20 mg daily; Moderate and severe reflux esophagitis, gastric and duodenal ulcer: 40 mg daily, may be doubled when there is no response to other treatment; Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other pathological hypersecretory conditions: Initially 80 mg per day, titrated up or down as needed. For dose >80 mg, give in 2 divided doses; Eradication of H. pylori with 2 appropriate antibiotics: Take second pantoprazole tab before evening meal. Treatment duration: 7 days, max 2 weeks. Twice daily doses. (a) 40 mg pantoprazole + 1,000 mg amoxicillin + 500 mg clarithromycin, (b) 40 mg pantoprazole + 500 mg metronidazole + 500 mg clarithromycin, (c) 40 mg pantoprazole + 1,000 mg amoxicillin + 500 mg metronidazole. Symptomatic improvement and healing of mild reflux esophagitis: Adults and adolescents ≥12 yrs - 20 mg daily for 2-4 weeks, recurring symptoms can be controlled with 20 mg once daily, when required. Treatment duration: ≥4 weeks. Long-term management and prevention of reflux esophagitis relapse: Adults and adolescents ≥12 yrs - 20 mg maintenance dose daily, increased to 40 mg daily if relapse occurs, can be reduced again to 20 mg after healing of the relapse. Symptomatic GERD: Childn 5-11 yrs - 20 mg daily, further investigation is recommended if symptom control has not been achieved after 4 weeks. Treatment of reflux esophagitis – Childn 5-17 yrs: >35 kg BW: 40 mg; 19-35 kg: 20 mg. Treatment duration: 4-8 weeks. Severe hepatic impairment: Max 20 mg daily or 40 mg every other day. Renal impairment: ≤40 mg. IV inj- Duodenal ulcer, gastric ulcer, and severe reflux esophagitis: 40 mg/day; Long-term management of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other hypersecretory conditions: Initially 80 mg/day, can be titrated up or down as needed. For dose >80 mg, give in 2 divided doses; If rapid acid control is required: Initially 2 x 80 mg to manage decrease of acid output into target range (< 10 mEq/h) within 1 hr; Upper digestive hemorrhage (complimentary to endoscopic therapy) and prevention of re-bleeding: 80 mg bolus, followed by 8 mg/hr infusion for 72 hrs; Prophylaxis of acute bleeding due to stress ulcer: 40-80 mg once to twice daily. May be given as bolus (≥2 mins) or infusion. Severe hepatic impairment: Max 20 mg daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Combination treatment for eradication of H. pylori in patients with moderate to severe hepatic or renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not for mild GI complaints. Restrict use of therapy as preventive of NSAID-induced gastroduodenal ulcers to patients requiring continued NSAID treatment and with increased risks for GI complications. Co-administration with HIV protease inhibitors (acidic intragastric pH dependent) is not recommended. May increase risk of GI infections or bone fractures. May masks symptoms of gastric malignancy. Severe hypomagnesemia, subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus. Vit B<sub>12</sub> malabsorption on prolonged use. Discontinue for at least 5 days prior CgA measurements. Monitor liver enzymes regularly in patients with severe liver impairment; long-term treatment (≥1 yr); magnesium levels prior to and periodically during treatment on patients requiring long-term treatment or who use drug-induced hypomagnesemia. Tab: Childn < 5 yrs.  IV: Childn < 18 yrs.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Fundic gland polyps (benign). IV: injection site thrombophlebitis.

Concomitant use with aminoglycosides. Discontinue if symptoms of pseudomembranous colitis by Clostridium difficile, and superinfection occurs. Monitor leukocyte count periodically. Premature infants and neonates. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Dizziness, tinnitus, hearing loss; increased bilirubin, AST and ALT, BUN and creatinine; exfoliative and bullous dermatitis, SJS and TEN; rash, erythema, flushing, hypotension, wheezing, dyspnea, urticaria and pruritus. flattened_sections.indications: Management of nausea and vomiting induced by cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Prevention and treatment of post-op nausea and vomiting.
flattened_sections.dose: Tab - Adults: 8 mg given up to 2 hrs before treatment, followed by 8 mg 12 hrs later, then 8 mg twice daily for up to 5 days after the end of chemotherapy to protect against delayed emesis. Prevention and treatment of post-op nausea and vomiting: 16 mg 1 hr before anesthesia or 8 mg 1 hr before anesthesia, followed by 2 further doses of 8 mg at 8-hr intervals. Childn 4-11 yrs: 4 mg given 30 mins before chemotherapy, with subsequent 4 mg doses given 4 and 8 hrs thereafter. May give 4 mg thrice daily for 1-2 days after the end of chemotherapy. Renal or hepatic impairment: Max 8 mg. IV/IM - Prevention of nausea and vomiting associated with emetogenic chemotherapy - Adults and childn 6 months-18 yrs: Dilute in 50 mL of 5% dextrose or 0.9% sodium chloride before administration. 3 doses of 0.15 mg/kg infused over 15 mins beginning 30 mins before the start of chemotherapy for the 1st dose, then administer subsequent doses 4 and 8 hrs after the 1st dose. Alternatively for adults, 32 mg IV single dose infused over 15 mins beginning 30 mins before the start of chemotherapy. Prevention of post-op nausea and vomiting - Adults: 2 mg IV or 4 mg IM as single dose. Childn 1 month-12 yrs (weighing >40 kg): 4 mg as single dose; ≤40 kg: 0.1 mg/kg as single dose. Administer IV doses in not <30 secs, preferably over 2-5 mins, immediately before induction of anesthesia or post-op if patients did not receive prophylactic antiemetics and experiences nausea and vomiting after surgery.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use of apomorphine.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with severe hepatic impairment. Patients with signs of subacute intestinal obstruction or ileus. Concomitant use of drugs that prolong QT interval or cause electrolyte abnormalities. Pregnancy and lactation. IM/IV: May mask a progressive ileus and gastric distention.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, sensation of warmth or flushing, hiccups, constipation, dizziness, and blurred vision.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Cardiotoxic drugs, antibiotics, antifungal, antiarrhythmics, beta-blockers, serotonergic drugs, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin. Incompatibilities: Alkaline solns.

flattened_sections.indications: Palliative treatment of locally advanced non-metastatic hormone-dependent prostate cancer, as an alternative to surgical castration. Treatment of metastatic hormone-dependent prostate cancer. Adjuvant treatment to radiotherapy in patients with high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer. 3.75 mg: In combination with tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor as adjuvant treatment of HR-positive early-stage breast cancer in premenopausal women at high risk of recurrence after completion of chemotherapy. For the pituitary down-regulation in assisted reproduction technology. 3.75 mg and 11.25 mg: Treatment of endometriosis. 22.5 mg: Treatment of central precocious puberty (CPP) in childn ≥2 yrs with onset before 8 yrs in girls and 10 yrs in boys.
flattened_sections.dose: Administered as single injection. Prostate cancer - Duration - 3.75 mg (IM/SC): Every month (4 weeks); 11.25 mg (IM): Every 3 months (12 weeks); 22.5 mg (IM): Every 6 months (24 weeks). Breast cancer (3.75 mg IM only): Every 4 weeks in combination with tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor. Commence after completion of chemotherapy, once premenopausal status is confirmed. Initiate 6-8 weeks (minimum of 2 injections with 2-week interval) before starting aromatase inhibitor treatment. Pituitary down-regulation in assisted reproduction (3.75 mg only) - Long protocol: Single injection prior to induction of stimulation with exogenous gonadotropins. Short protocol: Single injection induced at the same time as or every shortly before stimulation with exogenous gonadotropins. Endometriosis in women ≥18 yrs (3.75 mg and 11.25 mg only): 3.75 mg IM/SC every 28 days, to be initiated in the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle. Max duration of treatment: 6 months. CPP (22.5 mg only): Administer in a regular six-monthly (24 weekly) period. Discontinue around physiological age of puberty and bone maturation (12-13 yrs for girls, 13-14 yrs for boys).
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to triptorelin, GnRH, GnRH agonists analogs. Intravascular injection. Women with undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding. Patients with spinal cord compression secondary to prostate cancer metastases. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Risk for transient increase in serum testosterone levels, temporary amenorrhea or permanent loss of ovarian function, bone mineral density loss, hypogonadism, anemia, increased lymphocyte count, pituitary apoplexy, ovarian hyperstimulation. Patients with preexisting or at risk for hyperglycemia, metastatic vertebral lesions and/or upper or lower urinary tract obstruction, CV diseases (HTN, hyperlipidemia), QT/QTc prolongation, seizures, epilepsy, cerebrovascular disorders, CNS anomalies, depressive disorders. Concomitant use of drugs associated with QT-prolongation, induce convulsion (e.g. bupropion, SSRIs). Patients with renal and hepatic impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Childn <18 yrs. Elderly >65 yrs. Pregnancy Risk: Category X.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Men: Induced variation in serum testosterone levels. Women: Hot flushes, vaginal dryness, amenorrhea. Local, CV, nervous, endocrine, GI, hepatic, musculoskeletal, respiratory, dermatologic, genitourinary, and sensory effects. Asthenia, fatigue, and bruising. Decreased Hgb, RBC. Increased glucose, BUN, AST, ALT, ALP levels.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Should not be mixed with medicinal products. Drugs affecting pituitary secretion of gonadotropins; drugs that induce hyperprolactinemia e.g. antipsychotic agents (chlorpromazine, haloperidol, molindone, olanzapine, prochlorperazine, risperidone), methyldopa, metoclopramide, reserpine); drugs that prolong QTc interval and induce Torsades de pointes. Anticoagulants, antihypertensives.

flattened_sections.dose: All doses taken once daily at any time of day, with or without food. Monotherapy: 10 mg. Add-on combination therapy: 10 mg with metformin (with or without sulfonylurea), thiazolidinedione, sulfonylurea, DPP-4 inhibitor (with or without metformin), GLP-1 receptor antagonist (prolonged-release exenatide), Dapagliflozin (with metformin), or insulin (with or without oral antidiabetic therapy, either metformin plus insulin dual therapy or metformin plus sulfonylurea plus insulin triple therapy). Initial combination therapy: 10 mg plus 500 mg metformin. Dose of metformin may be increased in inadequate glycemic control. eGFR < 45 mL/min/1.73 m2: Additional glucose-lowering treatment.

flattened_sections.precautions: Not for type 1 DM and diabetic ketoacidosis. Patients with severe renal impairment (eGFR < 25 mL/min/1.73 m²); predisposing factors to ketoacidosis include low beta-cell function reserve resulting from pancreatic disorders (e.g. type 1 diabetes, history of pancreatitis or pancreatic surgery), insulin dose reduction, reduced caloric intake or increased insulin requirements due to infections, illness, or surgery and alcohol abuse. Assess signs and symptoms of ketoacidosis, including nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, malaise, and shortness of breath, blood glucose levels < 14 mmol/L (250 mg/dL). Advise patients to seek medical attention if combination of symptoms of pain, tenderness, erythema, or swelling in the genital or perineal area, with fever or malaise is experienced. Discontinue or temporarily interrupt treatment if ketoacidosis is suspected; Fournier’s gangrene. Concomitant use with insulin and insulin secretagogues. Elderly. Childn and adolescents.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Genital infection, UTI; back pain, polyuria, pollakiuria.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of Parkinson's disease and syndrome.
flattened_sections.dose: Patients not receiving levodopa - Initial: 100 mg/25 mg thrice daily, may be increased by 1 tab of 100 mg/25 mg daily or every other day. Max 2 g/200 mg; Maintenance: Individualized dosage. At least 70-100 mg of carbidopa/day should be provided. When more levodopa is required, 250 mg/25 mg should be substituted at a dosage of 1 tab of 100 mg/25 mg given 3 or 4x daily. If necessary, the dose of 250 mg/25 mg may be increased by ½-1 tab 100 mg/25 mg every other day. Max 8 tabs daily. Patients receiving levodopa alone: Discontinue levodopa at least 12 hrs before starting therapy. Levodopa + carbidopa should be given as the 1st morning dose after a night without any levodopa. The dose should be approx 20% of the previous daily dose of levodopa. Levodopa requirement - >1,500 mg/day: 250 mg/25 mg 3 or 4x daily; <1,500 mg/day: 100 mg/25 mg 3 or 4x daily. Patients receiving levodopa with another decarboxylase inhibitor: Discontinue levodopa at least 12 hrs before starting therapy. Start with the same amount of levodopa as with the other levodopa + decarboxylase inhibitor combination. Patients receiving other antiparkinsonian agents: Dose adjustment of levodopa + carbidopa may be necessary.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with non-selective MAOIs, sympathomimetic amine (e.g. epinephrine, norepinephrine or isoproterenol). Clinical or lab evidence of uncompensated CV, endocrine, hematologic, hepatic, pulmonary, renal disease. Narrow-angle glaucoma. Severe psychoses. Suspicious undiagnosed skin lesions or a history of melanoma.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not recommended for the treatment of medicine-induced extrapyramidal reactions. MI, dyskinesia, mental disturbance, somnolence, NMS, behavioral disturbances, glaucoma, melanoma. Peri-op considerations. Severe CV or pulmonary disease, bronchial asthma, renal, hepatic or endocrine disease, peptic ulcer, seizure. Childn <18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Orthostatic hypotension; anorexia; nausea, vomiting; involuntary movements (e.g. grimacing, bruxism, gnawing, chewing, twisting and protrusion of the tongue, rhythmic opening and closing of the mouth, bobbling and wave-like motions of the head with or without gesticulations, slow rhythmic movements of the neck, hands or feet, jerky movements of the shoulder or pelvic girdle, and opisthotonos or ballismus), intermittent myoclonic body jerks during sleep; dyskinesia, increased hand tremor, ataxia, agitation, anxiety, euphoria; dream abnormalities including nightmares, insomnia, drowsiness; blepharospasm.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Anesthetic, anticholinergic, antihypertensives, TCAs, selegiline, D<sub>2</sub>-receptor antagonists, isoniazid, dopamine-depleting agents and other drugs depleting monoamine stores, phenytoin and papaverine, iron salts, metoclopramide.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) to improve glycemic control in adults as monotherapy, when diet and exercise alone do not provide adequate glycemic control when use of metformin is inappropriate  due to intolerance, or add-on combination therapy with other glucose-lowering drugs (e.g. insulin). Used  in conjunction with other measures in line with the current standard of care in patients with type 2 DM and established cardiovascular (CV) disease to reduce the risk of CV death. For adults with heart failure  (NYHA class II-IV) independent of LVEF, with or without type 2 DM: to reduce risk of CV death and  hospitalization for heart failure, to slow kidney function decline. Chronic kidney disease (CKD): to reduce  the risk of kidney disease progression or CV death and all-cause hospitalization.
flattened_sections.dose: Type 2 DM: Initially 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 25 mg once daily for eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m2 and requiring additional glycemic control. Heart failure and CKD: 10 mg once daily. Consider lowering dose of sulfonylurea or insulin when combined with therapy. Renal impairment - eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2: 10 mg with additional glucose-lowering treatment if needed.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Rare hereditary conditions (e.g. galactose intolerance) incompatible with excipients. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not for type 1 DM. Patients with higher risk or history of ketoacidosis; CV disease, on antihypertensive with history of hypotension. Not recommended to initiate in patients on dialysis. Discontinue if ketoacidosis and Fournier’s gangrene is suspected. Temporary interruption in complicated UTI Assess renal function prior to initiation and periodically during treatment. Monitor ketones, vol status, and electrolytes. Elderly ≥75 yrs. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hypoglycemia (when used with sulfonylurea or insulin); vol depletion; UTI, vaginal moniliasis,  vulvovaginitis, balanitis, and other genital infections, Fournier’s gangrene; constipation; increased urination, dysuria; thirst; Increased blood creatinine, hematocrit, and serum lipids, decreased GFR.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Thiazide and loop diuretics, insulin and insulin secretagogues (e.g. sulfonylurea), lithium.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: General anesthesia, monitored anesthesia care, ICU sedation in intubated and mechanically ventilated patient.
flattened_sections.dose: General anesthesia induction - Adults <55 yrs: 40 mg every 10 secs until induction onset (2-2.5 mg/kg). Elderly, debilitated or ASA-PS III or IV patients: 20 mg every 10 secs until induction onset (1-1.5 mg/kg). Cardiac anesthesia: 20 mg every 10 secs until induction onset (0.5-1.5 mg/kg). Neurosurgical patients: 20 mg every 10 secs until induction onset (1-2 mg/kg). Childn 3-16 yrs: 2.5-3.5 mg/kg administered over 20-30 secs. General anesthesia maintenance: Infusion - Adults <55 yrs and neurosurgical patients: 100-200 mcg/kg/min. Elderly, debilitated, ASA-PS III or IV patients: 50-100 mcg/kg/min. Cardiac anesthesia: 100-150 mcg/kg/min (with secondary opioid), 50-100 mcg/kg/min (with primary opioid). Childn 2 months-16 yrs: 125-300 mcg/kg/min. Intermittent bolus - Adults <55 yrs: Increments of 20-50 mg, as needed. Monitored anesthesia care (MAC) sedation initiation - Adults <55 yrs: Slow infusion of 100-150 mcg/kg/min for 3-5 mins or slow injection of 0.5 mg/kg for 3-5 mins followed immediately by a maintenance infusion. Elderly, debilitated, neurosurgical, ASA-PS III or IV patients: Same with adult dose. Avoid rapid boluses. MAC sedation maintenance - Adults <55 yrs: Infusion of 25-75 mcg/kg/min or incremental bolus doses of 10 mg or 20 mg. Elderly, debilitated, neurosurgical, ASA-PS III or IV patients: Same with adult dose. Avoid rapid bolus. Initiation and maintenance of ICU sedation in intubated, mechanically ventilated – Adults: Initial infusion of 5 mcg/kg/min for at least 5 mins. Subsequent increments 5-10 mcg/kg/min for 5-10 mins. Maintenance 5-50 mcg/kg/min or higher may be required. Clinical effect evaluation and CNS function assessment should be carried out daily throughout the maintenance to determine minimum dose required for sedation.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to propofol and its component, egg and soy products. Epilepsy, seizure. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Monitor patient for signs of hypertension and/or bradycardia. Lipid metabolism disorder (e.g. primary hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipemia, pancreatitis). Epileptic patient.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nodal tachycardia, hypotension, decreased cardiac output, agitation, apnea, rash, hypersalivation, diplopia, ear and eye pain, nystagmus, taste perversion, tinnitus.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Narcotics, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, chloral hydrate, droperidol, nitrous oxide, opioids.
flattened_sections.packaging: Emulsion for injection 10 mg/mL x 20 mL (P500.00).

indication_long: Melanoma: Unresectable or metastatic m...

flattened_sections.indications: Melanoma: Unresectable or metastatic melanoma; treatment of adult and childn ≥12 yrs with stage IIB or IIC melanoma who have undergone complete resection; adjuvant treatment of patients with melanoma with lymph node involvement who have undergone complete resection. Non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC): 1st line treatment of patients with Metastatic NSCLC with no epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) or anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) genomic tumor aberrations, in combination with pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy; 1st line treatment of patients with metastatic squamous NSCLC, in combination with carboplatin and either paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel; monotherapy for 1st line treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC whose tumors express PD-L1 with a >1% tumor proportion score (TPS) as determined by a validated test, with no EGFR or ALK genomic tumor aberrations; monotherapy for patients with advanced NSCLC whose tumors express PD-L1 with a >1% TPS as determined by a validated test, who have received platinum-containing chemotherapy. Patients with EGFR or ALK genomic tumor aberrations should have received prior therapy for these aberrations prior to receiving pembrolizumab; treatment of patients with resectable Stage II, IIIA, or IIIB (T3-4N2) NSCLS in combination with platinum-containing chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment, and then continued as monotherapy as adjuvant treatment; monotherapy for adjuvant treatment of patients with stage IB (T2a ≥4 cm), II, or IIIA NSCLC who have undergone complete resection. Small cell lung cancer (SCLC): For patients with locally advanced or metastatic SCLC who have received two or more prior lines of therapy. Head and neck cancer: As monotherapy or in combination with platinum and 5-fluorouracil chemotherapy, for first-line treatment of patients with metastatic or unresectable recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC); as monotherapy for metastatic or unresectable recurrent HNSCC with disease progression on or after platinum-containing chemotherapy. Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL): Relapsed or refractory cHL in adult or childn. Urothelial carcinoma: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma who are not eligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy and whose tumors express PD-L1 [combined positive score (CPS >10)] as determined by a validated test, or those who are not eligible for any platinum-containing chemotherapy regardless of PD-L1 status; locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma who have received platinum-containing chemotherapy; BCG-unresponsive, high risk, non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in-situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors who are ineligible for or have elected not to undergo cystectomy. Gastric cancer: 1st line treatment of locally advanced unresectable or metastasis gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma in combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum containing chemotherapy; 1st line treatment of locally advanced unresectable or metastasis HER2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma in combination with trastuzumab, fluoropyrimidine- and platinum containing chemotherapy; as monotherapy, treatment of recurrent locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma whose tumors express PD-L1 (CPS ≥1) as determined by a validated test, with disease progression on or after two or more prior lines of therapy including fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy and if appropriate, HER2/neu-targeted therapy. Esophageal cancer: 1st line treatment of locally advanced unresectable or metastatic carcinoma of the esophagus or gastroesophageal junction in combination with platinum and fluoropyrimidine based chemotherapy; monotherapy for recurrent locally advanced or metastatic esophageal cancer whose tumors express PD-L1 (CPS >10) as determined by a validated test, and who have received one prior line of systemic therapy; monotherapy for recurrent locally advanced or metastatic esophageal cancer who have received two or more prior line of systemic therapy. Microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) cancer: Advanced microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H), including mismatch repair deficient (dMMR), cancer who have received prior therapy. Colorectal cancer: 1st line treatment of unresectable metastatic MSI-H or dMMR colorectal cancer (CRC). Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC): Hepatocellular carcinoma who have been previously treated with anti-angiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) or oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy. Biliary Tract Carcinoma:treatment of patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic biliary tract carcinoma (BTC), in combination with chemotherapy. Cervical cancer: High-risk, locally advanced cervical cancer in combination with chemoradiotherapy (CRT); Persistent, recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer in combination with chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab as monotherapy, treatment of recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer whose tumors express PD-L1 (CPS≥1) as determined by a validated test, with disease progression on or after chemotherapy. Renal cell carcinoma (RCC): 1st line treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma, in combination with axitinib; 1st line treatment of advanced RCC, in combination with lenvatinib; as monotherapy for adjuvant treatment of RCC at intermediate-high or high risk of recurrence following nephrectomy, or following nephrectomy and resection of metastatic lesions. Endometrial carcinoma: Primary advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma in combination with chemotherapy, followed by Pembrolizumab; advanced endometrial carcinoma who have disease progression following prior systemic therapy in any setting and are not candidates for curative surgery or radiation in combination with lenvatinib. Tumor mutational burden-High cancer (TMB-H): Unresectable or metastatic tumor mutational burden-high (TMB-H) [≥10 mutations/megabase (mut/Mb)] solid tumors, as determined by a validated test, that have progressed following prior treatment and who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options in adult and pediatric patients. Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC): High-risk early-stage TNBC in combination with chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment, then continued as monotherapy as adjuvant treatment after surgery; locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic TNBC whose tumors express PD-L1 (CPS ≥10) as determined by a validated test, in combination with chemotherapy.
flattened_sections.dose: IV infusion over 30 min. Adults: 200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. When administering pembrolizumab as part of a combination with intravenous chemotherapy, it should be administered first. RCC: In combination with axitinib, dose escalation above initial dose 5 mg may be considered at intervals of 6 weeks or longer. Endometrial carcinoma and RCC in combination of lenvatinib: Initial dose of lenvatinib is 20 mg orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Adjuvant treatment of melanoma, NSCLC, or RCC: Should be administered up to one year or until disease recurrence or unacceptable toxicity. Neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment of high-risk early-stage TNBC: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in combination with chemotherapy for 8 doses of 200 mg every 3 weeks or 4 doses of 400 mg every 6 weeks or until disease progression that precludes definitive surgery or unacceptable toxicity, followed by adjuvant treatment with pembrolizumab as monotherapy dose for 9 doses of 200 mg every 3 weeks or 5 doses of 400 mg every 6 weeks or until disease recurrence or unacceptable toxicity. Melanoma, cHL & TMB-H cancer in ped patients 2 mg/kg (up to max of 200 mg) as IV infusion over 30 min every 3 wk. Neoadjuvant & adjuvant treatment of resectable NSCLC: Patients should be treated w/ neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in combination w/ chemotherapy for 12 wk or until disease progression that precludes definitive surgery or unacceptable toxicity, followed by adjuvant treatment.
flattened_sections.precautions: Immune-mediated pneumonitis, -colitis, -nephritis, -hepatitis, -endocrinopathies (hypophysitis, thyroid disorders, type 1 DM, including diabetic ketoacidosis), -severe skin reactions, SJS, TEN, and other immune-mediated adverse reactions (uveitis, myositis, Guillain-Barre syndrome, pancreatitis, encephalitis, sarcoidosis, myasthenic syndrome/myasthenia gravis including exacerbation, myelitis, and vasculitis) may occur. Infusion-related reactions, including severe and life-threatening reactions. Solid organ transplant rejection. Acute GvHD, including fatal GvHD in patients with history or allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT). Elevated liver enzymes in combination with axitinib for renal cell carcinoma. Increased mortality in patients with multiple myeloma when added to thalidomide analogue and dexamethasone. Musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders: arthritis. Eye disorders: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada syndrome. Immune system disorders: hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Use highly effective contraception for reproductive potential (4 months after last dose). Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Arthralgia, back pain, cough, vitiligo, pruritus, hyponatremia. fatigue, asthenia, neutropenia, rash, dyspnea. HTN, hypothyroidism, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, decreased appetite, decreased weight, increased alanine transferase, proteinuria, urinary tract infection, headache, dysphoria, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome, immune-mediated adverse reactions.
flattened_sections.packaging: Solution for injection (IV) 25 mg/mL x 4 mL.

Biliary Tract Carcinoma:treatment of patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic biliary tract carcinoma (BTC), in combination with chemotherapy. Cervical cancer: High-risk, locally advanced cervical cancer in combination with chemoradiotherapy (CRT); Persistent, recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer in combination with chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab as monotherapy, treatment of recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer whose tumors express PD-L1 (CPS≥1) as determined by a validated test, with disease progression on or after chemotherapy. Renal cell carcinoma (RCC): 1st line treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma, in combination with axitinib; 1st line treatment of advanced RCC, in combination with lenvatinib; as monotherapy for adjuvant treatment of RCC at intermediate-high or high risk of recurrence following nephrectomy, or following nephrectomy and resection of metastatic lesions. Endometrial carcinoma: Primary advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma in combination with chemotherapy, followed by Pembrolizumab; advanced endometrial carcinoma who have disease progression following prior systemic therapy in any setting and are not candidates for curative surgery or radiation in combination with lenvatinib. Tumor mutational burden-High cancer (TMB-H): Unresectable or metastatic tumor mutational burden-high (TMB-H) [≥10 mutations/megabase (mut/Mb)] solid tumors, as determined by a validated test, that have progressed following prior treatment and who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options in adult and pediatric patients. Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC): High-risk early-stage TNBC in combination with chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment, then continued as monotherapy as adjuvant treatment after surgery; locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic TNBC whose tumors express PD-L1 (CPS ≥10) as determined by a validated test, in combination with chemotherapy.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: IV infusion over 30 min. Adults: 200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. When administering pembrolizumab as part of a combination with intravenous chemotherapy, it should be administered first. RCC: In combination with axitinib, dose escalation above initial dose 5 mg may be considered at intervals of 6 weeks or longer. Endometrial carcinoma and RCC in combination of lenvatinib: Initial dose of lenvatinib is 20 mg orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Adjuvant treatment of melanoma, NSCLC, or RCC: Should be administered up to one year or until disease recurrence or unacceptable toxicity. Neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment of high-risk early-stage TNBC: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in combination with chemotherapy for 8 doses of 200 mg every 3 weeks or 4 doses of 400 mg every 6 weeks or until disease progression that precludes definitive surgery or unacceptable toxicity, followed by adjuvant treatment with pembrolizumab as monotherapy dose for 9 doses of 200 mg every 3 weeks or 5 doses of 400 mg every 6 weeks or until disease recurrence or unacceptable toxicity. Melanoma, cHL & TMB-H cancer in ped patients 2 mg/kg (up to max of 200 mg) as IV infusion over 30 min every 3 wk. Neoadjuvant & adjuvant treatment of resectable NSCLC: Patients should be treated w/ neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in combination w/ chemotherapy for 12 wk or until disease progression that precludes definitive surgery or unacceptable toxicity, followed by adjuvant treatment.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Immune-mediated pneumonitis, -colitis, -nephritis, -hepatitis, -endocrinopathies (hypophysitis, thyroid disorders, type 1 DM, including diabetic ketoacidosis), -severe skin reactions, SJS, TEN, and other immune-mediated adverse reactions (uveitis, myositis, Guillain-Barre syndrome, pancreatitis, encephalitis, sarcoidosis, myasthenic syndrome/myasthenia gravis including exacerbation, myelitis, and vasculitis) may occur. Infusion-related reactions, including severe and life-threatening reactions. Solid organ transplant rejection. Acute GvHD, including fatal GvHD in patients with history or allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT). Elevated liver enzymes in combination with axitinib for renal cell carcinoma. Increased mortality in patients with multiple myeloma when added to thalidomide analogue and dexamethasone. Musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders: arthritis. Eye disorders: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada syndrome. Immune system disorders: hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Use highly effective contraception for reproductive potential (4 months after last dose). Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: To reduce risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with chronic heart failure especially in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) below normal. Administered in place of an ACE inhibitor or ARBs.
flattened_sections.dose: Initially 100 mg twice daily. Double the dose at 2-4 weeks to target dose of 200 mg twice daily as tolerated. Patients not currently on ACE inhibitors or ARBs or previously taking low doses of these agents: Start at 50 mg twice daily and slow dose titration (doubling every 3-4 weeks). Patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m2) and moderate hepatic impairment: Initially 50 mg twice daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with an ACE inhibitor (do not start Entresto for at least 36 hrs after discontinuing ACE inhibitor therapy) or ARBs. History of angioedema related to ACE inhibitor or ARBs therapy, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or with renal impairment (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Severe hepatic impairment, biliary cirrhosis and cholestasis. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester).
flattened_sections.precautions: Sodium and/or sodium depletion should be corrected before treatment. Hypotension, impaired renal function, hyperkalemia, angioedema. Patients with renal artery stenosis, CHF NYHA class IV, hepatic impairment. Not suitable with B-type natriuretic peptide as biomarker for heart failure. Psychiatric disorders (e.g. hallucination paranoia, and sleep disorders). May impair ability to drive and operate machinery.  Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hyperkalemia, hypotension, renal impairment,  cough, dizziness, diarrhea, anemia, fatigue, renal failure, hypokalemia, headache, syncope, asthenia, nausea, orthostatic hypotension, gastritis, vertigo, hypoglycemia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 substrates (e.g. statins), PDE5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil), lithium, furosemide, metformin, potassium-sparing diuretics including mineralocorticoid antagonists (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride), potassium supplements, or salt substitutes containing potassium, NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors, nitrates, inhibitors of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT3 (e.g. rifampin, ciclosporin) or multidrug resistance-associated protein (e.g. ritonavir).

flattened_sections.indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults and childn ≥10 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). For adults with type 2 DM and established cardiovascular (CV) disease, to reduce the risk of CV death; in conjunction with other measures to prevent CV death.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dose. Max 25 mg empagliflozin/2,000 mg metformin daily. Take 1 tab 2x daily with meals. Patients inadequately controlled on metformin alone or in combination with other products including insulin: Initially 5 mg empagliflozin 2x daily with dose of metformin already being taken, may be increased to total 25 mg empagliflozin daily if total 10 mg daily can be tolerated. Patients already treated with empagliflozin: Continue with the same daily dose. Switching from individual monocomponents to combination therapy: Continue with the same daily dose or the nearest therapeutically appropriate dose of metformin. Lower dose of sulfonylurea or insulin when combined with therapy. Renal impairment – GFR 60-89 mL/min: Max 3,000 mg metformin daily (may reduce in relation to declining renal function), max 25 mg empagliflozin daily; 45-59 mL/min: Max 2,000 mg metformin daily (starting dose: most ½ max dose), no dose adjustment for empagliflozin; 30-44 mL/min: Max 1 g metformin daily (starting dose: most ½ max dose), no dose adjustment for empagliflozin.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Any type of acute metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidoses). Diabetic pre-coma. Severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min or eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Acute conditions with the potential to alter renal function (e.g. dehydration, severe infection, shock, IV iodinated contrast agents). Diseases which may cause tissue hypoxia, especially acute disease, or worsening of chronic disease (e.g. decompensated heart failure, respiratory failure, recent MI, shock). Hepatic insufficiency, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not for type 1 DM. Patients with higher risk or history of ketoacidosis; CV disease, on antihypertensive with history of hypotension; childn with eGFR < 60 mL/min. Inform patients for risk of lactic acidosis (e.g. acidotic dyspnea, abdominal pain, muscle cramps asthenia, hypothermia followed by coma). Discontinue if pancreatitis, dehydration, ketoacidosis, Fournier’s gangrene is suspected; prior to or at the time of the imaging procedure or surgery under general, spinal, or epidural anesthesia until ≥48 hrs after surgery or resumption of oral nutrition and, provided that renal function has been re-evaluated and found to be stable. Temporary interruption in complicated UTI or until fluid loss is corrected. Assess GFR prior to initiation of treatment and at least annually; more frequently in patients with increased risk of further progression of renal impairment and elderly. Monitor vit B<sub>12</sub> levels periodically in patients with risk factors for vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency, ketones, vol status, and electrolytes. May be used with regular monitoring of cardiac and renal function in patients with stable chronic heart failure. Elderly ≥75 yrs. Childn < 10 yrs. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hypoglycemia; nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, constipation; lactic acidosis, vit B<sub>12</sub> decreased/deficiency, ketoacidosis; UTI, vaginal moniliasis, vulvovaginitis, balanitis and other genital infections; hepatitis, liver function tests abnormalities; taste disturbance; increased urination, dysuria; vol depletion; thirst; increased blood creatinine, hematocrit, and serum lipids, decreased GFR; pruritus, allergic skin reactions.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Alcohol, thiazide and loop diuretics, insulin and insulin secretagogues (sulfonylureas), lithium, iodinated contrast agents, NSAIDs, COX-2 inhibitors, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonist, verapamil, rifampicin, cimetidine, dolutegravir, ranolazine, trimethoprim, vandetanib, isavuconazole, crizotinib, olaparib.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Not for type 1 DM. Patients with risk for vol depletion, ketoacidosis, or hypoglycemia. Co-administration with drugs that can impair renal function (e.g., antihypertensives, diuretics, NSAIDs). Lower dose of insulin or insulin secretagogues to reduce risk of hypoglycemia. Initiation of metformin in patients with eGFR < 45 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> is not recommended. Discontinue or temporary interrupt if ketoacidosis is suspected; lactic acidosis; conditions characterized by hypoxemia, dehydration, severe infections, and hypoperfusion; prior to or at the time of administration of IV iodinated contrast agents, and not reinstituted until 48 hrs after and only after renal function is found stable; Fournier’s gangrene; any surgical procedure (except minor procedures not associated with restricted intake of food and fluids) and do not restart until patient’s oral intake resumes and renal function is stable. Assess renal function prior to initiation of therapy and periodically thereafter; serum electrolytes and ketones, blood glucose, if indicated, blood pH, lactate, pyruvate, and metformin levels with type 2 DM previously well-controlled on treatment develop laboratory abnormalities or illness. flattened_sections.indications: Upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) e.g. tonsillitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, otitis media and scarlet fever; LRTI e.g. bronchitis, pneumonia, empyema and lung abscess; skin and soft tissue (e.g. acne, furuncles, cellulitis, impetigo, abscesses, and wound infections), bone and joint (e.g. osteomyelitis and septic arthritis), gynecological (e.g. Chlamydia trachomatis cervicitis, endometritis, cellulitis, vaginal cuff infection and tubo-ovarian abscess, salpingitis and pelvic inflammatory disease), and intra-abdominal (e.g. peritonitis and abdominal abscess) infections; septicemia and endocarditis, dental infections, toxoplasmic encephalitis in patients with AIDS, Pneumocystis jirovecii (previously classified as Pneumocystis carinii) pneumonia in patients with AIDS, malaria, endocarditis in patients sensitive or allergic to penicillins.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults: 600-1,800 mg/day in 2, 3, or 4 equal doses. Childn >1 month: 8-25 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 equal doses. C. trachomatis cervicitis: 450-600 mg four times daily for 10-14 days. Toxoplasmic encephalitis in patients with AIDS: Clindamycin 600-1,200 mg every 6 hrs for 2 weeks followed by 300-600 mg every 6 hrs + pyrimethamine 25-75 mg each day for 8-10 weeks and folinic acid 10-20 mg/day should be given with higher doses of pyrimethamine. Total duration: 8-10 weeks. P. jirovecii (carinii) pneumonia in patients with AIDS: Clindamycin 300-450 mg every 6 hrs for 21 days + primaquine 15-30 mg once daily for 21 days. Acute streptococcal tonsillitis/pharyngitis: 300 mg twice daily for 10 days. Uncomplicated malaria, Plasmodium falciparum - Adults: Quinine sulfate 650 mg three times daily for 3-7 days + clindamycin 20 mg base/kg/day divided three times daily for 7 days; Childn: Quinine sulfate 10 mg/kg three times daily for 3-7 days + clindamycin 20 mg base/kg/day divided three times daily for 7 days. pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

Treatment of non-infectious intermediate, posterior and panuveitis. Childn: Treatment of active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pJIA) in patients ≥2 yrs who had inadequate response to ≥2 DMARDs; active enthesitis-related arthritis in patients ≥6 yrs. Reduction of signs and symptoms in childn ≥6 yrs with moderate to severe active Crohn’s disease. Treatment of severe chronic plaque psoriasis in childn and adolescents >4 yrs; active moderate to severe HS (acne inversa) in adolescents >12 yrs; chronic non-infectious anterior uveitis in childn ≥2 yrs; ulcerative colitis in childn ≥5 yrs.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults – RA, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis: 40 mg SC as single dose every other week. Patients with RA not taking methotrexate: May be given 40 mg every week or 80 mg every other week. Crohn’s disease: Initially 80 mg then 40 mg (2nd dose) on day 14. Maintenance: 40 mg on day 28 and continuing every 2 weeks. Ulcerative colitis: 160 mg in week 0 (given as 160 mg in one day or as 80 mg/day for 2 consecutive days); 80 mg in week 2. After induction: 40 mg every other week via SC inj. Plaque psoriasis: Initially 80 mg followed by 40 mg given every other week starting one week after initial dose. Reevaluate continuation of therapy after 16 weeks. HS: Initially 160 mg at day 1 (given as 160 mg in one day or as 80 mg per day for two consecutive days), followed by 80 mg two weeks later at day 15. Two weeks later (day 29), continue with 40 mg every week or 80 mg every other week. Uveitis: Initially 80 mg, followed by 40 mg given every other week starting one week after initial dose. Childn – pJIA (from 2 yrs) - ≥30 kg BW: 40 mg every other week; 10-30 kg BW: 20 mg every other week. Enthesitis-related arthritis (from 6 yrs) – ≥30 kg BW: 40 mg every other week; 15-30 kg BW: 20 mg every other week. Crohn’s disease (from 6-17 yrs) – ≥40 kg BW: 80 mg at week 0 and 40 mg at week 2; maintenance: 40 mg every other week. If there is need for more rapid response to therapy: 160 mg at week 0 and 80 mg at week 2. May be increased to 40 mg every week or 80 mg every other week; <40 kg BW: 40 mg at week 0 and 20 mg at week 2; maintenance: 20 mg every other week. If there is need for more rapid response to therapy: 80 mg at week 0 and 40 mg at week 2. May be increased to 20 mg every week. Plaque psoriasis (from 4-17 yrs) – ≥30 kg BW: Initially 40 mg followed by 40 mg every other week starting one week after initial dose; 15-<30 kg BW: Initially 20 mg followed by 20 mg given every other week starting one week after initial dose. Continue therapy beyond 16 weeks if patient is not responding within time period. Adolescent HS (from 12 yrs) – at least <30 kg: 80 mg at week 0 followed by 40 mg every other week starting at week 1 via SC inj. May be increased to 40 mg every week or 80 mg every other week. Continue therapy beyond 12 weeks if no improvement within time period. Uveitis (>2 yrs) – ≥30 kg BW: 40 mg every other week in combination with methotrexate; <30 kg BW: 20 mg every other week in combination with methotrexate. Ulcerative colitis (from 5-17 yrs) – ≥40 kg BW: 160 mg at week 0 and 80 mg at week 2. Maintenance: 80 mg every other week or 40 mg every week. <40 kg BW: 80 mg at week 0 and 40 mg at week 2. Maintenance: 40 mg every other week or 20 mg every week.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Moderate to severe heart failure (NYHA class III-IV).
flattened_sections.precautions: Active TB or other severe infections (e.g., sepsis, abscess, and opportunistic infections). Hepatitis B reactivation. Patients with history of recurrent infection or with underlying conditions which may predispose patients. Patients with preexisting or recent onset central (e.g., multiple sclerosis, optic neuritis) or peripheral nervous system demyelinating disease (e.g. Guillain-Barre syndrome). Coadministration of anakinra, abatacept, live vaccines. Infants exposed to adalimumab in utero should not receive live vaccines 5 months following mother’s last inj during pregnancy. Childn <2 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.

Tracheal intubation during rapid sequence induction: 1 mg/kg, then adequate intubation conditions are established within 60 secs; if a dose of 0.6 mg/kg is used, it is recommended to intubate the patient 90 secs after administration. Maintenance: 0.15 mg/kg; in case of long-term inhalational anesthesia, reduce dose to 0.075-0.1 mg/kg. Continuous infusion: 0.6 mg/kg loading dose; once neuromuscular block starts to recover, start administration by infusion (infusion rate adjusted to maintain twitch response at 10% of control twitch height or maintain 1-2 responses to train of four stimulation). Infusion rate to maintain neuromuscular block under IV anesthesia: 0.3-0.6 mg/kg/hr; For inhalation anesthesia: 0.3-0.4 mg/kg/hr. This may vary from patient to patient. Childn: Intubation dose during routine anesthesia and maintenance dose same with adult dose.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not for facilitating tracheal intubation conditions during rapid sequence induction in childn.
flattened_sections.precautions: Ventilatory support is mandatory until adequate spontaneous respiration is restored. History of reactions to other neuromuscular agents (e.g. suxamethonium). categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

In combination with oxaliplatin for metastatic colorectal cancer following failure of irinotecan-containing combination chemotherapy. As monotherapy or in combination with docetaxel for locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer resistant to paclitaxel or anthracycline-containing regimen or after failure or prior anthracycline-containing chemotherapy.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: Metastatic/adjuvant colorectal cancer and metastatic breast cancer: 1,250 mg/m2 twice daily for 2 weeks, followed by 1 week rest period, for 8 cycles. Combination with oxaliplatin for metastatic colorectal cancer: 1,000 mg/m2 twice daily for 2 weeks followed by 1 week rest period; capecitabine 1st dose is given on the evening of day 1 and last dose is given on the morning of day 15. Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 is administered as IV infusion over 2 hrs to be given as a 3-weekly schedule. Premedicate with antiemetic prior to oxaliplatin administration. Combination with docetaxel for metastatic breast cancer: 1,250 mg/m2 twice daily for 2 weeks followed by 1 week rest period. Docetaxel 75 mg/m2 is administered as 1-hr IV infusion on the first day of each 3-week cycle. Premedication prior to docetaxel administration. Renal impairment (CrCl 30-50 mL/min): Reduce to 75% of dose. Swallowed whole with water within 30 mins after a meal.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity to capecitabine, 5-fluorouracil, or fluoropyrimidine. Patients with known dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency. Patients with severe renal (CrCl <30 mL/min) and hepatic impairment; severe leucopenia, neutropenia, or thrombocytopenia. Patients on treatment with sorivudine or related analogues (e.g. brivudine). Pregnancy and lactation.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Concurrent use of oral coumarin-derivative anticoagulant. Patients with or at risk for diarrhea, dehydration, hypocalcemia or hypercalcemia, or other electrolyte disturbances; CAD, nervous system disease, DM, or ophthalmologic complications. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Fertility impairment. Elderly. Childn. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.

flattened_sections.indications: Management of hypertension (HTN) and angina pectoris. Adjunct to standard therapy in symptomatic heart failure.
flattened_sections.dose: HTN: Initially 6.25 mg twice daily, increase after 1-2 weeks to 12.5 mg twice daily. May be further increased at intervals of at least 2 weeks to 50 mg once daily or in divided doses if necessary. Elderly: 12.5 mg once daily. Angina pectoris: Initially 12.5 mg twice daily, increase after 2 days to 25 mg twice daily. Heart failure: Initially 3.125 mg twice daily, taken with food. If tolerated, double the dose after 2 weeks to 6.25 mg twice daily, then increase gradually at intervals of not < 2 weeks. Patients weighing >85 kg: Max 50 mg twice daily; < 65 kg: Max 25 mg twice daily. Monitor patients for 2-3 hrs after initiation and after each dose increase.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Unstable/decompensated heart failure, clinically manifest hepatic impairment, marked fluid retention or overload requiring IV inotropic support, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place), severe bradycardia (<50 bpm, sick sinus syndrome (including SA block), severe hypotension (SBP <85 mmHg), cardiogenic shock, metabolic acidosis, history of bronchospasm or asthma, or other obstructive lung disorders. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Bradycardia, hypotension, heart failure/fluid retention, non-allergic bronchospasm, diabetes and hypoglycemia, PVD, renal function deterioration, hepatic injury, anesthesia and major surgery. Thyrotoxicosis. Phaeochromocytoma. Prinzmetal’s variant angina. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Asthenia, allergy fatigue, fever, hypovolemia, malaise, edema, flu syndrome, pain in extremities.  Heart failure, heart block and bronchospasm. Fatigue and coldness of extremities. Bradycardia, hypotension/postural hypotension, fluid overload, syncope, AV block, palpitation, angina pectoris (including chest pain), cardiac failure, hypertension, peripheral ischemia, tachycardia, bundle branch block, myocardial ischemia, peripheral circulation disturbances (e.g. cold extremities, peripheral vascular disorder, exacerbation of intermittent claudication, Raynaud's phenomenon).
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Clonidine, ciclosporin, digoxin, amiodarone, anesthesia, verapamil, diltiazem. Inhibitors of CYP2D6 (e.g. quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, and propafenone), catecholamine-depleting agents (e.g. reserpine and MAOIs), insulin or oral hypoglycemics.

flattened_sections.indications: Control of hypertension (HTN), cardiac arrhythmias, anxiety and anxiety tachycardia. Management of pheochromocytoma (should only be started in the presence of effective alpha-blocker), angina pectoris, essential tremor, and hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. Adjunctive management of thyrotoxicosis and thyrotoxic crisis. Long-term prophylaxis after recovery from acute myocardial infarction (MI). Prophylaxis of migraine. Prophylaxis of upper gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding in patients with portal HTN.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults – HTN: Initially 40 mg twice or thrice daily, may be increased by 80 mg/day at weekly intervals. Usual dose: 160-320 mg/day. Angina, migraine, and essential tremor: Initially 40 mg twice to thrice daily, may be increased by same amount at weekly intervals. Usual dose for migraine: 80-160 mg/day; for angina and essential tumor: 120-140 mg/day. Arrhythmia, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and thyrotoxicosis: 10-40 mg 3-4 times daily. Portal HTN: 40 mg twice daily, may be increased to 80 mg up to max 160 mg twice daily depending on heart rate response. Pheochromocytoma (used only in the presence of effective alpha-blocker) - Pre-op: 60 mg daily for 3 days. Non-op malignant cases: 30 mg daily. Post-MI: Start treatment between days 5 and 21 after MI, with initial dose of 40 mg 4 times daily for 2-3 days. Total daily dose of 80 mg twice daily may be given in order to improve compliance. Hyperthyroidism: Adjust dose according to clinical response. Severe liver disease: Max 20 mg thrice daily. Childn – Arrhythmias: 250-500 mcg/kg 3-4 times daily. Migraine - Childn >12 yrs: Adult dose; Childn < 12 yrs: 20 mg twice or thrice daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. History of bronchial asthma, bronchospasm, COPD. Inadequately treated cardiac decompensation, severe bradycardia, hypotension; cardiogenic shock; 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree heart block; sick sinus syndrome; uncontrolled heart failure; metabolic acidosis; severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbances; untreated pheochromocytoma; Prinzmetal's angina. Patients at risk of hypoglycemia; asthma.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with poor cardiac reserve, less severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbances, 1<sup>st</sup>-degree heart block, decompensated cirrhosis, hepatic and renal impairment. Concomitant use with hypoglycemic therapy (e.g. insulin) in patients with DM. Concomitant use with CCBs with negative inotropic effects (e.g. diltiazem, verapamil) in patients with impaired ventricular function and/or SA or AV conduction abnormalities. May mask signs of thyrotoxicosis. May induce or aggravate myasthenia gravis. May deteriorate liver function and develop hepatic encephalopathy in patients with portal HTN. Avoid abrupt discontinuation in patients with IHD. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Fatigue and/or lassitude, bradycardia, Raynaud’s phenomenon, sleep disturbances, nightmares; thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, angioedema, hypoglycemia, arthralgia, reduced renal flow, impotence, dizziness; nervous system and psychiatric, eye, CV, respiratory, thoracic, mediastinal, GI, skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Hypoglycemic therapy, rizatriptan, Class I anti-arrhythmic drugs (e.g. disopyramide), amiodarone, digitalis glycosides, CCBs with negative inotropic effects (e.g. verapamil, diltiazem), DHP CCBs (e.g. nifedipine, nisoldipine, nicardipine, isradipine, lacidipine), sympathomimetic agents (e.g. adrenaline), lidocaine, cimetidine, hydralazine, alcohol, clonidine, ergot alkaloids, PG synthetase inhibitors (e.g. ibuprofen and indomethacin), chlorpromazine, anesthetic agents, quinidine, propafenone, rifampicin, theophylline, warfarin, thioridazine.

Patients with severe renal insufficiency: Caution on dosage >10 mg/day. Childn with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: 10 mg once daily in the evening; recommended dosing range is 10-40 mg/day. Max 40 mg/day. The 80 mg dose is only recommended in patients at high risk for cardiovascular complications who have not achieved treatment goals on lower doses and when the benefits are expected to outweigh the potential risks.

brand_info.content: Parenteral nutrition for adults when oral or enteral nutrition is impossible, insufficient, or contraindicated.

brand_info.content: Individualized dosage. Infusion rate < 3 mL/kg/hr (corresponding to 0.21 g glucose, 0.1 g amino acids, 0.08 g fat/kg/hr). Recommended infusion period: 14-24 hrs. See product information for complete instructions for use.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity to any ingredient of the formulation, fish, egg, soya, or peanuts. Hyperlipidemia, severe liver disorder, coagulation disorder, congenital error of amino acid metabolism, severe kidney disease without access to dialysis, acute shock, uncontrolled hyperglycemia, elevated serum levels of the included electrolytes, acute pulmonary edema, hyperhydration, untreated heart failure, hemophagocytic syndrome, unstable conditions (e.g. serious trauma, uncontrolled diabetes, acute heart attack, stroke, blood clot, metabolic acidosis, severe sepsis, coma, hypotonic dehydration). Newborn babies. Childn < 2 yrs.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Use continuous and well-controlled infusion to avoid risks associated with too rapid infusion rates. Strict aseptic precautions should be taken to avoid any contamination, especially during catheter insertion and manipulations. Monitor serum glucose, electrolytes, osmolarity, fluid balance, acid-base status, and liver enzyme test. Should not be given simultaneously with blood in the same infusion set due to the risk of pseudoagglutination. Any sign or symptom of anaphylactic reaction (e.g. fever, shivering, rash, or dyspnea) should lead to immediate interruption of the infusion. The catheter insertion site should be evaluated daily for local signs of thrombophlebitis. Pregnancy and lactation.

brand_info.title: Side Effects
brand_info.content: Thrombophlebitis, slight increase in body temp. High blood (plasma) levels of compounds from the liver, lack of appetite, nausea, vomiting, chills, dizziness, and headache.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of unstable angina pectoris including angina due to coronary artery spasm or following myocardial infarction and hypertension (HTN). Management of chronic stable angina (classic effort-associated angina) in patients who cannot tolerate beta-blocks and/or nitrates or who remain symptomatic. Prevention of graft failure following kidney transplantation. Monotherapy or in combination with antihypertensives for treatment of HTN.
flattened_sections.dose: IHD (exertional angina pectoris due to atherosclerotic coronary artery disease or angina pectoris at rest due to coronary artery spasm): Initially 120 mg/day in divided doses, before meals and at bedtime, increased gradually in divided doses 2-4x daily at 1-2 day interval until optimum response is obtained. Optimum dose: 180-360 mg/day. Max 480 mg/day in some cases. Hypertension: Initially 120-240 mg/day in divided doses, before meals and at bedtime. Usual dose: 240-360 mg/day. Kidney transplantation: Initially 120 mg/day in two divided doses. May be increased to max 360 mg/day in three divided doses depending on patient’s BP. Optimum dose: 180-360 mg/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Sick sinus syndrome and 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block, except in the presence of a functioning ventricular pacemaker. Hypotension (< 90 mmHg systolic). Acute MI. Pulmonary congestion. Concomitant use with lomitapide. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with renal and hepatic impairment; CHF. Cardiac conduction, symptomatic hypotension, acute hepatic injury. Discontinue if dermatological reactions persist. Childn. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, dizziness, 1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block, sinus bradycardia, flushing, nausea, rash, joint swelling, asthenia, fatigue, edema.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Lomitapide, beta-blockers, ivabradine, H2-antagonists, digitalis, anesthetics, ciclosporin, carbamazepine, erythromycin, warfarin, rifampin, lithium, statins, sirolimus, temsirolimus, everolimus.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of candidal vulvovaginitis due to Candida albicans, bacterial vaginitis due to anaerobic bacteria and Gardnerella vaginalis, trichomonal vaginitis due to Trichomonas vaginalis, and mixed vaginal infections.
flattened_sections.dose: Insert 1 suppository in lying position, high into the vagina, at night for 7 days; for recurrent cases, 14 days.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Alcohol use during or within 3 days after treatment. Concomitant use with disulfiram during or within 2 weeks of treatment. flattened_sections.precautions: Do not administer during menstruation. High doses and long-term metronidazole may cause peripheral neuropathy and convulsion. Sexual partners of patients with Trichomonas vaginalis should be treated at the same time. Patients on hemodialysis or with hepatic encephalopathy. Do not use concurrently with contraceptive diaphragms, tampons, douche, or spermicides. May affect ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy (2nd and 3rd trimesters). Pregnancy Risk: Category C.

Treatment of biopsy-confirmed, primary superficial basal cell carcinoma (sBCC) in immunocompetent adults with a maximum tumor diameter of 2 cm, located on the trunk (excluding anogenital skin), neck or extremities (excluding hands and feet). Treatment of external genital and perianal warts/condyloma acuminata in patients >12 yrs.
flattened_sections.dose: Apply to the entire treatment area and rub in until the cream is no longer visible. Actinic keratosis: Apply 2x per week for a full 16 weeks to a defined treatment area on the face or scalp (but not both concurrently), applied prior to normal sleeping hrs and left on the skin for approx 8 hrs, after which time the cream should be removed by washing the area with mild soap and water. sBCC: Apply 5x per week for a full 6 weeks, applied prior to normal sleeping hrs and left on the skin for approximately 8 hrs, after which time the cream should be removed by washing the area with mild soap and water. External genital warts: Apply 3x per week for a max of 16 weeks, applied prior to normal sleeping hrs and left on the skin for 6-10 hrs, after which time the cream should be removed by washing the area with mild soap and water.
flattened_sections.precautions: Pre-existing autoimmune conditions. Skin weeping or erosion. May exacerbate inflammatory conditions of the skin including graft versus host disease. Severe local inflammatory reactions of female external genitalia, severe vulvular swelling. Not recommended until skin is completely healed from any various drug or surgical treatment. Malaise, fever, nausea, myalgias and rigor. Avoid exposure to sunlight (including sunlamps). Not for oral, ophthalmic, or intravaginal use. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Itching, burning, erythema, flaking, scaling, dryness, scabbing/crusting, edema, induration, excoriation, erosion, ulceration. Fatigue, fever and headache.

flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with history of gout, hyperuricemia, urolithiasis, nephrolithiasis, renal impairment. flattened_sections.dose: 0.5 mL SC in the deltoid region of the upper arm or higher anterolateral area of the thigh. Childn 1-12 yrs: Single dose. If the 1st dose is given at 6-12 months of age, another (2nd) dose should be given at >1 yr. 3rd dose can be administered if warranted by official recommendations. At least 1 month should elapse between administration of doses.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Anaphylactoid reaction to neomycin. Malignant neoplasms affecting the bone marrow or lymphatic systems (e.g. blood dyscrasias, leukemia, lymphoma of any type). Immunosuppressive therapy (including high-dose corticosteroids; except those receiving corticosteroids as replacement therapy, e.g. Addison's disease). Primary and acquired immunodeficiency states, including immunosuppressed patients with HIV or AIDS, cellular immune deficiencies, hypogammaglobulinemia and dysgammaglobulinemia. Active untreated TB; active febrile illness (>38.5°C). Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Hypersensitivity to eggs. Patients with history of convulsions, cerebral injury or any other condition in which stress due to fever should be avoided. Individuals with HIV; thrombocytopenia and/or coagulation disorders. Risk of transmission of virus from vaccine recipients to susceptible high-risk individuals which include: Immunocompromised individuals, pregnant women and/or newborn infants of mothers without documented history of chickenpox or laboratory evidence of prior infection. Tuberculin test. Lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: URTI, irritability, diarrhea, vomiting, measles-like rash, rash, varicella-like rash, fever >38.9°C, erythema, pain or tenderness or soreness, swelling (ecchymosis), rash at injection site.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: M-M-R II, Attenuvax, Immune globulins (Ig), varicella zoster immune globulin (VZIG), salicylates.
