categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus infection in adults.
flattened_sections.dose: Patients without cirrhosis and patients with compensated cirrhosis: 1 tab once daily for 12 weeks. Addition of ribavirin may be considered for genotype 3 infected patients with compensated cirrhosis. Patients with decompensated cirrhosis: 1 tab once daily + ribavirin for 12 weeks. Ribavirin dosing guide - Child-Pugh-Turcotte (CPT) Class B cirrhosis pre-transplant: 1,000 mg/day for patients < 75 kg and 1,200 mg for those weighing ≥75 kg. CPT Class C cirrhosis pre-transplant or CPT Class B or C post-transplant: Starting dose of 600 mg, which can be titrated up to a max of 1,000 mg for patients weighing <75 kg and 1,200 mg for patients weighing ≥75 kg if well tolerated. If the starting dose is not well tolerated, the dose should be reduced as clinically indicated based on Hgb levels.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Co-administration with potent P-gp or potent CYP450 inducers.
flattened_sections.precautions: Should not be administered concurrently with other medicinal products containing sofosbuvir. Concomitant use with amiodarone or other medicinal products that lower heart rate. HCV/HBV (hepatitis virus) co-infection. Patients who have previously failed therapy with an NS5A-containing regimen. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) and ESRD requiring hemodialysis. Concomitant use with moderate P-gp inducers and/or moderate CYP inducers (e.g. efavirenz, modafinil, oxcarbazepine or rifapentine). Co-administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with the fixed-dose combination tab containing elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate given in conjunction with a boosted HIV protease inhibitor (e.g. atazanavir or darunavir). Diabetes. CPT class C cirrhosis. Liver transplant patients. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, fatigue, nausea. Rash, angioedema. Liver disease or known toxicity profile of ribavirin in patients receiving treatment in combination with ribavirin. Renal impairment.  Bradycardia and heart block in combination with amiodarone.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Acid-reducing agents (e.g. PPIs), antiarrhythmics (e.g. amiodarone, digoxin), anticoagulants (e.g. dabigatran, vit K antagonists), anticonvulsants (e.g. phenytoin. phenobarbital, carbamazepine, oxcarzepine), antimycobacterials (e.g. rifampicin, rifabutin, rifapentine), HIV antiviral agents (reverse transcriptase inhibitors e.g. tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir). St. John's wort, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (e.g. rosuvastatin).

flattened_sections.indications: Cryptococcosis, including cryptococcal meningitis and infections of other sites (e.g. pulmonary, cutaneous); used as maintenance therapy to prevent relapse of cryptococcal disease in patients with AIDS. Systemic candidiasis, including candidemia, disseminated candidiasis and other forms of invasive candidal infections; Patients with malignancy, in ICU, receiving cytotoxic or immunosuppressive therapy, or with other factors predisposing to candidal infection. Mucosal candidiasis; Prevention of relapse of oropharyngeal candidiasis in patients with AIDS. Genital candidiasis. Vaginal candidiasis, acute or recurrent, and prophylaxis to reduce the incidence of recurrent vaginal candidiasis (three or more episodes a yr). Candidal balanitis. Prevention of fungal infections in patients with malignancy who are predisposed to such infections as a result of cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Dermatomycosis, including tinea pedis, tinea corporis, tinea cruris, tinea versicolor, tinea unguium (onychomycosis), and dermal Candida infections. Deep endemic mycoses in immunocompetent patients, coccidioidomycosis, paracoccidioidomycosis, sporotrichosis and histoplasmosis.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - Cryptococcal meningitis and cryptococcal infections: 400 mg on 1st day followed by 200-400 mg once daily, duration of treatment will depend on clinical and mycological response for cryptococcal infections, at least 6-8 weeks for cryptococcal meningitis. Prevention of relapse of cryptococcal meningitis in patients with AIDS: After receiving full course of primary treatment, may administer a dose of 200 mg once daily. Candidemia, disseminated candidiasis and other forms of invasive candidal infections: 400 mg on 1st day followed by 200 mg once daily, may be increased to 400 mg daily. Oropharyngeal candidiasis: 50-100 mg once daily for 7-14 days, treatment can be continued for longer periods in patients with severely compromised immune function. Atrophic oral candidiasis associated with dentures: 50 mg once daily for 14 days administered concurrently with local antiseptic measures to the denture. Other candidal infections of mucosa except genital candidiasis: 50-100 mg once daily for 14-30 days. Prevention of relapse of oropharyngeal candidiasis in patients with AIDS: After receiving full course of primary treatment, may administer a 150 mg once-weekly dose. Vaginal candidiasis, Candida balanitis: 150 mg single oral dose. Reduce incidence of recurrent vaginal candidiasis: 150 mg once-monthly dose, ranges from 4-12 months. Prevention of candidiasis: 50-400 mg once daily based on patient's risk for developing fungal infection; For patients at high risk of systemic infection (e.g. patients anticipated to have profound or prolonged neutropenia): 400 once daily started days before onset of neutropenia and continued for 7 days until neutrophil counts >1000 cells/mm3. Dermal infections: 150 mg once weekly or 50 mg once daily, for 2-4 weeks, tinea pedis may require treatment for up to 6 weeks. Tinea versicolor: 300-400 mg may be needed in some patients may be sufficient; alternate dosing regimen 50 mg once daily for 2-4 weeks. Tinea unguium: 150 mg once weekly, continue treatment until uninfected nail grows in. Deep endemic mycoses: 200-400 mg once daily for up to 2 yrs may be required (11-24 months for coccidioidomycosis, 2-17 months for paracoccidioidomycosis, 1-16 months for sporotrichosis, 3-17 months for histoplasmosis). Childn - Mucosal candidiasis: 3 mg/kg once daily, loading dose of 6 mg/kg may be used on 1st day. Systemic candidiasis and cryptococcal infections: 6-12 mg/kg once daily. Suppression of relapse of cryptococcal meningitis in childn with AIDS: 6 mg/kg once daily. Prevention of fungal infections in immunocompromised patients at risk as a consequence of neutropenia following cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy: 3-12 mg/kg once daily. Infants <4 weeks old: 1st 2 weeks of life, same mg/kg dosing as childn, administered every 72 hrs, during weeks 3 and 4 of life, same dose given every 48 hrs. Renal impairment: Initial loading dose of 50-400 mg; CrCl ≤50 mL/min and no dialysis: 50% of recommended dose; Hemodialysis: 100% of recommended doses administered after each hemodialysis. IV - Infusion rate: Not exceeding 10 mL/min.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to fluconazole, any of the ingredients, or related azole compounds. Co-administration of terfenadine, other drugs known to prolong QT interval and are metabolized by CYP3A4 (e.g. cisapride, astemizole, erythromycin, pimozide, quinidine).
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with liver and renal dysfunction. Discontinue treatment if signs or symptoms consistent with liver disease develop; patients who develop abnormal liver function tests during therapy should be monitored. Discontinue treatment if rash develops in a patient treated for a superficial fungal infection; patients with invasive/systemic fungal infections who develop rashes should be monitored, discontinue if bullous lesions or erythema multiforme develop. Patients with hypokalemia, advanced cardiac failure, other proarrhythmic conditions, and concomitantly treated with CYP2C9, CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 substrates. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp-lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C for single low dose (150 mg); Category D for high chronic doses (400-800 mg/day).
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache; abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting; increased ALT/AST, blood alkaline phosphatase; rash.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Cisapride, terfenadine, astemizole, pimozide, quinidine, erythromycin; amiodarone; hydrochlorothiazide, rifampicin; alfentanil, amitriptyline, nortriptyline, amphotericin B, anticoagulants, azithromycin, short-acting benzodiazepines, carbamazepine, CCBs, celecoxib, ciclosporin, cyclophosphamide, fentanyl, halofantrine, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, losartan, methadone, NSAIDs, olaparib, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, prednisone, rifabutin, saquinavir, sirolimus, sulfonylureas, tacrolimus, theophylline, tofacitinib, vinca alkaloids, vit A, voriconazole, zidovudine.
flattened_sections.packaging: Capsule 50 mg, 150 mg, 200 mg. Solution for injection (IV) 2 mg/mL x 100 mL.

flattened_sections.indications: IM: Primary, secondary, or acute adrenocortical insufficiency; congenital adrenal hyperplasia; hypercalcemia associated with cancer; non-suppurative thyroiditis. Adjunct therapy for short-term administration in rheumatic disorders. During an exacerbation or as maintenance therapy in selected cases of collagen diseases. Dermatologic diseases. Control of severe or incapacitating allergic conditions intractable to adequate trials of conventional treatment. Severe acute and chronic allergic and inflammatory processes involving the eye. Gastrointestinal, respiratory, hematologic diseases. Palliative management of neoplastic diseases. Induces diuresis or remission of proteinuria in the nephrotic syndrome, without uremia, of the idiopathic type or due to lupus erythematosus. Acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis. Tuberculous meningitis with subarachnoid block or impending block when used concurrently with appropriate anti-tuberculous chemotherapy; trichinosis with neurologic or myocardial involvement. Intra-synovial or soft tissue administration: Adjunctive therapy for short-term administration in rheumatic disorders. Intralesional administration: Keloids, localized hypertrophic, infiltrated, inflammatory lesions of lichen planus, psoriatic plaques, discoid lupus erythematosus, necrobiosis lipoidica diabeticorum, granuloma annulare, lichen simplex chronicus (neurodermatitis) alopecia areata; may also be useful in cystic tumors or an aponeurosis or tendon (ganglia). Intrarectal administration: Ulcerative colitis.
flattened_sections.dose: Rheumatoid and osteoarthritis (Intra-articular injection) - Large joints: 20-80 mg; Medium joints: 10-40 mg; Small joints: 4-10 mg. In chronic cases may be repeated at intervals ranging from 1 to 5, or more weeks depending upon the degree of relief from initial injection. Ganglion, tendinitis or tenosynovitis, epicondylitis: 4-30 mg. Local effect in dermatologic conditions: 20-60 mg injected into the lesion; Large lesions: Distribute doses from 20-40 mg by repeated local injection. Patients with adrenogenital syndrome: Single dose 40 mg IM injection every 2 weeks. Maintenance of patients with rheumatoid arthritis: 40-120 mg weekly IM injection. Dermatologic lesions benefited by systemic corticoid therapy: 40-120 mg IM injection at weekly intervals for 1-4 weeks. Acute severe dermatitis: Single dose 80-120 mg IM injection, relief may result within 8-12 hrs. Chronic contact dermatitis: Repeated injection at 5- to 10-day intervals. Seborrheic dermatitis: Weekly dose of 80 mg. Asthmatic patients: Following IM injection of 80-120 mg, relief may result within 6-48 hrs for several days to 2 weeks. Patients with allergic rhinitis (hay fever): 80-120 mg IM injection followed by relief of coryzal symptoms within 6 hrs for several days to 3 weeks. Adjunct in treatment of some patients with ulcerative colitis (Intrarectal injection): 40-120 mg as retention enemas or by continuous drip 3-7 times weekly for periods of 2 or more weeks.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Systemic fungal infections. For use by intrathecal, epidural and IV routes of administration. Administration of live attenuated vaccine in patients receiving immunosuppressive doses of corticosteroids. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Dermal/subdermal changes may form depressions at injection site. Precaution in intra-synovial and IM injection against injection or leakage into the dermis. Septic arthritis. Avoid local injection of steroid into previously infected joints or unstable joints. Increase susceptibility or mask signs of infection and new infections, decrease resistance and inability to localize infection. Do not use intra-synovial, intrabursal or intratendinous administration for local effect in presence of acute infection. Use of corticosteroids in active TB should be restricted to those cases of fulminating or disseminated TB. Monitor patients with latent TB or tuberculin reactivity, during prolonged corticosteroid therapy, these patients should receive chemoprophylaxis. Kaposi’s sarcoma. Septic shock. Allergic reactions. Prolonged periods may result in HPA suppression. Acute adrenal and drug-induced secondary adrenocortical insufficiencies. Steroid "withdrawal syndrome". Patients with Cushing’s disease, hypothyroidism, pre-existing diabetes, psychic derangements, seizure disorders, myasthenia gravis, epidural lipomatosis in long-term use at high doses. Prolonged use may produce posterior subcapsular cataracts and nuclear cataracts (in childn), exophthalmos, or increased IOP, ocular herpes simplex (possible corneal perforation), central serous chorioretinopathy. Existing CV risk factors, patients who have or may be predisposed to thromboembolic disorders, HTN. GI ulcers, non-specific ulcerative colitis, diverticulitis, fresh intestinal anastomoses, active or latent peptic ulcer. Hepatobiliary disorders. Patients with disorders of neuromuscular transmission or in patients receiving concomitant therapy with anticholinergics, osteoporosis. Renal insufficiency. Elevation of BP, salt and water retention, and increased excretion of potassium. Should not be used to treat traumatic brain injury. Pheochromocytoma crisis. Intracranial pressure and pancreatitis in childn and infants in high doses. Should not drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Intrathecal/epidural: Arachnoiditis, functional GI disorders/bladder dysfunction, headache, meningitis, paraparesis/paraplegia, seizure, sensory disturbance.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. isoniazid, aprepitant, fosaprepitant, antifungals, protease inhibitors, diltiazem, oral contraceptives, ciclosporin, macrolide antibiotics, grapefruit juice. CYP3A4 inducers e.g. rifampin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin. Neuromuscular blockers, anticholinesterases, antidiabetics, aminoglutethimide, aspirin, potassium-depleting agents.
flattened_sections.packaging: Sterile aqueous suspension for injection 40 mg/mL.

flattened_sections.dose: Nosocomial pneumonia, CAP including concurrent bacteremia, complicated skin and skin structure infections – Adults and adolescents >12 yrs: 600 mg IV or oral every 12 hrs for 10-14 days. Childn from birth to 11 yrs: 10 mg/kg IV or oral every 8 hrs for 10-14 days. Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium infections, including concurrent bacteremia – Adults and adolescents >12yrs: 600 mg IV or oral every 12 hrs for 14-28 days. Childn from birth to 11 yrs: 10 mg/kg IV or oral every 8 hrs for 14-28 days. Uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections – Adults and adolescents >12 yrs: 400 mg (adults) or 600 mg (adolescents) orally every 12 hrs for 10-14 days. Childn 5-11 yrs: 10 mg/kg orally every 12 hrs; <5 yrs: 10 mg/kg orally 8 hrs for 10-14 days.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients taking MAO-A and B inhibitors or within 2 weeks of taking such products; sympathomimetics, vasopressive agents, dopaminergics, SSRIs, TCAs, triptans, meperidine, bupropion, busipirone.
flattened_sections.precautions: Monitor CBC in patients who received linezolid for >2 weeks. Thrombocytopenia in patients with severe renal impairment whether or not on dialysis, and in patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment, drugs that produce bone marrow suppression, and those with chronic infections. Monitor visual function in patients taking linezolid for ≥3 months, who experience visual impairment (e.g. changes in visual acuity, color vision, blurred vision, or visual field defect). Patients with carcinoid syndrome; uncontrolled HTN, pheochromocytoma, thyrotoxicosis. Should not be with catheter-related bloodstream infection or catheter-site infection, G(-) infections. C. difficile-associated diarrhea. Lactic acidosis. Hypoglycemia in patients with DM receiving insulin or oral hypoglycemic agents. Monitor serum sodium levels in elderly, patients taking diuretics; risk of hyponatremia or SIADH. Patients with phenylketonuria. Increase the risk development of drug resistant bacteria. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, rash, anemia, taste alteration, vaginal moniliasis, oral moniliasis, abnormal liver function tests, fungal infection, tongue discoloration, localized abdominal pain, generalized abdominal pain. Incompatibilities: Amphotericin B, chlorpromazine HCl, diazepam, pentamidine isothionate, erythromycin lactobionate, phenytoin sodium, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole; ceftriaxone sodium (IV).

categories.title: A

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus, particularly in overweight patients when dietary management and exercise alone does not result in adequate glycemic control.
flattened_sections.dose: Initially, 500 mg or 750 mg once daily with evening meal. Initial dose should be equivalent to the daily dose of immediate release tab. After 10-15 days, adjust dose based on blood glucose measurements. Max recommended dose - 1 g: 2 tabs. 750 mg: 3 tabs. 500 mg: 4 tabs. Doses to be taken once daily with evening meal. If glycemic control is not achieved on four 500 mg tabs once daily, consider two 500 mg tabs twice daily with breakfast and evening meal. If glycemic control is not achieved on three 750 mg tabs once daily, consider one 750 mg tab with breakfast and two tabs with evening meal. If glycemic control is not achieved on two 1 g tabs once daily, consider 1 tab during breakfast and 1 tab during evening meal.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe destabilization of diabetes (ketoacidosis or precoma); renal and hepatic insufficiency; severe infection; dehydration due to persistent or severe diarrhea, recurrent vomiting; conditions at risk for tissue hypoxia (heart failure, recent MI, respiratory insufficiency, shock). Lactation.

In combination with docetaxel, treatment for locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after failure of cytotoxic chemotherapy. Adjuvant treatment of patients with colon cancer. Treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer. 1<sup>st</sup>-line treatment of patients with advanced esophagogastric cancer. In combination with oxaliplatin, adjuvant treatment following complete resection of stage II and stage III gastric adenocarcinoma.
flattened_sections.dose: Monotherapy in colon, colorectal and breast cancer: 1,250 mg/m2 2x daily for 2 weeks followed by a 7-day rest period. Combination therapy for breast cancer: 1,250 mg/m2 2x daily for 2 weeks followed by a 7-day rest period, combined with docetaxel at 75 mg/m2 as a 1 hr IV infusion every 3 weeks. Combination therapy (except irinotecan) for colon, colorectal, gastric cancer and esophagogastric cancer: 800-1000 mg/m2 2x daily for 2 weeks followed by a 7-day rest period, or to 625 mg/m2 2x daily when administered continuously; Combination therapy with irinotecan: 800 mg/m2 2x daily for 2 weeks followed by a 7-day rest period, combined with irinotecan 200 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. 6 months adjuvant treatment for stage III colon cancer. Start premedication in combination therapy prior to docetaxel, cisplatin, or oxaliplatin. Should be swallowed with water within 30 mins after meal. Patients with moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30-50 mL/min): Dose reduction to 75% of 1250 mg/m2. See product insert for dose reductions based on BSA and toxicity.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with history of hypersensitivity to fluorouracil; known dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency; severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Concomitant use with sorivudine or its chemically related analogues (e.g.brivudine). Neutrophil counts < 1.5 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L and/or thrombocyte < 100 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with renal and hepatic impairment; severe diarrhea; anorexia, asthenia, nausea, vomiting; history of CAD. Avoid and manage dehydration. May induce SJS and TEN; Grade 1-3 hand-foot syndrome; hyperbilirubinemia. Concomitant use of vit B6 for symptomatic or secondary prophylactic treatment for hand-foot syndrome and oral coumarin anticoagulant. Discontinue treatment if CrCl decreases to < 30 mL/min, bilirubin >3 x ULN or AST and ALT >2.5 x ULN. Childn. Elderly ≥60 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.

Fatigue, lethargy, pyrexia, weakness, asthenia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Coumarin anticoagulants, CYP450 2C9 substrates, phenytoin, antacid, leucovorin, sorivudine and analogues, oxaliplatin, bevacizumab.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of Parkinson's disease and syndrome; manage associated tremor, dysphagia, sialorrhea, and postural instability; relieve many symptoms of parkinsonism (e.g. rigidity and bradykinesia). Alternative to levodopa when signs and symptoms of Parkinson’s disease are not evenly controlled throughout the day. Treatment of patients with Parkinsonism who are taking vitamin preparations containing vit B<sub>6</sub>.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - Initial dose: 1 tab of 100 mg/25 mg 3x daily, may be increased by 1 tab every day or every other day. Max 8 tabs/day. Alternatively, a starting dose of 1 tab of 250 mg/25 mg once daily may be used, can be increased using a combination of 100 mg/125 mg and 250 mg/125 mg tabs until optimal response is reached. From levodopa: Discontinue levodopa at least 12 or 24 hrs for slow preparations, prior to initiation of therapy. Give approximately 20% of previous levodopa daily dose; < 1,500 mg levodopa/day: 1 tab of 100 mg/25 mg 3-4x daily; >1,500 mg levodopa/day: 1 tab of 250 mg/25 mg 3-4x daily. Maintenance: Individualized dosage. At least 70-100 mg of carbidopa/day. When more levodopa is required, 250 mg/25 mg tab should be substituted for 100 mg/25 mg tab, then may increase by 1 tab every day or every other day. Max 8 tabs daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with narrow-angle glaucoma, suspicious undiagnosed skin lesion, or history of melanoma. Concomitant use with MAOIs.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not for drug-induced EPS. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with past or current psychoses; severe CV or pulmonary disease, bronchial asthma, renal, hepatic, or endocrine disease, history of PUD, MI who have residual atrial, nodal, or ventricular arrhythmia; chronic wide-angle glaucoma; Concomitant use with psychoactive drugs. Dyskinesia, involuntary movements and mental disturbances, somnolence and sudden sleep onset, melanoma, impulse control disorders. Evaluate hepatic, hematopoietic, CV, and renal function periodically. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.

flattened_sections.indications: Threatened and habitual miscarriage, dysmenorrhea, endometriosis, secondary amenorrhea, irregular cycles, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, pre-menstrual syndrome (PMS), infertility due to luteal insufficiency. Luteal support as part of an Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) treatment. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) for women with disorders due to natural or surgical-induced menopause with an intact uterus.
flattened_sections.dose: Threatened miscarriage: 40 mg at once, then 20 or 30 mg daily until symptoms remit. Habitual miscarriage: 10 mg twice daily until the 12th week of pregnancy. Dysmenorrhea: 10 or 20 mg daily from day 5-25 of the cycle. Endometriosis: 10-30 mg daily from day 5-25 of the cycle or continuously. Secondary amenorrhea: 10 or 20 mg daily for 14 days during the 2nd half of the theoretical menstrual cycle. Irregular cycles: 10 or 20 mg daily starting with the 2nd half of the menstrual cycle until the 1st day of the next cycle. Dysfunctional uterine bleeding - To arrest bleeding: 20 or 30 mg daily for up to 10 days. To prevent bleeding: 10 or 20 mg during the 2nd half of the menstrual cycle. PMS: 10 mg twice daily starting with the 2nd half of the menstrual cycle until the 1st day of the next cycle. Infertility due to luteal insufficiency: 10 or 20 mg daily starting with the 2nd half of the menstrual cycle until the 1st day of the next cycle. Luteal support as part of ART treatment: 1 tab of 10 mg thrice daily (30 mg daily) starting at the day of oocyte retrieval and continuing for 10 weeks if pregnancy is confirmed. HRT - Continuous sequential therapy: An estrogen is dosed continuously and 1 tab of 10 mg dydrogesterone is added for the last 14 days of every 28-day cycle. Cyclic therapy: When an estrogen is dosed cyclically with a treatment-free interval, usually 21 days on and 7 days off. 1 tab of 10 mg dydrogesterone is added for the last 12-14 days of estrogen therapy. Depending on the clinical response, the dosage can subsequently be adjusted to 20 mg/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Known or suspected progestogen-dependent neoplasms, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Treatment for luteal support as part of an ART treatment should be discontinued upon diagnosis of abortion or miscarriage. Use in combination with estrogen. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Breakthrough bleeding or spotting. Porphyria, depression, abnormal liver function values caused by acute or chronic liver disease. brand_info.title: Indications
brand_info.content: Threatened and habitual miscarriage, dysmenorrhea, endometriosis, secondary amenorrhea, irregular cycles, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, pre-menstrual syndrome (PMS), infertility due to luteal insufficiency. Luteal support as part of an Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) treatment. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) for women with disorders due to natural or surgical-induced menopause with an intact uterus.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: Threatened miscarriage: 40 mg at once, then 20 or 30 mg daily until symptoms remit. Habitual miscarriage: 10 mg twice daily until the 12th week of pregnancy. Dysmenorrhea: 10 or 20 mg daily from day 5-25 of the cycle. Endometriosis: 10-30 mg daily from day 5-25 of the cycle or continuously. Secondary amenorrhea: 10 or 20 mg daily for 14 days during the 2nd half of the theoretical menstrual cycle. Irregular cycles: 10 or 20 mg daily starting with the 2nd half of the menstrual cycle until the 1st day of the next cycle. Dysfunctional uterine bleeding - To arrest bleeding: 20 or 30 mg daily for up to 10 days. To prevent bleeding: 10 or 20 mg during the 2nd half of the menstrual cycle. PMS: 10 mg twice daily starting with the 2nd half of the menstrual cycle until the 1st day of the next cycle. Infertility due to luteal insufficiency: 10 or 20 mg daily starting with the 2nd half of the menstrual cycle until the 1st day of the next cycle. Luteal support as part of ART treatment: 1 tab of 10 mg thrice daily (30 mg daily) starting at the day of oocyte retrieval and continuing for 10 weeks if pregnancy is confirmed. HRT - Continuous sequential therapy: An estrogen is dosed continuously and 1 tab of 10 mg dydrogesterone is added for the last 14 days of every 28-day cycle. Cyclic therapy: When an estrogen is dosed cyclically with a treatment-free interval, usually 21 days on and 7 days off. 1 tab of 10 mg dydrogesterone is added for the last 12-14 days of estrogen therapy. Depending on the clinical response, the dosage can subsequently be adjusted to 20 mg/day.

brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Known or suspected progestogen-dependent neoplasms, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Treatment for luteal support as part of an ART treatment should be discontinued upon diagnosis of abortion or miscarriage. Use in combination with estrogen. Lactation.

categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

indication_long: Treatment of cryptococcal meningitis, coccidi...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of cryptococcal meningitis, coccidiomycosis, invasive candidiasis, mucosal candidiasis, including oropharyngeal, esophageal candidiasis, candiduria, and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, chronic oral atrophic candidiasis (denture soft mouth). Prophylaxis of relapse of cryptococcal meningitis in patients with high risk of recurrence, oropharyngeal or esophageal candidiasis in patients infected with HIV who are at high risk of experiencing relapse, candidal infections in patients with prolonged neutropenia.
flattened_sections.dose: Invasive candidiasis- Candidaemia: 400-800 mg for 2 weeks. Oropharyngeal candidiasis: Initial dose of 200-400 mg followed by 100-200 mg daily for 7-21 days. Esophageal candidiasis: Initial dose of 200-400 mg followed by 100-200 mg daily for 14-30 days. Candiduria: 200-400 mg daily for 7-21 days. Chronic atrophic candidiasis: Initial dose of 200-400 mg followed by 50-100 mg daily for 14 days. Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis: 50-100 mg daily up to 28 days. Prevention of relapse in patients infected with HIV who are at high risk of relapse: 100-200 mg or 200 mg 3x weekly. Treatment of cryptococcal meningitis: Initial dose of 400 mg followed by 200-400 mg daily for 6-8 weeks. Maintenance therapy to prevent relapse in patients with high risk of recurrence: 200 mg daily. Childn: Max dose 400 mg daily. Mucosal candidiasis: Loading dose of 6 mg/kg followed by 3 mg/kg daily. Invasive candidiasis and cryptococcal meningitis: 6-12mg/kg daily. Maintenance therapy (prevent relapse) of Cryptococcal meningitis in childn with high-risk recurrence: 6 mg/kg daily. Prophylaxis of Candida in immunocompromised patients: 3-12 mg/kg daily. Infants <2 weeks: Max 12 mg/kg every 72 hrs. 3-4 weeks: 12 mg/kg- every 48 hrs.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Co-administration of terfenadine, cisapride, astemizole, pimozide, quinidine, and erythromycin.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with tinea capitis, cryptococcosis, deep endemic mycoses, renal or hepatic dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, and potentially proarrhythmic conditions. Concomitant use of halofantrine. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, rash, elevated alkaline phosphatase, ASAT and ALAT.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Amiodarone, rifampicin, HCTZ, alfentanil, amitriptyline, notriptyline, amphotericin B, anticoagulants, carbamazepine, CCBs, celecoxib, cyclophosphamide, fentanyl, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, ibrutinib, ivacaftor, olaparib, ciclosporin, everolimus, sirolimus, tacrolimus, losartan, lurasidone, methadone, NSAIDs, phenytoin, prednisone, rifabutin, saquinavir.
flattened_sections.packaging: Solution for intravenous infusion 200 mg/100 mL (P2,377.76).

flattened_sections.indications: Initial therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) to improve glycemic control when diet and exercise do not provide adequate glycemic control. Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with inadequately controlled type 2 DM: on metformin or sitagliptin (alone or in combination); as part of triple combination therapy with a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist (i.e. thiazolidinediones); or in combination with insulin.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosage. Max recommended daily dose: 100 mg sitagliptin. Initial therapy: 50 mg/500 mg twice daily, may be titrated up to 50 mg/1 g twice daily. Patients with inadequately controlled DM on metformin monotherapy: Sitagliptin 50 mg twice daily plus the dose of metformin already being taken; on sitagliptin monotherapy: 50 mg/500 mg twice daily, may be increased up to 50 mg/1 g twice daily; as part of dual combination therapy with sitagliptin, metformin, or PPAR-gamma agonist, or sulfonylurea, or insulin: Sitagliptin 50 mg twice daily plus metformin dose based on glycemic control and current metformin dose (if any) being taken. Consider gradual dose escalation to reduce GI side effects. Patients currently on or initiating a sulfonylurea or insulin doses may require lower doses of sulfonylurea or insulin to reduce risk of hypoglycemia. Switching from co-administered sitagliptin with metformin: May be initiated at the dose of sitagliptin and metformin already being taken.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), acute or chronic metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis, with or without coma.
flattened_sections.precautions: Type 1 DM, treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis, acute pancreatitis. Assess renal function prior to initiation of therapy and at least annually after. Hypoglycemia in combination with a sulfonylurea or with insulin; in patients with deficient caloric intake, or during concomitant use with other glucose-lowering agents (e.g. sulfonylureas, and insulin) or ethanol, elderly, debilitated or malnourished, and those with adrenal or pituitary insufficiency or alcohol intoxication. Bullous pemphigoid. Lactic acidosis, patients with unstable or acute CHF who are at risk of hypoperfusion and hypoxemia, renal dysfunction, excessive alcohol intake. Temporarily discontinue treatment prior to any surgical procedure until the patient’s resumption of oral intake or in patients undergoing radiologic studies involving intravascular administration or iodinated contrast imaging with an eGFR ≥30-<60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>, with a history of hepatic impairment, alcoholism or heart failure, or in patients who will be administered intra-arterial iodinated contrast. Hypoxic states. Impaired hepatic function. Routinely monitor vitamin B<sub>12</sub> levels at 2-3-yrs intervals. Evaluate serum electrolytes and ketones, blood glucose, blood pH, lactate, pyruvate, and metformin levels. Exposure to stress (e.g. fever, trauma, infection, or surgery). Childn <18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hypoglycemia, diarrhea, nausea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, headache, abdominal pain, constipation, URTI, cough, fungal skin infection, peripheral edema, asthenia, indigestion, hypersensitivity reactions.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Furosemide, nifedipine. OCT2 or multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) inhibitors e.g. ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine. Thiazides and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, CCBs, isoniazid.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

indication_long: 1st line treatment of hypertension...

flattened_sections.indications: 1<sup>st</sup> line treatment of hypertension (HTN) and can be used as sole agent to control BP in the majority of patients. Reduce risk of coronary revascularization procedures and need for hospitalization due to angina in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). 1<sup>st</sup> line treatment of myocardial ischemia, whether due to fixed obstruction (stable angina) and/or vasospasm/vasoconstriction (Prinzmetal’s or variant angina) of coronary vasculature; may be used alone or in combination with other anti-anginal drugs for angina refractory to nitrates and/or adequate doses of beta-blockers. As adjunct to diet for treatment of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and triglycerides and to increase HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous familial and nonfamilial hypercholesterolemia), combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia (Fredrickson Types IIa and IIb), elevated triglyceride levels (Fredrickson Type IV), and in patients with dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson Type III) who do not respond adequately to diet.
flattened_sections.dose: 5 mg/10 mg to a max of 10 mg/20 mg once daily. Starting and maintenance dose should be individualized in the treatment of HTN/angina and dyslipidemia. Doses may be taken at any time of day with or without food. Concomitant administration of atorvastatin with cyclosporine, telaprevir, tipranavir/ritonavir, or glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: Atorvastatin should not exceed 10 mg. Childn 6-17 yrs – HTN: Amlodipine 2.5-5 mg once daily. Childn ≥10 yrs – Severe dyslipidemias: Atorvastatin 10 mg/day, may be increased to 80 mg based on response and tolerability.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to dihydropyridines, amlodipine, atorvastatin or any ingredient in the product. Patients with active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases >3x ULN. Women of childbearing potential who are not using adequate contraceptive measures. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Concomitant administration of atorvastatin with letermovir and cycloporin. Risk for pulmonary edema in patients with NYHA class III-IV heart failure, serum transaminases elevations of >3x ULN. Liver function tests should be performed before the initiation of treatment and periodically thereafter. Patients who consume substantial quantities of alcohol and/or have history of liver disease. Patients with risk factor predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis Risk for myopathy; hemorrhagic stroke in patients who had stroke or TIA in past 6 months; increased HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels. Concurrent administration of cyclosporine, fibric acid derivatives, erythromycin, niacin, azole antifungals, colchicine, telaprevir, boceprevir or the combination of tipranavir/ritonavir. Temporary suspend atorvastatin during fusidic acid therapy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea. Amlodipine: Headaches, dizziness, somnolence, palpitations, flushing, abdominal pain, edema, fatigue. Atorvastatin: Nasopharyngitis, pharyngolaryngeal pain, epistaxis, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, arthralgia, pain in extremities, musculoskeletal pain/spasms, joint swelling.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Amlodipine: CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir), clarithromycin, CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, Hypercicum perforatum), mTOR inhibitors (e.g. sirolimus, temsirolimus, everolimus), tacrolimus. Atorvastatin: Fibric acid derivatives, lipid-modifying doses of niacin, CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. erythromycin, clarithromycin, azole antifungals) and inducers (e.g. efavirenz, rifampin), OATP1B1 inhibitors (e.g., cyclosporine), protease inhibitors, glecaprevir, pibrentasvir, letermovir, elbasvir, grazoprevir, diltiazem, itraconazole, grapefruit juice, antacids containing magnesium and aluminum hydroxides, colestipol, digoxin, oral contraceptives containing norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol, fusidic acid, colchicine.

flattened_sections.indications: Infections caused by susceptible microorganisms e.g. skin and skin structure infections; bone and joint infections; genitourinary tract infections (e.g. acute prostatitis); respiratory tract infections (e.g. acute and chronic bronchitis and infected bronchiectasis); ears, nose, and throat infections (e.g. otitis media, mastoiditis, sinusitis, follicular tonsillitis, and pharyngitis); dental infections.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults: 250 mg every 6 hrs. Max 4 g daily. Streptococcal pharyngitis, skin and skin structure infections, uncomplicated cystitis (patients >15 yrs): 500 mg every 12 hrs. Duration of treatments - Mild to moderate infections: 5-7 days; Cystitis: 7-14 days; Beta-hemolytic streptococcal infections: At least 10 days. Renal impairment - CrCl 11-40 mL/min: 500 mg every 8-12 hrs; 5-10 mL/min: 250 mg every 12 hrs; <5 mL/min: 250 mg every 12-24 hrs; Patients receiving intermittent dialysis: 500 mg after each dialysis. Total dose of 1 g on that day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Penicillin-sensitive patients. Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea and colitis, seizures, renal or hepatic impairment. Monitoring prothrombin time in at-risk patients and exogenous vit K administration are recommended. Periodic assessment of organ system functions is recommended during prolonged therapy. Long-term or repeated use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms e.g. fungi. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.
flattened_sections.side_effects: GI disorders; dermatologic and hypersensitivity reactions; hematologic, renal, genitourinary, and hepatic disorders; nervous system disorders; arthralgia, myalgia, arthritis, joint disorder, back pain, nuchal swelling, cardiac arrhythmia, vasodilation, dyspnea, superinfection, elevated cholesterol.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Alcohol, probenecid, estrogens or progestins, metformin, aminoglycosides, colistin, polymyxin B, vancomycin, diuretics e.g. furosemide. False positive with Benedict’s and Fehling’s solutions, Coombs' test, and Clinitest.

indication_long: Sexually transmitted diseases (STD), urinary ...

flattened_sections.indications: Sexually transmitted diseases (STD), urinary tract infections (UTI), respiratory tract infections (RTI), gastrointestinal tract (GIT) infections, systemic infections, infections caused by E. coli, Enterobacter aerogenes, Shigella spp. and Acinetobacter spp.; as alternative to penicillin for uncomplicated gonorrhea, syphilis, yaws, listeriosis, anthrax, Vincent's infection, actinomycosis infections caused by Clostridium spp. Adjunctive therapy in acute intestinal amebiasis, severe acne, refractory periodontitis and periodontal abscess. Prophylaxis of malaria.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults: 100 mg every 12 hrs on 1st day. Maintenance 100 mg/day once daily. Management of more severe infections (chronic UTI): 100 mg every 12 hrs. STD (Chlamydial cervicitis): 100 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. Early syphilis for non-pregnant patients allergic to penicillin: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 14 days. Syphilis of >1 yr duration in patients allergic to penicillin: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 4 weeks. Uncomplicated gonococcal infections: 100 mg every 12 hrs or 300 mg immediately followed in 1 hr by a second 300 mg. Duration: 7 days. Uncomplicated urethral, endocervical, or rectal infection, non-gonococcal urethritis: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. Acute epididymo-orchitis: 100 mg every 12 hrs for at least 10 days. Acne vulgaris: 100 mg once daily for 12 weeks. Traveler's diarrhea: 200 mg (as single dose or 100 mg every 12 hrs) on the 1st day of travel followed by 100 mg daily throughout stay in the area. Cholera: 300 mg as single dose (treatment and prophylaxis). Leptospirosis – Treatment: 100 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days; Prophylaxis: 200 mg on weekly basis throughout stay in the area and 200 mg upon completion of the trip. Tick and louse-borne relapsing fevers and louse-borne typhus: Single dose of 100 or 200 mg depending on severity. Prophylaxis of scrub typhus: 200 mg as single dose. Malaria – Treatment of chloroquine-resistant of falciparum malaria: 200 mg daily for at least 7 days; Prophylaxis: 100 mg daily 1-2 days before travel to malarious areas, continue daily during travel in these areas and 4 weeks after leaving said areas. Refractory periodontitis in adults and periodontal abscess (if allergic to beta-lactam): 100 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Myasthenia gravis. SLE. Infants and childn <8 yrs (except for use as an alternative treatment for inhalational anthrax post-exposure). Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: May cause permanent teeth discoloration, esophageal irritation and ulceration, increase in BUN, photosensitivity, tissue hyperpigmentation, autoimmune syndromes, bulging fontanelles in infants, porphyria, superinfections; Fanconi-like syndrome, lupus erythematosus-like syndrome with use of deteriorated tetracyclines. C. difficile-associated diarrhea. Patients with obstructive esophagic pathology. Avoid exposure to direct sunlight during treatment. Use for treatment of venereal disease. Hepatic impairment. Periodic assessment of organ system functions is recommended during prolonged therapy. Long-term or repeated use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms e.g. fungi. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Diarrhea and other GI disorders; dermatologic disorders and hypersensitivity reactions; hepatobiliary, renal, hematologic, musculoskeletal, and nervous system disorders; bronchospasm, candidiasis, vulvovaginitis, conjunctivitis, papilledema/periorbital edema, myopia, hearing loss, permanent discoloration of the cornea; tissue hyperpigmentation of the skin, conjunctiva, oral mucosa, tongue, thyroid; Jarish-Herxheimer reaction, ocular inflammation.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Anticoagulants, aminoglycosides, penicillins, atovaquone, alcohol, barbiturates, carbamazepine, primidone, rifampicin, phenytoin, ciclosporin, ergot alkaloids (e. g. methysergide), methotrexate, live vaccines, methoxyflurane, oral contraceptives, oral retinoids, bismuth subsalicylate, PPIs, antacids, colestipol, cholestyramine, kaolin-pectin, sucralfate, disodium hydrogen edetate, sodium bicarbonate, sodium lactate, acetazolamide, ethoxzolamide, strontium ranelate, digoxin, halofantrine, lithium, theophylline. False negative in urine glucose tests using glucose oxidase reagents (e.g. Clinstix, Tes-tape). False elevations in catecholamine levels with fluorescence test.

flattened_sections.indications: Cryptococcosis. Systemic, mucosal, and genital candidiasis. Deep endemic mycoses. Superficial fungal infections. Prophylaxis of transplant patients. Patients with malignancy who are receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy. Immunosuppressive and radiation therapy. Prophylaxis of HIV or AIDS in patients who are at risk of developing Candida infections and serious fungal infections.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - Cryptococcal meningitis and other cryptococcal infections: 400 mg on 1st day, then 200-400 mg once daily for 6-8 weeks up to 10-12 weeks. Oropharyngeal candidiasis: 50-100 mg once daily for 7-14 days. Denture-associated atrophic oral candidiasis: 50 mg once daily for 14 days. flattened_sections.dose: General surgical cases: 1-1.5 g every 6-8 hrs. Prostatectomy: 1-1.5 g every 6-8 hrs until macroscopic hematuria is no longer present. Menorrhagia/menometrorrhagia: 1-1.5 g every 6-8 hrs for 3-4 days. Postpartum hemorrhage: 1-1.5 g (25 mg/kg) every 6-8 hrs. Conization of the cervix: 1.5 g every 8 hrs for 12-14 days after surgery. Epistaxis: 1.5 g every 8 hrs for 4-10 days. Gastrointestinal hemorrhage: 1.5 g every 6 hrs for max of 4 days. Hematuria: 1-1.5 g every 8-12 hrs daily until macroscopic hematuria is no longer present. Hereditary angioneurotic edema: 1-1.5 g every 8-12 hrs as intermittent or continuous treatment depending on the prodromal symptoms of the patient. Dental surgery in patients with coagulopathies: 1-1.5 g (25 mg/kg) every 6-8 hrs for 6-8 days after surgery. Childn: 25 mg/kg/dose twice or thrice daily, depending on the indication. Renal insufficiency - Serum creatinine >5.66 mg/dL: 15 mg/kg every 48 hrs or 7.5 mg/kg every 24 hrs; 2.83-5.66 mg/dL: 15 mg/kg once daily; 1.36-2.83 mg/dL: 15 mg/kg twice daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active or history of thromboembolic disease. Patients receiving thrombin, with acquired disturbances of color vision, subarachnoid hemorrhage.
flattened_sections.precautions: Perform ophthalmological examination before and at regular intervals (prolonged treatment). Renal insufficiency. Hematuria caused by disease of renal parenchyma, urinary tract obstruction due to clot formation from severe bleeding in upper urinary tract, high risk for thrombosis, concomitant use of hormonal contraceptives, disseminated intravascular coagulation, irregular menstrual bleeding, indissoluble clots in body cavities. Women taking either factor IX complex or anti-inhibitor coagulant concentrates. Cerebral edema and cerebral infarction in women with subarachnoid hemorrhage, acute promyelocytic leukemia treated with all-trans retinoic acid. Convulsion. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Childn and elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.

flattened_sections.indications: Induction of ovulation in patients with persistent ovulatory dysfunction who desire pregnancy. In conjunction with gonadotropins and in vitro fertilization programs. Treatment of male infertility due to oligospermia to stimulate gonadotropin release and enhance spermatogenesis.
flattened_sections.dose: 1st course: 50 mg once daily for 5 days. Treatment may be started at any time in patients who have had no recent uterine bleeding. If progestin-induced bleeding is planned or spontaneous bleeding occurs prior to therapy, start at about the 5th day of menstrual cycle. If ovulation do not occur, 2nd course: 100 mg (two 50 mg tabs) once daily for 5 days. Start as early as 30 days after previous course. Do not increase dose or duration beyond 100 mg/day for 5 days.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or history of liver dysfunction. Hormone-dependent tumors or abnormal uterine bleeding of undetermined origin. Uncontrolled thyroid or adrenal dysfunction. Pituitary or ovarian tumors. Ovarian cysts (other than in association with PCOS) and pre-existing endometriosis. Childn and elderly. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: May cause ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, occasional abdominal ovarian enlargement, PCOS, ovarian cyst formation, pain in the pelvic or abdominal area; visual symptoms e.g. spots or flashes (scintillating scotomata), diplopia, phosphenes, or photophobia; anovulatory disorders and tendency to develop endometrial carcinoma; ovarian cancer, pregnancy wastage, multiple pregnancy (simultaneous bilateral tubal pregnancy with chorionic gonadotropin), and ectopic pregnancy. Patients with uterine fibroids, hepatic impairment, pre-existing mental depression or thrombophlebitis, preexisting or family history of hyperlipidemia. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category X.

flattened_sections.indications: Infertility and pregnancy: Provides luteal support in luteal phase defects in threatened/recurrent abortion and prevents preterm delivery. Luteal phase insufficiency: Progesterone challenge test in secondary amenorrhea, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, menstrual irregularities due to dysovulation or anovulation, pre-menstrual syndrome (PMS), fibrocystic mastopathy, dysmenorrhea, pre-menopause. Postmenopausal women: Prevention of endometrial hyperplasia in postmenopausal women with intact uterus receiving estrogen as hormone replacement therapy (HRT).
flattened_sections.dose: Oral administration - Threatened/recurrent abortion with luteal phase defect: 200-600 mg daily. Preterm delivery: 400 mg every 6-8 hrs depending on acute phase, then supporting dose of 600 mg daily in 3 divided doses until 36th week of pregnancy. Progesterone challenge test in secondary amenorrhea: 400 mg daily at bedtime for 10 days. Dysfunctional uterine bleeding, menstrual irregularities due to dysovulation or anovulation: 200 mg once daily from 17th day of cycle for 10 days. PMS, fibrocystic mastopathy, dysmenorrhea, pre-menopause: 200 or 400 mg daily for 10 days (usually from 14th-17th day to complete 10 days). Prevention of endometrial hyperplasia in postmenopausal women with intact uterus receiving estrogen as HRT: 200 mg at bedtime for 12 days sequentially per 28-day cycle. Vaginal administration - Luteal support in assisted reproductive techniques (e.g. in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer): 200 mg 3x daily from embryo transfer until pregnancy is confirmed. If pregnant, continue up to the 12th week of pregnancy.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Allergy to peanuts. Active liver disease especially of the obstructive type, history of known or suspected estrogen- or progestin-dependent malignant neoplasia (e.g. breast or endometrial cancer). Undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding, active or past history of arterial thromboembolic disease (e.g. stroke, MI, CHD) or VTE (i.e. DVT or pulmonary embolism), active thrombophlebitis, classical migraine, cerebral hemorrhage, partial or complete loss of vision due to ophthalmic vascular disease, missed or incomplete abortion, porphyria. Not for pregnancy test. Childn.
flattened_sections.precautions: In combination with estrogen: Should not to be used for prevention of CV disease or dementia. Patient assessment (including special attention to the breast and pelvic organs) e.g. Pap smear should be done prior to taking HRT. Endometrial biopsy should be done when indicated. Baseline tests should include mammography, measurements of blood glucose, calcium, triglycerides, cholesterol, liver function test. Discontinue if stroke occurs or expected. Possible increased risk of CV morbidity in the 1st yr of use. Increased BP. Risk factors of developing VTE. Patients with conditions that might be aggravated by fluid retention. Women with familial hyperlipidemias or porphyria. Diabetics or those with predisposition to diabetes. Patients with metabolic and malignant bone diseases associated with hypercalcemia and renal insufficiency. Increased risk of breast cancer. Women with existing breast cancer or those with a history of the disease, known risk factors associated with the development of breast cancer. Increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma. May cause breakthrough bleeding and spotting bleeding during the 1st months of treatment. Increased risk of ovarian cancer in long-term use (at least ≥5 yrs). Discontinue if visual disturbances, classical migraine, transient aphasia, paralysis or loss of consciousness occurs. Increased risk of probable dementia in women after 65 yrs. Patients with pre-existing mental depression, discontinue if depression recurs to a serious degree. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Women >65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Infections and infestations, breast carcinoma, jaundice; immune system, endocrine, metabolism and nutrition, psychiatric, nervous system, eye, ear and labyrinth, cardiac and vascular, respiratory, thoracic, mediastinal, GI, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous tissue, renal and urinary, and musculoskeletal and connective disorders. Pregnancy puerperium, and perinatal conditions, reproductive system and breast disorders, congenital, familial, and genetic disorders, general disorders and administration site conditions; altered coagulation tests, lipid profile, breast excisional biopsy, decreased glucose tolerance and weight; increased blood glucose level, BP, liver function tests, weight.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Liver enzyme inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, griseofulvin, barbiturates, hydantoins, meprobamates, phenylbutazone, rifampicin), CYP450 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole), antidiabetics, bromocriptine, ciclosporin, conjugated estrogens, St. John’s wort; hepatic function tests, coagulation tests, pregnanediol determination, thyroid function tests.

flattened_sections.indications: Uterine hypermotility disorders e.g. threatened abortion and uncomplicated premature labor. Adjunct in the treatment of peripheral vascular disease, e.g. arteriosclerosis obliterans, thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger’s disease), Raynaud’s disease. Relief of symptoms associated with cerebrovascular insufficiency.
flattened_sections.dose: Uterine hypermotility – IV: 100 mg (20 mL) in 500 mL infusion fluid (normal saline or dextrose solution) at a rate 0.5 mL/min (10 drops/min), increase rate in increments of 10 drops/min at 10-min intervals until control of uterine motility is obtained. IM: 10 mg (2 mL) every 3 hrs for 24 hrs, then every 4-6 hrs for a further 48 hrs. Tab: 20 mg (2 tabs) 3-4x daily when uterine contractions have ceased for at least 12 hrs with parenteral isoxsuprine. Circulatory disturbances – IM: 5-10 mg (1-2 mL) 3x daily. Tab: 20 mg (2 tabs) 3-4x daily after meals.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Following recent arterial hemorrhage, patients with known heart disease, severe anemia. Childn. IM/IV: Hypotension, tachycardia, premature detachment of placenta, immediately post-partum, premature labor if there is infection.
flattened_sections.precautions: Discontinue if rash develops. Monitor state of hydration, cardiac, and respiratory function. Keep fluid infusion vol to the minimum. For infusion, hypotonic dextrose is preferred over isotonic saline solution. Discontinue immediately and institute diuretic therapy when signs of pulmonary edema develop. Elderly. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Trembling, nervousness, weakness, dizziness, flushing, transient palpitation, tachycardia, chest pain, hypotension, abdominal distress, nausea vomiting, intestinal distension, severe rash, slight increase in fetal heart rate (as IV infusion in premature labor).

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment and control of excessive bleeding in various surgical and medical conditions including general surgical cases, cardiovascular surgery (e.g. coronary artery bypass graft [CABG], valvular heart surgery, correction of congenital heart disease, thoracic aortic surgery), pulmonary surgery, orthopedic surgery (knee replacement/arthroplasty, total hip replacement/arthroplasty, scoliosis surgery), traumatic injuries, operative procedures on the lungs, bladder, uterus, thyroid, ovaries, adrenals, kidney, liver, brain, lymph nodes, soft tissues; menorrhagia, metrorrhagia, postpartum hemorrhage, conisation of the cervix), epistaxis, gastrointestinal (GI) hemorrhage, hematuria, hereditary angioneurotic edema, tooth extraction, dental surgery.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosage. Adults - General surgical cases: 0.5-1 g (10-15 mg/kg BW) IV every 8-12 hrs for the first few days immediately after surgery then 1-1.5 g orally every 6-8 hrs. CABG: 1 g by IV bolus or 30 mg/kg IV before surgery if treated with aspirin; during surgery 200 mg/hr by IV infusion. Valvular heart surgery: 100 mg/kg IV before surgery. Thoracic aortic surgery: 1 g IV before skin incision, 400 mg/hr by IV infusion during operation and 500 mg in the pump priming. Knee replacement/arthroplasty: 10 mg/kg IV before surgery, another 10 mg/kg IV 3 hrs after surgery. Total hip replacement/arthroplasty: Initially 10 mg/kg IV bolus before surgery, 2nd IV bolus of 10 mg/kg 3 hrs later; continuous IV infusion of 1 mg/kg/hr for 10 hrs after surgery. Scoliosis surgery: Initial 10 mg/kg by IV injection and IV infusion of 1 mg/kg/hr. Prostatectomy: 0.5-1 g IV every 8 hrs during surgery up to 3 days after, then orally, 1 to 1.5 g every 6-8 hrs until macroscopic hematuria is no longer present. Menorrhagia/metrorrhagia: 1-1.5 g orally every 6-8 hrs for 3-4 days. Post-partum hemorrhage: 1 g IV. If bleeding continues, repeat 1 g after 30 mins, then 1-1.5 g (25 mg/kg) every 6-8 hrs. Conisation of the cervix: 1.5 g orally every 8 hrs for 12-14 days. Epistaxis: 1.5 g orally every 8 hrs for 4-10 days. GI hemorrhage: 1 g IV every 4 hrs for max of 3 days, then 1.5 g orally every 6 hrs for max of 4 days. Hematuria: 1-1.5 g orally every 8-12 hrs until macroscopic hematuria is no longer present. Hereditary angioneurotic edema: 1-1.5 g orally every 8-12 hrs as intermittent or continuous treatment depending on the prodromal symptoms of the patient. Dental surgery in patients with coagulopathies: 10 mg/kg IV immediately before surgery; after surgery 1-1.5 g (25 mg/kg) every 6-8 hrs for 6-8 days. Renal insufficiency - Serum creatinine of 1.36-2.83 mg/dL: 10 mg/kg IV twice daily or 15 mg/kg orally twice daily; 2.83-5.66 mg/dL: 10 mg/kg IV once daily or 15 mg/kg orally once daily. >5.66 mg/dL: 10 mg/kg IV every 48 hrs or 5 mg/kg IV every 24 hrs; 15 mg/kg orally every 48 hrs or 7.5 mg/kg orally every 24 hrs. Childn – IV: 10 mg/kg twice to thrice daily. Oral: 25 mg/kg twice to thrice daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active thromboembolic disease (e.g. DVT, pulmonary embolism, cerebral thrombosis). History of thrombosis or thromboembolism (e.g., retinal vein or artery occlusion) or intrinsic risk of thrombosis or thromboembolism (e.g. thrombogenic valvular disease, thrombogenic cardiac rhythm disease, hypercoagulopathy) unless being treated with anticoagulants. Patients receiving thrombin because of increased risk of thrombosis, with acquired color vision disturbances, with subarachnoid hemorrhage.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with high risk of thrombosis, renal insufficiency, disseminated intravascular coagulation, subarachnoid hemorrhage, irregular menstrual bleeding. Indissoluble clots may develop in body cavities due to extravascular clots. May cause convulsions, severe allergic reactions, visual abnormalities (with prolonged use). Concomitant use with hormonal contraceptives, Factor IX complex concentrates or anti-inhibitor coagulant, all-trans retinoic acid (in women with acute promyelocytic leukemia). May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B. IV: Do not mix with blood or solutions containing penicillin.
flattened_sections.side_effects: GI disturbances e.g. nausea, diarrhea, vomiting.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Thrombin, batroxobin, coagulation factor agents, hemocoagulase, hormonal contraceptives, clotting factor complexes (e.g., Factor IX complex concentrates or anti-inhibitor coagulant concentrates), all-trans retinoic acid (oral tretinoin), tissue plasminogen activators, anticoagulants, fibrinolytic preparations.

categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

indication_long: Tab/IV: Acute bacterial exacerbations ...

flattened_sections.indications: Tab/IV: Acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections (SSSI), non-gonococcal urethritis and cervicitis, acute pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), uncomplicated cystitis, acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis, complicated urinary tract infection (UTI), prostatitis, enteric infections including typhoid fever and shigellosis. Otic soln: Otitis externa, acute otitis media with tympanostomy tubes, chronic suppurative otitis media with perforated tympanic membranes. Ophthalmic soln: Blepharitis, hordeolum, dacryocystitis, conjunctivitis, meibomitis, keratitis, trachoma. Prevention of infection following corneal ulceration caused by susceptible organisms. Aseptic treatment during a peri-op period for ocular surgery caused by Staphylococcus spp., Moraxella spp., Chlamydia trachomatis, Pseudomonas spp., Haemophilus spp., Klebsiella spp., Serratia spp., Proteus spp., Acinetobacter spp., Corynebacterium spp., and anaerobic bacteria.
flattened_sections.dose: Tab/IV: Adults - Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, CAP, uncomplicated SSSI: 400 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days. Non-gonococcal cervicitis/urethritis due to C. trachomatis: 300 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. Acute PID: 400 mg every 12 hrs for 10-14 days. Uncomplicated cystitis - Due to E. coli or K. pneumoniae: 200 mg every 12 hrs for 3 days; Due to other susceptible pathogens: 200 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. Complicated UTI: 200 mg every 12 hrs for 14 days. Acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis: 400 mg every 12 hrs for 14 days. Prostatitis: 300 mg every 12 hrs for 6 weeks. Typhoid fever: 15 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses every 12 hrs for 5-14 days. Shigella: 400 mg single dose or 200 mg every 8 hrs for 1 day. Renal impairment - CrCl of 20-50 mL/min: Give the recommended dose every 24 hrs; <20 mL/min: ½ of recommended dose every 24 hrs. Tab: Taken with or without food. IV: Slow IV infusion over 30-60 mins. Otic soln: Otitis externa – Adults and childn >13 yrs: Instill 10 drops into the affected ear once daily for 7 days; Childn 6 months to 13 yrs: 5 drops once daily for 7 days. Acute otitis media with tympanostomy tubes – Childn 1-12 yrs: 5 drops twice daily for 10 days. Chronic suppurative otitis media with perforated tympanic membranes – Adults and childn ≥12 yrs: 10 drops twice daily for 14 days. Ophthalmic soln - Adults and childn ≥1 yr: Instill 1-2 drops 3-4 times daily continue until 2 days after the eye/s appear normal. Treatment should not exceed 2 weeks.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Tab/IV: History of epilepsy or lowered seizure threshold. G6PD deficiency. History of myasthenia gravis.
flattened_sections.precautions: May increase risk of tendinitis and tendon rupture, especially in elderly <60 yrs and in patients taking corticosteroids, and/or with kidney, heart, or lung transplant. Patients with impaired renal function, G6PD deficiency. May cause overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms (e.g. fungi), Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea, CNS disorders, peripheral neuropathy, blood glucose disturbances, photosensitivity/phototoxicity. Avoid direct exposure to excessive sunlight or UV during treatment. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Tab/IV: Nausea, insomnia, headache, dizziness, diarrhea, vomiting, rash, pruritus, external genital pruritus in women, vaginitis, dysgeusia. Otic soln: Application site reaction, pruritus, earache, dizziness, headache, vertigo, nausea, seborrhea, loss of hearing, tinnitus, otitis externa, otitis media, tremor, HTN, fungal infection, dermatitis, eczema, erythematous rash, follicular rash, hypoaesthesia, dyspepsia, hot flushes, flushing, otorrhagia, taste perversion, paresthesia, rash, diarrhea, vomiting, dry mouth, fever, urticaria, abdominal pain, dysaesthesia, hyperkinesias, halitosis, inflammation, pain, insomnia, cough, pharyngitis, rhinitis, sinusitis, tachycardia. Ophthalmic soln: Transient ocular irritation or discomfort (burning, stinging, redness, itching, photophobia).
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Antacids, sucralfate, didanosine, metal cations (iron, vitamins with zinc), antidiabetic agents, aminoglycosides, antimycobacterial drugs, beta-lactam antibiotics, caffeine, ciclosporin, cimetidine, ranitidine, corticosteroids, drugs that prolong QT interval, and undergo renal tubular secretion, metronidazole, NSAIDs, probenecid, theophylline, warfarin, zidovudine. IV Incompatibilities: Heparin.
flattened_sections.packaging: Tablet 200 mg (P64.99), 400 mg (P88.65). Solution for IV infusion 200 mg/100 mL. Otic solution 3 mg/mL x 5 mL. Ophthalmic solution 3 mg/mL x 5 mL.
