indication_long: Cap: Lower respiratory tract infection...

flattened_sections.indications: Cap: Lower respiratory tract infections (RTI) (e.g. bronchitis, pneumonia, empyema, lung abscess), URTI (e.g. tonsillitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, otitis media, scarlet fever), skin and skin structure infections (e.g. inflammatory acne vulgaris, furuncles, cellulitis, impetigo, abscesses, contaminated wounds, erysipelas, paronychia), gynecological infections (e.g. endometritis, pelvic cellulitis, post-op vaginal cuff infection, nongonococcal tubo-ovarian abscess, salpingitis, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), cervicitis due to Chlamydia trachomatis), intra-abdominal infections (e.g. peritonitis, abdominal abscess), bone and joint infections (e.g. acute hematogenous osteomyelitis, septic arthritis), septicemia, endocarditis, dental infections (e.g. periodontal abscess, periodontitis), Pneumocystis jiroveci (carinii) pneumonia (PJP) in patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) (in combination with primaquine in patients who are intolerant to or do not respond to conventional treatment). Alternative treatment of multi-drug resistant Plasmodium falciparum in combination with quinine or amodiaquine. IV/IM: Acute and chronic bacterial infections caused by clindamycin-sensitive pathogens, e.g., infections of bones and joints, ear, nose, throat, dental and maxillary area, deep respiratory tract, pelvic and abdominal area, female genitalia, skin and soft tissues. Scarlet fever, septicemia, endocarditis.
flattened_sections.dose: Cap – Adults – Serious infections: 150-300 mg every 6 hrs. More severe infections: 300-450 mg every 6 hrs. Duration of treatment for beta-hemolytic streptococcal infections: ≥10 days. Acne: 150 mg every 12 hrs. Bacterial vaginosis: 300 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. Cervicitis due to Chlamydia trachomatis: 450 mg every 6 hrs for 10-14 days. PID (inpatient treatment): Initially 900 mg IV every 8 hrs + IV antibiotic with G(-) aerobic spectrum for ≥4 days and ≥48 hrs after the patient improves. Continue with 450 mg orally every 6 hrs to complete duration of 10-14 days. Prevention of bacterial endocarditis in penicillin-allergic patients: 600 mg 30-60 mins before procedure as single dose. PJP in AIDS patients: 300-450 mg every 6-8 hrs + primaquine for 21 days; reduce dose if serious hematologic adverse effects develop. Alternative treatment of multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum: 5-10 mg/kg twice daily + quinine or amodiaquine for ≥5 days. IV/IM – For IV infusion or IM injection. Adults and adolescents >14 yrs – Moderately severe infections: 8-12 mL daily (equiv to 1.2-1.8 g) in 2-4 single doses. Severe infections: 16-18 mL daily (equiv to 2.4-2.7 g) in 2-4 single doses. Max 32 mL/day (equiv to 4.8 g) in 2-4 single doses. Infants >4 weeks and childn ≤14 yrs – 20-40 mg/kg BW in 3-4 single doses. Patients with severe hepatic or renal insufficiency or anuria: Reduce dose or prolong interval (8-12 hrs for patients with renal insufficiency or anuria). IM injection: Max of 600 mg single dose. IV infusion: Max of 12 mg/mL diluted solution. Max infusion rate: 30 mg/min or 1,200 mg/hr as single infusion.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. IV/IM: Neonates especially premature infants.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not use for meningitis. May cause overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms (e.g. fungi), Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea, serious allergic reactions. Atopic individuals. Patients with history of GI disease (particularly colitis), G6PD deficiency, severe renal or hepatic impairment with severe metabolic aberrations. Concomitant use with neuromuscular blocking agents. Perform liver and kidney function tests and blood counts during prolonged therapy. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B. IV/IM: Infants, childn up to 3 yrs. Cap: Childn <16 yrs. Elderly >60 yrs.
flattened_sections.side_effects: CDAD, pseudomembranous colitis, and other GI diseases, dermatologic and hypersensitivity reactions, hepatobiliary and renal, and hematologic effects. Vaginal infection/vaginitis, polyarthritis, dysgeusia, lymphadenitis.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Neuromuscular blocking agents, aminoglycosides, ampicillin, erythromycin, neostigmine and physostigmine, estrogens, oral typhoid vaccine, vit K antagonists (e.g. warfarin, acenocoumarol, fluindione), liver function tests.
flattened_sections.packaging: Capsule 300 mg (P85.16). Solution for injection (IV/IM) 150 mg/mL x 4 mL.

indication_long: Treatment of mild, moderate, or severe infect...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of mild, moderate, or severe infections caused by susceptible strains of the microorganisms for acute bacterial sinusitis, acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), healthcare-associated pneumonia (HCAP), complicated skin and skin structure infections (SSSI) and uncomplicated SSSI (e.g. abscesses, cellulitis, furuncles, impetigo, pyoderma, wound infections), urinary tract infection (UTI), acute pyelonephritis, chronic bacterial prostatitis. Reduction of the incidence or progression of inhalational anthrax, due to Bacillus anthracis, in adults and childn ≥6 months. Treatment of plague, including pneumonic and septicemic plague, due to Yersinia pestis and prophylaxis for plague in adults and childn ≥6 months.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - Acute bacterial sinusitis: 500 mg once daily for 10-14 days or 750 mg once daily for 5 days. Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis: 500 mg once daily for 7 days or 750 mg once daily for 5 days. CAP: 500 mg once daily for 7-14 days or 750 mg once daily for 5 days. HCAP: 750 mg once daily for 7-14 days. Complicated SSSI: 750 mg once daily for 7-14 days. Uncomplicated SSSI: 500 mg once daily for 7-10 days. Complicated UTI: 250 mg once daily for 10 days or 750 mg once daily for 5 days. Uncomplicated UTI: 250 mg once daily for 3 days. Acute pyelonephritis: 250 mg once daily for 10 days or 750 mg once daily for 5 days. Chronic bacterial prostatitis: 500 mg once daily for 28 days. Inhalational anthrax (post-exposure): 500 mg once daily for 60 days. Plague: 500 mg once daily for 10-14 days. IV: Administered by slow IV infusion. Renal impairment - 750 mg once daily normal dose: CrCl 20-49 mL/min: 750 mg every 48 hrs; 10-19 mL/min: Initially 750 then 500 mg every 48 hrs; Hemodialysis or CAPD: Initially 750 mg then 500 mg every 48 hrs. 500 mg once daily normal dose: CrCl 20-49 mL/min: Initially 500 mg then 250 mg every 24 hrs; 10-19 mL/min: Initially 500 mg then 250 mg every 48 hrs; hemodialysis or CAPD: Initially 500 mg then 250 mg every 48 hrs. 250 mg once daily normal dose: CrCl 10-19 mL/min: 250 mg every 48 hrs. Childn - Inhalational anthrax (post-exposure) - ≥50 kg BW: 500 mg once daily every 24 hrs for 60 days; <50 kg BW and ≥6 months: 8 mg/kg BW/dose every 12 hrs for 60 days. Max 250 mg/dose. Plague – ≥50 kg BW: 500 mg once daily every 24 hrs for 10-14 days; <50 kg BW and ≥6 months: 8 mg/kg BW/dose every 12 hrs for 10-14 days. Max of 250 mg/dose. All doses should be given at the same time each day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with known history of myasthenia gravis, known prolongation of QT interval, uncorrected hypokalemia, significant bradycardia, cardiomyopathy, or myocardial ischemia. IV: IM, SC, intrathecal, intraperitoneal administration.
flattened_sections.precautions: May increase risk of tendinitis and tendon rupture, especially in elderly <60 yrs and in patients taking corticosteroids, and/or with kidney, heart, or lung transplant. Patients with impaired renal function, G6PD deficiency. May cause overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms (e.g. fungi), Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea, photosensitivity/phototoxicity, CNS disorders, peripheral neuropathy, blood glucose disturbances, hepatotoxicity. Avoid direct exposure to excessive sunlight or UV during treatment. Not for treatment of MRSA infections, syphillis, gonorrhea. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Elderly. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: CV, CNS, dermatologic and sensitivity reactions, metabolic, GI, hepatic, hematologic. musculoskeletal, reproductive/urogenital system, and respiratory system disorders. Moniliasis, fungal infection including Candida infection, edema, multiorgan failure, pyrexia, asthenia, pain, injection site reaction. Uveitis, vision disturbance (including diplopia), visual acuity reduced, vision blurred, transient vision loss, scotoma, hypoacusis, tinnitus, hearing loss, hearing impaired, anosmia, parosmia, dysgeusia, ageusia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Antidiabetic agents, antidepressants, chelation agents (e.g. antacids, sucralfate, metal cations, multivitamins), ciclosporin, corticosteroids, NSAIDs, probenecid, cimetidine, tacrolimus, theophylline, warfarin. Opiate screening tests. IV Incompatibilities: Solutions containing multivalent cations.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of anemia in patients with renal insufficiency or chronic renal failure (CRF); in zidovudine-treated HIV-infected patients; in cancer patients on chemotherapy. Reduction of allogenic blood transfusion in adult surgery patients. Increases the yield of autologous blood from adult surgery patients in a pre-donation program.
flattened_sections.dose: CRF patients – Adults: 50-100 IU/kg IV or SC injection thrice a week. Maintenance: Individually titrate to achieve and maintain lowest Hgb level sufficient to avoid need for RBC transfusion and not exceed 12 g/dL. Increases should not be made more than once a month. Childn on hemodialysis: 50 IU/kg IV or SC injection thrice a week. Maintenance: Adjust dose to maintain Hgb between 9.5-11 g/dL. Generally, childn under 30 kg require higher maintenance doses. Zidovudine-treated HIV-infected patients (serum erythropoietin ≤500 mU/mL who are receiving zidovudine ≤4,200 mg/week): 100 IU/kg IV or SC injection thrice a week. Cancer patients on chemotherapy – Adults: 150 IU/kg BW by SC injection thrice a week; or 40,000 IU by SC injection once a week. Childn: 600 IU/kg BW by IV injection once a week. Max 40,000 IU. Adult surgery patients (Hgb level >10-≤13 g/dL) - To reduce allogenic blood transfusion: 600 IU/kg BW by SC injection once a week (days 21, 14, and 7 days before surgery) plus a 4th dose on the day of surgery; or 300 IU/kg/day BW by SC injection daily for 10 days before surgery, on the day of surgery and 4 days immediately thereafter. In an autologous pre-donation program: 600 IU/kg BW by IV injection twice a week for 3 weeks before surgery.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to epoetin alfa or mammalian cell-derived products or albumin (human). Uncontrolled HTN.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not shake container. Patients with chronic renal failure and with insufficient response to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESA). Patients with advanced head and neck cancer receiving radiation therapy, receiving chemotherapy for metastatic cancer or lymphoid malignancy, with NSCLC or various malignancies not receiving chemo- or radiotherapy, with IHD or CHF, with pre-existing CV disease or history of HTN, with history of seizure or underlying hematologic disease, with known porphyria. May induce PRCA and severe anemia (with or without cytopenias) associated with neutralizing antibodies to erythropoietin, seizures, absolute or functional iron deficiency. Monitor and control BP. If patients fails to respond or maintain a response, consider the following: iron deficiency; underlying infectious, inflammatory, or malignant processes; occult blood loss; underlying hematologic diseases; folic acid or vit B12 deficiencies; hemolysis, aluminum intoxication; osteitis fibrosa cystica; PRCA or anti-erythropoietin antibody-assciated anemia. May affect ability to drive and operate machines. Infants and childn <1 month. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Immunogenicity. HTN, headache, arthralgia, nausea, edema, fatigue, diarrhea, vomiting, chest pain, administration site reaction, asthenia, dizziness, clotted access, tachycardia, shortness of breath, hyperkalemia, pyrexia, cough, rash, respiratory congestion, paresthesia, URTI, trunk pain, constipation, skin pain, pruritus, insomnia, UTI, DVT, dyspepsia, and anxiety.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment and control of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) in men to cause regression of the enlarged prostate, improve urinary flow and alleviate symptoms associated to BPH. flattened_sections.dose: 5 mg once daily.

Females of childbearing potential should avoid exposure to patient’s semen. Lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category X.

flattened_sections.indications: Pre- and post-exposure immunization against rabies, as a primary vaccination or as a booster dose.
flattened_sections.dose: IM inj - Pre-exposure: 0.5 mL on days 0, 7, and 28 or 21; booster after 1 yr then subsequent booster vaccination depending on exposure to risks. Post-exposure: In subjects unvaccinated against rabies, 5 doses of 0.5 mL IM on days 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28. Administer into the deltoid area in adults or the anterolateral aspect of the thigh in infants and toddlers. Intradermal inj: May be used as an alternative, on upper or forearm. One intradermal dose comprises 0.1 mL of reconstituted vaccine e.g. 1/45 of the IM dose. Non-immunized individuals: 1 inj of 0.1 mL at 2 sites on days 0, 3, 7, and 28. Fully immunized individuals: 2 inj on days 0 and 3.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe febrile infection, acute disease. Do not use intradermal route for individuals receiving long-term corticosteroid or other immunosuppressive therapy or chloroquine, immunocompromised individuals, with severe wounds especially to the head and neck or presenting late for consultation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not administer IV. Cases of true allergy to polymyxin B, streptomycin or neomycin. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Local minor reactions e.g. inj site pain, erythema, edema, pruritus, and induration. General reactions e.g. moderate fever, shivering, malaise, asthenia, headaches, dizziness, arthralgia, myalgia, GI disorders.

Patients receiving ototoxic drugs (e.g. aminoglycosides); monitor vestibular and auditory function during and after treatment. Elderly 65-81 yrs.

flattened_sections.indications: Control of generalized tonic-clonic (grand mal) and complex partial (psychomotor, temporal lobe) seizures and for the prevention and treatment of seizures occurring during or following neurosurgery.
flattened_sections.dose: Cap - Adults with no previous treatment: 300 mg daily in 3 equally divided doses. Maintenance: 300-400 mg daily in 3-4 equally divided doses, may increase up to 600 mg daily if necessary. Non-emergency oral loading dose – Adults: 1 g divided into 3 doses (400 mg, 300 mg, and 300 mg) at 2-hr intervals. Normal maintenance dosage is then instituted 24 hrs after the loading dose, with frequent serum level determinations. Seizures – Childn: Initially 5 mg/kg/day in 2 or 3 equally divided doses with subsequent individualized dosage to max 300 mg daily. Maintenance: 4-8 mg/kg; Childn >6 yrs and adolescents: may require 300 mg/day. Susp – Adults with no previous treatment: 5 mL three times daily, may increase to 25 mL daily if necessary. Seizures – Childn: Initially 5 mg/kg/day in 2 or 3 equally divided doses with subsequent individualized dosage to max 300 mg daily. Maintenance: 4-8 mg/kg; Childn >6 yrs and adolescents: may require 300 mg/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to phenytoin or other hydantoins. Co-administration with delavirdine.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not effective for absence (petit mal) seizures. Not indicated for seizures due to hypoglycemic or other metabolic causes. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Suicidal ideation or behavior. Cases of bradycardia and asystole/cardiac arrest. Hypersensitivity syndrome or drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms. Serious dermatologic reactions. Discontinue immediately if symptoms of angioedema occur. Hepatic injury. Hematopoietic complications occasionally. May produce confusional states, rarely irreversible cerebellar dysfunction and/or cerebellar atrophy. Porphyria. May affect bone mineral metabolism. Good dental hygiene to minimize development of gingival hyperplasia. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Oral contraceptives. Pregnancy and lactation.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) in adults. Treatment of adult patients with heart failure and impaired left ventricular systolic function (LVEF 40%) as add-on therapy to ACE inhibitors or when ACE inhibitors are not tolerated.
flattened_sections.dose: HTN: Initially 8 mg once daily, can be increased to 16 mg once daily. Max 32 mg once daily. Patients with intravascular volume depletion, renal (including on hemodialysis) or mild to moderate hepatic impairment: Initially 4 mg once daily. Heart failure: Initially 4 mg once daily. Max 32 mg once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment and/or cholestasis. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Periodic monitoring of serum potassium and creatinine levels in patients with renal impairment. Assess renal function periodically. Concomitant therapy with ACE inhibitor in heart failure. Monitor BP in patient on hemodialysis. Patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a solitary kidney; heart failure, intravascular vol depletion, receiving high-dose diuretics, during anesthesia and surgery. Aortic or mitral valve stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Not recommended in primary hyperaldosteronism. Hyperkalemia. indication_long: Treatment of symptoms of depression, includin...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of symptoms of depression, including depression accompanied by symptoms of anxiety, in patients with or without a history of mania; obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD); panic disorder with or without agoraphobia; post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD); social phobia (social anxiety disorder); premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD).
flattened_sections.dose: To be taken once daily, either in the morning or evening. Depression and OCD: Initially 50 mg/day. Max 200 mg/day. Panic disorder, PTSD, and social phobia: Initially 25 mg/day, increased to 50 mg/day after 1 week. OCD - Childn 13-17 yrs: 50 mg/day; 6-12 yrs: 25 mg/day, increased to 50 mg/day after 1 week and further, in increments, if needed up to 200 mg/day. Titration in doses should not occur at intervals of < 1 week. PMDD: Initially 50 mg/day, either daily throughout the menstrual cycle or limited to the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle, may be increased in 50 mg/menstrual cycle increments up to 150 mg/day (menstrual cycle) or 100 mg/day (luteal phase).

flattened_sections.precautions: Risk for serotonin syndrome, NMS; activation of mania or hypomania; seizures; sexual dysfunction; bleeding abnormalities; hyponatremia; bone fractures; new-onset DM, loss of glycemic control in patients with or without pre-existing DM. Patients with or at risk for QTc prolongation, Torsades de Pointes; unstable epilepsy; angle-closure glaucoma, hepatic disease. Concomitant use of serotonergic drugs, antipsychotics, and other dopamine agonists; drugs known to affect platelet function (atypical antipsychotics and phenothiazines, TCAs, aspirin, and NSAIDs). May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Women of childbearing potential. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Blood and lymphatic; immune; endocrine, metabolism and nutrition; psychiatric; neurologic; eye, ear and labyrinth; cardiovascular; respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal; GI and hepatobiliary; skin and subcutaneous tissue; musculoskeletal and connective tissue; renal and urinary; reproductive and breast disorders.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Disulfiram, drugs that prolong QTc interval, CNS depressants and alcohol, lithium, phenytoin, sumatriptan, other serotonergic drugs, warfarin. indication_long: Adjunctive therapy to diet to reduce elevated...

flattened_sections.indications: Adjunctive therapy to diet to reduce elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, non-HDL-C and triglycerides and to increase HDL-C in adults with primary hyperlipidemia or mixed dyslipidemia; to reduce total cholesterol, LDL-C and apolipoprotein B in adolescent boys and girls (who are at least 1 yr post-menarche) 10-17 yrs with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (LDL-C >190 mg/dL or >160 mg/dL and positive family history of premature cardiovascular (CV) disease or ≥2 other CV disease risk factors); patients with hypertriglyceridemia; primary dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III hyperlipoproteinemia); in combination with other lipid-lowering treatments (e.g. LDL apheresis) or alone if such treatments are unavailable to reduce LDL-C, total cholesterol and apolipoprotein B in adult patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia; to slow the progression of atherosclerosis in adults, as part of a treatment strategy to lower total cholesterol and LDL-C. To reduce risk of stroke, myocardial infarction and arterial revascularization procedures.

Patients with severe hypercholesterolemia at high CV risk: Final titration to max 40 mg if treatment goal is not achieved at 20 mg. Prevention of CV events: 20 mg daily. Childn and adolescent 10-17 yrs (boys Tanner stage ≥2 and girls at least 1 yr post-menarche) - Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: Initially 5 mg daily. Dose range: 5-20 mg once daily. Elderly >70 yrs, Asian ancestry, patients with predisposing factors myopathy or moderate renal insufficiency: 5 mg.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease, severe renal impairment, myopathy. Concomitant use of ciclosporin. 40 mg dose is contraindicated in patients with predisposing factors for myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Renal effects (e.g. proteinuria). Monitor liver function tests. Patients who consume excessive alcohol, with history of liver disease, secondary hypercholesterolemia caused by hypothyroidism or nephrotic syndrome. Skeletal muscle effects, predisposing factors for myopathy/rhabdomyolysis; DM. Concomitant use of protease inhibitors. ILD may develop. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Asian race. Childn.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, dizziness, constipation, nausea, abdominal pain, myalgia, asthenia, DM.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Ciclosporin, protease inhibitors, gemfibrozil, ezetimibe, antacid, erythromycin, vitamin K antagonists, oral contraceptives, hormone replacement therapy, transporter protein inhibitors, fusidic acid.

flattened_sections.indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. May be used concomitantly with sulfonylureas or insulin to improve glycemic control.

flattened_sections.precautions: Risk of lactic acidosis. Determine CrCl or serum creatinine levels before treatment and regularly thereafter. indication_long: Tab: Treatment of erosive reflux esoph...

flattened_sections.indications: Tab: Treatment of erosive reflux esophagitis; long-term management of patients with healed esophagitis to prevent relapse; symptomatic treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcers associated with NSAID therapy in patients at risk. Healing of Helicobacter pylori-associated duodenal ulcer; prevention of relapse of peptic ulcers in patients with H. pylori-associated ulcer disease. In combination with appropriate antibacterial regimens for H. pylori eradication, prevention of relapse of peptic ulcer with H. pylori-associated ulcer disease. IV: Treatment of peptic ulcer disease (PUD), NSAID-associated ulceration, GERD and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
flattened_sections.dose: Tab - Treatment of erosive reflux esophagitis: 40 mg once daily for 4 weeks. Additional 4 weeks for patients with esophagitis that has not healed or with persistent symptoms. Long-term management of healed esophagitis to prevent relapse: 20 mg once daily. Symptomatic treatment of GERD without esophagitis: 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks. Prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcers associated with NSAID therapy in patients at risk: 20 mg or 40 mg once daily. H. pylori eradication or prevention of relapse of peptic ulcers with H. pylori-associated ulcer disease: 20 mg esomeprazole + 1 g amoxicillin + 500 mg clarithromycin, twice daily for 7 days. Severe liver impairment: Max 20 mg daily. Tabs may be dispersed in half a glass of non-carbonated water. Stir until tabs disintegrate and drink immediately or within 30 mins. IV – Adults: 20 mg or 40 mg IV injection (not <3 min) or IV infusion (10-13 min) once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to esomeprazole or substituted benzimidazoles. Concomitant administration with atazanavir and nelfinavir.
flattened_sections.precautions: In the presence of any alarm symptoms (e.g. significant unintentional weight loss, recurrent vomiting, dysphagia, hematemesis or melena) and when gastric ulcer is suspected or present, malignancy should be excluded. Long-term treatment (>1 yr). Slightly increased risk of GI infections e.g. Salmonella and Campylobacter. Concomitant use of atazanavir. Severe renal insufficiency. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. IV: Concomitant use of an imidazole antifungal.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache; abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, flatulence, nausea/vomiting. Dry mouth; gas; pain, swelling or redness at injection site.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Ketoconazole and itraconazole; diazepam; phenytoin; warfarin; clarithromycin. Saquinavir; methotrexate; tacrolimus; erlotinib, digoxin; citalopram, imipramine, clomipramine; voriconazole; cilostazol; cisapride; warfarin; clopidogrel; rifampicin and St. John’s wort.

Maintenance of healing erosive esophagitis and reduction in relapse rates at daytime and nighttime heartburn symptoms in adult patients with GERD: 40 mg once daily. PUD: 40 mg once daily, may be given for 2-4 weeks for duodenal ulceration, 4-8 weeks for benign gastric ulceration. Hepatic impairment: Max 20 mg daily, or 40 mg on alternate days. Renal impairment: Max 40 mg.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Monotherapy or in combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or dexamethasone for the treatment of adults with progressive multiple myeloma who have received at least 1 prior therapy and have undergone or are unsuitable for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. In combination with melphalan and prednisone for the treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are not eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. In combination with dexamethasone and thalidone for the induction treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
flattened_sections.dose: IV/SC. Progressive multiple myeloma (patients who have received at least 1 prior therapy) - Monotherapy: 1.3 mg/m2 twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8 and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. After confirmation of complete response: 2 cycles. Patients who do not achieve a complete remission: Receive a total of 8 cycles. At least 72 hrs should relapse between consecutive doses. Adjust dose if toxicity develops. Combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 30 mg/m2 on day 4 of treatment cycle as 1-hr IV infusion after bortezomib injection. May administer up to 8 cycles as long as patient has not progressed and tolerate treatment; Combination with dexamethasone: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Dexamethasone 20 mg orally on days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, and 12 of the bortezomib for injection treatment cycle, patients achieving a response or a stable disease after 4 cycles of this combination therapy can continue to receive the same combination for max 4 additional cycles. Previously untreated multiple myeloma patients not eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation - Combination with melphalan and prednisone: 6-week period treatment cycle. Cycles 1-4: Bortezomib administered twice weekly on days 1, 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, 29, and 32. Cycles 5-9: Bortezomib administered once weekly on days 1, 8, 22 and 29. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib injection. Melphalan and prednisone orally on days 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the 1st week of each bortezomib injection treatment cycle. Previously untreated multiple myeloma patients eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (induction therapy) - Combination therapy with dexamethasone: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, and 11 of the bortezomib injection treatment cycle for 4 treatment cycles; Combination therapy with dexamethasone and thalidomide: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 28-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib injection + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, and 11 of the bortezomib injection treatment cycle + thalidomide 50 mg orally daily on days 1-14, may be increased to 100 mg on days 15-28, and may be further increased to 200 mg daily from cycle 2 as tolerated. Hepatic impairment (moderate or severe): 0.7 mg/m2/injection on 1st treatment cycle and subsequent escalation to 1 mg/m2 or further dose reduction to 0.5 mg/m2.

Pregnancy and lactation.

brand_info.title: Indications
brand_info.content: Monotherapy or in combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or dexamethasone for the treatment of adults with progressive multiple myeloma who have received at least 1 prior therapy and have undergone or are unsuitable for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. In combination with melphalan and prednisone for the treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are not eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. In combination with dexamethasone and thalidone for the induction treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: IV/SC. Progressive multiple myeloma (patients who have received at least 1 prior therapy) - Monotherapy: 1.3 mg/m2 twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8 and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. After confirmation of complete response: 2 cycles. Patients who do not achieve a complete remission: Receive a total of 8 cycles. At least 72 hrs should relapse between consecutive doses. Adjust dose if toxicity develops. Combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 30 mg/m2 on day 4 of treatment cycle as 1-hr IV infusion after bortezomib injection. May administer up to 8 cycles as long as patient has not progressed and tolerate treatment; Combination with dexamethasone: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Dexamethasone 20 mg orally on days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, and 12 of the bortezomib for injection treatment cycle, patients achieving a response or a stable disease after 4 cycles of this combination therapy can continue to receive the same combination for max 4 additional cycles. Previously untreated multiple myeloma patients not eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation - Combination with melphalan and prednisone: 6-week period treatment cycle. Cycles 1-4: Bortezomib administered twice weekly on days 1, 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, 29, and 32. Cycles 5-9: Bortezomib administered once weekly on days 1, 8, 22 and 29. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib injection. Melphalan and prednisone orally on days 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the 1st week of each bortezomib injection treatment cycle. Previously untreated multiple myeloma patients eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (induction therapy) - Combination therapy with dexamethasone: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, and 11 of the bortezomib injection treatment cycle for 4 treatment cycles; Combination therapy with dexamethasone and thalidomide: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 28-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib injection + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, and 11 of the bortezomib injection treatment cycle + thalidomide 50 mg orally daily on days 1-14, may be increased to 100 mg on days 15-28, and may be further increased to 200 mg daily from cycle 2 as tolerated. flattened_sections.indications: Passive immunization against rabies.
flattened_sections.dose: Perform a skin test before administration. First-aid treatment: Thorough flushing and washing of wound with soap and water, detergent or other substance of proven lethal effect on rabies virus. Inject immunoserum as soon as possible after exposure. Nibbling of uncovered skin, minor scratches or abrasions without bleeding, licks on broken skin: Administer vaccine immediately. Discontinue if animal remains healthy throughout 10-day observation or if animal is killed humanely and found negative for rabies. Administer anti-rabies serum along with anti-rabies vaccine for immunocompromised patients. Single or multiple transdermal bites or scratches, contamination of mucous membrane with saliva (e.g. licks): Administer immunoserum and rabies vaccine immediately. Discontinue if animal remains healthy throughout 10-day observation or if animal is killed humanely and found negative for rabies. Prevention of rabies: 40 IU/kg for childn and adults. Infiltrate dose around wounds. Administer the remainder intramuscular (gluteal region) as a single dose. Inoculate 1st dose of vaccine at the same time as immunoglobulin, but in different parts of the body. When indicated, administer anti-tetanus and antimicrobials to control other infections.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Perform a skin test before administration. A positive result is a warning, not a contraindication for serotherapy. Administer only after ensuring facility to overcome anaphylactic shock. A negative result is not guaranteed for absence of an immediate allergic type reaction. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Anaphylactoid reactions with hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria, inflammatory reaction, fever, pruritus, rash, adenopathy, arthralgia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Simultaneous inoculation of immunoglobulin and vaccine to be done in different parts of the body. Do not administer the antiserum from the same syringe as the vaccine.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

For reduction of total-C and LDL-C in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Reduce risk for fatal coronary heart disease (CHD) and non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI); stroke; revascularization procedures and angina pectoris in patients without clinically evident cardiovascular disease (CVD), and with or without dyslipidemia, but with multiple risk factors for CHD. Reduce the risk for non-fatal MI; fatal and non-fatal stroke; revascularization procedures; hospitalization for congestive heart failure; angina. As adjunct to lifestyle changes to halt the progression of atherosclerosis (total atheroma or plaque volume) in patients with CAD and other individuals who are at high risk for CVD. Adjunct to diet to reduce total cholesterol, LDL-C, and apolipoprotein B levels in boys and post-menarchal girls, age 10-17 yrs, and with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Reduce the risk of CV disease in patients with diabetes with moderately decreased eGFR. Reduce the risk of major CV events including stroke in patients with clinically evident CHD and chronic kidney disease (CKD) not requiring dialysis. Reduce the rate of GFR decline and progression of CKD in patients with clinically evident CHD and/or diabetes with microalbuminuria.
flattened_sections.dose: 10-80 mg once daily. Starting and maintenance dosage should be individualized according to baseline LDL-C levels, the goal of therapy, and patient response. After initiation and/or upon titration of atorvastatin, lipid levels should be analyzed within 2-4 weeks, and dosage adjusted accordingly. Primary hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia: 10 mg once daily. Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: 80 mg. Severe dyslipidemias in childn ≥10 yrs: 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 80 mg daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases >3x ULN. flattened_sections.precautions: Moderate elevations of serum transaminases. Perform liver function tests before the initiation of treatment and periodically thereafter. Patients who consume substantial amounts of alcohol and/or have a history of liver disease. Discontinue if markedly elevated creatine phosphokinase occur or if myopathy is diagnosed or suspected. Temporarily withhold or discontinue in patients with acute, serious condition suggestive of myopathy or with risk factor predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Increased risk for recurrent hemorrhagic stroke. Increase in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels.

Reduce risk for fatal coronary heart disease (CHD) and non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI); stroke; revascularization procedures and angina pectoris in patients without clinically evident cardiovascular disease (CVD), and with or without dyslipidemia, but with multiple risk factors for CHD. Reduce the risk for non-fatal MI; fatal and non-fatal stroke; revascularization procedures; hospitalization for congestive heart failure; angina. As adjunct to lifestyle changes to halt the progression of atherosclerosis (total atheroma or plaque volume) in patients with CAD and other individuals who are at high risk for CVD. Adjunct to diet to reduce total cholesterol, LDL-C, and apolipoprotein B levels in boys and post-menarchal girls, age 10-17 yrs, and with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Reduce the risk of CV disease in patients with diabetes with moderately decreased eGFR. Reduce the risk of major CV events including stroke in patients with clinically evident CHD and chronic kidney disease (CKD) not requiring dialysis. Reduce the rate of GFR decline and progression of CKD in patients with clinically evident CHD and/or diabetes with microalbuminuria.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: 10-80 mg once daily. Starting and maintenance dosage should be individualized according to baseline LDL-C levels, the goal of therapy, and patient response. After initiation and/or upon titration of atorvastatin, lipid levels should be analyzed within 2-4 weeks, and dosage adjusted accordingly. Primary hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia: 10 mg once daily. Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: 80 mg. Severe dyslipidemias in childn ≥10 yrs: 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 80 mg daily.

brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Patients with active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases >3x ULN. Concomitant use with letermovir wtih ciclosporin. Women of childbearing potential not using contraceptive measures. Pregnancy and lactation.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Moderate elevations of serum transaminases. Perform liver function tests before the initiation of treatment and periodically thereafter. Temporarily withhold or discontinue in patients with acute, serious condition suggestive of myopathy or with risk factor predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Increased risk for recurrent hemorrhagic stroke. Increase in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels.

brand_info.title: Indications
brand_info.content: Edema associated with congestive heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis, corticosteroid and estrogen therapy. Edema due to various forms of renal dysfunction (e.g. nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and stable chronic renal failure). Diabetes insipidus. Control of essential hypertension (HTN).

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: Edema – Adults: 25-100 mg daily in 1-3 divided doses; may be reduced to 25-50 mg daily or intermittently. Diabetes insipidus – Adults: 50-100 mg daily in 1-3 divided doses. HTN – Adults: Initially 12.5-25 mg once daily. Usual dose range 12.5-50 mg daily. Max 50 mg daily, another antihypertensive drug may be added or substituted if adequate response is not achieved. Elderly >65 yrs: Initially 12.5 mg once daily, adjust in increments of 12.5 mg if needed. Childn 6 months-12 yrs: 1-2 mg/kg daily in 1-2 divided doses. < 6 months: Up to 3 mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses; Max 100 mg daily in children 2-12 yrs; 37.5 mg daily in childn < 2 yrs.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Anuria. Lactation.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Serum electrolytes should be monitored regularly. Fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Hypokalemia, dilutional hyponatremia. May exacerbate SLE and cause idiosyncratic reactions (e.g. acute myopia, acute angle-closure glaucoma) and non-melanoma skin cancer. Patients with hepatic and renal impairment. May impair glucose tolerance. Post-sympathectomy patients. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

brand_info.title: Side Effects
brand_info.content: Blood and lymphatic system disorders. Anaphylaxis, electrolyte imbalance and other metabolism and nutrition disorders. Insomnia and nervous system disorders. Eye, CV, respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal, GI, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue, renal and urinary, breast and reproductive systems disorders. Asthenia, fever, weakness, increased total cholesterol, LDL-C, VLDL-C, and triglycerides.

brand_info.title: Drug Interactions
brand_info.content: Alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, amantadine, aminoglycosides, diazoxide, calcium salts, vit D supplements, carbamazepine, cardiac glycosides, cholestyramine, and colestipol resins, corticosteroids, ciclosporin, lithium, pressor amines, NSAIDs (i.e. COX-2 inhibitors), skeletal muscle relaxants, SSRIs, topiramate, and iodinated contrast media. Anticholinergic, antidiabetic, antigout, cytotoxic, and other antihypertensive agents.

brand_info.content: Film-coated tablet 12.5 mg (P4.93), 25 mg (P6.21).

indication_long: Treatment of unresectable thyroid cancer (TC)...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of unresectable thyroid cancer (TC). In combination with pembrolizumab, for the 1st-line treatment of patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC). In combination with everolimus, for the treatment of patients with advanced RCC following 1 prior antiangiogenic therapy. Treatment of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In combination with pembrolizumab, for the treatment of patients with advanced endometrial carcinoma (EC) who have disease progression following prior systemic therapy in any setting and are not candidates for curative surgery or radiation.
flattened_sections.dose: TC: Initially 24 mg once daily (two 10 mg cap and one 4 mg cap). RCC: 20 mg (two 10 mg cap) once daily in combination with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks; or 18 mg (one 10 mg cap and two 4 mg cap) once daily in combination with everolimus 5 mg at the same time each day. HCC - Patients ≥60 kg: 12 mg (three 4 mg cap) once daily; < 60 kg: 8 mg (two 4 mg cap) once daily. EC: 20 mg once daily in combination with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks. Severe hepatic (Child-Pugh C) or severe renal (CrCl < 30 mL/min) impairment – TC: 14 mg once daily. RCC, EC: 10 mg once daily. Take at the same time each day. Caps are swallowed whole with water. Alternatively, add the caps (without breaking or crushing) to 1 tbsp of water or apple juice in a small glass to produce a suspension. Leave caps in the liquid for at least 10 mins. Stir for at least 3 mins and drink the mixture. After drinking, add the same amount of water or apple juice (1 tbsp) to the glass, swirl the contents and swallow the additional liquid.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid repeat exposure to contents of the caps. Patients with or at risk for renal impairment (renal failure, proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome); GI impairment (fistula formation or GI perforation); CV events (cardiac failure and decreased left ventricular ejection fraction, QT interval prolongation, hemorrhage, arterial thromboembolism); hepatic impairment (hepatic encephalopathy, failure); thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, TSH suppression impairment); wound healing complications. Risk for fertility impairment for men. Childn. Pregnancy and Lactation.

flattened_sections.dose: Adults: 4 mg once daily. May be tapered to 2 mg once daily if sustained control of disease activity is achieved and is eligible for dose tapering. flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active TB. Pregnancy and lactation.

Patients with active, chronic or recurrent infections. Diverticulitis and GI perforations, risk of malignancies. Consider anti-TB therapy prior to initiation of treatment in patients with previously untreated latent TB. Do not initiate or temporarily interrupt in patients with absolute neutrophil count < 1 x 10<sup>9</sup> cells/L, absolute lymphocyte count <0.5 x 10<sup>9</sup> cells/L, or Hgb < 8 g/dL; herpes zoster; increased in ALT or AST and suspected drug-induced liver injury; DVT/PE. Screen for viral hepatitis prior to initiation of treatment. Assess lipid parameters approx 12 weeks following initiation of therapy and thereafter. Elderly. Childn and adolescents ≤18 yrs. Use effective contraception during and ≥1 week after therapy in women.
flattened_sections.side_effects: URTI, hypercholesterolemia, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, gastroenteritis, UTI, pneumonia, folliculitis, thrombocytosis( >600 x 10<sup>9</sup> cells/L), headache, nausea, abdominal pain, increased ALT (≥3 x ULN), rash, acne, increased creatine phosphokinase (>5 x ULN).
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Azathioprine, tacrolimus, ciclosporin, probenecid, leflunomide, teriflunomide. Ibuprofen, diclofenac.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.dose: Primary hyperaldosteronism - Long test: 400 mg daily for 3-4 weeks. Correction of hypokalemia and HTN provides presumptive evidence for diagnosis of primary hyperaldosteronism. Short test: 400 mg for 4 days. If serum potassium increases during treatment but drops when discontinued, a presumptive diagnosis should be considered. After definitive diagnosis of hyperaldosteronism: Spironolactone 100-400 mg may be administered daily in preparation for surgery. For patients considered unsuitable for surgery, spironolactone may be employed for long-term maintenance therapy. Edema in adults (CHF, hepatic cirrhosis, or nephrotic syndrome): Initially 100 mg as single dose or in divided doses. Doses may range from 25-200 mg daily. Essential HTN: Initially 50-100 mg administered in single or divided doses; Hypokalemia: 25-100 mg daily; Severe heart failure (NYHA class III-IV) – Serum potassium ≤5.0 mEq/mL and serum creatinine ≤2.5 mg/dL: Initially 25 mg once daily, may be increased to 50 mg once daily if tolerated or reduced to 25 mg every other day if not.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Patients with anuria, acute renal insufficiency, impairment of renal excretory function, or hyperkalemia.
flattened_sections.precautions: Potassium supplementation from medications or diet. Patients with severe heart failure, impaired hepatic function. Concomitant use of lithium, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs. Dilutional hyponatremia, transient elevation of BUN, mild acidosis, gynecomastia. Observe for evidence of fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Childn. Lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Gastric bleeding, ulceration, gastritis, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting. Gynecomastia, inability to achieve or maintain erection, irregular menses or amenorrhea, post-menopausal bleeding. Agranulocytosis, fever, urticaria, maculopapular/erythematous eruptions, vasculitis. Confusion, ataxia, headache, drowsiness, lethargy. Renal dysfunction.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: ACE inhibitors. Alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics. Corticosteroids, ACTH, norepinephrine, tubocurarine, lithium, NSAIDs, digoxin.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

brand_info.content: Duodenal ulcer, gastric ulcer, NSAID-associated complications, peptic ulcer associated with Helicobacter pylori, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), acid reflux disease, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Prevention of acid aspiration syndrome, acid-related dyspepsia.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: NSAID-associated complications: 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks if not fully healed. Prophylaxis in patients with history of NSAID-associated complications who require continued NSAID treatment: 20 mg once daily. Peptic ulcer associated with H. pylori: Omeprazole 40 mg once daily + clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily + amoxicillin 1 g twice daily for 1 week. Acid-related dyspepsia: 10-20 mg daily for 2-4 weeks. GERD: 20-40 mg daily for 4-12 weeks. Maintenance: 20 mg daily; Childn: 0.7-1.4 mg/kg BW daily up to max 40 mg daily for 4-12 weeks. PUD: 20 or 40 mg in severe cases, once daily; Duodenal ulcer: for 4 weeks; Gastric ulcer: 8 weeks. Maintenance: 10-20 mg daily. Prophylaxis of acid aspiration: 40 mg the evening before surgery, then 40 mg on the day of surgery 2-6 hrs pre-op. Taken before meals.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Gastric malignancy. Lactation.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Exclude the possibility of malignancy before treatment if gastric ulcer is suspected. Pregnancy.

brand_info.title: Side Effects
brand_info.content: Reversible confusional states, agitation, depression, hallucinations on severely ill patients. Arthralgia, paresthesia, aggression, blurred vision, taste disturbances, peripheral edema, hyponatremia, agranulocytosis, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, interstitial nephritis, hepatotoxicity.

brand_info.title: Drug Interactions
brand_info.content: Diazepam, phenytoin, warfarin.

brand_info.title: Packaging

Post-exposure in incomplete or unvaccinated persons – Active vaccination: 1 dose (1 mL) on days 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28 into deltoid, or in the anterolateral thigh in small childn, or 0.1 mL intradermally at 2 sites on days 0, 3, 7 and 28; Initiate with 20 IU/kg human rabies immunoglobulin. flattened_sections.precautions: Use rabies vaccines derived from non-avian sources for persons with known sensitivity to avian proteins. indication_long: Tab/IV infusion: Prophylaxis and preve...

flattened_sections.indications: Tab/IV infusion: Prophylaxis and prevention of post-op infection due to anaerobic bacteria, particularly Bacteroides spp. and anaerobic streptococci. Treatment of septicemia, bacteremia, peritonitis, brain abscess, necrotizing pneumonia, osteomyelitis, puerperal sepsis, pelvic abscess, pelvic cellulitis, and post-op wound infection from which pathogenic anaerobes have been isolated. Treatment of Helicobacter pylori infection associated with peptic ulcer as part of triple therapy. IV infusion: Treatment of intestinal and extraintestinal or invasive amebiasis including amoebic liver abscess. Tab: Urogenital trichomoniasis (symptomatic and asymptomatic), amebiasis, giardiasis, balantidiasis, Blastocystis hominis infection. Vaginal infections (including bacterial vaginosis), acute ulcerative gingivitis, acute dental infections (e.g. acute pericoronitis and acute apical infections). Anaerobically-infected leg ulcers and pressure sores.
flattened_sections.dose: IV infusion: Administer by slow IV infusion (30-60 mins) at a rate of 5 mL/min. Adults – Prophylaxis and prevention of post-op anaerobic bacterial infections: Initial loading dose 15 mg/kg completed 1 hr before surgery, followed by 7.5 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs after initial dose; or 500 mg pre-op and at 8 and 16 hrs after initial dose. Treatment of infections caused by susceptible anaerobic microorganisms: Initial loading dose 15 mg/kg, followed by maintenance 7.5 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs for 7-10 days. Max 4 g every 24 hrs. Treatment of intestinal and hepatic amebiasis: 400-800 mg 3x daily for 5-10 days. Childn - Treatment of infections caused by anaerobes, trichomoniasis, Gardnerella vaginitis, amebiasis, giardiasis, pseudomembranous colitis, prophylaxis in colon surgery and part of combination therapy for H. pylori – Infants and childn: 15-30 mg/kg every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. >7 days with >2 kg BW: 30 mg/kg every 12 hrs; >7 days with 1.2-2 kg BW: 15 mg/kg every 12 hrs;<< 7 days with >2 kg BW: 15 mg/kg every 12 hrs; <7 days with 1.2-2 kg BW: 7.5 mg/kg every 24 hrs; 0-4 weeks with <1.2 kg BW: 7.5 mg/kg every 48 hrs. Tab – Treatment of infections caused by susceptible anaerobic microorganisms – Adults: 7.5 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs. or 500 mg every 8 hrs. Max 4 g/24 hrs. Childn <12 yrs: 7.5 mg/kg every 8 hrs or 20-30 mg/kg as single dose. May be increased to 40 mg/kg daily depending on severity of infection. Duration of treatment: 7-10 days or longer for serious bacterial infections. Prophylaxis and prevention of post-op anaerobic bacterial infections – Adults: 500 mg. Childn <12 yrs: 20-30 mg/kg as single dose given 1-2 hrs pre-op. Initiate 48 hrs before surgery, repeated every 8 hrs. Eradication of H. pylori: 20 mg/kg for 7-14 days as part of a combination therapy. Max 500 mg twice daily. Urogenital trichomoniasis – Adults and adolescents: 400-500 mg twice daily for 5-7 days or 2,000 mg as single dose. Childn 15-30 mg/kg every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. Bacterial vaginosis – Adults and adolescents: 400-500 mg twice daily for 5-7 days or 2,000 mg as single dose. Amebiasis – Adults and adolescents - Acute intestinal amebiasis: 750 mg 3x daily; Amebic liver abscess: 500 mg or 750 mg 3x daily for 5-10 days; Childn: 15-30 mg/kg/day every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. Giardiasis – Adults and adolescents: 2,000 mg once daily for 3 days, or 500 mg twice daily for 7-10 days; Childn: 15-30 mg/kg/day every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. Acute ulcerative gingivitis – Adults and adolescents: 200-250 mg 3x daily for 3 days. Balantidiasis and B. hominis infection – Adults and adolescents: 750 mg 3x daily for 5-10 days.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active neurological disorders, history of blood dyscrasia, hypothyroidism, hypoadrenalism. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) in patients with trichomoniasis.
flattened_sections.precautions: Monitor regularly if administered for >10 days. Patients with active or chronic severe peripheral and CNS disease. Candidiasis. Sodium retention; patients receiving corticosteroids or predisposed to edema. Hepatic and renal impairment, history of blood dyscrasias. May develop pancreatitis. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.
flattened_sections.side_effects: CV, dermatologic or hypersensitivity, endocrine or metabolic, GI, genitourinary or reproductive, hematologic, hepatic, musculoskeletal, nervous system, respiratory effects. Fever, thrombophlebitis, sharp, unpleasant, metallic taste, glossitis, tongue discoloration/furry tongue, transient vision disorders, tinnitus.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Alcohol, propylene glycol; anticoagulants; antiepileptics; busulfan; ciclosporin; cimetidine; corticosteroids; cyclophosphamide, carmustine; disulfiram; estrogens; fluorouracil, azathioprine; lithium, vecuronium. May interfere with serum chemistry values. IV: Equipment containing aluminum. Cefamandole nafate, cefoxitin, dextrose 10%, compound sodium lactate injection, penicillin G potassium.
flattened_sections.packaging: Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P25.05). Solution for IV infusion 500 mg/100 mL (P271.39).

brand_info.content: Tab/IV infusion: Prophylaxis and prevention of post-op infection due to anaerobic bacteria, particularly Bacteroides spp. and anaerobic streptococci. Treatment of septicemia, bacteremia, peritonitis, brain abscess, necrotizing pneumonia, osteomyelitis, puerperal sepsis, pelvic abscess, pelvic cellulitis, and post-op wound infection from which pathogenic anaerobes have been isolated. Treatment of Helicobacter pylori infection associated with peptic ulcer as part of triple therapy. IV infusion: Treatment of intestinal and extraintestinal or invasive amebiasis including amoebic liver abscess. Tab: Urogenital trichomoniasis (symptomatic and asymptomatic), amebiasis, giardiasis, balantidiasis, Blastocystis hominis infection. Vaginal infections (including bacterial vaginosis), acute ulcerative gingivitis, acute dental infections (e.g. acute pericoronitis and acute apical infections). Anaerobically-infected leg ulcers and pressure sores.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: IV infusion: Administer by slow IV infusion (30-60 mins) at a rate of 5 mL/min. Adults – Prophylaxis and prevention of post-op anaerobic bacterial infections: Initial loading dose 15 mg/kg completed 1 hr before surgery, followed by 7.5 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs after initial dose; or 500 mg pre-op and at 8 and 16 hrs after initial dose. Treatment of infections caused by susceptible anaerobic microorganisms: Initial loading dose 15 mg/kg, followed by maintenance 7.5 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs for 7-10 days. Max 4 g every 24 hrs. Treatment of intestinal and hepatic amebiasis: 400-800 mg 3x daily for 5-10 days. Childn - Treatment of infections caused by anaerobes, trichomoniasis, Gardnerella vaginitis, amebiasis, giardiasis, pseudomembranous colitis, prophylaxis in colon surgery and part of combination therapy for H. pylori – Infants and childn: 15-30 mg/kg every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. >7 days with >2 kg BW: 30 mg/kg every 12 hrs; >7 days with 1.2-2 kg BW: 15 mg/kg every 12 hrs;<< 7 days with >2 kg BW: 15 mg/kg every 12 hrs; <7 days with 1.2-2 kg BW: 7.5 mg/kg every 24 hrs; 0-4 weeks with <1.2 kg BW: 7.5 mg/kg every 48 hrs. Tab – Treatment of infections caused by susceptible anaerobic microorganisms – Adults: 7.5 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs. or 500 mg every 8 hrs. Max 4 g/24 hrs. Childn <12 yrs: 7.5 mg/kg every 8 hrs or 20-30 mg/kg as single dose. May be increased to 40 mg/kg daily depending on severity of infection. Duration of treatment: 7-10 days or longer for serious bacterial infections. Prophylaxis and prevention of post-op anaerobic bacterial infections – Adults: 500 mg. Childn <12 yrs: 20-30 mg/kg as single dose given 1-2 hrs pre-op. Initiate 48 hrs before surgery, repeated every 8 hrs. Eradication of H. pylori: 20 mg/kg for 7-14 days as part of a combination therapy. Max 500 mg twice daily. Urogenital trichomoniasis – Adults and adolescents: 400-500 mg twice daily for 5-7 days or 2,000 mg as single dose. Childn 15-30 mg/kg every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. Bacterial vaginosis – Adults and adolescents: 400-500 mg twice daily for 5-7 days or 2,000 mg as single dose. Amebiasis – Adults and adolescents - Acute intestinal amebiasis: 750 mg 3x daily; Amebic liver abscess: 500 mg or 750 mg 3x daily for 5-10 days; Childn: 15-30 mg/kg/day every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. Giardiasis – Adults and adolescents: 2,000 mg once daily for 3 days, or 500 mg twice daily for 7-10 days; Childn: 15-30 mg/kg/day every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day. Acute ulcerative gingivitis – Adults and adolescents: 200-250 mg 3x daily for 3 days. Balantidiasis and B. hominis infection – Adults and adolescents: 750 mg 3x daily for 5-10 days.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Active neurological disorders, history of blood dyscrasia, hypothyroidism, hypoadrenalism. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) in patients with trichomoniasis.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Monitor regularly if administered for >10 days. Patients with active or chronic severe peripheral and CNS disease. Candidiasis. Sodium retention; patients receiving corticosteroids or predisposed to edema. Hepatic and renal impairment, history of blood dyscrasias. May develop pancreatitis. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.

flattened_sections.dose: Adults and childn ≥12 yrs: 250-500 mg every 12 hrs for 5-14 days. Pharyngitis or tonsillitis: 250 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days. Helicobacter pylori infection – Triple therapy: Clarithromycin 500 mg + amoxicillin 1 g + omeprazole 20 mg all twice daily for 7-10 days. Additional 18 days of omeprazole 20 mg once a day for ulcer healing and symptom relief in patients with an ulcer present at the time of initiation. Dual therapy: Clarithromycin 500 mg 3 times daily + omeprazole 40 mg once daily for 14 days, followed by omeprazole 20 or 40 mg once a day for additional 14 days. Renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min): Reduce dose by ½, e.g. 250 mg once a day in adults, up to max of 250 mg once a day in pediatric patients (every 12 hrs in more severe infections in both). brand_info.content: Rx

brand_info.title: Indications
brand_info.content: Upper respiratory tract infections, e.g. streptococcal pharyngitis and tonsillitis, acute maxillary sinusitis, acute otitis media; Lower respiratory tract infections, e.g. bronchitis, pneumonia; Uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections, e.g. impetigo, folliculitis, cellulitis, abscess; Disseminated or localized mycobacterial infections due to M. avium or M. intracellulare; Localized infections due to M. kansasii, M. chelonae, M. fortuitum (usually in combination with other antimicrobial agents); Helicobacter pylori infections (in combination with other drugs); Odontogenic infections. Prevention of disseminated M. avium complex (MAC) infection in advanced human immunodeficiency virus patients.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: Adults and childn ≥12 yrs: 250-500 mg every 12 hrs for 5-14 days. Pharyngitis or tonsillitis: 250 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days. Acute maxillary sinusitis: 500 mg every 12 hrs for 7-14 days. Acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis and community-acquired pneumonia: 250-500 mg every 12 hrs for 7-14 days. Uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections: 250 mg every 12 hrs for 7-14 days. Odontogenic infections: 250 mg every 12 hrs for 5 days. Treatment of disseminated or localized mycobacterial infections: 500 mg every 12 hrs. Prevention of disseminated M. avium complex infection in advanced human immunodeficiency virus patients: 500 mg every 12 hrs. Helicobacter pylori infection – Triple therapy: Clarithromycin 500 mg + amoxicillin 1 g + omeprazole 20 mg all twice daily for 7-10 days. Additional 18 days of omeprazole 20 mg once a day for ulcer healing and symptom relief in patients with an ulcer present at the time of initiation. Dual therapy: Clarithromycin 500 mg 3 times daily + omeprazole 40 mg once daily for 14 days, followed by omeprazole 20 or 40 mg once a day for additional 14 days. Renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min): Reduce dose by ½, e.g. 250 mg once a day in adults, up to max of 250 mg once a day in pediatric patients (every 12 hrs in more severe infections in both). Do not continue beyond 14 days.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. History of cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction associated with prior use of clarithromycin. History of QT prolongation or ventricular cardiac arrhythmia including torsades de pointes. Concomitant use with ticagrelor and ranolazine.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Renal impairment, QT prolongation, hepatotoxicity, CAD, Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea, myasthenia gravis, HIV, skin and soft tissue infections, pneumonia, ototoxicity, porphyria. Cross-resistance between other macrolides. Risk of development of drug-resistant microorganisms. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms in long-term or repeated use. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn and elderly. Lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

Nicotinic acid: Nausea, heartburn, headache, fatigue, sore throat, dry hair, dry skin, tightness of the face, hives and blurred vision (chronic administration). Elevated liver function tests and liver damage including jaundice, cholestatic hepatitis and portal fibrosis (large doses). Dizziness, diarrhea, vomiting, moderate increase in gastric secretion and bile flow, abnormal prothrombin time and hypoalbuminemia. Zinc: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, GI discomfort, metallic taste, headache, and drowsiness (high doses). Low HDL levels. UTI and kidney stones (long-term).

Zinc: Bisphosphonates; cholesterol medicines; copper or iron; penicillamine; quinolones; tetracyclines; foods containing high amounts of phosphorus, calcium (dairy), or phytates (e.g. bran, brown bread).

indication_long: Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus as mono...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus as monotherapy or in combination with a sulfonylurea, metformin, or insulin when adequate glycemic control is not achieved by diet and exercise.
flattened_sections.dose: Monotherapy: Dose may be titrated in increments of 15 mg up to max 45 mg daily. Patients without congestive heart failure (CHF): Initially 15 or 30 mg once daily taken with or without meals. Patients with CHF NYHA Class I or II: Initially 15 mg once daily. Combination therapy – With metformin: Initially 15 or 30 mg once daily; continue current metformin dose. With sulfonylureas: Initially 15 or 30 mg once daily; continue current sulfonylurea dose. Decrease sulfonylurea dose in case of hypoglycemia. With insulin: Continue current insulin dose. Decrease insulin dose by 10-25% in case of hypoglycemia or FBS < 100 mg/dL. Individualize further adjustments based on glucose-lowering response. Coadministration with strong CYP2C8 inhibitors: Max 15 mg once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. CHF NYHA Class III or IV. Severe hepatic impairment, ALT >2.5x ULN, or active liver disease. Type 1 DM, diabetic ketoacidosis. Active bladder cancer. Dialysis patients. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with existing edema or heart failure. History of CAD, CABG, MI. Use the lowest dose for patients with at least one risk factor for CHF. History of bladder cancer. Increased risk of fractures in women. Hypoglycemia. May cause ovulation in anovulatory premenopausal women with insulin resistance. Decreases in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Undesirable effects on respiratory, endocrine, CV, CNS, musculoskeletal, hepatic, hematologic, renal, eye, and GI systems. Tumors.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Oral contraceptives e.g. norethindrone/ethinylestradiol, insulin, insulin secretagogues e.g. sulfonylureas, midazolam, strong CYP2C8 inhibitors e.g. gemfibrozil, CYP2C8 inducers e.g. rifampicin, CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g.ketoconazole.

indication_long: As monotherapy or in combination therapy for ...
Treatment of multiple myeloma.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of multiple myeloma.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults ≥18 yrs: 16 mg/kg IV infusion. Infusion rate: 50 mL/hr increased by 50 mL/hr every hr (in absence of infusion-related reactions) up to max rate 200 mL/hr. Monotherapy for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma or in combination with lenalidomide and low-dose dexamethasone (4-week cycle) for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma ineligible for autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) or for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma - Weeks 1-8: Weekly, total 8 doses; Weeks 9-24: Every 2 weeks, total 8 doses; Week 25 onwards until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. In combination with bortezomib, melphalan and prednisone (6-week cycle) for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma ineligible for ASCT - Weeks 1-6: Weekly, total 6 doses; Weeks 7-54: Every 3 weeks, total 16 doses; Week 55 onwards until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. Administer bortezomib 2x weekly at weeks 1, 2, 4, 5 for 1st 6-week cycle, then once weekly at weeks 1, 2, 4, 5 for 8 more 6-week cycles. In combination with bortezomib, thalidomide, and dexamethasone (4-week cycle) - Induction: Weeks 1-8: Weekly, total of 8 doses; Weeks 9-16: Every 2 weeks, total of 4 doses. Then stop for high dose chemotherapy and ASCT. Consolidation: Weeks 1-8 (reinitiation): Every 2 weeks, total of 4 doses. In combination with bortezomib (3-week cycle) for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma - Weeks 1-9: Weekly, total 9 doses; Weeks 10-24: Every 2 weeks, total 5 doses; Week 25 onwards until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. See full prescribing information for premedication and post-infusion regimen and management of infusion-related reactions.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Infusion-related reactions. Neutropenia/thrombocytopenia may be induced. Interference with indirect antiglobulin test (indirect Coombs test) and serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation tests. HBV reactivation. Women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during and for 3 months after treatment. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Infusion reactions, diarrhea, constipation, nausea, peripheral edema, fatigue, back pain, asthenia, pyrexia, urinary tract infection, bronchitis, nasopharyngitis, pneumonia. Decreased appetite, muscle spasms, peripheral sensory neuropathy, dyspnea, cough. Anemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, neutropenia, lymphopenia. Arthralgia, pain in extremity, musculoskeletal chest pain.
flattened_sections.packaging: Concentrate for solution for IV infusion 20 mg/mL x 5 mL (P22,384.82), 20 mL (P110,000.00).
