flattened_sections.indications: Reduce risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with chronic heart failure especially in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) below normal. Administered in place of an ACE inhibitor or ARBs.
flattened_sections.dose: Initially 100 mg twice daily. Double the dose at 2-4 weeks to target dose of 200 mg twice daily as tolerated. Patients not currently on ACE inhibitors or ARBs or previously taking low doses of these agents: Start at 50 mg twice daily and slow dose titration (doubling every 3-4 weeks). Patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m2) and moderate hepatic impairment: Initially 50 mg twice daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with an ACE inhibitor (do not start Vymada for at least 36 hrs after discontinuing ACE inhibitor therapy) or ARBs. History of angioedema related to ACE inhibitor or ARBs therapy, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or with renal impairment (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Severe hepatic impairment, biliary cirrhosis and cholestasis. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester).
flattened_sections.precautions: Sodium and/or sodium depletion should be corrected before treatment. Hypotension, impaired renal function, hyperkalemia, angioedema. Patients with renal artery stenosis, CHF NYHA class IV, hepatic impairment. Not suitable with B-type natriuretic peptide as biomarker for heart failure. Psychiatric disorders (e.g. hallucination paranoia, and sleep disorders). Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hyperkalemia, hypotension, renal impairment,  cough, dizziness, diarrhea, anemia, fatigue, renal failure, hypokalemia, headache, syncope, asthenia, nausea, orthostatic hypotension, gastritis, vertigo, hypoglycemia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 substrates (e.g. statins), PDE5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil), lithium, furosemide, metformin, potassium-sparing diuretics including mineralocorticoid antagonists (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride), potassium supplements, or salt substitutes containing potassium, NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors, nitrates, inhibitors of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT3 (e.g. rifampin, ciclosporin) or multidrug resistance-associated protein (e.g. ritonavir).

flattened_sections.indications: Thrombolytic treatment in acute myocardial infarction (MI), acute massive pulmonary embolism (PE)  with hemodynamic instability, and acute ischemic stroke.
flattened_sections.dose: Given as early as possible after symptom onset. Acute MI - 90-min accelerated dose regimen (started within 6 hrs after symptom onset) - ≥65 kg BW: 15 mg IV bolus, followed by 50 mg IV infusion for 1st 30 mins, then 35 mg IV infusion for 60 mins, until max total dose of 100 mg; < 65 kg: 15 mg IV bolus, followed by 0.75 mg/kg IV infusion for 1st 30 mins, then 0.5 mg/kg IV infusion for 60 mins. 3-hr dose regimen (started between 6-12 hrs after symptom onset) - >65 kg: 10 mg IV bolus, followed by 50 mg IV infusion for 1st hr, then 40 mg IV infusion for 60 mins, until max total dose of 100 mg; < 65 kg: 10 mg IV bolus followed by up to max total dose of 1.5 mg/kg IV infusion for 3 hrs. Acute massive PE - ≥65 kg BW: 10 mg IV bolus for 1-2 mins, followed by 90 mg IV infusion for 2 hrs, until max total dose of 100 mg; < 65 kg: 10 mg IV bolus for 1-2 mins, followed by up to max total dose of 1.5 mg/kg IV infusion for 2 hrs; Adjunctive therapy: After therapy, initiate heparin therapy when aPTT values are < 2x ULN. Adjust infusion to maintain aPTT between 50-70 secs (1.5-2.5 fold of reference value). flattened_sections.indications: Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angina pectoris in adults with coronary artery disease with normal sinus rhythm and heart rate (HR) ≥70 bpm and treatment of chronic heart failure (NYHA class II-IV) with systolic dysfunction in sinus rhythm and HR ≥75 bpm.
flattened_sections.dose: Chronic stable angina pectoris - Adults <75 yrs: Should not exceed 5 mg twice daily. If tolerated and HR remains >60 bpm dose may increase to higher dose in patients receiving 2.5 mg or 5 mg twice daily after 3-4 weeks of treatment. Maintenance: Max 7.5 mg twice daily. Discontinue treatment if no improvement of symptoms after 3 months. If HR decreases <50 bpm at rest or the patient experiences symptoms related to bradycardia: Titrate downward to 2.5 mg twice daily. Discontinue if HR remains <50 bpm. CHF: Initially 5 mg twice daily. May be increased to 7.5 mg twice daily if resting HR >60 bpm or decreased to 2.5 mg twice daily if resting HR is <50 bpm after 2 weeks. If HR is between 50-60 bpm: 5 mg twice daily. Discontinue if HR remains <50 bpm or bradycardia persist. Elderly >75 yrs: 2.5 mg twice daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Resting HR <70 bpm prior to treatment, cardiogenic shock, acute MI, severe hypotension (<90 mmHg), severe hepatic insufficiency, sick sinus syndrome, SA block, unstable or acute heart failure, pacemaker dependent, unstable angina, 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block. Combination with verapamil or diltiazem and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. azole antifungals, macrolide antibiotics, HIV protease inhibitors and nefazodone. Patients with congenital QT syndrome or treated with QT-prolonging medicinal products. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with 2<sup>nd</sup>-degree AV-block, heart failure with NYHA class IV, retinitis pigmentosa, hypotension, renal impairment (CrCl <15 mL/min), moderate hepatic impairment. Not recommended in patients with atrial fibrillation or other cardiac arrhythmias that interfere with sinus node function. Not recommended immediately after a stroke. Monitor CHF patients with intraventricular conduction defects and ventricular dyssynchrony. Elderly. Childn and adolescents <18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Luminous phenomena. Headache, dizziness; blurred vision; 1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block (ECG prolonged PQ interval), ventricular extrasystoles, atrial fibrillation; uncontrolled BP.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: QT-prolonging medications (e.g. quinidine, disopyramide, bepridil, sotalol, ibutilide, amiodarone); pimozide, ziprasidone, sertindole, mefloquine, halofantrine, pentamidine, cisapride, IV erythromycin; potassium-depleting diuretics (thiazide and loop diuretics); grapefruit juice; fluconazole; rifampicin, barbiturates, phenytoin, Hypericum perforatum (St. John’s wort).

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Established postmenopausal osteoporosis. Renal osteodystrophy in patients with chronic renal failure, particularly those undergoing hemodialysis. Secondary hyperparathyroidism in patients with moderate to severe chronic renal failure (pre-dialysis). Postsurgical hypoparathyroidism. Idiopathic hypoparathyroidism. Pseudohypoparathyroidism. Vitamin D-dependent rickets. Hypophosphatemic vitamin D-resistant rickets.
flattened_sections.dose: Postmenopausal osteoporosis: 0.25 mcg 2x daily. Determine serum calcium and creatinine at 1, 3, and 6 months and at 6-month intervals thereafter. Renal osteodystrophy (dialysis patients): Initially 0.25 mcg daily; patients with normal or only slightly reduced serum calcium levels: 0.25 mcg every other day. May be increased by 0.25 mcg at 2- to 4-week intervals if no satisfactory response is observed within 2-4 weeks. Determine serum calcium at least 2x weekly. Secondary hyperparathyroidism (pre-dialysis patients i.e. CrCl 15-55 mL/min): Initially 0.25 mcg/day in adults, may be increased to 0.5 mcg/day. Hypoparathyroidism, rickets: Initially 0.25 mcg/day in the morning, may be increased at 2- to 4-week intervals if no satisfactory response is observed. Determine serum calcium at least 2x weekly.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. All diseases associated-hypercalcemia. Evidence of vit D toxicity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Ensure adequate calcium intake at the beginning of therapy. Patients with renal failure; immobilized patients (e.g. undergone surgery). Development of hypercalcemia. Increased serum inorganic phosphate levels. Possible stimulation of intestinal absorption of phosphate on patients with vit D-resistant rickets. Do not give other vit D preparation. Avoid dehydration and maintain adequate fluid intake in patients with normal renal function. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hypercalcemia. Headache, abdominal pain, nausea, rash, UTI.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Calcium supplements and calcium-containing preparations. Thiazide diuretic, digitalis. Magnesium-containing drugs (e.g. antacids). Phosphate binding agents. Bile acid sequestrants (e.g. cholestyramine, sevelamer).

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

In combination with cyclophosphamide as a conditioning regimen prior to bone marrow or peripheral blood progenitor cell replacement - Patients weighing >12 kg: 0.8 mg/kg IV via a central venous catheter as a 2-hr infusion every 6 hrs for 4 consecutive days for a total of 16 doses (Days 7, 6, 5, and 4); Cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg IV as 1-hr infusion on each of 2 days beginning no sooner than 6 hrs following the 16th dose of busulfan (IV Busulfex) (Days 3 and 2). Administer hematopoietic progenitor cells on Day 0.

flattened_sections.indications: Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation with one or more risk factor e.g. congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 yrs, diabetes mellitus, prior stroke or transient ischemic attack. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE in adults.
flattened_sections.dose: Patients with renal insufficiency – Mild (CrCl >50-80 mL/min): 60 mg once daily; Moderate or severe (CrCl 15-50 mL/min): 30 mg once daily. Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment: 60 mg once daily. Take with or without food.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Clinically significant active bleeding. Patients with hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk. Lesion or condition, if considered to be a significant risk for major bleeding. Uncontrolled severe HTN. Concomitant treatment with any other anticoagulants e.g. unfractionated heparin, LMWH (enoxaparin, dalteparin), heparin derivatives (fondaparinux), oral anticoagulants (warfarin, dabigatran, etexilate, rivaroxaban, apixaban) except under specific circumstances of switching oral anticoagulant therapy or when unfractionated heparin is given at doses necessary to maintain an open central venous or arterial catheter. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Hemorrhagic risk. Discontinue use if severe hemorrhage occurs. Not recommended in patients with ESRD (CrCl <15 mL/min) or in dialysis, and severe hepatic impairment. Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment, elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST >2x ULN) or total bilirubin ≥1.5x ULN. Discontinue use at least 24 hrs before the procedure and interventions. Concomitant use of medicines affecting hemostasis. Not recommended in patients with mechanical heart valves, during the first 3 months after implantation of a bioprosthetic heart valve, with or without atrial fibrillation, moderate to severe mitral stenosis. Not recommended as an alternative to unfractionated heparin in patients with PE who are hemodynamically unstable or may receive thrombolysis or pulmonary embolectomy. Patients with active cancer. Not recommended in patients with history of thrombosis with antiphospholipid syndrome. Adolescents and childn <18 yrs.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Anemia; dizziness, headache; epistaxis; abdominal pain, lower and upper GI hemorrhage, oral/pharyngeal hemorrhage, nausea; increased blood bilirubin and gamma-glutamyl transferase; cutaneous soft tissue hemorrhage, rash, pruritus; macroscopic hematuria/urethral hemorrhage; vaginal hemorrhage; puncture site hemorrhage; abnormal liver function test.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: P-gp inhibitors (e.g. ciclosporin, dronedarone, erythromycin, ketoconazole, quinidine or verapamil). P-gp inducers (e.g. rifampicin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital or St. John’s wort). Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, NSAIDs, SSRIs/SNRIs.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of multiple myeloma in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone in adults who have received at least one prior therapy. flattened_sections.dose: Multiple myeloma in adults who have received at least one prior therapy - Initial ixazomib dose: 4 mg once a week on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle; Initial lenalidomide dose: 25 mg once daily on days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle; Initial dexamethasone dose: 40 mg once a week on days 1, 8, 15, and 22 of a 28-day cycle. Patients with moderate/severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, or ESRD requiring dialysis: Reduce ixazomib dose to 3 mg. Maintenance of multiple myeloma following ASCT and those who had not been treated with stem cell transplantation - Cycles 1-4: 3 mg; Cycle 5 onwards: 4 mg; All doses taken in a fasted state once a week on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle, then the cycle is repeated. Patients with moderate/severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, or ESRD requiring dialysis: Reduce to 2.3 mg for cycles 1-4 and 3 mg for cycle 5 onwards. Men and women of childbearing potential should use contraception during and for 90 days after stopping treatment. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: URTI, bronchitis; thrombocytopenia, neutropenia; peripheral neuropathies; diarrhea, constipation, nausea and vomiting; rash; back pain; peripheral edema. Herpes zoster.

flattened_sections.indications: Acute treatment of migraine attacks and cluster headache.
flattened_sections.dose: Treatment of acute migraine - Adults ≥18 yrs: 50 mg. Administer orally as soon as possible after the onset of the headache phase. If no response is obtained with initial dose by any route, 2nd dose should not be given for the same attack. Further doses may be given at minimum 2-hr interval between doses and not >300 mg in the 24-hr period if symptoms recur. Lower dose of 25 mg may be used, although some patients require 50 or 100 mg, followed by a 2nd dose of up to 100 mg if the headache returns or the patient has a partial response provided that the total daily dose does not exceed the recommended max of 200 mg and at a min 2-hr interval between doses. Childn 10-12 yrs: 50 mg; 6-10 yrs: 25 mg. Repeated once after at least 2 hrs if symptoms recur after an initial response. Hepatic impairment: 50 mg.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with uncontrolled HTN, IHD (CAD), history of MI, coronary vasospasm (Prinzmetal’s angina), PVD or previous CVA or TIA. Severe hepatic impairment.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not use for prophylaxis and in patients with basilar, hemiplegic, or ophthalmoplegic migraine. Should not be given as IV because of the risk of producing coronary vasospasm. Should not be used for prophylaxis and should not be given to patients with basilar, hemiplegic or ophthalmoplegic migraine. Exclude unrecognized CV disease prior to treatment in postmenopausal women, men >40 yrs, patients with risk factors for IHD. Patients with hepatic, renal impairment, or history of epilepsy or conditions predisposing seizures, hypersensitivity to sulfonamides. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Dizziness, flushing, weakness, drowsiness and fatigue. Nausea and vomiting. Dyspnea and sensory disturbance including paresthesia and hypoesthesia. Pain or sensations of heaviness, heat or cold, pressure or tightness. Transient increase in BP. Hypotension, bradycardia or tachycardia, palpitations, Raynaud’s syndrome and ischemic colitis. Hypersensitivity reactions. Pain or tightness in the chest or angina pain. Cerebrovascular spasm. Mesenteric ischemia, and esophageal constriction. Dysphoria and apathetic sedation.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Ergotamine and its derivatives (including methysergide), MAOIs, St. John's Wort, paracetamol.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of symptoms of idiopathic Parkinson’s disease (paralysis agitans), post-encephalitic parkinsonism, and symptomatic parkinsonism which may follow injury to the nervous system by carbon monoxide or manganese intoxication.
flattened_sections.dose: Discontinue levodopa 12 hrs prior to initiation of carbidopa-levodopa therapy. Patients taking <1,500 mg levodopa a day: Initially carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg 3-4x daily. Patients taking >1,500 mg levodopa a day: Initially carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg 3-4x daily. Maintenance: Individualized and adjusted according to desired therapeutic response. At least 70-100 mg carbidopa per day. When greater proportion of carbidopa is required, 1 tab of carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg may be substituted for each tab of carbidopa 10 mg/levodopa 100 mg. Carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg may be increased by ½ or 1 tab every day or every other day to max 8 tabs/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with non-selective MAOIs. Patients with narrow-angle glaucoma, suspicious and undiagnosed skin lesions or history of melanoma.
flattened_sections.precautions: Development of depression with concomitant suicidal tendencies. Patients with past or current psychoses, CV or pulmonary disease, bronchial asthma, renal, hepatic or endocrine disease, history of MI who have residual atrial, nodal or ventricular arrhythmias, sporadic cases of a symptom complex NMS, chronic wide-angle glaucoma. May increase possibility of upper GI hemorrhage in patients with history of peptic ulcer. Sporadic cases of a symptom complex resembling NMS. Periodic evaluations of hepatic, hematopoietic, CV and renal function, and periodic skin examinations. High protein diet and excessive acidity may delay absorption. Sudden onset of sleep during daily activities. Elevations of liver function tests e.g. alkaline phosphatase, SGOT (AST), SGPT (ALT), lactic dehydrogenase, and bilirubin. Abnormalities in BUN and positive Coombs’ test, creatinine, and uric acid are lower. False positive reaction for urinary ketone bodies. False negative tests may result with the use of glucose-oxidase methods of testing for glucosuria. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn <18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Dyskinesias (e.g. choreiform, dystonic, other involuntary movements), nausea.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Antihypertensive drugs, MAOIs (type A or B), TCAs, D2-receptor antagonists (e.g. phenothiazines, butyrophenones, risperidone) and INH, phenytoin and papaverine, iron salts, metoclopramide.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. Risk factors predisposing to development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Liver dysfunction. Worsening angina and acute MI in patients with severe obstructive CAD. Symptomatic hypotension particularly in with severe aortic stenosis. Increase in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels. Concomitant use with ciclosporin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, HIV protease inhibitors, colchicine. Childn.

flattened_sections.indications: Prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), ischemic complications of unstable angina, and non-Q-wave myocardial infarction (MI). Treatment of acute DVT and acute ST-segment elevation MI.
flattened_sections.dose: Abdominal surgery: 40 mg SC once/day with the initial dose given 2 hrs prior to surgery. Duration of administration: 7-10 days, up to 12 days. Hip or knee replacement surgery: 30 mg SC every 12 hrs with the initial dose given 12-24 hrs after surgery. Hip replacement surgery: 40 mg SC once a day given initially 12 hrs prior to surgery. The initial phase of thromboprophylaxis in hip replacement surgery patients, continued prophylaxis with 40 mg once a day for 3 weeks. Duration of administration: 7-10 days up to 14 days. Patients at risk of thromboembolic complications due to severely restricted mobility during acute illness: 40 mg SC once a day. Duration of administration: 6-11 days, up to 14 days.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with active major bleeding, thrombocytopenia associated with positive in vitro test for anti-platelet antibody.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not administer by IM injection. Do not mix with other injections for infusion. Patients with bleeding diathesis, uncontrolled arterial HTN or history of recent GI ulceration, diabetic retinopathy, and increased risk of hemorrhage. History of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Major hemorrhages e.g. retroperitoneal and intracranial bleeding. Low-weight patients (< 57 kg). Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hemorrhage; mild to moderate thrombocytopenia; mild local irritation, pain, hematoma, ecchymosis, and erythema. Non-hemorrhagic, primarily injection site ecchymoses and hematomas.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Anticoagulants, platelet inhibitors i.e. aspirin, salicylates, NSAIDs (e.g. ketorolac, tromethamine), dipyridamole, or sulfinpyrazone.
flattened_sections.packaging: Solution for injection (SC) 4,000 IU (equiv to 40 mg)/0.4 mL in 1 mL pre-filled syringe, 6,000 IU (equiv to 60 mg)/0.6 mL in 1 mL pre-filled syringe.

indication_long: Treatment of endometriosis.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of endometriosis.
flattened_sections.dose: Start on any day of the menstrual cycle. 1 tab daily without any break, taken preferably at the same time each day; must be taken continuously without regard to vaginal bleeding.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active venous thromboembolic disorder. Present or in history of arterial and CV disease (e.g. MI, IHD). DM with vascular involvement. Presence or history of severe hepatic disease as long as liver function values have not returned to normal. Presence or history of liver tumors (benign or malignant). Known or suspected sex hormone-dependent malignancies. Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not indicated in childn prior to menarche. Decrease in bone mineral density over a treatment of 12 months in adolescents. Women with history of extrauterine pregnancy or impaired tube function. Increased risk of MI and cerebral thromboembolism. Affects menstrual bleeding pattern. May aggravate uterine bleeding in women and adenomyosis uteri or uterine leiomyomata. Patients with history of depression. Withdraw if sustained clinically significant HTN develops. Discontinue if recurrence of cholestatic jaundice and/or pruritus occurred during pregnancy or previous use of sex steroids. Slight effect on peripheral insulin resistance and glucose tolerance. Diabetic women especially with history of gestational DM. Chloasma especially in women with history of chloasma gravidarum. Persistent ovarian follicles may occur. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Increased weight, depressed mood, sleep disorder, nervousness, loss of libido, altered mood, headache, migraine, nausea, abdominal pain, flatulence, abdominal distension, vomiting, acne, alopecia, back pain, breast discomfort, ovarian cyst, hot flushes, uterine or vaginal bleeding including spotting, asthenic conditions, and irritability.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers, phenytoin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampicin, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, felbamate, griseofulvin, products containing St. John's Wort, HIV/HCV protease inhibitors and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, azole antifungals (e.g. itraconazole, voriconazole, fluconazole), verapamil, macrolides (e.g. clarithromycin, erythromycin), diltiazem, grapefruit juice, ketoconazole.

flattened_sections.indications: Palliative treatment of advanced prostate cancer.
flattened_sections.dose: Single SC injection. 7.5 mg (every month); 22.5 mg (every 3 months); 45 mg (every 6 months). See package insert for mixing and administration procedure.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to leuprorelin acetate or other GnRH agonist analogs.
flattened_sections.precautions: QTc prolonging drugs. Use of bupropion and SSRIs. Patients with metastatic vertebral lesions and/or with urinary tract obstruction, congenital long QT syndrome, CHF, frequent electrolyte abnormalities, history of seizures, epilepsy, cerebrovascular disorders, CNS anomalies or tumors. Increased risk of convulsions, developing DM or hyperglycemia, MI, sudden cardiac death, or stroke in men. May cause transient increase in serum concentrations of testosterone during the 1st week of treatment resulting in bone pain, neuropathy, hematuria or bladder outlet obstruction. Monitor serum glucose, glycosylated Hgb (HbA1c), testosterone, and prostate-specific antigen. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. Infertility.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Malaise, fatigue, weakness; dizziness; hot flashes/sweats; urinary frequency, nocturia; nausea, gastroenteritis/colitis; pruritus, clamminess, night sweats, alopecia; arthralgia, myalgia, pain in limb; testicular atrophy, gynecomastia, testicular pain; decreased libido; transient burning/ stinging, pain, erythema, bruising, erythema, induration in injection site; decreased bone density in men.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Diagnostic tests of pituitary gonadotropic and gonadal functions.
flattened_sections.packaging: Lyophilized powder for suspension for injection (SC) 7.5 mg, 22.5 mg, 45 mg.

indication_long: Treatment of chronic hepatitis B in adults an...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of chronic hepatitis B in adults and adolescents ≥12 yrs with at least 35 kg BW.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults and adolescents ≥12 yrs with at least 35 kg BW: 1 tab once daily with food. Treatment duration - HBeAG-positive without cirrhosis: at least 6-12 months after HBe seroconversion (HBeAg loss and HBV DNA loss with anti-HBe detection) is confirmed or until HBs seroconversion or until there is loss of efficacy; HBeAG-negative without cirrhosis: at least until evidence of loss of efficacy occurs.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Does not prevent risk of transmission of HBV through sexual contact or contamination with blood. Patients with decompensated liver disease and have a Child-Pugh score >9 (e.g. class C), cirrhosis, renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min), co-infected with HBV and hepatitis C or D virus or HIV, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Acute exacerbations of hepatitis after treatment discontinuation. Monitor hepatic function at least 6 months after treatment discontinuation. Potential risk of nephrotoxicity. Childn < 12 yrs or weighing < 35 kg. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain/distension, flatulence; fatigue; headache, dizziness; rash, pruritus; increased ALT; arthralgia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Products containing tenofovir alafenamide, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate or adefovir dipivoxil. P-gp inducers (e.g. rifampicin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John's wort). Strong P-gp inhibitors (e.g. itraconazole and ketoconazole). Phenobarbital, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin. Rifampicin, rifapentine, rifabutin. Atazanavir/cobicistat, atazanavir/ritonavir, darunavir/cobicistat, darunavir/ritonavir, lopinavir/ritonavir, tipranavir/ritonavir.

indication_long: Treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) ...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) in adults and childn ≥3 yrs.
flattened_sections.dose: 1 tab once daily with or without food. Do not chew or crush tab. Treatment duration - Adults - without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis: 12 weeks, may add ribavirin for genotype 3 infected patients with compensated cirrhosis; decompensated cirrhosis: 12 weeks (plus ribavirin). Ribavirin dose - Child-Pugh-Turcotte Class B cirrhosis pre-transplant: 1,000 mg/day (weighing < 75 kg) or 1,200 mg/day (weighing ≥75 kg); CPT Class C cirrhosis pre-transplant and CPT Class B or C post-transplant: Initially 600 mg, can be titrated up to max 1,000 mg (weighing < 75 kg) or 1,200 mg (weighing ≥75 kg); genotype 3 infected with compensated cirrhosis: 1,000 mg (weighing < 75 kg) or 1,200 mg (weighing ≥75 kg). Previously failed therapy with an NS5A-containing regimen: 24 weeks (plus ribavirin). Childn 3 to < 18 yrs with ≥30 kg BW: 1 tab once daily for 12 weeks; 17 to < 30 kg BW: 200 mg/50 mg tab once daily for 12 weeks.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Co-administration with strong P-gp or CYP450 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, rifabutin, St. John’s wort, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin). Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients who have previously failed therapy with an NS5A-containing regimen; severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) or ESRD requiring hemodialysis; HCV/HBV co-infection; diabetes; CPT Class C cirrhosis; post-liver transplant. Co-administration with moderate P-gp or CYP inducers (e.g. oxcarbazepine, modafinil, efavirenz) and certain HIV antiretroviral regimens. Severe bradycardia and heart block with amiodarone. Monitor glucose levels within the first 3 months. Childn and adolescents < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, rash.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Antacids (e.g. aluminum or magnesium hydroxide, calcium carbonate); H2-receptor antagonists (e.g. famotidine, cimetidine, nizatidine, ranitidine); PPIs (e.g. omeprazole, lansoprazole, rabeprazole, pantoprazole, esomeprazole); anti-arrhythmics (e.g. amiodarone; digoxin); anticoagulants (e.g. dabigatran, vit K antagonists); anticonvulsants (e.g. carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, oxcarbazepine); antifungals (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, posaconazole, isavuconazole); antimycobacterials (e.g. rifampicin; rifabutin, rifapentine); HIV antiviral agents (e.g. tenofovir, efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir); St. John’s wort; rosuvastatin, other statins.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

indication_long: Control of hyperphosphatemia in adult patient...

flattened_sections.indications: Control of hyperphosphatemia in adult patients receiving hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis, and adult patients with chronic kidney disease not on dialysis with serum phosphorus >1.78 mmol/L.
flattened_sections.dose: Starting dose – Serum phosphorus level 1.78-2.42 mmol/L (5.5-7.5 mg/dL): 2.4 g/day; >2.42 mmol/L (>7.5 mg/dL): 4.8 g/day. Total daily doses are taken in 3 divided doses with meals. Patients previously on phosphate binders (i.e. sevelamer HCl or calcium-based): Give on a gram-for-gram basis with monitoring of serum phosphorus levels. Titration and maintenance: Titrate dose every 2-4 weeks until acceptable serum phosphorus level is reached. Continue treatment based on the need to control serum phosphorus levels; the daily dose is approximately 6 g/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Hypophosphatemia. Bowel obstruction.

indication_long: Hypertension (HTN) - Reduction of blood press...

flattened_sections.indications: Hypertension (HTN) - Reduction of blood pressure and risk of cardiovascular and coronary mortality, including sudden death, and morbidity. Angina pectoris. Disturbance of cardiac rhythm including especially supraventricular tachycardia. Maintenance treatment after myocardial infarction (MI). Functional heart disorders with palpitations. Migraine prophylaxis. 25 mg tab: Symptomatic mild to severe chronic heart failure and adjunct to other heart failure therapy.
flattened_sections.dose: HTN: 50 mg once daily, could be increased to 100-200 mg once daily and/or combined with other hypertensive agents. Angina pectoris: 100-200 mg once daily, can be combined with other anti-anginal agents if needed. Cardiac arrhythmias: 100-200 mg once daily. Maintenance treatment after MI: 200 mg once daily. Functional heart disorders with palpitations: 100 mg once daily, can be increased to 200 mg. Migraine prophylaxis: 100-200 mg once daily. Childn and adolescents >6 yrs: 1 mg/kg, not exceeding 50 mg once daily. Can be increased to max daily dose 2 mg/kg/day. 25 mg tab - Chronic heart failure: Individualized dosage. Initially 25 mg once daily during the first 2 weeks. Double the dose every 2nd weeks up to max 200 mg once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block; patients with unstable decompensated cardiac heart failure (pulmonary edema, hypoperfusion or hypotension), and patients with continuous or intermittent inotropic therapy acting through beta-receptor agonism; clinically relevant sinus bradycardia, sick-sinus syndrome, cardiogenic shock; severe peripheral arterial circulatory disorder. Patients with suspected acute MI as long as the heart rate is < 45 bpm, the P-Q interval is >0.24 secs or the systolic BP is < 100 mmHg.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not give IV administration of verapamil-type CCBs. Patients with asthma. Risk of interfering with carbohydrate metabolism or masking hypoglycemia. May aggravate the symptoms of peripheral arterial circulatory disorders. Pheochromocytoma. Avoid abrupt withdrawal of beta-blockade is hazardous especially in high-risk patients. If there is a need to discontinue treatment, this should preferably be done gradually over at least 2 weeks when the dose is reduced by half in each step down to the final step when a whole 25 mg tab is reduced to a half-tab. The final dose should be taken for at least 4 days before discontinuation. If symptoms occur, a slower withdrawal rate is recommended. Avoid acute initiation of high-dose metoprolol to patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. May impair ability to drive or use machines. Childn < 6 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Fatigue. Bradycardia, postural disorders (very rarely with syncope), cold hands and feet, palpitations; dizziness, headache; nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation; Dyspnea on exertion.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Compounds metabolized by cytochrome P2D6 (e.g. antiarrhythmics, antihistamines, H<sub>2</sub>-receptor antagonists, antidepressants, antipsychotics, and COX2-inhibitors). Rifampicin, alcohol and hydralazine. Sympathetic ganglion-blocking agents, other beta-blockers (e.g. eye drops), or MAOIs. Clonidine. Verapamil and diltiazem. Antiarrhythmic agents (of the quinidine type and amiodarone). Digitalis glycoside. Inhalation anesthetics. Indomethacin or other prostaglandin synthetase inhibiting drugs. Adrenaline. Oral antidiabetics.

brand_info.content: Rx

brand_info.title: Indications
brand_info.content: Adjunct to diet for treatment of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B and triglycerides and to increase HDL-C in primary hypercholesterolemia, combined hyperlipidemia, elevated serum triglyceride levels, and dysbetalipoproteinemia who do not respond adequately to diet. Reduction of total cholesterol and LDL-C in homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia when response to diet and other non-pharmacological measures are inadequate.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: 10-80 mg once daily, may be given with or without food. Primary hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia: 10 mg once daily. Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: 80 mg.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevation of serum transaminase. Pregnancy and lactation.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: History of liver disease. Excessive alcohol consumption. Myopathy, renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Perform liver function tests before therapy and 12 weeks after; then periodically thereafter. Concomitant use with ketoconazole, spironolactone, and cimetidine. Childn <18 yrs.

brand_info.title: Side Effects
brand_info.content: Chest pain, edema, fever, neck rigidity, malaise, photosensitivity reaction; amblyopia, tinnitus, dry eyes, refraction disorder, eye hemorrhage, deafness, glaucoma, parosmia, taste loss and perversion. GI, respiratory, musculoskeletal, skin and appendages, urogenital, CV, hemic and lymphatic system effects. Anaphylaxis, angioneurotic edema, bullous rashes, rhabdomyolysis, fatigue.

brand_info.title: Drug Interactions
brand_info.content: Ciclosporin, fibric acid derivatives, erythromycin, azole antifungals, niacin, grapefruit juice, nelfinavir, ritonavir, saquinavir, phenazine, digoxin, clarithromycin, oral contraceptives, amlodipine, colestipol, antacid, warfarin, CYP3A4 inhibitors.

brand_info.content: Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P14.00), 20 mg (P17.75), 40 mg (P24.50).

indication_long: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glyce...

flattened_sections.indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus; monotherapy or in combination with other oral diabetic agents or insulin.
flattened_sections.dose: 500 mg every 12 hrs or 850 mg once a day. May be increased to max 2 g daily in divided doses as needed. Patient can be titrated from 500 mg-850 mg 2x a day after 2 weeks. SR and ER tab: Initially 500 mg once a day with the evening meal, may be increased weekly in increments of 500 mg. Max 2,000 mg/day. Tab should be swallowed whole, not chewed or crushed.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Unstable or type 1 DM. History of lactic acidosis. Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, including diabetic ketoacidosis, with or without coma. Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Acute conditions that may alter renal function. Acute or chronic disease which may cause tissue hypoxia. Acute or chronic alcoholism. Severe liver disease. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Lactic acidosis. Patients with CHF receiving digoxin and furosemide; renal impairment (eGFR 30-45 mL/min/1.73 m2), clinical or laboratory evidence of hepatic disease. Macrovascular risk reduction. Discontinue prior to an iodinated contrast imaging procedure in patients with eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m2, history of liver disease, alcoholism, or heart failure, or patients who will be administered intra-arterial iodinated contrast. CV collapse, acute CHF, MI, and other conditions characterized by hypoxemia. Temporarily discontinue in patients undergoing surgery; in periods of stress (e.g. fever, trauma, infection). Excessive alcohol intake. Evaluate hematologic parameters before treatment and at least annually. Elderly, debilitated or malnourished patients, or with adrenal or pituitary insufficiency or alcohol intoxication. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Cationic drugs, other antidiabetic drugs, thiazides and other diuretics, nifedipine, beta-blockers, protein-bound drugs, ACE inhibitors, alcohol, clomifene, anticoagulants, iodinated contrast media, glyburide, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, CCBs, isoniazid.
flattened_sections.packaging: Tablet 500 mg (P4.25), 850 mg (P8.00). Film-coated tablet 1 g. Extended-release tablet 1 g. Sustained-release tablet 500 mg.

flattened_sections.indications: Control of generalized convulsive status epilepticus, prevention and treatment of seizures occurring during neurosurgery.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - Status epilepticus loading dose: 15-20 mg PE (phenytoin sodium equivalent) per kg BW administered at 100-150 mg PE/min. Rate should not be >150 mg PE/min. Non-emergent situation loading and maintenance dosing: 10-20 mg PE/kg given IV or IM. Rate should not be >150 mg PE/min. Maintenance dose for status epilepticus or non-emergent situation: 4-6 mg PE/kg/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with sinus bradycardia, SA block, 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree AV block, and Adams-Stokes syndrome. Concomitant use with delavirdine or to the class of non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs).
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not make any adjustment in the recommended doses when substituting fosphenytoin for phenytoin sodium. Do not confuse the amount of drug to be given in PE with the concentration of the drug in the vial. Risk of adverse CV reactions associated with rapid administration (>150 mg PE/min). Not to be used for absence (petit mal) seizures, seizures due to hypoglycemic or other metabolic causes. Patients with renal and/or hepatic disease, or with hypoalbuminemia. Potential to lower serum folate levels. May increase risk of suicidal ideation and/or behavior, all patients should be routinely evaluated for depression, anxiety, and suicidality. Hypotension may occur especially after IV administration at high doses and high rates of administration. Severe CV reactions (e.g. atrial and ventricular conduction depression and ventricular fibrillation). Patients with hypotension and severe myocardial insufficiency. Edema, discoloration, and pain distal to the site of injection ("purple glove syndrome"). May develop hypersensitivity syndrome or drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms. Patients at higher risk for developing hypersensitivity syndrome/drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (e.g. black patients, patients who have experienced syndrome in the past). Patients with family history of syndrome and immunosuppressed patients. Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (e.g. acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis and drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms). Discontinue treatment if rash appears. If rash of a milder type (measles-like or scarlatiniform), therapy may be resumed after the rash has completely disappeared. Discontinue immediately if symptoms of angioedema (e.g. facial, perioral, or upper airway swelling) occur; acute hepatotoxicity. Impaired liver function, or those who are gravely ill may show early signs of toxicity. Hematopoietic complications (e.g. thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, granulocytopenia, agranulocytosis, and pancytopenia with or without bone marrow suppression). May develop lymphadenopathy (local or generalized), including benign lymph node hyperplasia, pseudolymphoma, lymphoma and Hodgkin's disease. May produce confusional states. Exacerbation of porphyria; hyperglycemia. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy. Not recommended for breastfeeding women. Elderly.
flattened_sections.side_effects: CV collapse and/or central nervous system depression. Nystagmus and dizziness; pruritus. Tinnitus, ear disorder, vertigo; visual impairment, vision blurred; nausea, dry mouth, vomiting; pain, asthenia, injection site pain, chills; paresthesia, somnolence, ataxia, headache, tremor, abnormal coordination, dysgeusia, stupor, dysarthria; euphoric mood; ecchymosis; hypotension, vasodilatation.

Epididymo-orchitis and PID: 400 mg 2-3x daily for at least 14 days. GIT and intra-abdominal infections – Diarrhea caused by Shigella spp. and severe traveler’s diarrhea: 400 mg twice daily for 1 day. By Shigella dysenteriae: 400 mg twice daily for 5 days. By Vibrio cholerae: 400 mg twice daily for 3 days. Typhoid fever: 400 mg twice daily for 7 days. Intra-abdominal infections due to G(-): 400 mg 2-3x daily for 5-14 days. Infections of the skin and soft tissue: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 7-14 days. Bone and joint infections: 400 mg 2-3x daily for max 3 months. Neutropenic patients with fever suspected to be due to bacterial infections: 400 mg 2-3x daily continued over the entire period of neutropenia. Inhalation anthrax post-exposure prophylaxis: 400 mg twice daily for 60 days (from B. anthracis exposure). Childn – Cystic fibrosis: 10 mg/kg BW thrice daily for 10-14 days. Max 400 mg. Complicated UTI and pyelonephritis: 6-10 mg/kg thrice daily for 10-21 days. Max 400 mg. Inhalation anthrax post-exposure prophylaxis: 10-15 mg/kg twice daily for 60 days (from B. anthracis exposure). Max 400 mg. Renal impairment – CrCl 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m2: 200-400 mg every 12 hrs. <30 mL/min/1.73 m2: 200-400 mg every 24 hrs. flattened_sections.indications: ICU sedation: Indicated for sedation of initially intubated and mechanically ventilated patients during treatment in an intensive care setting. Procedural sedation: Indicated for sedation of non-intubated patients prior to and/or during surgical and other procedures.
flattened_sections.dose: Administer using a controlled infusion device. Dexmedetomidine concentration after dilution should be 4 mcg/mL. Initiation of ICU sedation – Adults: Loading infusion of 1 mcg/kg over 10 mins; For less invasive procedures: Loading infusion of 0.5 mcg/kg given over 10 mins. Patients >65 yrs: Loading infusion of 0.5 mcg/kg over 10 mins. Maintenance of procedural sedation – Adults: Initiated at 0.6 mcg/kg/hr and titrated to achieve desired clinical effect with doses ranging from 0.2 to 1 mcg/kg/hr. Awake fiberoptic intubation patients: Maintenance infusion of 0.7 mcg/kg/hr is recommended until the endotracheal tube is secured. Elderly, patients with impaired renal or hepatic function: Reduce dose.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with preexisting severe bradycardia disorders (e.g. advanced heart block), or ventricular dysfunction (e.g. ejection fraction <30%) including CHF and cardiac failure. Hypotension in hypovolemic patients, elderly >65 yrs, and diabetic patients. Should not be administered for greater than 24 hrs. Abrupt discontinuation may result in clonidine-like withdrawal symptoms (e.g. nervousness, agitation and headache, accompanied or followed by a rapid rise in blood pressure and elevated catecholamine concentrations in the plasma). Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hypotension, hypertension, bradycardia, dry mouth, and nausea.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Anesthetics, sedatives, hypnotics, opioids; vasodilators, negative chronotropic agents; propofol or midazolam.

flattened_sections.indications: For the control of hyperphosphatemia in adult patients receiving hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis; patients with chronic kidney disease not on dialysis with serum phosphorus >1.78 mmol/L.

Patients with hypothyroidism treated with levothyroxine; hyperparathyroidism; lactose intolerance (hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption). Patients taking anti-arrhythmic or anti-seizure medicinal products. Possible accumulation in long-term chronic treatment (>1 yr). Childn <18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of susceptible infections e.g. bone and joint infections, bronchitis and other lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI), gonorrhea, meningitis, otitis media, peritonitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, skin infections (e.g. soft tissue infections), and urinary tract infections (UTI). Prophylaxis to surgical infections.
flattened_sections.dose: Tab – Adults – Uncomplicated UTI: 125 mg twice daily. RTI: 250-500 mg twice daily. Pneumonia or exacerbations of chronic bronchitis: 1.5 g twice daily or 750 mg twice daily, respectively, in parenteral route followed by oral 500 mg twice daily. Lyme disease: 500 mg twice daily for 20 days. Uncomplicated gonorrhea: 1 g single dose. Childn >2 yrs with otitis media: 250 mg or 15 mg/kg, twice daily. Max 500 mg daily. >3 months: 125 mg or 10 mg/kg, twice daily. Max 250 mg daily. IM/IV - Adults: 750 mg three times daily. Severe infections: 1.5 g thrice daily, may be increased to total dose 3-6 g daily given every 6 hrs. Infants and childn: 30-60 mg/kg/day, may be increased to 100 mg/kg given in 3-4 divided doses. Most infections: 60 mg/kg/day. Renal impairment – CrCl < 20 mL/min: Reduce dose. 10 mL/min: 750 mg once daily. Hemodialysis: A further 750 mg given at the end of dialysis. Continuous peritoneal dialysis: 750 mg twice daily. Susp – Adults – Uncomplicated UTI: 250 mg (1 tsp) twice daily. RTI: 250-500 mg twice daily. Childn >3 months: 250 mg or 10 mg/kg twice daily, max: 250 mg daily. Childn >2 yrs with otitis media: 250 mg or 15 mg/kg twice daily, max: 500 mg daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Cross-sensitivity in patients allergic to penicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics, history of hypersensitivity to other beta-lactam agents, renal impairment. May cause Jarisch-Herxheimer reactions following treatment of Lyme disease, overgrowth of Candida and other non-susceptible microorganisms (e.g. Enterococci and Clostridium difficile), mild to life-threatening pseudomembranous colitis. Pregnancy and lactation. IM/IV: Patients receiving concurrent treatment of potent diuretics. Superinfection. Susp: Patients with renal impairment. Monitor renal and hematological status.
flattened_sections.side_effects: GI disturbances e.g. diarrhea, nausea, vomiting. Overgrowth of Candida. Pseudomembranous colitis. Tab: Erythema multiforme, SJS, toxic epidermal necrolysis. Mild to moderate hearing loss. IM/IV: Pain in IM injection site. Hypersensitivity reactions e.g. skin rashes (maculopapular, urticaria), drug fever, anaphylaxis. Decreased hemoglobin concentration and/or eosinophilia, leukopenia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. High levels of SGOT, SGPT and bilirubin.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Tab and Susp: Probenecid. IM/IV: Diuretics e.g. furosemide and aminoglycoside.
flattened_sections.packaging: Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P63.72). Powder for injection (IM/IV) 750 mg (P362.88). Granules for oral suspension 250 mg/5 mL x 50 mL (P444.67).

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Management of hypertension (HTN) and angina pectoris. Adjunct to standard therapy in symptomatic heart failure.
flattened_sections.dose: HTN - Initial dose: 12.5 mg once daily, increase to 25 mg once daily after two days; Alternative initial dose: 6.25 mg twice daily, increase to 12.5 mg twice daily after 1-2 weeks. May be further increased at intervals of 2 weeks to 50 mg once daily or in divided doses at 2 weeks intervals; Elderly: 12.5 mg once daily. Angina pectoris: 12.5 mg twice daily, increase to 25 mg twice daily after two days. Heart failure: Initially 3.125 mg twice daily with food, double the dose to 6.25 mg twice daily after 2 weeks, then increase gradually to the max tolerated dose not >25 mg twice daily. Mild to moderate heart failure with BW >85 kg: 50 mg twice daily. Severe heart failure or BW <85 kg: Max 25 mg twice daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Unstable/decompensated heart failure; liver dysfunction. Patients with 2<sup>nd</sup>- or 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree AV block (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place); severe bradycardia (<50 bpm); sick sinus syndrome (including SA block); severe hypotension (systolic <85 mmHg); cardiogenic shock and history of bronchospasm or asthma; metabolic acidosis; severe PAD.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not give to patients with bronchospasm or asthma or those with history of obstructive airways disease. 1<sup>st</sup>-degree AV block. Pheochromocytoma without concomitant alpha-adrenoceptor blocking therapy. Abrupt withdrawal may exacerbate angina. Reduced peripheral circulation can produce coldness of the extremities and may exacerbate PVD (e.g. Raynaud's syndrome). Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Heart failure, heart block, and bronchospasm; bradycardia and hypotension. Fatigue and coldness of the extremities.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: ACE inhibitors, CCBs, clonidine; aldesleukin, general anesthetics; NSAIDs; antiarrhythmics; digoxin; insulin and oral hypoglycemics; adrenaline (epinephrine); aluminum salts and bile acid-binding resins such as cholestyramine; barbiturates, rifampicin; cimetidine, erythromycin, fluvoxamine, hydralazine.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). Initial therapy in patients with inadequate glycemic control by diet and exercise alone, or with max tolerated dose of metformin alone. In combination with sulfonylurea in patients inadequately controlled on max tolerated dose of metformin alone and a sulfonylurea. In combination with insulin in patients with inadequate glycemic control with insulin monotherapy or insulin and metformin dual therapy. In patients already receiving an identical combination of gemigliptin and metformin as separate tabs.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosage. 1 tab of 50 mg/500 mg or 50 mg/1g once daily with meals in the evening. Patients who need 50 mg gemigliptin and not currently treated with metformin: Initially 50 mg gemigliptin and 500 mg metformin extended-release once daily with gradual dose escalation. Patients with inadequate glycemic control on metformin monotherapy, dual combination of metformin and sulfonylurea or metformin and insulin: 50 mg gemigliptin and the dose of metformin already being taken. Patients switching from co-administration of gemigliptin and metformin as separate tabs: Initiate the dose already being taken. Max: 50 mg gemigliptin and 2,000 mg metformin. When in combination with sulfonylurea or insulin, use a lower dose of sulfonylurea or insulin.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Renal impairment (serum creatinine ≥15 mg/dL for men, ≥14 mg/dL for women, or abnormal CrCl). CHF requiring medication. For any surgical procedure (except minor procedures not associated with restricted intake of food and fluids) or radiologic studies involving use of IV iodinated contrast materials, temporarily discontinue treatment at least 48 hrs prior to and 48 hrs after the procedure and reinstitute only after renal function has been re-evaluated and found to be normal. Patients with type 1 diabetes or metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis with or without coma, or history of ketoacidosis. Suspend therapy in presence of severe infection or traumatism and not be restarted until the patient’s oral intake has resumed and renal function is normal. Pre-diabetic coma. Debilitated, malnourished, or starved patients, and those with adrenal or pituitary insufficiency. Hepatic impairment. Pulmonary infarction, severe respiratory insufficiency, and any conditions that induce hypoxemia; promptly discontinue if hypoxic states occur. Excessive alcohol, dehydration, GI symptoms e.g. diarrhea and vomiting. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. Gemigliptin: History of pancreatitis. Risk of hypoglycemia with sulfonylurea; severe and disabling arthralgia. Discontinue use if bullous pemphigoid is suspected. Metformin: Lactic acidosis; evaluation of serum electrolytes, ketones, blood glucose, blood pH, lactate, lactate/pyruvate ratio, and metformin may be useful. Hypoglycemia due to deficient caloric intake, strenuous exercise without caloric supplementation, or concomitant use with other glucose-lowering agents (e.g. sulfonylurea and insulin) or alcohol. Patients with inadequate vit B12 or calcium intake or absorption. Concomitant use with cationic drugs.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Dyspepsia, dizziness, dyslipidemia, headache, constipation. Gemigliptin: Arthralgia, nasopharyngitis, bacteriuria, URTI, increased blood amylase and lipase; pyrexia. Metformin: Diarrhea; nausea, vomiting.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Gemigliptin: Metformin (2,000 mg). Pioglitazone. Strong CYP3A4 inducers e.g. rifampicin, dexamethasone, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifabutin and phenobarbital. Ketoconazole. Metformin: Insulin, sulfonylamides, sulfonylureas, alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, anabolic steroids, guanethidine, salicylates (aspirin), beta-blockers (propranolol), MAOIs, ARBs. Epinephrine, sympathomimetics, corticosteroids, thyroid hormones, follicle hormone, estrogen, oral contraceptives, thiazides and other diuretics, pyrazinamide, isoniazid, nicotinic acid, phenothiazines, phenytoin, CCBs. Alcohol or medicinal products that contain alcohol. Iodinated contrast agents. Furosemide. Nifedipine. OCT1 inhibitors (verapamil). OCT1 inducers (rifampicin). OCT2 inhibitors (cimetidine, dolutegravir, lanolazine, trimethoprim, vandetanib, isavuconazole). OCT2 and OCT1 co-inhibitors (crizotinib, olaparib).

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: In combination with oral antidepressant therapy: for treatment-resistant depression (TRD), a major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults who have not responded adequately to at least two different antidepressants of adequate dose and duration to treat the current depressive episode), or for rapid reduction of depressive symptoms in adult patients with MDD who have acute suicidal ideation or behavior.
flattened_sections.dose: For nasal use only. Single-use nasal spray device delivers a total of 28 mg of esketamine in 2 sprays (one spray per nostril). Do not be prime before use. Use 1 device (for a 28 mg dose), 2 devices (for a 56 mg dose), or 3 devices (for an 84 mg dose), with a 5-mins rest between use of each device. TRD - Induction Phase - Week 1-4 (2 treatment sessions/week): Starting day 1 dose of 56 mg; if ≥65 yrs: 28 mg. Subsequent doses of 56 mg or 84 mg. Maintenance Phase - Week 5-8: 56 mg or 84 mg once weekly. From week 9: 56 mg or 84 mg every 2 weeks or once weekly. After depressive symptoms improve, treatment is recommended for at least 6 months. MDD with acute suicidal ideation or behavior: 84 mg twice weekly for 4 weeks. Dose reduction to 56 mg may be done based on tolerability.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with increased BP or intracranial pressure; with known aneurysmal vascular disease (including intracranial, thoracic, or abdominal aorta, or peripheral arterial vessels); with known history of intracranial hemorrhage.
flattened_sections.precautions: Administer under supervision of a healthcare professional. Patients with history of suicide-related events or has significant degree of suicidal ideation; unstable or poorly controlled HTN; with history (within 6 weeks) of CV event including MI, ischemic stroke, or TIA; with hemodynamically significant valvular heart disease e.g. mitral regurgitation, aortic stenosis, or aortic regurgitation; with NYHA class III-IV heart failure of any etiology. Potential for short-term and long-term cognitive impairment and motor impairment. Long-term use. Patients with history of drug abuse or dependence including alcohol. Patients with presence or history of psychosis, mania or bipolar disorder; hyperthyroidism, pulmonary insufficiency, known uncontrolled brady- or tachyarrhythmias. May impair the ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Dissociation, dizziness, nausea, sedation, headache, dysgeusia, hypoesthesia, vertigo, anxiety, increased BP, and vomiting.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CNS depressants e.g. benzodiazepines, opioids, and alcohol. Psychostimulants e.g. amphetamines, methylphenidate, modafinil, and armodafinil. MAOIs e.g. tranylcypromine, selegiline, and phenelzine. CYP3A4 inhibitor e.g. clarithromycin (oral). CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 inducer e.g. rifampicin (oral). CYP3A4 substrate e.g. midazolam (oral). CYP2B6 substrate e.g. bupropion (oral). Other nasally administered medicinal products e.g. oxymetazoline and mometasone furoate.

indication_long: Treatment of arterial hypertension (HTN) and ...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of arterial hypertension (HTN) and congestive heart failure. Prevention of stroke recurrence in combination with indapamide in patients with history of cerebrovascular disease. Reduction of risk of cardiovascular events in patients with stable coronary artery disease (CAD).
flattened_sections.dose: HTN: As monotherapy or in combination with other antihypertensives. Initially 5 mg/day in the morning. Patients with strongly activated RAAS (renovascular HTN, salt and/or vol depletion, cardiac decompensation, or severe HTN): Initially 2.5 mg. May increase to 10 mg/day after 1 month. Concomitant treatment with diuretics: Discontinue diuretic 2-3 days before start of Coversyl. If not possible, initiate Coversyl at 2.5 mg, monitor renal function and serum potassium, and adjust subsequent dose according to blood pressure response. Elderly: Initially 2.5 mg. May increase to 5 mg after 1 month, then 10 mg if necessary depending on renal function. Symptomatic heart failure: Initially 2.5 mg/day in the morning, may increase to 5 mg/day after 2 weeks if tolerated. Adjust dose based on clinical response. Stable CAD: Initially 5 mg/day for 2 weeks, then increase to 10 mg/day if tolerated depending on renal function. Elderly: 2.5 mg/day for 1 week, then 5 mg/day the next week, before increasing to 10 mg/day if well tolerated depending on renal function. Renal impairment - CrCl ≥60 mL/min: 5 mg/day; 30-60 mL/min: 2.5 mg/day; 15-30 mL/min: 2.5 mg every other day; < 15 mL/min: 2.5 mg on the day of dialysis. Take after dialysis on hemodialysis patients. Take in the morning before a meal.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with history of ACE inhibitor-associated angioedema, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema, significant bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney, or those receiving extracorporeal treatments leading to contact of blood with negatively charged surfaces. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), and sacubitril/valsartan (therapy must not be initiated until after 36 hrs of last dose). Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters).
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with renal/hepatic impairment and failure; galactose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption, total lactase deficiency; collagen vascular disease, undergoing immunosuppressant therapy, treated with allopurinol or procainamide, or combination of these factors; primary hyperaldosteronism, diabetes, mitral valve stenosis, obstruction in the outflow of the left ventricle (e.g. aortic stenosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy); at high risk of symptomatic hypotension; receiving desensitization treatment (e.g. hymenoptera venom); on hemodialysis or underwent kidney transplantation. LDL-apheresis with dextran. Neutropenia/agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia, anemia, hyperkalemia. Non-productive, persistent cough. Unstable angina pectoris, hypotension. May impair ability to drive or operate the machinery. Black patients. Childn and adolescents < 18 yrs. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Dizziness, headache, paresthesia, vertigo, visual disturbances, tinnitus, hypotension, cough, dyspnea, abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, dysgeusia, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, pruritus, rash, muscle cramps, asthenia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: mTOR inhibitors (e.g. sirolimus, everolimus, temsirolimus), gliptins, oral antidiabetics or insulin, lithium, potassium and non-potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, ARBs, aliskiren, sacubitril/valsartan, NSAIDs (including aspirin >3 g/day), heparins, immunosuppressants (e.g. ciclosporin, tacrolimus), trimethoprim, co-trimoxazole, etramustine, baclofen, antihypertensives and vasodilators, TCAs, antipsychotics, anesthetics, sympathomimetics, injectable gold (sodium aurothiomalate).
flattened_sections.packaging: Film-coated tablet 5 mg x 30s (P927.01), 10 mg x 30s (P1,568.53).

indication_long: Treatment of symptomatic anemia associated wi...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of symptomatic anemia associated with chronic renal failure (CRF). Treatment of anemia in patients receiving chemotherapy and to reduce transfusion requirements. To increase the yield of autologous blood in adults in pre donation program (given only to patients with moderate anemia [Hgb 10-13 g/dL or 6.2-8.1 mmol/L], no iron deficiency). Reduce exposure to allogeneic blood transfusions in non-iron deficient adults with anticipated high-risk transfusion complications who will undergo major elective orthopedic surgery (given to patients with moderate anemia and do not have an autologous pre donation program).
flattened_sections.dose: Patients with CRF (available venous access: IV; no available venous access: SC) - Starting dose - Adults: 50-100 IU/kg 3x a week; Childn: 25-50 IU/kg 3x a week. Correction phase: 50 IU/kg 3x a week. Adjust dose in increments or decrements of 25 IU/kg 3x a week at intervals of 4 weeks. Maintenance phase: Desired Hgb levels is 10-12 g/dL (6.2-7.5 mmol/L). Recommended total weekly dose is 75-300 IU/kg. Adult cancer patients with anemia (Hgb < 10 g/dL): Initially, 150 IU/kg SC 3x a week. If after 4 weeks, Hgb increased at least 1 g/dL (0.62 mmol/L) or reticulocytes count increased ≥40,000 cells/microL above baseline, maintain dosage. Increase to 300 IU/kg 3x a week if Hgb increased < 1mg/dL (<0.62 mmol/L) and the reticulocytes count increased < 4,000 cells/microL. If after an additional 4 weeks with 300 IU/kg 3x a week, Hgb increased ≥1 g/dL and reticulocytes count increased < 40,000 cells/microL, maintain dosage. If Hgb increased < 1 g/dL and reticulocytes count increased < 40,000 cells/microL, discontinue treatment. Adult surgery patients in an autologous pre-donation program: 300-600 IU/kg IV injection 2x a week for 3 weeks with at least 200 mg of elemental iron. Adults scheduled for elective surgery: 600 IU/kg SC injection weekly for 3 weeks (Days 21, 14, and 7) prior and the day of surgery. If planned time before surgery is shortened to < 3 weeks, administer 300 IU/kg daily for 10 consecutive days prior and the day of surgery and for 4 days immediately after surgery.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to epoetin alfa, and products derived from mammalian cells or albumin. Uncontrolled HTN. Patients scheduled for major elective surgery, not participating in autologous blood pre-donation and not having CAD, PAD, carotid arterial disease or stroke, including patients with recent MI or stroke. Surgical patients who for any reason cannot receive adequate antithrombotic prophylaxis. Patients developing pure red cell aplasia with any erythropoietin.
flattened_sections.precautions: Control BP before initiation and during treatment. Advice patients on importance of compliance with antihypertensive therapy and dietary restrictions. Patients with epilepsy, history of seizures, conditions associated with predisposition to seizure activity as CNS infections or brain metastases. Patients with pure red cell aplasia receiving erythropoietin via SC injection. Patients with gout and chronic liver disease. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Increased BP or worsening of pre-existing HTN. Increased incidence of thrombotic vascular events. Hypersensitivity reactions, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, pyrexia, chills, injection site reactions, headache and flu-like syndrome.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Ciclosporin. Anti-anemia agents. Drugs lowering erythropoiesis.

flattened_sections.indications: For contraception. Treatment of menorrhagia, secondary amenorrhea, and mild to moderate endometriosis.
flattened_sections.dose: IM injection. Contraception and menorrhagia: 150 mg/mL within first 7 days of cycle or within first 4 weeks after giving birth or delay until 6 weeks after giving birth if breastfeeding. Secondary amenorrhea: 5-10 mg daily for about 5-10 days until 2 days before menstruation. Mild to moderate endometriosis: 50 mg weekly or 10 mg every 2 weeks for at least 6 months.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. History or current risk of arterial disease and thromboembolic disorders. Cerebrovascular disease. Hormone-dependent neoplasm. Hepatic impairment especially severe porphyria. After recent evacuation of hydatidiform mole. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Bone density loss. Not recommended as long-term (>2 yrs) contraceptive method unless other options are inadequate. Breast cancer, vaginal bleeding, fluid retention. Patients with asthma; cardiac or renal impairment; type 2 DM, history of depression; epilepsy, HTN, hepatic dysfunction, migraine, past ectopic pregnancy, masking of climacteric conditions that reduce bone mineral that may cause osteoporotic fractures. Discontinue use in sudden partial or complete loss of vision, onset of proptosis, diplopia especially if there is papilledema or retinal vascular lesions on examination.  May affect plasma, urinary steroid, gonadotropin levels, sex-hormone binding globulin concentrations, coagulation test values for prothrombin, protein-bound iodine and T3 uptake values.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Rise in BP, headache, fatigue, dizziness. PMS, irregular menstruation. Changes in libido, appetite and weight; cystitis-like syndrome. Nervousness. flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Antibiotics that induce liver enzyme production. Barbiturates, carbamazepine, felbamate, griseofulvin, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin, St. John’s wort, topiramate. Aminoglutethimide.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.
