flattened_sections.indications: Prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adults who have undergone elective hip or knee replacement surgery; of stroke and systemic embolism in adults with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) with one or more risk factors e.g. prior stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), ≥75 yrs, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class ≥II). Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE in adults.
flattened_sections.dose: Prevention of VTE - Elective hip or knee replacement surgery: 2.5 mg twice daily, should be taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. Duration of treatment - Hip replacement surgery: 32-38 days; Knee replacement surgery: 10-14 days. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with NVAF: 5 mg twice daily and 2.5 mg twice daily in patients with at least 2 of the following characteristics: ≥80 yrs, BW ≤60 kg, serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL (133 micromole/L). Severe renal impairment (CrCl 15-29 mL/min): 2.5 mg twice daily. Treatment of DVT and PE: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE: 2.5 mg twice daily after 6 months of treatment for DVT or PE. Switching treatment - Vit K antagonist (VKA) to apixaban: Discontinue VKA, initiate apixaban tabs when INR is <2; Apixaban to VKA therapy: Co-administration of apixaban tabs and VKA therapy until the INR is ≥2. Patients undergoing cardioversion but not previously treated with anticoagulants and initiating treatment with apixaban: 5 mg twice daily for at least 2.5 days (5 single doses) before cardioversion, reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily if patient meets the criteria for dose reduction. If cardioversion is required before 5 doses of apixaban can be administered, give 10 mg loading dose, followed by 5 mg twice daily, reduce to 5 mg loading dose, then 2.5 mg twice daily if patient meets the criteria for dose reduction. Administer loading dose 2 hrs prior to cardioversion.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active clinically significant bleeding. Hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk. Lesion or condition if considered a significant risk factor for major bleeding. Concomitant use with other anticoagulant agents.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with conditions with increased risk of hemorrhage, prosthetic heart valves, history of thrombosis diagnosed with antiphospholipid syndrome; triple positive results for lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin antibodies and anti-beta 2-glycoprotein I antibodies; pulmonary embolism and are hemodynamically unstable; active cancer; severe renal impairment; low BW <60 kg; hepatic impairment and elevated liver enzymes; undergoing hip fracture surgery; rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Spinal/epidural anesthesia or puncture. Concomitant use with antiplatelets, SSRIs, SNRIs, NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin), other platelet aggregation inhibitors (following surgery), thrombolytic agents (for treatment of acute ischemic stroke), CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors and inducers. Discontinue at least 48 hrs prior to elective surgery or invasive procedures with moderate or high risk of bleeding and 24 hrs prior to invasive procedures with a low risk of bleeding. Discontinuing therapy may increase risk of thrombosis. Elderly. Childn <18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Anemia, hemorrhage, hematoma, nausea, confusion. Treatment of DVT and PE and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE: Thrombocytopenia, epistaxis, increased GGT and ALT, skin rash, hematuria. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with NVAF: Epistaxis, increased GGT, hematuria.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors (e.g. azole-antimycotics, HIV protease inhibitors, diltiazem, naproxen, clarithromycin, amiodarone, fluconazole, verapamil, quinidine) and inducers (e.g. rifampicin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John’s wort), anticoagulants, platelet aggregation inhibitors, SSRIs or SNRIs, NSAIDs, P2Y12 inhibitors (e.g. aspirin), thrombolytic agents, GPIIb/IIIa receptor antagonists, thienopyridines (e.g. clopidogrel), dipyridamole, dextran, sulfinpyrazone, activated charcoal; clotting tests.

indication_long: Adults and childn: Treatment of newly ...

flattened_sections.indications: Adults and childn: Treatment of newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome (bcr-abl) positive (Ph+) chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) for whom bone marrow transplantation is not considered as the 1st-line treatment; Ph+ CML in chronic phase after failure of interferon-alpha therapy, or in accelerated phase or blast crisis; newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL) integrated with chemotherapy. Adults: Treatment of relapsed or refractory Ph+ ALL as monotherapy; myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative diseases (MDS/MPD) associated with platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) gene re-arrangements; advanced hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES) and/or chronic eosinophilic leukemia (CEL) with FIP1L1-PDGFR-alpha rearrangement; unresectable dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) and with recurrent and/or metastatic DFSP who are not eligible for surgery.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults – CML - Chronic phase: 400 mg/day, may be increased to 600 or 800 mg/day; Accelerated phase or blast crisis: 600 mg/day, may be increased to max 800 mg (400 mg twice daily); Ph+ ALL: 600 mg/day; MDS/MPD: 400 mg/day; HES/CEL: 100 mg/day, may be increased to 400 mg; DFSP: 800 mg/day. Childn – CML - Chronic and advanced phase: 340 mg/m2 once daily or may be divided into two doses (one in the morning and one in the evening), may be increased to 570 mg/m2 daily. Max 800 mg; Ph+ ALL: 340 mg/m2 daily. Max 600 mg. Hepatic impairment: 400 mg/day, may be reduced if not tolerated. Renal impairment: Initially 400 mg/day, may be reduced if not tolerated or increased for lack of efficacy. For patients unable to swallow tabs, tabs may be dispersed in sufficient vol of water or apple juice.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with hepatic dysfunction, cardiac dysfunction or disease, risks for cardiac failure, history of renal failure. Thyroidectomy patients on levothyroxine replacement therapy. May induce hypothyroidism, liver injury, severe fluid retention, GI and intra-tumoral hemorrhages in patients with GIST, gastric antral vascular ectasia, TLS, reactivation of HBV in chronic carriers. Concomitant use with protease inhibitors, azole antifungals, certain macrolides, CYP3A4 substrates with a narrow therapeutic window (e.g. cyclosporine, pimozide, tacrolimus, sirolimus, ergotamine, diergotamine, fentanyl, alfentanil, terfenadine, bortezomib, docetaxel, quinidine) or warfarin, other coumarin derivatives, CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. dexamethasone, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, phenobarbital, St. John’s wort). Perform ECG and determine serum troponin in patients with HES/CEL and MDS/MPD before treatment. Correct clinically significant dehydration and treat high uric acid levels prior to treatment. Avoid exposure to direct sunlight. Discontinue if thrombotic microangiopathy develops. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception. Pregnancy and lactation. pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

General contraindication to infusion therapy (e.g. acute pulmonary edema, hyperhydration and decompensated cardiac insufficiency and hypotonic dehydration). flattened_sections.precautions: Monitor lipid elimination. CBC and coagulation should be monitored if given in long periods. In patients with renal insufficiency, control phosphate and potassium intake. Any signs or symptoms of anaphylactic reactions (e.g. fever, shivering, rash or dyspnea). May interfere with certain laboratory measurements (e.g. bilirubin, lactate dehydrogenase, oxygen saturation, hemoglobin). In malnourished patients, may precipitate fluid shifts resulting in pulmonary edema and CHF. Should not be given together with blood or blood products in the same infusion set. categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

flattened_sections.indications: Management of conditions associated with progesterone insufficiency: dysmenorrhea, endometriosis, infertility, irregular menstrual cycles, and pre-menstrual syndrome (PMS). Management of dysfunctional bleeding or secondary amenorrhea, or in association with estrogen in hormone replacement therapy (HRT).
flattened_sections.dose: Dysfunctional uterine bleeding - To arrest bleeding episode: 10 mg twice daily for 5-7 days. For continuous treatment: 10 mg twice daily from day 11-25 of the cycle. Secondary amenorrhea, irregular cycles: 10 mg twice daily from day 11-25. PMS: 10 mg twice daily from day 12-26 of the cycle. Endometriosis, dysmenorrhea: 10 mg twice daily from day 5-25 of the cycle. Infertility due to luteal insufficiency: 10 mg twice daily from day 11-25 of the cycle. Treatment should be maintained for at least 3 consecutive cycles. HRT: 10 mg daily for the 14 days of each 28-day estrogen treatment cycle, may be increased to 10 mg twice daily if either early withdrawal bleeding occurs or if endometrial biopsy reveals inadequate progestational response.

flattened_sections.side_effects: Migraine, headache, nausea. Disturbed menstruation, painful/sensitive breast.

Max dose per administration: ≤4 mg. Max duration: 10 days. Childn >5 yrs: Up to 6 mg/day divided into 1-4 doses; 6 months-5 yrs: 1.5-4 mg/day divided into 1-4 doses. pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

Empiric therapy for febrile neutropenia.
flattened_sections.dose: May be administered IV or IM. Moderate to severe pneumonia - Adults and childn >40 kg: 1-2 g; Childn < 40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 10 days. Uncomplicated or complicated UTIs including pyelonephritis and/or concurrent bacteremia - Mild to moderate: Adults and childn >40 kg: 500 mg-1 g; Childn < 40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 7-10 days; Severe: Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn < 40 kg: < 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 7-10 days. Complicated intra-abdominal infections (in combination with metronidazole) - Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn < 40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 7-10 days. Empiric therapy for febrile neutropenia - Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn ≤40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 8 hrs for 7 days or until resolution of neutropenia. In patients whose fever resolves but remain neutropenic for >7 days, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated. Very severe or life-threatening infections - Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn ≤40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 8 hrs for 7-10- days. More severe infections may require longer treatment. Renal impairment - CrCl 30-60 mL/min: Mild to moderate UTI: 500 mg daily; Mild to moderate infections other than UTI: 1 g daily; Severe infections: 2 g every 24 hrs; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 2 g every 12 hrs; 11-29 mL/min: Mild to moderate infections including UTI: 500 mg; Severe infections: 1 g; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 2 g. All doses administered every 24 hrs; < 11 mL/min: Mild to moderate infections including UTI: 250 mg; Severe infections: 500 mg; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 1 g. All doses administered every 24 hrs; CAPD: Mild to moderate UTI: 500 mg; Mild to moderate infections other than UTI: 1 g; Severe infections: 2 g; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 2 g. All doses administered every 48 hrs; Hemodialysis: 1 g on Day 1, then 500 mg every day for all infections except febrile neutropenia (1 g every 24 hrs). Dose should be administered after hemodialysis at the same time each day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with renal or hepatic impairment; high risk of severe infections, underlying malignancy, severe or prolonged neutropenia; poor nutritional state; receiving protracted course of antimicrobials or previously stabilized on anticoagulants. CDAD, colitis; encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures, renal failure; fall in prothrombin activity. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms during prolonged use. Childn ≤16 yrs. Elderly. brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: May be administered IV or IM. Moderate to severe pneumonia - Adults and childn >40 kg: 1-2 g; Childn < 40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 10 days. Uncomplicated or complicated UTIs including pyelonephritis and/or concurrent bacteremia - Mild to moderate: Adults and childn >40 kg: 500 mg-1 g; Childn < 40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 7-10 days; Severe: Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn < 40 kg: < 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 7-10 days. Complicated intra-abdominal infections (in combination with metronidazole) - Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn < 40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 7-10 days. Empiric therapy for febrile neutropenia - Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn ≤40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 8 hrs for 7 days or until resolution of neutropenia. In patients whose fever resolves but remain neutropenic for >7 days, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated. Very severe or life-threatening infections - Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn ≤40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 8 hrs for 7-10- days. More severe infections may require longer treatment. Renal impairment - CrCl 30-60 mL/min: Mild to moderate UTI: 500 mg daily; Mild to moderate infections other than UTI: 1 g daily; Severe infections: 2 g every 24 hrs; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 2 g every 12 hrs; 11-29 mL/min: Mild to moderate infections including UTI: 500 mg; Severe infections: 1 g; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 2 g. All doses administered every 24 hrs; < 11 mL/min: Mild to moderate infections including UTI: 250 mg; Severe infections: 500 mg; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 1 g. All doses administered every 24 hrs; CAPD: Mild to moderate UTI: 500 mg; Mild to moderate infections other than UTI: 1 g; Severe infections: 2 g; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 2 g. All doses administered every 48 hrs; Hemodialysis: 1 g on Day 1, then 500 mg every day for all infections except febrile neutropenia (1 g every 24 hrs). categories.title: A

categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

indication_long: For locally advanced or metastatic non-small ...

flattened_sections.indications: For locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), first-line therapy alone or in combination with cisplatin; cervical cancer in combination with cisplatin; epithelial ovarian carcinoma in combination with carboplatin in patients with relapsed disease following a recurrence-free interval of at least 6 months after platinum-based, first-line therapy; adenocarcinoma of pancreas; 5-FU refractory pancreatic cancer. Treatment of patients with bladder cancer; advanced breast cancer; unresectable, locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who have relapsed following adjuvant/neoadjuvant chemotherapy in combination with paclitaxel or following chemotherapy for metastatic disease as monotherapy. Has shown activity in renal cancer, alone or in combination; advanced small cell lung cancer and advanced refractory testicular cancer.
flattened_sections.dose: NSCLC – Monotherapy: 1,000 mg/m2 IV infusion for 30 mins. Repeat once weekly for 3 weeks, followed by 1-week rest period. Repeat 4-week cycle; Combination with cisplatin (2 dosage schedules) - 3-week cycle: 1,250 mg/m2 IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1 and 8, followed by 1 week rest period, then repeat cycle; 4-week cycle: 1,000 mg/m2 IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period, then repeat cycle; With carboplatin: 1,000 or 1,200 mg/m2, given by 30-min infusion on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. Carboplatin is given on day 1 after gemcitabine. Pancreatic cancer: 1,000 mg/m2 IV infusion for 30 mins. Repeat once weekly up to 7 weeks, followed by 1 week of rest. On subsequent cycles, give inj once weekly for 3 consecutive weeks out of every 4 weeks. Bladder cancer - Monotherapy: 1,250 mg/m2 IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Repeat 4-week cycle; Combination with cisplatin: 1,000 mg/m2 IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1, 8 and 15, followed by 1-week rest period for 28 day cycle; Cisplatin: 70 mg/m2 at day 2. Repeat 4-week cycle. Breast cancer – Combination with paclitaxel: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 over approx 3-hr IV infusion, followed by gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m2 IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. Patients should have ≥1,500 x 106/L absolute granulocyte count prior to initiation of combination therapy. Cervical cancer (neoadjuvant treatment and metastatic disease) – Combination with cisplatin: Cisplatin 70 mg/m2 on day 1, followed by gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 every 21 days. Repeat 3-week cycle; Combination therapy using radiation – with cisplatin: 40 mg/m2, followed immediately by gemcitabine 125 mg/m2 IV infusion once weekly for 6 weeks (days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, and 36), 1-2 hrs before concurrent pelvic radiation therapy. Ovarian cancer – Combination with carboplatin: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV infusion for 30 mins on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. After gemcitabine, give carboplatin on day 1 to attain target AUC of 4 mg/mL min.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with renal and hepatic impairment; concurrent liver metastases or pre-existing history of hepatitis, alcoholism, liver cirrhosis. Can suppress bone marrow function. Induce hemolytic uremic syndrome, adult respiratory distress syndrome, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. Discontinue when capillary leak syndrome, interstitial pneumonitis, pulmonary edema occur. Monitor platelet, leukocyte, and granulocyte counts prior to each dose; renal and hepatic function periodically. Childn. Elderly.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia. Abnormal liver function tests, nausea, vomiting, mild proteinuria, hematuria, rash, fever, headaches, chills, myalgia, asthenia, anorexia, edema/peripheral edema, alopecia, cough, rhinitis, malaise, sweating, diarrhea, stomatitis, febrile neutropenia, dyspnea.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis to reduce risk of fractures.
flattened_sections.dose: 1 tab once a month, on the same date each month. Taken 60 mins before the first food or drink (other than water) or any other oral medication or supplementation (including calcium). Swallowed whole only with full glass of plain water while sitting or standing in an upright position. Do not lie down 60 mins after. Do not chew or suck tab.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Uncorrected hypocalcemia. Abnormalities of esophagus which delay esophageal emptying (e.g. stricture or achalasia). Unable to stand or sit upright for at least 60 mins. Rare hereditary galactose intolerance.
flattened_sections.precautions: Ensure adequate intake of calcium and vit D. Correct preexisting hypocalcemia and disturbances of bone and mineral metabolism prior initiation of therapy. Patients with renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min); active upper GI problems (e.g. Barrett’s esophagus, dysphagia, other esophageal disease, gastritis, duodenitis or ulcers); requiring dental procedures. Concomitant use of NSAIDs. Severe esophageal adverse reactions; osteonecrosis of the jaw and external auditory canal; atypical fractures of the femur. Discontinue if dysphagia, odynophagia, retrosternal pain, new or worsening heartburn. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: GERD, diarrhea, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, nausea, flatulence, headache, influenza-like illness, fatigue, muscle cramps, musculoskeletal pain, arthralgia, myalgia, musculoskeletal stiffness, rash.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Calcium supplements, antacids, products with multivalent cations (e.g. aluminum, magnesium, iron).

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.description: The FreeStyle Freedom Lite Blood Glucose Meter is for self-testing and for use by healthcare professionals for people with diabetes mellitus (DM) at home as an aid in monitoring the effectiveness of DM control program.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of candidal vulvovaginitis due to Candida albicans, in bacterial vaginosis due to anaerobic bacteria and Gardnerella vaginalis, in trichomonal vaginitis due to Trichomonas vaginalis and in mixed vaginal infections.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults (including Elderly ≥65 yrs): Vaginally, administer 1 vaginal suppository in morning and at night, in a supine position for 7 days. Recurrent case of vaginitis or vaginitis resistant to treatment: Administer 1 vaginal suppository once daily in the evening for 14 days. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment: Dose adjustment is required. Application instruction: Insert the ovule high into the vagina using disposable finger stalls provided in the package. Do not swallow or apply by other routes.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with epilepsy or porphyria. Severe liver function impairment. Childn <18 yrs. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: For vaginal use only. Patients with alteration of hematopoietic function, with CNS and peripheral nervous system disorders. Simultaneous treatment of sexual partner is recommended and serves as prophylaxis for reinfection. Administration of vaginal suppositories can reduce the efficacy of local contraception (e.g. preservatives, vaginal diaphragms) due to interactions of the suppository base with the latex. Avoid sexual contact and use of alcohol during treatment. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.dose: HTN, hypertensive type II diabetics with proteinuria ≥0.5 g/day: Initial and maintenance dose of 50 mg once daily. May be increased to 100 mg once daily in the morning. HF: Initially 12.5 mg once daily, titrated at weekly intervals up to max 150 mg once daily. Reduction in the risk of stroke in hypertensive adults with left ventricular hypertrophy: Initially 50 mg once daily, added with low dose of HCTZ and/or dose is increased to 100 mg once daily. Intravascular volume depletion: Initially 25 once daily. History of hepatic impairment: Lower dose. Childn 6-18 yrs with >20 to < 50 kg BW: 25 mg once daily; >50 kg: 50 mg once daily, may be increased to max 100 mg once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with aliskiren-containing products in DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters).
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with history of angioedema; recent kidney transplantation; HF and concomitant severe renal impairment, severe HF (NYHA class IV), HF and symptomatic life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias; aortic or mitral stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Not recommended in primary hyperaldosteronism. Changes in renal function (e.g., renal failure) in RAAS-dependent patients (e.g., severe cardiac insufficiency or pre-existing renal dysfunction). Increased blood urea and serum creatinine in bilateral renal artery stenosis of the artery to a solitary kidney. MI or stroke in ischemic CV and cerebrovascular disease. Correct volume and/or sodium depletion and electrolyte imbalances before administration. Monitor plasma concentration of potassium and CrCl in patients with HF and CrCl 30-50 mL/min. Childn < 6 yrs; GFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Lactation.

indication_long: Essential HTN. Chronic stable angina pectoris...

flattened_sections.indications: Essential HTN. Chronic stable angina pectoris. Adjunctive treatment of moderate to severe stable CHF.
flattened_sections.dose: Essential HTN - Adults: Initially 12.5 mg once daily for first two days, continued at 25 mg/day; Elderly: 12.5 mg once daily as initial and maintenance dose. May be further increased gradually at intervals of ≥2 weeks. Max 25 mg as single dose and max 50 mg daily. Chronic stable angina pectoris - Adults and elderly: 12.5 mg twice daily for first two days, continued at 25 mg twice daily (max dose for elderly). May be further increased gradually at intervals of ≥2 weeks (adults). HF: 3.125 mg twice daily for 2 weeks, may be increased slowly with intervals of not < 2 weeks up to 6.25 mg twice daily, then up to 12.5 mg twice daily, and finally up to 25 mg twice daily. Max 25 mg twice daily for BW < 85 kg; 50 mg twice daily for BW >85 kg if HF is not severe. Taken with food in patients with HF.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. HF (NYHA Class IV) with marked fluid retention or overload requiring IV inotropic. COPD with bronchial obstruction. Clinically significant hepatic dysfunction. Bronchial asthma. 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block. Severe bradycardia (< 50 bpm). Sick sinus syndrome (including sinoatrial block). Cardiogenic shock. Severe hypotension (< 85 mmHg SBP). Prinzmetal’s angina. Untreated pheochromocytoma. Metabolic acidosis. Severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbance. Concomitant IV verapamil or diltiazem. Rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, fructose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt withdrawal. CHF treated with digitalis; suspected Prinzmetal’s angina; COPD with risk of bronchospasms not treated with oral or inhalation drug; wearing contact lenses; history of serious hypersensitivity and undergoing desensitization therapy; psoriasis; peripheral vascular diseases; Raynaud’s syndrome; poor metabolizers of debrisoquine; pheochromocytoma; 1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block; use of anesthetics. Monitor patients with severe HF, salt and vol-depleted, elderly, or low basic BP for 2 hrs after treatment initiation or dose increase. Hypotension. Worsening of HF or fluid retention. May mask symptoms and signs of acute hypoglycemia and thyrotoxicosis. Bradycardia. Impaired blood glucose control in DM and HF. Manage symptoms due to worsening HF or hypotension due to vasodilation before dose increase. Reduce dose or discontinue therapy if significant worsening renal function occurs. Do not administer in labile or secondary HTN, orthostasis, acute inflammatory heart disease, concomitant alpha 1-receptor antagonist and alpha 2-receptor agonist. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Dizziness, headache, cardiac failure, hypotension, asthenia, bronchitis, pneumonia, URTI, UTI, anemia, increased weight, hypercholesterolemia, hyperglycemia/hypoglycemia (in pre-existing DM), depression, depressed mood, visual impairment, decreased lacrimation, eye irritation, bradycardia, edema, hypervolemia, fluid overload, orthostatic hypotension, peripheral circulation disturbances (cold extremities, peripheral vascular disease, exacerbation of intermittent claudication and Raynauld’s phenomenon) dyspnea, pulmonary edema, asthma, pain in extremities, renal failure and function abnormalities in diffuse vascular and/or underlying renal insufficiency, pain.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Diltiazem, cimetidine, antiarrhythmics, dihydropyridines, nitrates, cardiac glycosides, other antihypertensives, antidiabetics, clonidine, inhalational anesthetics, NSAIDs, estrogens, corticosteroids, CYP450 inducers (e.g., rifampicin, barbiturates) and inhibitors (e.g., cimetidine, ketoconazole, fluoxetine haloperidol, verapamil, erythromycin), alpha- and beta-sympathomimetics, ergotamine, neuromuscular blockers.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of schizophrenia. Acute treatment of manic and mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder, maintenance treatment of bipolar I disorder, both as monotherapy and as adjunct to either lithium or valproate. Adjunctive for major depressive disorder (MDD). Irritability associated with autistic disorder. Tourette’s disorder.
flattened_sections.dose: Schizophrenia - Adults: Initially 10 or 15 mg/day once daily. Effective dose range: 10-30 mg/day. Adolescents (13-17 yrs): 10 mg/day. Initially 2 mg, titrated to 5 mg after 2 days then to 10 mg after 2 additional days. Dose may be increased in 5 mg increments. Bipolar I disorder - Adults: Initially 15 mg once daily as monotherapy and 10-15 mg once daily as adjunct with lithium or valproate. Recommended target dose is 15 mg/day may be increased to 30 mg/day based on clinical response. Childn 10-17 yrs: Initially 2 mg/day, titrated to 5 mg/day after 2 days then to 10 mg/day after 2 additional days, may be increased in 5 mg/day increments. Adjunctive treatment of MDD - Adults: Initially 2-5 mg/day. Dose range: 2-15 mg/day. Adjust dose gradually by 5 mg/day at intervals not <1 week. Irritability associated with autistic disorder - Childn 6-17 yrs: 5-15 mg/day. Initially 2 mg/day, increased to 5 mg/day, then 10 or 15 mg/day, if needed. Adjust dose gradually by 5 mg/day at intervals not <1 week. Tourette’s disorder - Childn 6-18 yrs: 5-20 mg/day; Patients weighing ≥50 kg: Initially 2 mg/day for 2 days, increased to 5 mg/day for 5 days, then 10 mg/day on day 8. Adjust dose gradually up to 20 mg/day for patients who do not achieve optimal control of tics, in increments of 5 mg/day at intervals of not <1 week; <50 kg: Initially 2 mg/day then 5 mg/day after 2 days, may be increased to 10 mg/day at intervals of not <1 week. Poor CYP2D6 metabolizers, patients taking concomitant CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 inhibitors or CYP3A4 inducers: Adjust dose except when used as adjunctive treatment of MDD.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with dementia-related psychosis; worsening and/or emergence of suicidal ideation and behavior. NMS, tardive dyskinesia, hyperglycemia, DM, dyslipidemia, weight gain, compulsive behaviors, orthostatic hypotension, fall-related injury, leukopenia, neutropenia, and agranulocytosis. Patients with history of seizures, at risk for aspiration. Disruption of body temp regulation. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, headache, constipation, dizziness, akathisia, anxiety, insomnia, and restlessness. Somnolence, extrapyramidal disorder, fatigue, increased appetite, nasopharyngitis, and weight increased.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. itraconazole, clarithromycin) or strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g. quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine), strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, rifampin), antihypertensive drugs, benzodiazepines e.g. lorazepam.

brand_info.content: Treatment of schizophrenia. Acute treatment of manic and mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder, maintenance treatment of bipolar I disorder, both as monotherapy and as adjunct to either lithium or valproate. Adjunctive for major depressive disorder (MDD). Irritability associated with autistic disorder. Tourette’s disorder.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: Schizophrenia - Adults: Initially 10 or 15 mg/day once daily. Effective dose range: 10-30 mg/day. Adolescents (13-17 yrs): 10 mg/day. Initially 2 mg, titrated to 5 mg after 2 days then to 10 mg after 2 additional days. Dose may be increased in 5 mg increments. Bipolar I disorder - Adults: Initially 15 mg once daily as monotherapy and 10-15 mg once daily as adjunct with lithium or valproate. Recommended target dose is 15 mg/day may be increased to 30 mg/day based on clinical response. Childn 10-17 yrs: Initially 2 mg/day, titrated to 5 mg/day after 2 days then to 10 mg/day after 2 additional days, may be increased in 5 mg/day increments. Adjunctive treatment of MDD - Adults: Initially 2-5 mg/day. Dose range: 2-15 mg/day. Adjust dose gradually by 5 mg/day at intervals not <1 week. Irritability associated with autistic disorder - Childn 6-17 yrs: 5-15 mg/day. Initially 2 mg/day, increased to 5 mg/day, then 10 or 15 mg/day, if needed. Adjust dose gradually by 5 mg/day at intervals not <1 week. Tourette’s disorder - Childn 6-18 yrs: 5-20 mg/day; Patients weighing ≥50 kg: Initially 2 mg/day for 2 days, increased to 5 mg/day for 5 days, then 10 mg/day on day 8. Adjust dose gradually up to 20 mg/day for patients who do not achieve optimal control of tics, in increments of 5 mg/day at intervals of not <1 week; <50 kg: Initially 2 mg/day then 5 mg/day after 2 days, may be increased to 10 mg/day at intervals of not <1 week. Poor CYP2D6 metabolizers, patients taking concomitant CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 inhibitors or CYP3A4 inducers: Adjust dose except when used as adjunctive treatment of MDD.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Patients with dementia-related psychosis; worsening and/or emergence of suicidal ideation and behavior. NMS, tardive dyskinesia, hyperglycemia, DM, dyslipidemia, weight gain, compulsive behaviors, orthostatic hypotension, fall-related injury, leukopenia, neutropenia, and agranulocytosis. Patients with history of seizures, at risk for aspiration. Disruption of body temp regulation. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.

categories.title: A

indication_long: Ovarian carcinoma: 1st-line...

flattened_sections.indications: Ovarian carcinoma: 1st-line chemotherapy: Treatment of patients with advanced carcinoma of the ovary or with residual disease (>1 cm) after initial laparotomy, in combination with cisplatin; 2nd-line: Treatment of metastatic carcinoma of the ovary after failure of standard, platinum-containing therapy. Breast carcinoma: Treatment of node-positive breast carcinoma following anthracycline and cyclophosphamide (AC) therapy; initial treatment of locally-advanced or metastatic breast cancer either in combination with an anthracycline therapy is suitable, or in combination with trastuzumab, in patients who over-express HER-2 at a 3+ level as determined by immunohistochemistry and for whom an anthracycline is not suitable; as a single agent, treatment of metastatic carcinoma of the breast in patients who have failed, or are not candidates for standard, anthracycline-containing therapy. Advanced non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC): Treatment of NSCLC in combination with cisplatin, in patients who are not candidates for potentially curative surgery and/or radiation therapy. AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma (KS): Treatment of advanced AIDS-related KS who have failed prior liposomal anthracycline therapy.
flattened_sections.dose: Premedication prior to paclitaxel administration: Oral dexamethasone 20 mg approx 12 and 6 hrs before or IV dexamethasone 20 mg for 30-60 mins before; diphenhydramine 50 mg IV for 30-60 mins (8-20 mg for KS patients) before; cimetidine 300 mg IV or ranitidine 50 mg IV for 30-60 mins before. Ovarian carcinoma - 1st-line chemotherapy: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs, followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or paclitaxel 135 mg/m2 in a 24-hr infusion, followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m2 with 3-week intervals between courses; 2nd-line: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 over 3 hrs, with 3-week intervals between courses. Breast carcinoma - Adjuvant chemotherapy: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs every 3 weeks for 4 courses, following AC therapy. 1st-line - In combination with doxorubicin (50 mg/m2): Paclitaxel 220 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs, with 3-week intervals between courses. Administer paclitaxel 24 hrs after doxorubicin; In combination with trastuzumab (4 mg/kg loading dose then 2 mg/kg weekly): Paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs, with 3-week intervals between courses. Paclitaxel infusion may be started the day following the 1st dose of trastuzumab or immediately after the subsequent doses of trastuzumab if the preceding dose of trastuzumab was well tolerated. 2nd-line: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 over 3 hrs, with 3-week intervals between courses. Treatment of advanced NSCLC: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 over 3 hrs, followed by cisplatin 80 mg/m2 with 3-week intervals between courses. Treatment of AIDS-related KS: Paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 administered as 3-hr IV infusion every 2 weeks. Patients experiencing severe neutropenia or severe peripheral neuropathy: Dose reduction of 20% for subsequent courses and 25% for KS patients.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to paclitaxel or polyoxyethylated castor oil. Patients with baseline neutrophils < 1,500/mm<sup>3</sup> (< 1,000/mm<sup>3</sup> for KS patients) and those suffering from uncontrolled infections. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Risk for extravasation, bone marrow suppression, grade 3-4 myelosuppression (patients with hepatic impairment), severe cardiac conduction abnormalities, and interstitial pneumonitis. Patients must be pretreated with corticosteroids, antihistamines, and H2-antagonists before paclitaxel treatment. Patients should not be treated with paclitaxel until neutrophil counts recover to ≥1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup> (≥1,000/mm<sup>3</sup> for KS patients), and platelet counts recover to ≥100,000 platelets/mm<sup>3</sup> (≥75,000/mm<sup>3</sup> for KS patients). Give before cisplatin when used in combination. Radiation of the lung. Severe hepatic impairment. Patients of fertile age and their partners should use contraception for at least 6 months after treatment. Possibility of infertility in males. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Bone marrow suppression. Infections (mainly UTI and URTI), myelosuppression, neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, bleeding, minor hypersensitivity reactions (mainly flushing and rash), peripheral neuropathy, bradycardia, hypotension, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, mucosal inflammation, alopecia, and transient nail and skin changes, arthralgia, myalgia, injection site reactions, severe elevation in AST and alkaline phosphatase.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CYP2C8 or CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole and other imidazole antifungals, erythromycin, fluoxetine, gemfibrozil, clopidogrel, cimetidine, ritonavir, saquinavir, indinavir, and nelfinavir). CYP2C8 or CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, efavirenz, nevirapine). Protease inhibitors.
flattened_sections.packaging: Concentrate for solution for injection (IV) 6 mg/mL x 5 mL (P2,500.00). Concentrate solution for IV infusion 6 mg/mL x 16.7 mL (P6,500.00).

indication_long: Treatment of infections caused by susceptible...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of infections caused by susceptible microorganisms: Lower respiratory tract (bronchitis, pneumonia, empyema, and lung abscess), upper respiratory tract (tonsillitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, otitis media, scarlet fever), skin and skin structure (inflammatory acne vulgaris, furuncles, cellulitis, impetigo, abscesses, paronychia), gynecological (endometritis, pelvic cellulitis, post-op vaginal cuff infection, nongonococcal tubo-ovarian abscess, salpingitis, and pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) in combination with other agents), intra-abdominal (peritonitis, abdominal abscess), bone and joint (acute hematogenous osteomyelitis, septic arthritis), and dental infections (periodontal abscess and periodontitis); septicemia ad endocarditis; Pneumocystis jiroveci (carinii) pneumonia in patients with AIDS. Prophylaxis of bacterial endocarditis in patients allergic to penicillin. Alternative treatment of multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum infection, in combination with quinine or amodiaquine.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - Serious infections: 150-300 mg every 6 hrs. More severe infections: 300-450 mg every 6 hrs. Acne: 150 mg every 12 hrs. Bacterial vaginosis: 300 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. Cervicitis due to Chlamydia trachomatis: 450 mg every 6 hrs for 10-14 days. PID (inpatient treatment): Initially with IV therapy for at least 4 days and at least 48 hrs after patient improves, then continue with oral therapy 450 mg every 6 hrs for 10-14 days. Prevention of bacterial endocarditis in penicillin-allergic patients: 600 mg single dose 30-60 mins before procedure. Pneumocystis jiroveci (carinii) pneumonia in patients with AIDS: 300-450 mg every 6 hrs + primaquine for 21 days. Alternative treatment of multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum infection: 5-10 mg/kg/day twice a day + quinine or amodiaquine for at least 5 days.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Overgrowth of Clostridium difficile. Discontinue when hypersensitivity or severe skin reactions occur. Patients with history of GI disease (colitis), G6PD deficiency (when used in combination with primaquine), severe renal and hepatic impairment accompanied by severe metabolic aberrations. Atopic individuals. Not used for the treatment of meningitis. Perform liver and kidney function tests and blood counts periodically during prolonged therapy. Childn ≤16 yrs. Elderly >60 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.
flattened_sections.side_effects: CDAD, pseudomembranous colitis; dermatologic and hypersensitivity reactions; vaginal infection or vaginitis; polyarthritis; dysgeusia; lymphadenitis.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Neuromuscular blocking agents (e.g. ether, tubocurarine, pancuronium), aminoglycosides, ampicillin, erythromycin, neostigmine and physostigmine, estrogens, vaccines, VKAs (e.g. warfarin, acenocoumarol, fluindione).

flattened_sections.dose: Epilepsy: Monotherapy - Adults and childn >10 yrs with partial onset or primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures: 400 mg once daily, titrated according to the following schedule - Week 1: 50 mg once daily; week 2: 100 mg once daily; week 3: 150 mg once daily; week 4: 200 mg once daily; week 5: 300 mg once daily; week 6: 400 mg once daily. Childn 6-9 yrs: 25 mg/day, given at night, for the first week and can be increased to 50 mg/day based upon tolerability. Dose can be increased by 25-50 mg each week as tolerated. Target total daily maintenance dosing for childn 6-9 yrs - BW up to 11 kg - Minimum 150 mg/day; max: 250 mg/day, 12-22 kg - minimum 200 mg/day; max 300, 23-31 kg - minimum 200 mg/day; max 350, 32-38 kg - minimum 250 mg/day; max 350 mg/day, >38 kg - minimum 250 mg/day; max 400 mg/day. Adjunctive therapy - Adults ≥17 yrs: Initially 25-50 mg once daily followed by titration effective dose in increments of 25-50 mg every week. 200 mg-400 mg once daily for partial-onset seizures or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and 400 mg once daily for primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Childn 6-16 yrs: 5-9 mg/kg once daily. Begin titration at 25 mg once daily, given nightly for the first week. Then increase the dosage at 1- or 2-week intervals by increments of 1-3 mg/kg/day. Max 400 mg/day. Migraine prophylaxis: Initially 100 mg once daily, titrated to the following schedule - week 1: 25 mg/day; week 2: 50 mg/day; week 3: 75 mg/day; 100 mg/day. Renal impairment (CrCl >70 mL/min/1.73 m2): Half of usual adult dose. Supplemental dose may be required for patients undergoing hemodialysis. Swallow cap whole and intact. Do not sprinkle on food, chew, or crush.

flattened_sections.side_effects: Increased risk of bleeding. Temporary discontinue in patients with acute, serious conditions suggestive of myopathy or risk factor predisposed to renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Perform liver enzyme tests prior to initiation of therapy. Childn.

indication_long: Prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in...

flattened_sections.indications: Prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in adults who have undergone elective hip or knee replacement surgery. To reduce the risk of stroke, systemic embolism, and death in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) with ≥1 risk factors, including patients unsuitable for warfarin. Treatment and prevention of (recurrent) deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE).
flattened_sections.dose: Prevention of VTE in elective hip or knee replacement surgery: Initially 2.5 mg twice daily taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. Duration of treatment: 32-38 days for hip replacement surgery; 10-14 days for knee replacement surgery. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism, patients with NVAF: 5 mg twice daily. Patients with at least 2 risk factors (≥80 yrs, ≤60 kg BW, or serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL [133 mmol/L]): 2.5 mg twice daily. Treatment of DVT and PE: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days followed by 5 mg twice daily. Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE: 2.5 mg twice daily after 6 months of treatment. Surgery and invasive procedures, patients not previously treated with anticoagulants: At least 5 doses of 5 mg twice daily (2.5 mg twice daily if for dose reduction) twice daily before cardioversion. If cardioversion is required before 5 doses of Apixaban: 10 mg loading dose, followed by 5 mg twice daily, may be reduced to 5 mg loading dose followed by 2.5 mg twice daily. Loading dose should be given at least 2 hrs before cardioversion.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Clinically significant active bleeding.
flattened_sections.precautions: Conditions with increased risk of hemorrhage. Patients with hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk; undergoing hip fracture surgery; prosthetic heart valves with or without atrial fibrillation. Temporarily discontinue for active bleeding, elective surgery, or invasive procedures; avoid lapses in therapy and restart as soon as possible. Risk of developing spinal or epidural hematoma during spinal/epidural anesthesia or puncture which can result in long-term or permanent paralysis. Indwelling epidural or intrathecal catheters must be removed at least 5 hrs prior to the 1<sup>st</sup> dose. Monitor for signs and symptoms of neurological impairment. Patients with history of thrombosis who are diagnosed with antiphospholipid syndrome. Patients with CrCl < 15 mL/min or those undergoing dialysis or with severe hepatic impairment. Mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B). Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Anemia, hemorrhage, hematoma, epistaxis. Nausea, GI hemorrhage, hematuria, contusion.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Ketoconazole. Diltiazem, naproxen, clarithromycin, amiodarone, verapamil, quinidine. Rifampin. Phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John’s wort. Enoxaparin, NSAIDs, aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitors. Agents associated with serious bleeding e.g. unfractionated heparin and heparin derivatives (LMWH), FXa inhibiting oligosaccharides e.g. fondaparinux, direct thrombin II inhibitors e.g. desirudin, thrombolytic agents, GPIIb/IIa receptor antagonists, dipyridamole, dextran, sulfinpyrazone, vit K antagonist, and other oral anticoagulants.

flattened_sections.indications: Long-term management of angina pectoris due to coronary atherosclerosis. Management of hypertension (HTN); may be used alone or in combination with other antihypertensive drugs. Acute myocardial infarction (MI).
flattened_sections.dose: Adults: Initially 50 mg once daily. Maintenance dose: 25-100 mg daily. HTN: 50-100 mg daily. Angina pectoris: 100 mg daily as a single or in divided doses, may be increased to 200 mg if needed. MI: 100 mg daily as single or in divided doses is recommended for long-term prophylaxis.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Shock, CHF, hypotension, sick sinus syndrome, sinus bradycardia, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree heart block, significant right ventricular hypertrophy, right ventricular failure secondary to pulmonary HTN, bronchospasm, metabolic acidosis, and untreated pheochromocytoma. Concurrent use anesthetic agents that produce myocardial depression (e.g. ether, chloroform, cyclopropane).
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt discontinuation. May precipitate severe heart failure and thyroid storm. May mask signs of acute hypoglycemia i.e. tachycardia. Use with caution during anesthesia and major surgery. May increase serum free-thyroxine levels. May impair peripheral circulation and renal function. Patients with bronchospastic diseases, Prinzmetal angina, 1st degree heart block, MI with < 120 mmHg systolic BP, atrial fibrillation after MI, bradycardia, history of anaphylaxis, eye and skin reactions. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk:Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Fever with aching and sore throat, laryngospasm, respiratory distress; fatigue; malaise; lupus; sclerosing serositis. Undesirable effects on CV, GI, hematologic, metabolic-nutritional, musculoskeletal, nervous, reproductive, respiratory, skin and appendages, and urogenital system disorders. Visual disturbance, dry eyes, conjunctivitis, tinnitus, and otitis.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CCBs, antiarrhythmic agents, catecholamine-depleting agents, clonidine, anesthetics, digitalis/digitalis glycosides, sympathomimetic agents, and prostaglandin synthetase inhibitors.

flattened_sections.indications: Monotherapy or in combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or dexamethasone for the treatment of adults with progressive multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior therapy and who have already undergone or unsuitable for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). In combination with melphalan and prednisone for the treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are not eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with HSCT. In combination with dexamethasone, or with dexamethasone and thalidomide for the induction treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with HSCT. In combination with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone for the treatment of adults with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma who are unsuitable for HSCT.
flattened_sections.dose: For the treatment of adults with progressive multiple myoma who have received at least one prior therapy - General dosing: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA via IV or SC twice weekly for 2 weeks (days 1, 4, 8, 11), followed by a 10-day rest period (days 12-21) in a 21-day treatment cycle. This 3-week period is considered a treatment cycle. Monotherapy: Two cycles of bortezomib after a complete response is confirmed; for patients responding to treatment but do not achieve complete remission: A total of 8 cycles therapy is recommended. In combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin: Follow general dosing recommendation. Recommended dose of pegylated liposomal doxorubicin: 30 mg/m2 to be administered as a 1-hr IV infusion following bortezomib injection on day 4 of the treatment cycle. Up to 8 cycles of this combination therapy can be administered if patients have not progressed and can tolerate the treatment. Patients achieving a complete response can continue with the combination therapy for at least two cycles after the first evidence of complete response, even if this requires treatment for more than 8 cycles. Patients whose paraprotein levels continue to decrease after 8 cycles can still receive this combination therapy for as long as the patient can tolerate and respond with the treatment. In combination with dexamethasone: Follow general dosing recommendation. Dexamethasone 20 mg is administered orally at days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, and 12 of the bortezomib treatment cycle. Patients achieving a response or a stable disease after 4 cycles of this combination therapy may continue to be administered with the same combination for a max of 4 additional cycles. For the treatment of adults with progressive multiple myeloma - In combination with melphalan and prednisone - Administered IV or SC in combination with oral melphalan and oral prednisone; a 6-week period is a treatment cycle. For treatment cycles 1-4: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 for Day 1, 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, 29, 32, melphalan 9 mg/m2 and prednisone 60 mg/m2 for Day 1, 2, 3, 4. For treatment cycles 5-9: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 for Day 1, 8, 22, 29, melphalan 9 mg/m2 and prednisone 60 mg/m2 for Day 1, 2, 3, 4. Prior to initiating a treatment cycle, platelet counts (PC) should be ≥70 x 109/L and the absolute neutrophils count (ANC) should be ≥1 x 109/L; Non-hematological toxicities should have resolved to Grade 1 or baseline. For previously untreated multiple myeloma patients eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (induction therapy) - In combination therapy with dexamethasone: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 via IV or SC twice weekly for two weeks (i.e., on days 1, 4, 8, and 11), followed by a 10-day rest period (days 12-20) in a 21 days treatment cycle. This 3-week period is considered a treatment cycle. Dexamethasone 40 mg is administered orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of the bortezomib treatment cycle. Four treatment cycles of this combination therapy are administered. In combination therapy with dexamethasone and thalidomide: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 BSA via IV or SC twice weekly for two weeks (i.e., 1, 4, 8 and 11), followed by a 17-day rest period (days 12-28) in a 28-day treatment cycle. This four-week period is considered a treatment cycle. Dexamethasone 40 mg is orally administered on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, and 11 of the bortezomib treatment cycle. Thalidomide 50 mg is orally administered daily on days 1 to 14 and if tolerated, the dose is increased to 100 mg on days 15 to 28. Thereafter, the dose may be further increased to 200 mg daily from cycle 2. Four treatment cycles of this combination are administered. It is recommended that patients with at least partial response should receive two additional cycles. When thalidomide is used, particular attention to pregnancy testing and prevention requirements is needed. Dosage adjustment for transplant eligible patients: Follow dosage adjustment guidelines described for monotherapy. For patients with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) - Combination therapy with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/ m2 via IV or SC twice weekly for two weeks (i.e., on days 1, 4, 8, and 11), followed by a 10-day rest period (days 12-21) in a 21-day treatment cycle. This 3-week period is considered a treatment cycle. It is recommended to administer 6 bortezomib treatment cycles. For patients with a response first documented at cycle 6, two additional bortezomib treatment cycles may be given. Prednisone is administered orally at 100 mg/m2 on days 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 of each bortezomib treatment cycle. The medicinal products are administered on day 1 of each 3-week treatment cycle as IV infusion: rituximab at 375 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide at 750 mg/m2, doxorubicin at 50 mg/m2. Dose adjustment during treatment for patients with previously untreated MCL: Prior to initiating a new treatment cycle, PC should be ≥100,000 cells/mcL (≥75,000 cells/mcL in patients with bone marrow filtration or splenic sequestration), and the ANC should be ≥1,500 cells/mcL, hemoglobin ≥8 g/dL, non-hematological toxicities should have resolved to Grade 1 or baseline. Moderate to severe hepatic impairment: Reduced starting dose of 0.7 mg/m2 per injection during first treatment cycle. A subsequent dose escalation to 1 mg/m2 or further dose reduction to 0.5 mg/m2 may be considered, depending on patient’s tolerability. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron, mannitol, or any component in the product. Intrathecal administration. Patients with acute diffuse infiltrative pulmonary and pericardial disease. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Has a narrow therapeutic window. Risk for hematologic toxicities (neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia); posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES); progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy; peripheral and autonomic neuropathy; dehydration; herpes zoster reactivation. Patients with moderate to severe thrombocytopenia; pulmonary disorders; renal and hepatic impairment. Patients at risk for bleeding, infections, CHF, cardiogenic shock, QT-prolongation. May impair ability to drive and use machines. Childn <18 yrs. Lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, fatigue, asthenia, pyrexia, headache, paresthesia, decreased appetite, dyspnea, rash, herpes zoster, myalgia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, ritonavir). CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, St. John’s wort, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital. Oral antidiabetic agents. Melphalan-prednisone. Drugs associated with peripheral neuropathy or decrease in BP (e.g. amiodarone, anti-viral, INH, nitrofurantoin, statins).

flattened_sections.indications: Adjuvant treatment of postmenopausal women with HR-positive early breast cancer and extended adjuvant treatment of hormone-dependent early breast cancer in postmenopausal women who have received prior standard adjuvant tamoxifen therapy for 5 yrs. Treatment of advanced breast cancer in women with natural or artificially induced postmenopausal status after relapse or disease progression, who have previously been treated with antiestrogens. 1<sup>st</sup> line treatment in postmenopausal women with hormone-dependent advanced breast cancer.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults (including elderly): 2.5 mg once daily. As adjuvant treatment – Duration: 5 yrs or until tumor relapse occurs. For patients with advanced or metastatic disease or as extended adjuvant treatment: Continue treatment until tumor progression is evident.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Premenopausal women. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with CrCl <10 mL/min. Patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score C). Increased risk for osteoporosis and/or bone fractures. Sexually active females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during and until 20 days after stopping treatment. Only women of confirmed postmenopausal endocrine status should receive letrozole. May impair fertility in males of reproductive potential. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery.

flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Other anti-estrogens or estrogen-containing products. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin, and telithromycin. CYP2A6 inhibitors e.g. methoxsalen. CYP3A4 inducers e.g. phenytoin, rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, and St. John’s wort. Tamoxifen. Clopidogrel

flattened_sections.indications: Adjunct to diet for treatment of primary hypercholesterolemia as substitute in adults adequately controlled with rosuvastatin and ezetimibe given concurrently but as separate products.
flattened_sections.dose: 1 tab with or without food. Not suitable for initial therapy. Take ≥2 hrs before or ≥4 hrs after administration of bile acid sequestrant.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease including unexplained, persistent elevations of serum transaminases and any serum transaminase elevation exceeding 3x ULN, severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Patients with myopathy, receiving concomitant ciclosporin. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Use in elderly >70 yrs, patients with renal impairment (CrCl < 60 mL/min), Asian, or have predisposing factors to myopathy should use monocomponent preparations. Discontinue if myopathy or rhabdomyolysis is suspected. Monitor liver function tests. Severe skin reactions (e.g. SJS or DRESS), CK levels >5x ULN, ILD. Patients with moderate or severe hepatic insufficiency, history of liver disease or consumption of alcohol, acute and serious conditions suggestive of myopathy or predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Monitor patients at risk for DM. Concomitant use with protease inhibitors, fibrates, and anticoagulants, fusidic acid. Childn < 18 yrs.

flattened_sections.indications: For the treatment of infections caused by susceptible isolates of the designated microorganisms in specific conditions: Otitis externa in adults and childn >6 months due to Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus; Chronic suppurative otitis media in patients >12 yrs with perforated tympanic membranes due to Proteus mirabilis, P. aeruginosa, S. aureus; Acute otitis media in childn >1 yr with tympanostomy tubes due to Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, P. aerugunosa, S. aureus, and Streptococcus pneumoniae.
flattened_sections.dose: Otitis externa - Patients >13 yrs: 10 drops instilled into the affected ear once daily for 7 days; Childn 6 months-13 yrs: 5 drops instilled into the affected ear once daily for 7 days; Acute otitis media in childn with tympanostomy tubes - Childn 1-12 yrs: 5 drops instilled into the affected ear twice daily for 10 days. Chronic suppurative otitis media with perforated tympanic membranes - >12 yrs: 10 drops instilled into the affected ear twice daily for 14 days. Soln should be warmed by holding it in the hand for 1 or 2 mins. The patient should lie with the affected ear upwards and then drops should be instilled. The tragus should be pumped 4x by pushing inwards to facilitate penetration of drops into the middle ear. The position should be maintained for 5 mins.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ofloxacin, other quinolones, or any of the components in this medication.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not for ophthalmic use or injection. Avoid contaminating applicator tip. Discontinue use if allergic reaction is suspected. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms e.g. fungi during prolonged use. If infection does not improve after 1 week, cultures should be obtained to guide further treatment. Further evaluation is recommended if otorrhea persists after a full course of therapy, or if two or more episodes occur within 6 months. Childn < 6 months. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, seborrhea, transient loss of hearing, tinnitus, otitis externa, otitis media, tremor, HTN, and fungal infection. Dermatitis, eczema, erythematous rash, follicular rash, hypoaesthesia, dyspepsia, hot flushes, flushing and otorrhagia. Taste perversion, earache, pruritus, paraesthesia, rash, dizziness. Vomiting, dry mouth, headache, vertigo, fever. Application site reaction, urticaria, abdominal pain, dysaesthesia, hyperkinesia, halitosis, inflammation, pain, insomnia, coughing, pharyngitis, rhinitis, sinusitis, and tachycardia.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: For short-term treatment of acute pain and post-op pain i.e. oral surgery, abdominal hysterectomy, myomectomy, total knee replacement, total hip arthroplasty, laparoscopic cholecystectomy, inguinal hernia repair, and other general surgery e.g. diagnostic laparoscopy, gastrectomy, hernioplasty, appendectomy, hemithyroidectomy and splenectomy. May be used pre-op to prevent or reduce post-op pain and it can reduce opioid requirements used concomitantly.
flattened_sections.dose: Management of acute pain: Single or initial dose of 40 mg slow IM or IV bolus, followed by 20 mg or 40 mg every 6-12 hrs. Max 80 mg/day. Prevention or reduction of post-op pain: 40 mg IM or IV 30-45 mins prior to surgical incision. Continue medication post-op for adequate analgesic effect. Elderly weighing < 50 kg: Reduce initial dose by 50%. Max 40 mg/day. Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or who may be predisposed to fluid retention: Lowest recommended dose and patient's kidney function closely monitored. Patients with moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B), and concurrently taking fluconazole: Lowest recommended dose.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamides, previous allergic drug reaction especially cutaneous reactions (e.g., SJS, TEN, erythema multiforme). History of CVA, MI, CABG, uncontrolled HTN, CHF (NYHA II-IV). Active peptic ulceration or GI bleeding. Patients who experienced bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps, bronchial asthma, angioneurotic edema, urticaria or other allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or NSAIDs. Severe hepatic dysfunction. IBD, treatment of post-op pain immediately following CABG surgery. Established IHD, PAD and/or cerebrovascular disease. Pregnancy (3<sup>rd</sup> trimester) and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Increased risk of CV and thrombotic adverse events on long term treatment. Not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment. Upper GI perforations, ulcers, or bleeding; severe hypotension. Patients with CV disease, concomitantly using aspirin, corticosteroids, SSRIs, other antiplatelet drugs or NSAIDs, ingesting alcohol, with history of, or active GI diseases; concomitant use of anticoagulants; HTN; compromised cardiac function, pre-existing edema, or other condition predisposing to, or worsened by fluid retention in diuretic treatment or at risk of hypovolemia. Closely monitor BP during initiation and throughout the course of therapy; renal function in patients with advanced renal disease. Rehydrate patients with dehydration prior to treatment. Discontinue treatment at 1<sup>st</sup> appearance of skin rash, mucosal lesion or any sign of hypersensitivity. May impair diagnostic signs in detecting infections (e.g., fever). Female fertility. Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, abdominal pain, constipation, dyspepsia, vomiting, peripheral edema, alveolar osteitis (dry socket), dizziness, insomnia, oliguria, increased sweating, pruritis, hypotension.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Fluconazole, ketoconazole, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, beta-blockers, diuretics, ciclosporin, methotrexate lithium.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) in adults. Reduction of cardiovascular (CV) morbidity with manifest atherothrombotic CV disease (e.g. history of CHD, stroke, peripheral arterial disease) or type 2 diabetes mellitus with documented target organ damage.
flattened_sections.dose: Essential HTN: 40 mg once daily, may be increased to max 80 mg once daily if target BP is not achieved. Some may already benefit from 20 mg once daily. May be used in combination with thiazide diuretics (e.g. HCTZ). The max effect is attained 4-8 weeks after start of treatment. CV morbidity reduction: 80 mg once daily. Severe renal impairment, on hemodialysis: Initially 20 mg. Mild to moderate hepatic impairment: Max 40 mg once daily. Take with or without food.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with cholestasis, severe hepatic impairment and biliary obstructive disorders. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters).
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment; bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney, recent kidney transplantation; vol/sodium depletion; primary aldosteronism; aortic and mitral stenosis, obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; diabetes treated with insulin or antidiabetics; fructose intolerance; ischemic cardiopathy or CV disease. Dual blockade of RAAS with concomitant use of products that affect this system. Patients at risk for hyperkalemia.  Correct volume and sodium depletion prior to initiation of treatment. Monitor BP closely when initiating therapy for CV morbidity reduction; potassium and creatinine serum levels in patients with renal impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Black hypertensive patients. Childn < 18 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Sepsis. Hypotension. Abnormal hepatic function or liver disorder. Interstitial lung disease.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Salt substitutes containing potassium, potassium-sparing diuretics or supplements, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, heparin, cyclosporin, tacrolimus, trimethoprim, lithium.
