flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of major depressive episodes (MDE), panic disorder with or without agoraphobia, social anxiety disorder (SAD), generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).
flattened_sections.dose: All doses taken once daily. MDE, GAD, OCD: Initially 10 mg, may be increased to max 20 mg. Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia: Initially 5 mg during the 1st week, then increased to 10 mg and may be further increased up to max 20 mg. SAD: 10 mg, may be decreased to 5 mg or increased to max 20 mg. Elderly >65 yrs: Reduce initial dose by half. A lower max dose should be considered. Mild to moderate hepatic impairment, poor metabolizers of CYP2C19: Initially 5 mg during the 1st 2 weeks, may be increased to 10 mg; Severe hepatic impairment: Titrate dose. Treatment duration - MDE: Usually 2-4 weeks to obtain a response, then at least 6 months after symptoms resolve. Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia: Max effectiveness after 3 months. SAD: 2-4 weeks to obtain symptom relief, 12 weeks to consolidate response, and 6 months to prevent relapse. OCD: Until patient is symptom-free. Taken with or without food.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with MAOIs (e.g. moclobemide and linezolid). Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with severe renal (CrCl < 30 mL/min) and hepatic impairment, unstable or controlled epilepsy, history of mania/hypomania, diabetes, CHD. Concomitant use with oral anticoagulants, atypical antipsychotics, phenothiazines, TCAs, aspirin, NSAIDs, ticlopidine, dipyridamole; electroconvulsive therapy; sumatriptan or other triptans, tramadol, tryptophan; St. John’s Wort. Increased anxiety symptoms at the beginning of treatment in some patients with panic disorder; suicidal thoughts, self-harm, and suicide (suicide-related events) in patients with depression; akathisia; hyponatremia; cutaneous bleeding abnormalities (e.g. ecchymoses, purpura) in patients with known bleeding tendencies. Discontinue if seizure develops or if there is an increase in seizure frequency. Gradually taper dose upon discontinuation. Elderly with SAD. Lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Decreased/Increased appetite, increased weight; anxiety, restlessness, abnormal dreams, decreased libido, anorgasmia; insomnia, somnolence, dizziness, paresthesia, tremor; sinusitis, yawning; diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, dry mouth; increased sweating; arthralgia, myalgia; ejaculation disorder, impotence; fatigue, pyrexia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: MAOIs, tramadol, sumatriptan and other triptans, TCAs, SSRIs, phenothiazines, thioxanthenes, mefloquine, bupropion, lithium, tryptophan, St. John’s Wort, oral anticoagulants, NSAIDs, alcohol.

flattened_sections.dose: MDD, GAD: Initially 75 mg, may be increased up to max 225 mg/day. Some may start at 37.5 mg for 4-7 days, then increase to 75 mg. Dose increases should be in increments of up to 75 mg/day at intervals of not < 4 days. SAD: 75 mg. Panic disorder: Initially 37.5 mg for 7 days, increased to 75 mg the following week and may be increased up to max 225 mg/day. Dose increases should be in increments of up to 75 mg/day at intervals of not < 7 days. Mild to moderate hepatic impairment: Reduce dose by 50%. Renal impairment: Reduce total daily dose by 25-50%. All taken as a single dose with meals either in the morning or evening at approx same time each day. Swallow whole; do not divide/crush/chew/place in water. Cap may be opened carefully and sprinkled on a spoonful of applesauce, then swallowed immediately followed by a glass of water.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with MAOIs (e.g. linezolid, IV methylene blue) or use within 7-14 days of treatment discontinuation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Suicide risk and suicidal ideation/behavior or unusual change in behavior. Screen for bipolar disorder; not for treatment of bipolar depression. Patients with history of mania/hypomania, MI, unstable heart disease, hyperthyroidism, heart failure, renal impairment, liver cirrhosis, HTN. Concomitant use with other serotonergic drugs (triptans, TCAs, fentanyl, lithium, tramadol, tryptophan, buspirone, St. John’s Wort). Worsening of symptoms of MDD. Serotonin syndrome, angle-closure glaucoma, sustained HTN; insomnia, nervousness; weight changes; hyponatremia risk in elderly, diuretic use and volume depletion; abnormal bleeding; ILD, eosinophilic pneumonia. Monitor BP regularly. Gradual withdrawal upon discontinuation. Childn. Elderly with hepatic impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Sexual function abnormalities (e.g. abnormal ejaculation, impotence), GI disturbances (e.g. nausea, dry mouth, anorexia, constipation), CNS complaints (e.g. dizziness, somnolence, abnormal dreams, decreased libido, nervousness, insomnia, tremor), abnormal vision, sweating, asthenia, yawning. Chest and neck pain, chills, fever; migraine, tachycardia; increased appetite; ecchymosis; edema, weight gain; amnesia, confusion, depersonalization, hypesthesia, abnormal thinking, trismus, vertigo; increased cough, dyspnea; pruritus; accommodation abnormality, mydriasis, taste perversion; albuminuria, impaired urination.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Cimetidine, haloperidol; NSAIDs, aspirin, warfarin; drugs metabolized by CYP2D6; metoprolol; CNS active drugs; triptans; QT-prolonging drugs. False positive urine immunoassay screening tests for phencyclidine and amphetamine.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

If symptoms persist into the afternoon of day 2, take 2 tabs at bedtime on day 2, then 3 tabs (1 in the morning, 2 at bedtime) on day 3. flattened_sections.indications: For acute treatment of the signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA); treatment of ankylosing spondylitis; relief of acute pain caused by acute gouty arthritis, moderate to severe acute post-op pain associated with dental surgery or abdominal gynecological surgery,  primary dysmenorrhea.
flattened_sections.dose: OA: 30 mg once daily; for patients with insufficient relief of symptoms from taking 30 mg once daily, dose may be increased to 60 mg once daily. Max 60 mg/day. RA or ankylosing spondylitis: 60 mg once daily; patients with insufficient relief of symptoms from taking 60 mg once daily, dose may be increased to 90 mg once daily. Dose reduction to 60 mg may be appropriate once patient has clinically stabilized. Max 90 mg/day. Acute pain: 90 mg or 120 mg, Should only taken during the acute symptomatic period, max 8 days treatment. Acute gouty arthritis: 120 mg once daily for max 8 days. Post-op dental surgery pain: 90 once daily for max 3 days. Primary dysmenorrhea: Max 120 mg once daily. Post-op gynecological pain: 90 mg once daily. Max 120 mg once daily. Hepatic impairment - Mild (Child-Pugh scores 5-6): Max 60 mg. Moderate (Child-Pugh score 7-9): Max 30 mg once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to etoricoxib, other NSAIDs, or to any component of the product. Severe hepatic dysfunction (serum albumin <25 g/L or Child-Pugh score >10). Severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) or deteriorating renal disease. Patients who have history of CVA, MI, CABG, uncontrolled  HTN, CHF (NYHA II-IV). Patients who have experienced asthma, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps,  angioneurotic edema, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs, including other COX-2 specific inhibitors. Previous or active gastric, duodenal, or peptic ulcerations, or active GI bleeding, or IBD. Unstable or significant established IHD, PAD, and/or cerebrovascular disease. Patients who have undergone angioplasty. Use in peri-op in patients undergoing cardiac or  major vascular surgery. Childn and adolescents <16 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Increased risk of serious CV thrombotic events, Ml, and stroke; serious GI adverse events including bleeding, ulceration, and perforation of the stomach or intestines; which can be fatal. Patients with known CV disease, history of atherosclerotic CV disease, or significant risk factors for  CV events (e.g. HTN, hyperlipidemia, DM, a 1<sup>st</sup>-degree relative with IHD, cardiac failure, smoking). Risk of fluid retention and edema; patients with history of cardiac failure, left ventricular dysfunction, or HTN; pre existing edema. Renal papillary necrosis and other renal injury in long-term therapy. Patients with considerable dehydration. Elevation in ALT or AST (approx >3x ULN).Patients with co morbid conditions e.g. coagulation disorders or concomitant use of drugs that increase risk of  bleeding. Not recommended in women attempting to conceive. Elderly.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Abdominal pain, HTN, dizziness, headache, ecchymosis, alveolar osteitis, edema, fluid retention, palpitations, arrhythmia, bronchospasm, constipation, flatulence, gastritis, dyspepsia, GERD, diarrhea, epigastric discomfort, nausea, vomiting, esophagitis, pharyngitis, oral ulcer, asthenia, fatigue, influenza-like illness, and increased ALT and/or AST.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Aspirin. Ciclosporin, tacrolimus. CYP inducers (e.g. rifampicin). CYP inhibitors (e.g.  ketoconazole). Digoxin. Diuretics, ARBs, and ACE inhibitors. Drugs metabolized by human  sulfotransferases (e.g. ethinylestradiol, oral salbutamol, minoxidil). HRT. Lithium. Methotrexate. Oral anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin). Oral contraceptives.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of multiple myeloma and light chain (AL) amyloidosis.
flattened_sections.dose: SC use only. Multiple myeloma - Adults ≥18 yrs: 1,800 mg SC injection over 3-5 mins. Dosing schedule - Monotherapy or in combination therapy with 4-week cycle regimens for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma(e.g. with lenalidomide or pomalidomide, or carfilzomib and low-dose dexamethasone) or newly diagnosed multiple myeloma ineligible for autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) (e.g. with lenalidomide and low-dose dexamethasone) - Weeks 1-8: Weekly (8 total doses); Weeks 9-24: every 2 weeks (8 total doses); Week 25 onwards until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. In combination with 6-week cycle regimens for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma ineligible for ASCT (with bortezomib, melphalan, and prednisone) - Weeks 1-6: Weekly (6 total doses); Weeks 7-54: Every 3 weeks (16 total doses); Week 55 onwards until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. Administer bortezomib 2x weekly at weeks 1, 2, 4, 5 for 1st 6-week cycle, then once weekly at weeks 1, 2, 4, 5 for 8 more 6-week cycles. In combination with 4-week cycle regimens for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma eligible for ASCT (with bortezomib, thalidomide, and dexamethasone - Induction: Weeks 1-8: Weekly, (8 total doses); Weeks 9-16: Every 2 weeks, (4 total doses). Then stop for high-dose chemotherapy and ASCT. Consolidation: Weeks 1-8 (reinitiation): Every 2 weeks, (4 total doses). In combination with 3-week cycle regimens for patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (e.g. with bortezomib) - Weeks 1-9: Weekly (9 total doses); Weeks 10-24: Every 3 weeks (5 total doses); Week 25 onwards until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. AL amyloidosis: 1,800 mg SC injection over 3-5 mins. In combination with bortezomib, cyclophosphamide, and dexamethasone (4-week cycle regimen) - Weeks 1-8: Weekly (8 total doses); Weeks 9-24: Every 2 weeks (8 total doses); Week 25 until disease progression: Every 4 weeks. Pre-injection medications (e.g. corticosteroids, antipyretics, antihistamine): Administer 1-3 hrs prior to every daratumumab SC injection. Post-injection medications - Oral corticosteroid (i.e. intermediate-acting, long-acting): Administer 2 days following daratumumab SC injection. Low-dose oral methylprednisolone: Administer 1 day after daratumumab administration.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Consider antiviral prophylaxis for prevention of HZV reactivation. Infusion-related reactions. History of COPD. May increase therapy-induced neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. Interference with indirect antiglobulin test (indirect Coombs test) and serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation tests. HBV reactivation. Women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during and for 3 months after treatment. Childn ≤17 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Fatigue, nausea, diarrhea, constipation, pyrexia, cough, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, peripheral edema, peripheral sensory neuropathy and URTI. Pneumonia, bronchitis, sepsis, pulmonary edema, influenza, pyrexia, dehydration, diarrhea, atrial fibrillation, and syncope.
flattened_sections.packaging: Solution for injection (SC) 120 mg/mL x 15 mL (P235,714.00).

flattened_sections.dose: Schizophrenia: Initially 50 mg given in 2 divided doses on day 1, increased in increments of 50-150 mg on days 2 and 3, to a target of 300-400 mg daily by day 4, given in 3 divided doses. Daily dose may further be adjusted in steps of 50-100 mg at intervals not <2 days. Max 750 mg/day. Bipolar disorder - Acute manic episode: Initially 50 mg twice daily on day 1, 100 mg twice daily on day 2, 150 mg twice daily on day 3, and 200 mg twice daily on day 4. Dose may then be adjusted to 400-800 mg/day if needed; Depressive phase: Initially 50 mg once daily at bedtime, increased to 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, 300 mg on day 4, may further be increased to 400 mg on day 5, and 600 mg on day 8, if necessary. Maintenance treatment as adjunct to lithium or valproate: Continue dose that controlled intial symptoms. Elderly, patients with hepatic and renal impairment: Initially 25 mg, may be increased daily in increments of 25-50 mg.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use of CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. HIV-protease inhibitors, azole antifungal agents, erythromycin, clarithromycin, and nefazodone.
flattened_sections.precautions: Long-term treatment. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with hepatic or renal impairment, CV disease or other conditions predisposing to hypotension, cerebrovascular disease, history of seizures or conditions that lower seizure threshold. Monitor patients during early therapy for depressive phase in bipolar disorder. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of acute life-threatening hypertension (HTN); malignant arterial HTN or hypertensive encephalopathy; aortic dissection when short-acting beta-blocker therapy is not suitable or in combination with beta-blocker; severe preeclampsia when other IV antihypertensive agents are contraindicated; post-op HTN.
flattened_sections.dose: Unless given by central venous line, dilute to a concentration of 0.1-0.2 mg/mL before use. Adults - Initial: 3-5 mg/hr for 15 mins, may be increased in increments of 0.5 mg or 1 mg every 15 mins. Infusion rate should not be >15 mg/hr. Maintenance: 2-4 mg/hr. Transition to oral antihypertensive - 20 mg cap: 60 mg/day in 3 divided doses; 50 mg ER tab: 100 mg/day in 2 divided doses. Elderly and pregnancy: Initially 1-5 mg/hr, may be increased or decreased by 0.5 mg/hr after 30 mins, depending on BP and clinical situation. Dose should not be >4 mg/hr, rate not >15 mg/hr (treatment of preeclampsia). Childn - Initial: 0.5-5 mcg/kg/min. Maintenance: 1-4 mcg/kg/min.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe aortic stenosis, compensatory HTN (e.g. arteriovenous shunt or aortic coarctation), unstable angina; within 8 days after MI. Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Continuous IV infusion only. Decrease dose by half or discontinue infusion when systemic hypotension and reflex tachycardia occur. Patients with CHF or pulmonary edema, suspected coronary ischemia, history of hepatic dysfunction or hepatic impairment, portal HTN, pre-existing elevated intracranial pressure, acute cerebral infarction, and renal impairment. Concomitant use with beta-blockers, magnesium sulfate. Infants and childn. Childn with renal impairment. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, dizziness, peripheral edema, palpitations, flushing. Hypotension, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, nausea, vomiting.

flattened_sections.dose: Primary hyperaldosteronism - Long test: 400 mg daily for 3-4 weeks. Short test: 400 mg daily for 4 days. May administer 100-400 mg in preparation for surgery. Edema in adults (CHF, liver cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome): Initially 100 mg daily in single or divided doses for 5 at least days. Dose may range from 25-200 mg daily. Essential HTN: Initially 50-100 mg daily in single or divided doses for at least 2 weeks. Diuretic-induced hypokalemia: 25-100 mg daily. Severe heart failure - Serum potassium ≤5.0 mEq/L and creatinine ≤2.5 mg/dL: 25 mg once daily, may increase to 50 mg once daily if tolerated, and decrease to 25 mg every other day for patients unable to tolerate.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Patients with anuria, acute renal insufficiency, renal impairment, or hyperkalemia.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with hepatic impairment, severe heart failure. Observe for evidence of fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Monitor serum potassium levels. Delusional hyponatremia may occur in edematous patients in hot weather. May cause transient elevation of BUN in patients with preexisting renal impairment. Concomitant use with other potassium-sparing diuretics, oral potassium supplements, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs (e.g. indomethacin), lithium. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: GI bleeding, ulceration, gastritis, diarrhea and cramping, nausea, vomiting; gynecomastia, erectile dysfunction, irregular menses or amenorrhea, post-menopausal bleeding; agranulocytosis; fever, urticaria, maculopapular or erythematous cutaneous eruptions, anaphylactic reactions, vasculitis; mental confusion, ataxia, headache, drowsiness, lethargy; renal dysfunction.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: ACE inhibitors, alcohol, barbiturates, or narcotics, corticosteroids, ACTH, pressor amines (e.g. norepinephrine), nondepolarizing skeletal muscle relaxants (e.g. tubocurarine), lithium NSAIDs, digoxin.

flattened_sections.indications: To improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: (1) As monotherapy in patients inadequately controlled by diet and exercise alone or for whom metformin is inappropriate; (2) in combination with metformin, a sulfonylurea, or a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-gamma) agonist (i.e. thiazolidinedione), as dual therapy, when diet and exercise plus the individual agent alone do not provide adequate glycemic control; (3) with a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist and metformin, as triple therapy, when diet and exercise plus dual therapy with these agents do not provide adequate glycemic control; (4) with insulin as an adjunct to diet and exercise.
flattened_sections.dose: 100 mg once daily. In combination with metformin and/or PPAR-gamma agonist: Maintain dose and administer sitagliptin concomitantly. In combination with sulfonylurea or with insulin: Consider lower dose for sulfonylurea or insulin. Renal impairment - Moderate (eGFR ≥30-<45 mL/min/1.73 m2): 50 mg once daily; Severe (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2) or with ESRD requiring hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis: 25 mg once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with type 1 DM. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not used to treat diabetic ketoacidosis. Patients with severe hepatic impairment, history of pancreatitis, heart failure. Discontinue if pancreatitis, hypersensitivity reactions, bullous pemphigoid are suspected. May cause severe joint pain. Concomitant use with other anti-hyperglycemic agents. Pregnancy. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hypoglycemia, headache.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors, metformin, ciclosporin, digoxin.

brand_info.content: To improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: (1) As monotherapy in patients inadequately controlled by diet and exercise alone or for whom metformin is inappropriate; (2) in combination with metformin, a sulfonylurea, or a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-gamma) agonist (i.e. thiazolidinedione), as dual therapy, when diet and exercise plus the individual agent alone do not provide adequate glycemic control; (3) with a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist and metformin, as triple therapy, when diet and exercise plus dual therapy with these agents do not provide adequate glycemic control; (4) with insulin as an adjunct to diet and exercise.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: 100 mg once daily. In combination with metformin and/or PPAR-gamma agonist: Maintain dose and administer sitagliptin concomitantly. In combination with sulfonylurea or with insulin: Consider lower dose for sulfonylurea or insulin. Renal impairment - Moderate (eGFR ≥30-<45 mL/min/1.73 m2): 50 mg once daily; Severe (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2) or with ESRD requiring hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis: 25 mg once daily.

brand_info.title: Contraindications

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Not used to treat diabetic ketoacidosis. Patients with severe hepatic impairment, history of pancreatitis, heart failure. pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

indication_long: Treatment for schizophrenia; moderate to seve...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment for schizophrenia; moderate to severe manic episodes. Prevention of recurrence in patients with bipolar disorder whose manic episodes have responded to olanzapine treatment.
flattened_sections.dose: Daily dosage may be individually adjusted within the range of 5-20 mg/day at intervals of >24 hrs. Adults - Schizophrenia: 10 mg/day. Manic episodes: Initially 15 mg once daily as monotherapy or 10 mg daily in combination therapy. Prevention of recurrence in bipolar disorder: Initially 10 mg/day. Continue at the same dose of treatment for manic episodes. If new manic, mixed, or depressive episode occurs, olanzapine should be continued (with dose optimization as needed), with supplementary therapy to treat mood symptoms. Elderly ≥65 yrs and patients with renal and/or hepatic impairment: Initially 5 mg/day. Moderate hepatic insufficiency (e.g. cirrhosis, Child-Pugh class A or B): Initially 5 mg, only increased with caution. Place tab immediately in the mouth and allow it to disperse in saliva to be easily swallowed or immediately dispersed in a full glass of water or other beverages (e.g. orange or apple juice, milk, coffee) before administration.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with known risk of narrow-angle glaucoma.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Not indicated for dementia-related psychosis and/or behavioral disturbances; dopamine agonist-associated psychosis in patients with Parkinson’s disease. Patients with prostatic hypertrophy, paralytic ileus, and related conditions; ALT and/or AST, with signs and symptoms of hepatic impairment, pre-existing conditions associated with limited hepatic functional reserve, or treated with hepatotoxic drugs; neutropenia, neutropenia-causing drugs, history of bone marrow depression, radiation therapy or chemotherapy, hyper eosinophilic conditions, myeloproliferative disease; congenital long QT prolongation, CHF, heart hypertrophy, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia; history of seizures or other conditions that potentially lower the seizure threshold; phenylketonuria. Concomitant use with other centrally acting medicines and alcohol. Consider lowering the initial dose when >1 factor which might result in slower metabolism (e.g. female, geriatric age, non-smoking status) is present. Monitor BP regularly of patients >65 yrs, signs and symptoms of hyperglycemia and/or development or exacerbation of diabetes, weight, lipid alterations, anticholinergic activity, QT prolongation, VTE, tardive dyskinesia, postural hypotension, sudden cardiac death. Discontinue treatment when hepatitis, hepatocellular, cholestatic, mixed liver injury or signs and symptoms of NMS occur. Childn and adolescents < 18 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Sedation, hypersomnia, lethargy, somnolence, weight gain, eosinophilia, elevated prolactin, cholesterol, glucose, and triglyceride levels, decreased total bilirubin, glucosuria, increased appetite, dizziness, akathisia, parkinsonism, dyskinesia, orthostatic hypotension, anticholinergic effects, ALT/AST elevations, rash, asthenia, fatigue, edema.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CYP1A2 inducers (e.g. smoking, carbamazepine) and inhibitors (e.g. fluvoxamine). Activated charcoal. Direct and indirect dopamine agonists. Alcohol, CNS depressants, anti-Parkisonian medications. QT-prolonging agents.

flattened_sections.indications: In combination with prednisone or prednisolone, treatment of newly diagnosed high risk metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) in adult men with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT); metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) in adult men who are asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic after failure of ADT in whom chemotherapy is not yet clinically indicated, or in adult men whose disease has progressed on or after a docetaxel-based chemotherapy regimen.
flattened_sections.dose: 4 tabs (1000 mg) once daily swallowed whole with water, without meals. Prednisone or prednisolone dose in combination - mHSPC: 5 mg daily; mCRPC: 10 mg daily. Continue medical castration with luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) analogue during treatment if not surgically castrated. Re-treatment following return of liver function to baseline: Reduced dose of 500 mg once daily. See complete product insert for dose modifications during toxicity. Taken at least 2 hrs after eating and no food at least 1 hr after administration.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with prednisone or prednisolone in combination with Ra-223 dichloride. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Maintain potassium level at ≥4 mM in patients with pre-existing or have developed hypokalemia during treatment. Patients with moderate hepatic or severe renal impairment; underlying medical conditions who might be compromised by an increase in BP, hypokalemia, or fluid retention, severe or unstable angina pectoris, recent MI or ventricular arrhythmia; history of CV disease; active or symptomatic viral hepatitis; previously treated with ketoconazole; galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption; on a controlled sodium diet. HTN, hypokalemia and fluid retention; QT prolongation; adrenocortical insufficiency on corticosteroid withdrawal; decreased bone density, hyperglycemia; anemia, sexual dysfunction; myopathy. Concomitant use with corticosteroids, cytotoxic chemotherapy, drugs associated with myopathy/rhabdomyolysis, strong CYP3A4 inducers. Measure serum transaminases prior to therapy, every 2 weeks for the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months, and monthly thereafter; minimum of every 2 weeks for 3 months and monthly for re-treatment. Monitor BP, serum potassium, and fluid retention monthly; if with significant risk for CHF, every 2 weeks for 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months and monthly thereafter. Assess cardiac functions (e.g. ECG) before treating patients with significant risk for CHF. Withhold treatment when Grade ≥3 toxicities or hepatotoxicity (ALT or AST >5x ULN) occur or recur. Affect fertility. Childn. Use contraception.
flattened_sections.side_effects: UTI; hypokalemia; HTN; diarrhea; increased ALT an/or AST; peripheral edema. Sepsis; hypertriglyceridemia; cardiac failure (including CHF, left ventricular dysfunction, decreased ejection fraction), angina pectoris, atrial fibrillation, tachycardia; dyspepsia; rash; hematuria; fractures except pathological fractures.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, rifabutin, rifapentine, phenobarbital, St. John’s Wort) and inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole); CYP2D6-metabolized drugs (e.g. dextromethorphan, metoprolol, propranolol, desipramine, venlafaxine, haloperidol, risperidone, propafenone, flecainide, codeine, oxycodone, tramadol); pioglitazone; drugs eliminated by OATP1B1, QT-prolonging drugs (e.g. class IA or III antiarrhythmics, methadone, moxifloxacin, antipsychotics); spironolactone.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Management of Kaposi’s sarcoma (KS) in patients with AIDS. Treatment of metastatic breast and ovarian cancers; multiple myeloma with bortezomib.
flattened_sections.dose: IV infusion. Breast or ovarian cancer: 50 mg/m2 at an initial rate of 1 mg/min once every 4 weeks, can be increased to complete administration over 1 hr if no infusion-related reactions are observed; if infusion-related reaction occurs: 5% of the total dose slowly over the 1st 15 mins, may be doubled for the next 15 mins if tolerated without reaction, then completed over the next hr for a total infusion time of 90 mins. A minimum of 4 courses is recommended. Concomitant or pretreatment with antiemetics. AIDS-KS: 20 mg/m2 over 30 mins once every 3 weeks when tolerated. Should not be administered as bolus injection or undiluted soln. If any signs or symptoms of extravasation are observed, terminate immediately and restart in another vein. Apply ice over the extravasation site for approx 30 mins to alleviate local reaction. Multiple myeloma: 30 mg/m over 60 mins on day 4 after bortezomib of each 21-day cycle for 8 cycles or until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Hepatic impairment - Bilirubin 1.2-3.0 mg/dL: Reduce dose by 25%; >3.0 mg/dL: Reduce dose by 50%. Increase to full dose for cycle 2 if the first dose is tolerated without an increase in serum bilirubin or liver enzymes. If reduced by 50%, increase to 75% for cycle 2, can be increased to full dose for subsequent cycles. See product insert for dose modifications during toxicity and preparation.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not suitable for IM or SC administration. Should not be used interchangeably with other formulations of doxorubicin. Patients with hepatic impairment; previous or concomitant therapy with other anthracyclines or related compounds; history of CV disease; AIDS-KS with baseline myelosuppression. Concomitant use with other anthracyclines or drugs that can cause bone marrow suppression. Cardiac toxicity at dose 450 mg/min<sup>2</sup> prior mediastinal irradiation or those receiving concurrent cyclophosphamide therapy; CHF due to cardiomyopathy; acute infusion-related reactions; serious, life-threatening or fatal allergic/anaphylactoid-like infusion reactions; hematologic toxicities; radiation-induced toxicity. Monitor ECG frequently; if reduction of the QRS complex or cardiomyopathy occurs, consider endomyocardial biopsy. Perform echocardiography or multigated angiography prior to initiation and during therapy. Monitor WBC, neutrophil, platelet count, and Hgb/Hct. Evaluate hepatic function prior to administration; left ventricular function before each added administration that exceeds lifetime cumulative anthracycline 450 mg/min<sup>2</sup>. Discontinue treatment if sepsis occurs. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Hematological adverse effects (e.g. leukopenia, neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia), palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, stomatitis, nausea, asthenia, vomiting, rash, alopecia, constipation, anorexia, mucous membrane disorder, diarrhea, abdominal pain, paresthesia, pain, fever, pharyngitis, dry skin, headache, dyspepsia, somnolence, skin discoloration; alopecia, increased alkaline phosphatase, vomiting, stomatitis, oral moniliasis.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Antineoplastics (e.g. cyclophosphamide, 6-mercaptopurine), cytotoxic (especially myelotoxic) agents.
flattened_sections.packaging: Liposomal concentrate solution for IV infusion 2 mg/mL (P25,000.00).

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of chemotherapy-naive patients with unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma in combination with cisplatin. Treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer other than predominantly squamous cell histology: (1) 1<sup>st</sup>-line in combination with cisplatin, (2) maintenance as monotherapy in patients whose disease has not progressed immediately following platinum-based chemotherapy, and (3) 2<sup>nd</sup>-line as monotherapy.
flattened_sections.dose: All doses given via IV infusion over 10 mins on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Reconstitute and dilute with preservative-free normal saline inj. In combination with cisplatin: 500 mg/m2 before 2 hrs infusion of 75 mg/m2 cisplatin. Antiemetics and appropriate hydration must be given prior and/or after receiving cisplatin. Monotherapy: 500 mg/m2. Pre-medication regimen: Give corticosteroid (4 mg oral dexamethasone 2x daily) prior to, the same day and day after each dose; oral folic acid or multivitamin containing 350-1,000 mcg folic acid daily, at least 5 doses for 7 days prior to 1st dose of treatment, continued throughout therapy and on day 21 after last dose; 1,000 mcg vit B12 IM 1 week prior to 1st dose of treatment and once on the same day every 3 cycles. Prior to start of any cycle, patient should have ANC ≥1,500 cells/mm3 and platelets ≥100,000 cells/mm3; total bilirubin ≤1.5x ULN; alkaline phosphate, AST/SGOT, and ALT/SGPT ≤3x ULN or ≤5x ULN if liver has tumor involvement. See complete product insert for preparation method and dose modifications during toxicity.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with yellow fever vaccine. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Contact on skin and mucous membranes. Patients with renal (CrCl < 45 mL/min) or hepatic (bilirubin >1.5x ULN, aminotransferase >3x ULN without hepatic metastases or >5x ULN with hepatic metastases) impairment; risk factors for the development of renal events (e.g. dehydration, preexisting HTN or diabetes) and CV disease; pleural effusion or ascites; on a controlled sodium diet. Bone marrow suppression; myelosuppression; skin reactions; serious renal events including acute renal failure; severe dehydration; serious CV events including MI and cerebrovascular events; immunodepression; radiation pneumonitis or recall. Concomitant use with NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen, aspirin >1.3 g daily) or radiotherapy. Incompatibility with calcium containing (e.g. Lactated Ringer’s and Ringer’s inj). Monitor CBC including differential WBC and platelet count and evaluate renal and hepatic function using blood chemistry tests prior each dose. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Irreversible men infertility. Use contraception and avoid fathering a child during and 6 months after treatment. Women of childbearing potential.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Decreased neutrophils/granulocytes, leucocytes, Hgb, platelets; sensory neuropathy; diarrhea, vomiting, stomatitis/pharyngitis, nausea, anorexia, constipation; rash, alopecia; elevated creatinine, decreased CrCl; fatigue. Dehydration; taste disturbance; conjunctivitis; dyspepsia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, platinum compounds, ciclosporin; probenecid, penicillin; high doses of NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen >1.6 g/day, aspirin ≥1.3 g/day; piroxicam, rofecoxib; oral anticoagulants; live attenuated vaccines. Incompatibility with calcium-containing diluents (e.g. Lactated Ringer’s and Ringer’s inj).
flattened_sections.packaging: Lyophilized powder for IV infusion 500 mg (P17,857.14).

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of ocular infections caused by susceptible microorganisms. Prevention of post-op ocular inflammation and bacterial infection.
flattened_sections.dose: Prevention of post-op ocular inflammation and infection: 1 drop 4x daily in the eye to be operated, given 1 day pre-op until 15 days post-op; Cataract surgery: Instill immediately post-op; Refractive surgery by LASIK: Instill within 15 mins post-op. Treatment of ocular infections caused by susceptible organisms: 1 drop 4x daily for 7 days.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Herpes simplex keratitis, vaccinia, varicella, other corneal or conjunctival viral infections; mycobacterial and fungal ocular infections.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not for injection. Do not inject subconjunctivally nor introduce directly into the anterior chamber of the eye. Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity reactions, cardiovascular collapse, loss of consciousness, angioedema, airway obstruction, dyspnea, urticaria, and itching in patients receiving systemically administered quinolones. Prolonged use may cause ocular HTN or glaucoma with optic nerve damage, reduced visual acuity, visual field defects, and posterior subcapsular cataract formation; increased hazard of secondary ocular infections; thinning or cornea or sclera, perforations; reduction of resistance to and development of non-susceptible bacterial, fungal, or viral infections; tendon inflammation and rupture; delayed corneal wound healing; overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms (e.g. fungi). Discontinue treatment at first sign of tendon inflammation and superinfection. May mask clinical signs of infection. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Eye pruritus and irritation.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of hypertension (HTN) and in renovascular HTN. Management of congestive heart failure (CHF) as an adjunct treatment with diuretics. Treatment of hemodynamically stable patients within 24 hrs of an acute myocardial infarction (MI) to prevent subsequent development of left ventricular dysfunction or heart failure. To reduce urinary albumin excretion rate in normotensive insulin-dependent and hypertensive non-insulindependent diabetes mellitus (DM) patients with incipient nephropathy.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - HTN: Initially 10 mg. Maintenance dose: 20 mg as single daily dose. Max 80 mg daily. Patients on diuretics: Initially 5 mg. Renovascular HTN: Initially 2.5 or 5 mg. Renal impairment – CrCl 31-80 mL/min: Initially 5-10 mg/day. 10-30 mL/min: 2.5-5 mg/day; <10 mL/min/1.73 m2: 2.5 mg/day. Dosage may be titrated until BP is controlled or to max of 40 mg daily. CHF: Initially 2.5 mg once daily, may be increased by increments not >10 mg, at intervals of not <2 weeks up to max 35 mg once daily. Acute MI: 5 mg once daily, followed by 5 mg after 24 hrs, 10 mg after 48 hrs, then 10 mg once daily thereafter. Patients with low systolic BP (<120 mmHg): 2.5 mg initially or during the first 3 days; if hypotension (SBP ≤100 mmHg) occurs, maintenance of 5 mg/day may be reduced to 2.5 mg. Renal complications of DM: 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 20 mg once daily. Childn and adolescents 6-16 yrs – ≥50 kg BW: 5 mg once daily. Max 40 mg daily; 20-50 kg BW: 2.5 mg. Max 20 mg daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with history of anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reactions or angioedema from previous treatment with ACE inhibitors. Concomitant use of aliskiren-containing drugs in patients with DM (type 1 or 2) or with moderate to severe renal impairment (GFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters).
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with vol-depletion, CHF with or without renal insufficiency, IHD, or cerebrovascular disease; aortic stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; SBP ≤100 mmHg or cardiogenic shock. Dual blockade of RAAS. Major surgery or during anesthesia. Renal impairment and dialysis. Withhold treatment during desensitization treatment (Hymenoptera venom). ACE-inhibitor induced cough. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Black patients. Childn <6yrs or in childn with severe renal impairment (GFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Elderly. Lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Dizziness, headache; orthostatic effects (including hyotension); diarrhea, vomiting; cough, renal dysfunction.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Temsirolimus, sirolimus, everolimus, racecadotril. Diuretics, antidiabetics. Potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium-containing salt substitutes. Lithium, gold, NSAIDs.

flattened_sections.indications: Replacement therapy for male adults with hypogonadism when testosterone deficiency has been clinically and biologically confirmed.
flattened_sections.dose: Prime the canister pump before the 1<sup>st</sup> dose; discard the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 pumps. Apply 2 pumps once daily on clean, dry, and healthy skin on the right and left shoulder and upper arms, at approx same time each day preferably in the morning. Spread in a thin layer and let dry for at least 3-5 mins before covering the application site with clothing. Dose can be adjusted in increments of 1 pump (20.25 mg testosterone or 1.25 g gel) based on patient’s response. Max 4 pumps/day. Take a shower or wash hands and the application site thoroughly with soap and water to remove any residue before any anticipated contact with another person’s skin.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with confirmed or suspected prostate cancer or breast carcinoma.
flattened_sections.precautions: Intended for use by men only. Not indicated for male sterility or impotence. Should not be applied to the genitals. Perform a thorough examination to rule out any risk of preexisting prostate cancer before initiating treatment. Regular monitoring of prostate and breasts should be done using the recommended methods (rectal examination and PSA-prostate-specific antigen assay) at least once a yr; twice a yr in elderly patients and patients at risk. May accelerate progression of subclinical prostate cancer or BPH. Patients with cancer with risk of hypercalcemia (and associated hypercalciuria related to bone metastases; severe heart, liver, or kidney failure; IHD; HTN; thrombophilia or with risk factors for VTE; epilepsy, migraine; obesity, chronic respiratory disease. Irritability, nervousness, weight gain, prolonged or frequent erections; spermatogenesis suppression; gynecomastia. Risk of inadvertent testosterone transfer. May induce a positive reaction to tests performed during anti-doping controls. Contains alcohol; may cause burning sensation on damaged skin. May interfere with laboratory tests for thyroid hormones. Female patients. Male childn < 18 yrs. Elderly >65 yrs.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Emotional symptoms (e.g. mood swings, affective disorders, anger, aggression, impatience, insomnia, abnormal dreams, increased libido); skin reactions (e.g. acne, alopecia, skin dryness or lesions, contact dermatitis, hair color changes, rash, hypersensitivity, pruritus); increased PSA, Hgb, or Hct.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Oral anticoagulants, ACTH or corticosteroids, antidiabetics. Positive reaction to anti-doping controls.
flattened_sections.packaging: Transdermal gel 16.2 mg/g x 88 g (approx 60 doses) (P2,588.75).

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of endometriosis.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults: Start on any day of the menstrual cycle. 1 tab daily without break, preferably at the same time each day; must be taken continuously regardless of any vaginal bleeding. When pack is finished, start the next pack without interruption.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active venous thromboembolic disorder. Present or history of arterial and CV disease (e.g. MI, CVA, IHD); severe hepatic disease as long as liver function values have not returned to normal; liver tumors (benign or malignant). DM with vascular involvement.  Known or suspected sex hormone-dependent malignancies. Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Ocular lesion due to ophthalmic vascular disease (e.g. partial or complete loss of vision or visual field defect). Current or history of migraine with focal aura. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid smoking. Serious uterine bleeding. Risk for osteoporosis and changes in bone mineral density. Women with diabetes; history of chloasma, depression, extrauterine pregnancy or impairment of tube function. May experience changes in bleeding pattern, HTN, recurrence of cholestatic jaundice and/or pruritus, persistent ovarian follicles. Discontinue if there is a presence or suspected arterial or venous thrombotic event. Monitor any irregularity or anomaly of the breast.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of the following infections due to susceptible organisms: lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) including pneumonia; acute bacterial otitis media; skin and skin structure infections, complicated and uncomplicated urinary tract infections; uncomplicated cervical/urethral, pharyngeal, and rectal uncomplicated gonorrhea; pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), bacterial septicemia, bone and joint infections, intraabdominal infections (e.g. peritonitis, infections of the biliary and gastrointestinal tracts), meningitis. Peri-op prophylaxis for the reduction of post-op infections in patients undergoing contaminated or potentially contaminated surgical procedures and in patients for whom infection at the operative site would pose a serious risk.
flattened_sections.dose: Administered via IV injection for 2-4 mins, IM injection, or IV infusion for 30 mins (doses >50 mg/kg). Adults: 1-2 g once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily. Max 4 g/day; LRTI including pneumonia: 1 g IV once or twice daily in combination with other anti-infectives; Uncomplicated gonorrhea: 250 mg IM single dose; PID: 250 mg IM single dose, followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days, with or without oral metronidazole 500 mg twice daily; Surgical prophylaxis: 1 g IV single dose, administered ½-2 hrs before surgery; For cholecystectomy: 1-2 g IV single dose, administered ½-2 hrs before surgery; Meningitis: 2 g IV twice daily for 7- 21 days. Renal and hepatic impairment: Max 2 g/day. Childn - >12 yrs weighing >50 kg: Adult dose. Childn and infants 15 days-12 yrs: 20-80 mg/kg once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily. Neonates ≤14 days: 20-50 mg/kg IV for 60 mins once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily. Childn and neonates ≤12 yrs - Skin and skin structure infections: 50-75 mg/kg once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily. Max 2 g/day; Acute bacterial otitis media: 50 mg/kg IM single dose. Max 1 g; Serious infections other than meningitis: 50-75 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses twice daily. Max 2 g/day; Meningitis: 100 mg/kg once daily or in equally divided doses twice daily for 7-21 days. Max 4 g/day. Childn < 50 kg with uncomplicated gonococcal vulvovaginitis, cervicitis, urethritis, epididymitis, pharyngitis, or proctitis: Single 125 mg IM. Treatment duration - Usual: 4-14 days. Complicated infections may require longer treatment; Most infections except gonorrhea: At least 48-72 hrs after the patient becomes asymptomatic or evidence of bacterial eradication has been obtained; Infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes: At least 10 days.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Neonates (especially premature) with hyperbilirubinemia or jaundice. Infants ≤28 days who require or expected to require treatment with calcium-containing IV solns, including continuous calcium-containing infusions (e.g. parenteral nutrition).
flattened_sections.precautions: Cross-sensitivity with other beta-lactam antibiotics. Patients with history of cephalosporin-associated hemolytic anemia; history of GI disease, particularly colitis; renal or hepatic impairment, poor nutritional state; those receiving a protracted course of antimicrobials or previously stabilized on anticoagulants. Concomitant use with calcium-containing IV solns, including continuous calcium-containing infusions (e.g. parenteral nutrition). Gallbladder disease including sonographic abnormalities; seizures; fall in prothrombin activity may occur. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms. Monitor blood levels of patients with severe renal impairment and those with both renal and hepatic impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. IM: Do not inject >1 g at a single site.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Alcohol, aminoglycosides (e.g. amikacin, gentamicin, tobramycin), chloramphenicol, oral anticoagulants and contraceptives, probenecid, trovafloxacin. False positive Benedict’s soln, Clinitest, Coomb’s test, tests for galactosemia. False elevation of serum creatinine values. Incompatibilities: Calcium-containing diluents (e.g. Ringer’s or Hartmann’s soln) should not be used for reconstitution.

flattened_sections.dose: May be administered by slow IM injection, IV infusion (10-30 mins), and IV bolus (not <15 secs). 50 mg every 8-12 hrs, intervals may be reduced to every 6 hrs if necessary. Max 150 mg/day. Hepatic (Child-Pugh score 5-9) and renal (CrCl 50-80 mL/min) impairment: 50 mg/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with active or suspected peptic ulcer or hemorrhage, history of recurrent peptic ulcer or hemorrhage or chronic dyspepsia, GI bleeding or other bleeding disorders, history of NSAID-induced GI bleeding or perforation, Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis, severe heart failure, moderate to severe renal dysfunction (CrCl <50 mL/min), severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 10-15), hemorrhagic diathesis and other coagulation disorders. Patients in whom aspirin and NSAIDs precipitate asthma attacks, bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, cause nasal polyps, urticaria or angioneurotic edema. Not for neuraxial (intrathecal or epidural) administration. Pregnancy (3<sup>rd</sup> trimester) and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: History of allergic conditions, GI disease, esophagitis, gastritis or peptic ulcer, HTN and/or mild CHF. Concomitant use with other NSAIDs, including COX-2 inhibitors, oral corticosteroids, warfarin, aspirin, heparin, and other coumarins. Discontinue when GI bleeding or ulceration occurs. Consider combination with protective agents (e.g. misoprostol or PPIs). Patients with uncontrolled HTN, CHF, IHD, PAD, and CVD, renal and hepatic impairment, hematopoietic disorders, SLE or mixed connective tissue disease; receiving diuretics; who could develop hypovolemia. Childn and adolescents. Elderly. Women attempting to conceive. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> and 2<sup>nd</sup> trimester).
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, injection site pain, inflammation, bruising or hemorrhage.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Other NSAIDs, warfarin, heparin, corticosteroids, lithium, methotrexate, hydantoins and sulfonamides. flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of serious infections due to susceptible organisms, including respiratory tract, urinary tract (UTI), skin and skin structure, biliary tract, bone and joint, and genital infections; septicemia and endocarditis; peri-op prophylaxis. Treatment and prevention of streptococcal infections, including prophylaxis of rheumatic fever.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - Moderate to severe infections: 500 mg-1 g every 6-8 hrs; Mild infections caused by susceptible G(+) cocci: 250-500 mg every 8 hrs; Acute, uncomplicated UTI: 1 g every 12 hrs; Pneumococcal pneumonia: 500 mg every 12 hrs; Severe, life-threatening infections (e.g. endocarditis, septicemia): 1-1.5 g every 6 hrs. Peri-op prophylaxis: (1) 1 g IV/IM given 30 mins-1 hr before surgery; (2) 500-1 g IV/IM during surgery; (3) 500 mg-1 g IV/IM every 6-8 hrs for 24 hrs post-op. Renal impairment - CrCl 35-54 mL/min: Full doses every 8 hrs; 11-34 mL/min: Half of usual dose every 12 hrs; 10 mL/min: Half of usual dose every 18-24 hrs. Childn - Mild to moderate infections: 25-50 mg/kg in 3-4 divided doses; Severe infections: 100 mg/kg. Renal impairment - CrCl 70-40 mL/min: 60% of normal daily dose in divided doses every 12 hrs; 40-20 mL/min: 25% of normal daily dose in divided doses every 12 hrs; 20-5 mL/min: 10% of normal daily dose every 24 hrs.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: History of allergy to penicillins. Discontinue when allergic reaction occurs. Prolonged use may result in overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, history of GI disease (colitis), poor nutritional state; receiving protracted course of antimicrobial therapy, previously stabilized on anticoagulant therapy. Premature infants and neonates. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Diarrhea, oral candidiasis, vomiting, nausea, stomach cramps, anorexia and pseudomembranous colitis, anaphylaxis, eosinophilia, itching, drug fever, skin rash, SJS, neutropenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, thrombocythemia, transient increase in SGOT, SGPT and alkaline phosphatase, genital and anal pruritus.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Probenecid. False positive for glucose in urine with Benedict’s solution, Fehling’s solution, or Clinitest tabs.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of nosocomial pneumonia, bronchopulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis, bacterial meningitis, chronic suppurative otitis media, malignant otitis externa; complicated urinary tract (UTI), skin and soft tissue, intra-abdominal, bone and joint infections; peritonitis associated with dialysis in patients on CAPD; bacteremia. Management of neutropenic patients with fever suspected due to a bacterial infection; peri-op prophylaxis of UTI for patients undergoing trans-urethral resection of the prostate (TURP).
flattened_sections.dose: Adults and childn weighing ≥40 kg - Intermittent administration - Bronchopulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis: 100-150 mg/kg/day every 8 hrs. Max 9 g/day. Febrile neutropenia, nosocomial pneumonia, bacterial meningitis, bacteremia: 2 g every 8 hrs. Bone and joint, complicated skin and soft tissue, intra-abdominal infections, peritonitis associated with dialysis in CAPD patients, chronic suppurative otitis media, malignant otitis media: 1-2 g every 8 hrs. Complicated UTI: 1-2 g every 8 or 12 hrs. Peri-op prophylaxis for TURP: 1 g at induction of anesthesia, and 2nd dose at catheter removal. Continuous infusion: Loading dose of 2 g, followed by 4-6 g continuous infusion every 24 hrs. Renal impairment - CrCl 50-31 mL/min: 1 g every 12 hrs (intermittent administration), loading dose of 2 g followed by 1-3 g continuous infusion every 24 hrs; 30-16 mL/min: 1 g every 24 hrs (intermittent administration), loading dose of 2 g followed by 1 g continuous infusion every 24 hrs; 15-6 mL/min: 0.5 g every 24 hrs; <5 mL/min: 0.5 g every 48 hrs. Infants and toddlers >2 months and childn weighing <40 kg - Intermittent administration - Most infections: 100-150 mg/kg/day given in 3 divided doses. Max 6 g/day. Neutropenia, bronchopulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis, bacterial meningitis, bacteremia: 150 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. Max 6 g/day. Continuous infusion: Loading dose of 60-100 mg/kg followed by 100-200 mg/kg/day continuous infusion. Max 6 g/day. Neonates and infants ≤2 months: 25-60 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. Renal impairment - CrCl 50-31 mL/min: 25 mg/kg every 12 hrs; 3-16 mL/min: 25 mg/kg every 24 hrs; 15-6 mL/min: 12.5 mg/kg every 24 hrs; <5 mL/min: 12.5 mg/kg every 48 hrs. Hemodialysis: 1 g daily as single dose or in divided doses.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not used as single agent for treatment of some types of infections. Discontinue if severe hypersensitivity reactions, and diarrhea occur. Patients with renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Eosinophilia, thrombocytopenia, phlebitis or thrombophlebitis, diarrhea, transient elevations of hepatic enzymes, maculopapular or urticarial rash, pain and inflammation, positive Coombs’ test.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Probenecid, furosemide, chloramphenicol.

Start with the tab marked number '1' and follow the arrows indicated on the pack. Clarithromycin, erythromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, ritonavir, or grapefruit juice. Carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, felbamate, topiramate, phenytoin, griseofulvin, troglitazone, phenylbutazone, rifampicin and troleandomycin.

flattened_sections.dose: Administered as single IV infusion for not <15 mins. Prevention of skeletal-related events with advanced bone malignancies: 4 mg every 3-4 weeks. Also administer 500 mg oral calcium supplement and 400 IU vitamin D daily. Patients with renal impairment - CrCl >60 mL/min: 4 mg; 50-60 mL/min: 3.5 mg; 40-49 mL/min: 3.3 mg; 30-39 mL/min: 3 mg. Treatment of TIH: 4 mg single dose.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Assess patient hydration before therapy. Avoid overhydration in patients at risk of cardiac failure. Monitor calcium, phosphate, and magnesium serum levels. Do not mix with calcium or other divalent cation-containing infusion solutions e.g. Lactated Ringer’s soln. Discontinue when atypical femur fracture develops. Coadministration with other medicinal products known to cause hypercalcemia. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy.

Patients with deformation of penis (e.g. angulation, cavernosal fibrosis or Peyronie’s disease) or patients who have conditions which predispose priapism (e.g. sickle cell anemia, multiple myeloma, leukemia). flattened_sections.indications: Reduction in duration of neutropenia in bone marrow transplant (BMT) and in patients receiving cytotoxic therapy. Mobilization of peripheral blood progenitor cells (PBPCs) in patients undergoing myelosuppressive therapy followed by autologous PBPC transplantation or in normal donors prior to allogeneic PBPC transplantation. Treatment of severe congenital, cyclic, or idiopathic neutropenia; persistent neutropenia in patients with advanced HIV infection.
flattened_sections.dose: Cytotoxic therapy: 0.5 MIU (5 mcg/kg/day) as single SC injection or IV infusion for 15-30 mins daily up to 2 weeks until absolute neutrophil count (ANC) has reached 10,000/mm3 following expected neutrophil nadir; may be increased by 0.5 MIU/kg/day depending on duration and severity of ANC nadir. Administer at least 24 hrs after cytotoxic therapy. Following BMT: 1 MIU (10 mcg/kg/day) IV infusion for 4 or 24 hrs, or continuous 24-hr SC infusion; 1st dose is administered at least 24 hrs after cytotoxic chemotherapy and bone marrow infusion. Mobilization of PBPC: 1 MIU (10 mcg/kg/day) SC, as bolus or continuous infusion, at least 4 days before 1st leukapheresis until last leukapheresis. Congenital neutropenia: 0.6 MIU (6 mcg/kg) SC twice daily. Idiopathic or cyclic neutropenia: 0.5 MIU (5 mcg/kg) SC daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Cross-reactivity with endogenous G-CSF and other E. coli-derived proteins. Patients with myelodysplasia, acute myelogenous leukemia, chronic myelogenous leukemia; pre-malignant myeloid conditions; high-dose chemotherapy; sepsis; sickle cell disease (i.e. homozygous sickle cell anemia, sickle cell-Hgb C disease, sickle cell beta+-thalassemia). May induce splenic rupture, alveolar hemorrhage manifesting as pulmonary infiltrates, hemoptysis, allergic-type reactions; mild to moderate cutaneous vasculitis in patients with SCN. Perform CBC and platelet counts regularly. Rule out any conditions causing neutropenia, other than SCN, prior to treatment of SCN. Discontinue if ANC >10,000/mm3 or if ARDS develops. Childn. Elderly <65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Medullary and musculoskeletal bone pain. Transient decrease in BP.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Myelosuppressive cytotoxic drugs, drugs which may potentiate neutrophil release (e.g. lithium), bone scan. IV incompatibilities: Saline solns.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

indication_long: Prior to childbirth: (1) labor inducti...

flattened_sections.indications: Prior to childbirth: (1) labor induction at term for medical reasons, (2) primary and secondary uterine inertia, and (3) stimulation of contractions (oxytocin stress test). After childbirth: (1) prophylaxis of post-abortion hemorrhage and increased postpartum bleeding, (2) stimulation and acceleration of placental separation and expulsion, (3) prophylaxis and treatment of uterine subinvolution in the puerperium, and (4) alternative agent for atonic postpartum hemorrhage when other uterine contraction agents (e.g. methylergometrine, prostaglandins or their derivates) are contraindicated or not tolerated.
flattened_sections.dose: May be administered via IM injection, IV injection, or IV infusion. Labor induction at term for medical reasons, primary and secondary uterine inertia: 1 IU diluted in 100 mL isotonic sodium chloride soln via IV drop infusion. Initially, the infusion rate should be 0.5-2x10-3 IU/min (i.e. 0.05-0.2 mL equiv to 1-4 drops/min), which can be gradually increased at intervals of not less than 15 mins by 1-2x10-3 IU/min until a contraction pattern comparable with spontaneous labor is achieved. Max infusion rate of 20-30x10-3 IU/min (i.e. 2-3 mL, equiv to 40-60 drops/min). If regular contractions are still absent after the infusion of 500 mL (5 IU), discontinue and attempt again on the following day. Reduce infusion rate as soon as appropriate uterine activity has been achieved and discontinue immediately in the event of excessive uterine activity and/or signs of placental malnutrition (fetal distress). During caesarian section after infant development: 5 IU via slow IV or prophylactically as IV infusion (30x10-3 IU/min) immediately after infant extraction. Postpartum period (atonic hemorrhage): 5-10 IU IM or 5-6 IU slow IV. For evacuation post-abortion: 3-6 IU IV or IM.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with pre-eclampsia, uterine tetany tendency, hypertonic uterine activity, imminent uterine rupture, placental abruption, placenta or vasa previa, immature cervix, imminent fetal asphyxiation, fetal distress unless delivery is immediately imminent, abnormal position (e.g. breech presentation), mechanical obstacle to delivery, and umbilical cord entanglement or prolapse.
flattened_sections.precautions: For single use only. Contains sodium. Prolonged use in patients with uterine inertia not sufficiently responding to oxytocin and severe CV disorders. Overdose or rapid administration may induce hypertonic labor, uterine tetany or rupture, fetal asphyxia or distress, or even infant death. Status post-gynecological surgery with opening of the uterine cavity (e.g. fibroid removal). Status post-cesarean section. Female patients who had >4 previous births; with secondary uterine inertia, presence of borderline head/pelvis misalignment, mild to moderate pre-eclampsia, and cardiac disorders. Older multiparous women. Hyperactive uterine activity may lead to retinal hemorrhage in infants. Concomitant use with parenteral galactagogues containing oxytocin. Postpartum DIC, water intoxication associated with hyponatremia, hemodynamic form of acute pulmonary edema without hyponatremia may occur. Restrict oral fluid intake and monitor fluid and serum balance. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Females ≥35 yrs.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Excessive uterine activity. Headache; cardiac arrhythmias; increased BP; nausea, vomiting.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Prostaglandins, methylergometrine, QT-prolonging drugs, hypertensive sympathomimetics, halothane anesthesia.

indication_long: Progesterone replacement during the course of...

flattened_sections.indications: Progesterone replacement during the course of complete deficits in women with non-functioning ovaries (ovum transplant). Luteal phase supplementation during in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles; spontaneous or induced cycles in case of hypofertility or primary or secondary sterility due to dysovulation. Threat of abortion or prevention of repetitive abortions due to luteal insufficiency.
flattened_sections.dose: Progesterone replacement for women with non-functioning ovaries (ovum transplant): As adjunct to estrogen therapy, start with 100 mg/day on days 13 and 14 of transfer cycle, then 200 mg/day (100 mg in the morning, 100 mg at night) from days 15 to 25. From day 26 and in case of pregnancy, increase dose by 100 mg/day weekly to reach max 600 mg/day divided into 3 doses, maintained until day 60. Luteal phase supplementation - IVF cycles: 400-600 mg/day, from HCG injection until 12th week of pregnancy; Spontaneous or induced cycles (in cases of hypofertility or primary/secondary sterility due to dysovulation): 200-300 mg/day for 10 days from day 17 of cycle. In case of absence of periods or pregnancy, resume treatment as soon as possible. Threat of abortion or prevention of repetitive abortions due to luteal insufficiency: 200-400 mg/day divided into 2 doses. Caps are to be inserted deep into the vagina.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Allergy to peanut or soya. Patients with undiagnosed genital bleeding, severe liver dysfunction, liver tumors, suspected or confirmed breast or genital organ neoplasia, active or history of thromboembolic diseases, cerebral hemorrhage, porphyria. Contraindications related to estrogens when used for HRT in conjunction with estrogen. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not a contraceptive. Patients with history of venous thrombosis. Carefully examine uterine bleeding before initiation of dose. May aggravate metabolic and thromboembolic risks; discontinue if ocular disorders (e.g. reduced vision, diplopia, retinal vascular lesions), VTE or thrombotic events, or severe headaches occur. Should be used for threatened or recurrent abortion only if corpus luteum secretion is insufficient. Assess medical and family history before initiating or restarting treatment; adapt physical exams and regular check-ups to patient’s needs. Regular period-like bleeding may occur upon withdrawal in women with an intact uterus; if withdrawal bleeding is absent, endometrial hyperplasia should be ruled out. Breakthrough bleeding and spotting may occur during the 1<sup>st</sup> few months of treatment. Regular endometrial monitoring is recommended in long-term treatment (>5 yrs). May cause reduction in glucose tolerance. Contains soya bean lecithin. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters).
flattened_sections.side_effects: Irregular menstruation, amenorrhea, metrorrhagia, headaches.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: CYP450-3A4 inducers e.g. barbiturates, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, phenylbutazone, spironolactone, griseofulvin, ampicillin, tetracyclines, St. John’s wort. CYP450-3A4 inhibitors e.g. ketoconazole. Insulin and other antidiabetic agents. Liver and/or endocrine function tests.

brand_info.content: Progesterone replacement for women with non-functioning ovaries (ovum transplant): As adjunct to estrogen therapy, start with 100 mg/day on days 13 and 14 of transfer cycle, then 200 mg/day (100 mg in the morning, 100 mg at night) from days 15 to 25. From day 26 and in case of pregnancy, increase dose by 100 mg/day weekly to reach max 600 mg/day divided into 3 doses, maintained until day 60. Luteal phase supplementation - IVF cycles: 400-600 mg/day, from HCG injection until 12th week of pregnancy; Spontaneous or induced cycles (in cases of hypofertility or primary/secondary sterility due to dysovulation): 200-300 mg/day for 10 days from day 17 of cycle. brand_info.title: Precautions

Regular period-like bleeding may occur upon withdrawal in women with an intact uterus; if withdrawal bleeding is absent, endometrial hyperplasia should be ruled out. pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of bleeding in hemophilia A patients with inhibitors; in hemophilia B patients with inhibitors, if no other specific treatment is available; in non-hemophiliacs with acquired factor VIII inhibitors. Prophylaxis of bleeding in hemophilia A patients with inhibitors at high risk or with history of significant bleeding. Also used for long-term therapy, in combination with factor VIII concentrate, to achieve complete and permanent elimination of the factor VIII inhibitor.
flattened_sections.dose: Reconstituted soln conc: 50 U/mL. Usual dose: 50-100 U/kg. Max 100 U/kg BW single dose and 200 U/kg BW/day. Max infusion rate of 2 U/kg BW/min. Spontaneous bleeding - Joint, muscle, and soft tissue hemorrhage - Minor to moderately severe: 50-75 U/kg BW every 12 hrs. Severe (e.g. retroperitoneal hemorrhages): 100 U/kg BW every 12 hrs. Mucous membrane hemorrhage: 50 U/kg BW every 6 hrs, if bleeding does not stop, may be increased to 100 U/kg BW. Max 200 U/kg BW/day. Other severe hemorrhages: 100 U/kg BW every 12 hrs, may be administered every 6 hrs in individual cases. Max 200 U/kg BW/day. flattened_sections.description: A digital BP monitor that facilitates daily BP regimen in homecare setting.
flattened_sections.uses: Used to measure BP and pulse rate of adults.
flattened_sections.direction: Select the correct cuff size. Wrap the cuff around bare upper arm (preferably left arm), about 1-2 cm above the inside of the elbow. Press the start button. Squeeze the rubber bulb until the up mark disappears, then, the automatic exhaust mechanism will gradually reduce pressure in the cuff until the heart mark is displayed, along with the current pressure reading. Remain still during measurement. Once the measurement is complete, the down mark is displayed. Press the exhaust valve, then, remove the cuff from the arm. Press the start button to turn off. See instruction manual for complete instructions for use.
flattened_sections.contraindications: History of mastectomy. History of severe circulatory deficit in the arm. Childn. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid extreme temperature, humidity, direct sunlight, shock, or dust. Never use alcohol, benzene, thinner, or other harsh chemicals when cleaning. Avoid tightly folding the cuff or storing the hose tightly twisted for long periods. Device and cuff are not water-resistant. Do not use closely to televisions, microwave ovens, cellular telephones, X-ray or other devices with strong electrical fields. Keep a minimum distance of 30 cm from wireless communication devices. Do not use near flammable gases and highly concentrated oxygen environments. Using too frequently may cause prolonged impairment of blood circulation. Patients who had mastectomy. Allow the device to adapt for about 1 hr to surrounding environment before use.
flattened_sections.packaging:
A&D UA-704 Manual Inflation Digital Blood Pressure Monitor (P2,700.00).
