indication_long: For hypertension (HTN) as monotherapy or as c...

flattened_sections.indications: For hypertension (HTN) as monotherapy or as component of a multiple-drug regimen in the stepped care approach. Treatment of chronic heart failure with reduction of systolic ventricular function, in combination with diuretics, digitalis and beta blockers (when appropriate); macroproteinuric diabetic nephropathy in patients with type 1 diabetes. To improve survival following myocardial infarction (MI) in clinically stable patients with left ventricular dysfunction manifested as ejection fraction ≤40%; to reduce the incidence of overt heart failure and subsequent hospitalizations for congestive heart failure.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dose. Take 1 hr before meals. HTN: Initially 25 mg 2-3x a day, may be increased up to 150 mg 2-3x a day (with a diuretic), after 1 or 2 weeks. Max 450 mg/day in divided doses. Heart failure: 25 mg 3x a day. Max: 450 mg/day in divided doses. Patients with normal or low BP, are treated with diuretics and may be hyponatremic or hypovolemic: 6.25 or 12.5 mg 3x a day. Left ventricular dysfunction after MI: After a single dose of 6.25 mg, initiate 12.5 mg 3x a day, may be increased to 25 mg 3x a day after several days. Maintenance dose: 50 mg 3x a day. Diabetic nephropathy: 75-100 mg/day in divided doses. Patients with renal impairment: Initially 12.5 mg 2x a day. Elderly: Initially 6.25 mg 2x a day. Renal impairment - CrCl >40 mL/min/1.73 m2: 25-50 mg/day. Max 150 mg/day; 21-40 mL/min/1.73 m2: 25 mg/day. Max 100 mg/day; 10-20 mL/min/1.73 m2: 12.5 mg/day. Max 75 mg/day; < 10 mL/min/1.73 m2: 6.25 mg/day. Max 37.5 mg/day. Childn 12-18 yrs: 0.1 mg/kg. Max 6.25 mg (test dose). If tolerated, give 12.5-25 mg 2-3x a day. Max 150 mg/day; 1 month-12 yrs: 0.1 mg/kg. Max 6.25 mg (test dose). If tolerated, give 0.1-0.3 mg/kg 2-3x a day. Max 6 mg/kg/day in divided doses; and 4 mg/kg/day in divided doses (1 month-1 yr).
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. History of angioedema associated with previous ACE inhibitor therapy. Hereditary or idiopathic angioneurotic edema. Coadministration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients undergoing desensitization procedures; hemodialyzed with high-flux polyacrylonitrile membranes. Patients with collagen vascular disease, immunosuppressant therapy, pre-existing impaired renal function, bilateral renal artery stenosis or renal artery stenosis of a solitary kidney, heart failure, hepatic failure, renal insufficiency, DM, ischemic CV or cerebrovascular disease, left ventricular valvular and outflow tract obstruction, aortic stenosis. Perform WBC and differential counts before therapy and every 2 weeks during the 1st 3 months. Dual blockade of RAAS. Correct vol- and sodium depletion before treatment. Coadministration with mTOR, allopurinol or procainamide. Concomitant use with potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes. Surgery; anesthesia use. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Infants. Pregnancy Risk: Category C for 1st trimester and D for 2nd and 3rd trimester.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Angioedema, malaise, fatigue, asthenia, fever; blurred vision, itching or dry eyes, taste impairment, dysgeusia. CV, nervous system, GI, hematologic, musculoskeletal, metabolic or nutritional, respiratory, hepatic, skin and appendages, urogenital or reproductive effects.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Agents affecting sympathetic activity (e.g. ganglionic or adrenergic neuron-blocking agents); nitroglycerin or other nitrates; allopurinol, procainamide, cytostatic or immunosuppressive agents (e.g. azathioprine); antacids, antidiabetics, clonidine, lithium, NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin), probenecid. Other antihypertensive agents (e.g. beta-blockers, long-acting CCBs), potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride) or potassium supplements, TCAs, sympathomimetics. False-positive urine test for acetone.

categories.title: A

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt withdrawal. pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

data.description: Panbio COVID-19 Antigen Self-Test detects the nucleocapsid protein antigen of the Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 in a swab from the mid-turbinate nasal region. Includes a test device, a tube with buffer soln, and a nasal swab. Active ingredients of the test device are antibodies specific to the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein antigen.
data.directions: A human nasal specimen is collected using the swab provided in the kit. After sample collection, the nasal swab is transferred to the buffer tube to extract the Coronavirus proteins. Apply 5 drops of extracted sample to the round well on the test device. A line in the Control (C) line area within the result reading window will only become visible if the test was performed correctly. A line in the Test (T) line area within the result reading window indicates that Coronavirus proteins are detected. The presence of only a Control (C) line without visible Test (T) line indicates the absence of Coronavirus proteins. See user’s manual for complete instructions for use.
data.uses: Panbio COVID-19 Antigen Self-Test is a single-use, in vitro visually read rapid immunoassay that uses a human nasal swab specimen for the qualitative detection of nucleocapsid protein SARS-CoV-2 antigen. For manual use of untrained lay users in a private setting to aid in the diagnosis of an active SARS-CoV-2 infection.

data.description: Panbio COVID-19/Flu A&B Rapid Panel (nasopharyngeal) contains a membrane strip, which is pre-coated with immobilized anti-SARS-CoV-2, ani-influenza A, and B antibodies on the test line and mouse monoclonal anti-chicken IgY on the control line. It is an in vitro diagnostic rapid test for the qualitative detection of SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza A&B antigen in human nasopharyngeal swab specimens from individuals who meet COVID-19 and/or Influenza clinical and epidemiological criteria.
data.directions: Prepare the test device and buffer tube. Collect nasopharyngeal specimen by inserting the swab through the nostril, then insert it into the extraction buffer tube. Dispense 4 drops of extracted specimen into the specimen well on the test device. 4 types of gold conjugates move upward on the membrane chromatographically and react with anti-SARS-CoV-2, anti-influenza A, and B antibodies respectively. For a positive result, each pathogen of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A, and B will form a test line in the result window. See user’s manual for complete instructions for use.
data.uses: Panbio COVID-10/Flu A&B Rapid Panel is for professional use and is intended as an aid in the diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza infection, and provides preliminary test results. May be used in laboratory and non-laboratory environment.

categories.title: B

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, moderate to severe manic episodes in bipolar disorder, major depressive episodes in bipolar disorder. For the prevention of recurrence of manic or depressed episodes in patients with bipolar disorder who previously responded to quetiapine treatment.
flattened_sections.dose: Adult – Schizophrenia: Total daily dose for the 1st 4 days of therapy is 50 mg on day 1, 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, and 300 mg on day 4. All administered twice daily. From day 4 onwards, titrate dose to the usual effective dose range of 300-450 mg/day, may be adjusted within the dose range of 150-750 mg/day depending on clinical response and tolerability. Moderate to severe manic episodes in bipolar disorder: Total daily dose for the 1st 4 days of therapy is 100 mg on day 1, 200 mg on day 2, 300 mg on day 3, and 400 mg on day 4. All administered twice daily. Adjust dose to 800 mg/day by Day 6 and no increments of no greater than 200 mg/day. Major depressive episodes in bipolar disorder: Total daily dose for the 1st 4 days of therapy is 50 mg on day 1, 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, and 300 mg on day 4. Dose is adjusted depending on clinical response and tolerability of the individual patient, within the range of 200 to 800 mg/day. Recommended daily dose is 300 mg; usual effective dose is 400-800 mg/day. All administered once daily at bedtime. Reduction of risk of stroke, systemic embolism, and death in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), with one or more risk factors, including patients unsuitable for warfarin. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE.
flattened_sections.dose: Prevention of VTE - Elective hip or knee replacement surgery: 2.5 mg twice daily, initial dose should be taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. Recommended duration of treatment - Hip replacement surgery: 32-38 days; Knee replacement surgery: 10-14 days. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism - NVAF: 5 mg twice daily. In patients with at least 2 of the following characteristics: age ≥80 yrs, BW ≤60 kg, or serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL (133 micromole/L): 2.5 mg twice daily. Treatment of DVT and PE: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE: 2.5 mg twice daily after at least 6 months of treatment for DVT or PE. Patients who may require cardioversion but not previously treated with anticoagulants: 5 doses of apixaban 5 mg twice daily before cardioversion. If cardioversion is required before 5 doses of apixaban can be administered, give 10 mg loading dose then 5 mg twice daily. Give loading dose at least 2 hrs before cardioversion. Tabs may be crushed and suspended in a suitable liquid for patients unable to swallow or through nasogastric tube.

flattened_sections.precautions: Increased risk of hemorrhage e.g. congenital or acquired bleeding disorders, active ulcerative GI disease, bacterial endocarditis, thrombocytopenia, platelet disorders, history of hemorrhagic stroke, severe uncontrolled HTN, and recent brain, spinal, or ophthalmological surgery. Concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors and inducers, and antiplatelet agents. Monitor for signs and symptoms of neurological impairment when neuraxial or spinal/epidural anesthesia is employed. pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Non-insulin dependent type II diabetes in adults when dietary measures, physical exercise and weight loss alone are not sufficient to control blood glucose.
flattened_sections.dose: Initially 30 mg (half-tab) daily. If blood glucose is not adequately controlled, the dose may be increased to 60, 90, or 120 mg daily, the interval between each dose increment should be at least 1 month. Max: 120 mg daily. Switching from another oral antidiabetic agent to gliclazide MR 60 mg tab: Initially 30 mg daily, followed by a stepwise increase in dose, depending on the metabolic response. Combination treatment with other antidiabetic agents: 60 mg daily. Can be given in combination with biguanides, alpha glucosidase inhibitors or insulin.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to gliclazide, other sulfonylurea or sulfonamides. Type 1 diabetes, diabetic pre-coma and coma, diabetic keto-acidosis. Severe hepatic and renal insufficiency. Treatment with miconazole. Lactation.

Rash, pruritus, urticaria, angioedema, erythema, maculopapular rashes, bullous reactions (e.g. SJS and toxic epidermal necrolysis), and exceptionally, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS). Raised hepatic enzymes levels (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase). Transient visual disturbances. Cases of erythrocytopenia, agranulocytosis, hemolytic anemia, pancytopenia, allergic vasculitis, hyponatremia, elevated liver enzymes levels and even impairment of liver function (e.g. with cholestasis and jaundice) and hepatitis.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Hypoglycemia, irregular meal time, imbalance between physical exercise and carbohydrate intake. Renal and hepatic insufficiency. Dysglycemia; concomitant treatment with fluroquinolones, especially with elderly. Patients with G6PD-deficiency. Pregnancy and lactation.

brand_info.title: Side Effects
brand_info.content: Hypoglycemia. GI disturbances. Rash, pruritus, urticaria, angioedema, erythema, maculopapular rashes, bullous reactions (e.g. SJS and toxic epidermal necrolysis), and exceptionally, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS). Raised hepatic enzymes levels (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase). Transient visual disturbances. Cases of erythrocytopenia, agranulocytosis, hemolytic anemia, pancytopenia, allergic vasculitis, hyponatremia, elevated liver enzymes levels and even impairment of liver function (e.g. with cholestasis and jaundice) and hepatitis.

categories.title: A

categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with activating epidermal-growth factor receptor (EGFR) Exon 20 insertion mutations whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults (≥18 yrs): < 80 kg: 1050 mg; ≥80 kg: 1400 mg. Dosing schedule: Week 1-4: weekly (total of 4 doses). Week 5 onwards: every 2 weeks. Infusion rates: 1050 mg dose: Week 1 (split dose) – Day 1: 350 mg; Day 2: 700 mg both at 50 mL/hr, increased to 75 mL/hr after 2 hrs if no infusion-related reaction (IRR) occurs. Week 2: 1050 mg at 85 mL/hr. Subsequent weeks: 1050 mg at 125 mL/hr. 1400 mg dose: Week 1 (split dose) – Day 1: 350 mg at 50 mL/hr, increased to 75 mL/hr after 2 hrs if no IRR occurs; Day 2: 1050 mg at 35 mL/hr, increased to 50 mL/hr after 2 hrs if no IRR occurs. Week 2: 1400 mg at 65 mL/hr. Week 3: 1400 mg at 85 mL/hr. Subsequent weeks: 1400 mg at 125 mL/hr. Week 5 onwards: Dosing is every 2 weeks. Dose reduction: Adjustments may be required based on the severity of adverse reactions.
flattened_sections.precautions: Infusion-related reactions (IRR): Pre-medicate with antihistamines (diphenhydramine), antipyretics (paracetamol), glucocorticoids (dexamethasone, methylprednisolone), and antiemetics to reduce the risk of IRRs. Monitor for symptoms indicative of interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis (e.g., dyspnea, cough, fever). Limit sun exposure during and for 2 months after treatment. Use sun protection and emollients. Monitor for symptoms of eye disorders. Advise against contact lens use until evaluated. Pregnancy and lactation.

Prophylaxis of surgical site infection following elective colorectal surgery in adults.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults >13 yrs: 1 g IV or IM once a day. Infants and childn 3 months-12 yrs: 15 mg/kg twice daily. Max 1 g/day. IV to be infused over 30 mins period. Patients with renal insufficiency (CrCl ≤30 mL/min/1.73 m2) including those on hemodialysis: 500 mg daily. When daily dose of 500 mg is given within 6 hrs prior to hemodialysis, administer a supplementary dose of 150 mg following hemodialysis. No supplementary dose is needed if given at least 6 hrs prior to hemodialysis.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

indication_long: Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) and...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) and stable mild and moderate chronic heart failure (CHF) in addition to standard therapies in elderly patients.
flattened_sections.dose: HTN - Adults: 5 mg once daily. In combination with HCTZ: 5 mg plus HCTZ 12.5-25 mg. Patients with renal insufficiency: 2.5 mg daily. May be increased to 5 mg. Elderly >65 yrs: Initially 2.5 mg daily. May be increased to 5 mg daily. CHF: Initially 1.25 mg once daily, increase at interval of 1-2 weeks based on patient's tolerability to 2.5, 5, and 10 mg once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Liver insufficiency or impairment. Acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock or episodes of heart failure decompensation. Sick sinus syndrome including SA block; 2nd and 3rd degree heart block (without a pacemaker); history of bronchospasm and bronchial asthma; untreated pheochromocytoma; metabolic acidosis; bradycardia (HR < 60 bpm); hypotension (systolic BP < 90 mmHg); severe peripheral circulatory disturbances.
flattened_sections.precautions: Concomitant use with anesthetics. Untreated CHF, IHD. Peripheral circulatory disorders (Raynaud's disease or syndrome, intermittent claudication); 1st degree heart block; Prinzmetal's angina. DM, hyperthyroidism, COPD, history of psoriasis. Increased sensitivity to allergens and severity of anaphylactic reactions. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, dizziness, paresthesia, dyspnea, constipation, nausea, diarrhea, tiredness, edema, bradycardia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Class I antiarrhythmics and amiodarone, verapamil or diltiazem-type calcium antagonist, centrally acting antihypertensives, anesthetics, insulin and oral antidiabetic drugs. Digitalis glycosides; dihydropyridines; TCAs, barbiturates, phenothiazines, sympathomimetic agents. CYP2D6 inhibitors, cimetidine, nicardipine.

indication_long: Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angin...

flattened_sections.indications: Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angina pectoris in coronary artery disease adults with normal sinus rhythm and HR ≥70bpmin adults unable to tolerate or with a contraindication to the use of beta-blockers or in combination with beta-blockers in patients inadequately controlled with an optimal beta-blocker dose. Treatment of stable chronic heart failure NYHA II to IV class with systolic dysfunction, in adult patients who are in sinus rhythm with HR ≥75 bpm, in combination with standard therapy including beta-blocker therapy or when beta-blocker therapy is contraindicated or not tolerated.
flattened_sections.dose: Chronic stable angina - Adults < 75 yrs: Initially, 5 mg twice daily. If tolerated and resting HR remains >60 bpm dose may increase to the next higher dose in patients receiving 2.5 mg or 5 mg twice daily. Maintenance: Max 7.5 mg twice daily. Discontinue if no improvement of symptoms after 3 months. If HR decreases < 50 bpm at rest, titrate the dose downward including the lowest dose of 2.5 mg twice daily. Discontinue if HR remains < 50 bpm. CHF: Initially 5 mg twice daily. If resting heart rate >60 bpm: increase dose by 2.5 mg twice daily with max 7.5 mg twice daily. If HR is 50-60 bpm: Maintain dose. If heart rate is < 50 bpm: decrease dose by 2.5 mg twice daily or discontinue if current dose is 2.5 mg. Elderly >75 yrs: 2.5 mg twice daily initially.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Resting heart rate < 70 bpm prior to treatment, cardiogenic shock, acute MI, severe hypotension (< 90/50 mmHg), severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), sick sinus syndrome, SA block, unstable or acute heart failure, pacemaker dependent, unstable angina, 3rd-degree AV block. Patients with existing prolonged QT interval. Concomitant use with verapamil or diltiazem and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, macrolide antibiotics, HIV protease inhibitors and nefazodone. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Monitor HR and ECG. Patients with 2nd-degree AV-block, CHF, atrial fibrillation or other cardiac arrhythmias that interfere with sinus node function. Not recommended immediately after a stroke. Moderate hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min). Retinitis pigmentosa. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Luminous phenomena (phosphenes) and bradycardia. Eosinophilia. Hyperuricemia, hypokalemia; Headache, dizziness, vertigo, tinnitus, dyspnea; Eye, cardiac, vascular, skin, and GI disorders; arthralgia, muscle cramps; asthenia, fatigue, malaise.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. azole antifungals, macrolide antibiotics, HIV protease inhibitors) and nefazodone. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. diltiazem or verapamil). CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. St. John’s Wort, rifampicin, barbiturates, phenytoin). QT-prolonging medications (e.g. quinidine, disopyramide, bepridil, sotalol, ibutilide, amiodarone); pimozide, ziprasidone, sertindole, mefloquine, halofantrine, pentamidine, cisapride, erythromycin IV. Digoxin, beta-blockers. Furosemide, HCTZ, indapamide. Omeprazole, lansoprazole. Sildenafil. HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (e.g. simvastatin); dihydropyridine CCBs (e.g. amlodipine, lacidipine); aspirin, warfarin. Grapefruit juice.

indication_long: For control of hypothyroidism, congenital hyp...

flattened_sections.indications: For control of hypothyroidism, congenital hypothyroidism in infants. Treatment for acquired hypothyroidism in children and juvenile myxedema.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults: Initially 50-100 mcg daily, preferably taken before breakfast or first meal of the day, adjust by 50 mcg at 3-4 weeks intervals until normal metabolism is steadily maintained. Final dose 100-200 mcg. Elderly >50 yrs: Max 50 mcg, the daily dose may be increased by 50 mcg at 3-4 weeks intervals, until stable thyroxine levels are attained. Final dose 50-200 mcg daily. Patients >50 yrs with cardiac disease: 25 mcg or 50 mcg on alternate days, may increased daily dose by 25 mcg at 4-week intervals. Final daily dose 50-200 mcg. Child: 100-150 mcg2 BSA. Acquired hypothyroidism: Initially 12.5-50 mcg/day, increased gradually every 2-4 weeks according to clinical findings and thyroid hormones and TSH values. Juvenile myxedema: Initially 25 mcg daily, may be increased by 25 mcg at 2-4 weeks until mild symptoms of hyperthyroidism are seen, then reduce the dose slightly. Infants and neonates - Congenital hypothyroidism: Initially 10-15 mcg/kg/day for the 1st 3 months, adjust dose individually according to clinical findings and thyroid hormone and TSH values.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Thyrotoxicosis. Adrenal gland disorder or adrenal insufficiency.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with panhypopituitarism or other causes predisposing to adrenal insufficiency, initiate corticosteroid therapy first. Patients with cardiac symptoms, DM, diabetes insipidus, angina, arrhythmias, MI, cardiac failure. Should not be used for the treatment of obesity and weight loss. Larger doses may produce serious or life-threatening manifestations of toxicity, particularly when given in association with sympathomimetic amines. Patients with myxedema have an increased sensitivity to thyroid hormones. In women, long-term levothyroxine has been associated with increased bone resorption. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Increased appetite, abnormal loss of weight. Hyperthyroidism. Abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. Headache, tremors, seizures. Anginal pain, cardiac arrthyhmias, palpitations, tachycardia, increased blood pressure, heart failure, MI. Dyspnea, sweating, alopecia, flushing. Anxiety, emotional lability, nervousness, excitability, insomnia, restlessness. Menstrual irregularity, impaired fertility. Fatigue, heat intolerance, fever.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Anticonvulsants (e.g. carbamazepine and phenytoin), rifampicin, barbiturates, cardiac glycosides. Cholestyramine, calcium, aluminum, magnesium, iron supplements, aluminum hydroxide, polystyrene sulfonates, sucralfate, lanthanum, bile acid sequesterants (e.g. colestipol), calcium carbonate, ferrous sulfate, PPIs. Oral contraceptives, estrogens, tamoxifen, clofibrate, methadone, 5-fluorouracil. Propanalol, amiodarone, lithium, iodide, oral contrast agents.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of breast cancer after failure of combination chemotherapy for metastatic disease or relapse within 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy; combination with carboplatin is the 1<sup>st</sup>-line for locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer for patients not candidates for curative surgery or radiation therapy; combination with gemcitabine is 1<sup>st</sup>-line for metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas.
flattened_sections.dose: IV infusion. Metastatic breast cancer (MBC): 260 mg/m2 or 295 mg/m2 for 30 mins every 3 weeks. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): 100 mg/m2 over 30 mins on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 21-day cycle, administered immediately after with carboplatin on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Adenocarcinoma of the pancreas: 125 mg/m2 over 30-40 mins on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle, administered immediately after with gemcitabine on the same days. Hepatic impairment - MBC – AST < 10 x ULN and bilirubin >1.5-≤5 x ULN: 200 mg/m2b. NSCLC - AST < 10 x ULN and bilirubin >1.5-≤5 x ULN: 80 mg/m2b. The dose increases in subsequent courses if the reduced dose for two cycles are tolerated. See product insert for dose modifications during toxicity and preparation.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Baseline neutrophil counts of < 1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with total bilirubin >5 x ULN or AST >10 x ULN; metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas with moderate to severe hepatic impairment; biliary obstruction or presence of stent; pneumonitis. May induce severe myelosuppression; severe neuropathy; sepsis; febrile neutropenia; severe or fatal hypersensitivity reactions and cross-hypersensitivity. Perform CBC frequently, prior to dosing on day 1 (for MBC) and days 1, 8, and 15 (for NSCLC and for pancreatic cancer). Childn. Elderly. Use contraception during and at least 6 months after treatment. Avoid fathering a child during treatment and at least 3 months after last dose. Women of child bearing potential. Breastfeeding should be avoided for 2 weeks after last dose. May impair fertility in males and females of reproductive age.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Alopecia, neutropenia, sensory neuropathy, abnormal ECG, fatigue/asthenia, myalgia/arthralgia, AST elevation, alkaline phosphatase elevation, anemia, nausea, vomiting, infections, diarrhea, pneumonia, peripheral edema, pyrexia, decreased appetite, rash, dehydration.

indication_long: Treatment of acute GI hemorrhage, resulting f...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of acute GI hemorrhage, resulting from gastric or duodenal ulcers, hemorrhagic gastritis, and bleeding esophageal varices, intestinal and pancreatic fistulae. Symptomatic treatment of excessive secretion from GIT endocrine tumors. Prevention of complication after pancreatic surgery or endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP).
flattened_sections.dose: 3.5 mcg/kg/hr, or usually 6 mg/24 hrs for a 75-kg patient, as continuous infusion of 250 mcg/hr. Adjust the infusion rate for 12 or 24 hours (for 3 or 6 mg respectively). Treatment of GI hemorrhage: Initiate before endoscopy as soon as possible after the first signs of bleeding and continue for 5 days minimum duration of 48 hrs. Additionally, a bolus inj of 3.5 mcg/kg should be given immediately after the start of the continuous infusion and another bolus about 1 min before endoscopy. After endoscopic treatment, similar boluses should be given when patients show clinical signs of bleeding. Fistulae or excessive secretion from endocrine tumors: Infuse ½ the dose for the next 48 hrs after healing. Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min): 1.75 mcg/kg/hr for continuous infusion. 1.75 mcg/kg for bolus dose.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Renal impairment. Hypoglycemia may occur at the beginning of the infusion, measure blood sugar every 4-6 hrs. May induce transient systemic HTN, transiently reduced cardiac output, increased pulmonary arterial pressure and central venous pressure, systemic hypotension, bradycardia, AV block. Regularly check renal function and plasma electrolytes. Patients with compromised CV status or a history cardiac arrhythmias. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea and vomiting.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Drugs that influence blood glucose regulation, plasma renin level, and arterial BP. Any form of sugar (glucose and fructose solutions or total parenteral nutrition).

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: For treatment-resistant schizophrenia patients. Indicated to reduce the risk of recurrent suicidal behavior or psychotic disorders occurring during the course of Parkinson’s disease.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosage. Treatment resistant schizophrenia – Initial dose: 12.5 mg once or twice on the 1 st day, followed by one or two 25 mg tabs on the 2nd day. May be increased slowly in increments of 25-50 mg in order to achieve a dose level of up to 300 mg/day within 2-3 weeks. May be further increased in increments of 50-100 mg at weekly intervals. Therapeutic dose: 300 to 450 mg/day given in divided doses. Max 900 mg/day in divided doses. Maintenance: Careful downward titration. Treatment should be maintained for at least 6 months. If dose ≤200 mg, give once a day in the evening. Ending therapy: Withdraw gradually over 1-2 weeks period. Psychotic disorders occurring during the course of Parkinson’s disease – Initial dose:  ≤12.5 mg once daily in the evening, subsequent increase to 12.5 mg, up to 2 increases each week, 50 mg should not be reached before the end of 2nd week. Therapeutic dose: 25-37.5 mg daily, may be increased to 50 mg at weekly intervals. Max 100 mg daily. Maintenance: 12.5 mg, max 100 mg daily, as single dose or 2 divided doses. Ending therapy: gradual reduction in dose by steps of 12.5 mg over a period of at least 1 week. Elderly: 12.5 mg once daily on the 1st day, with subsequent dose increments of 25 mg/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients with uncontrolled epilepsy, alcoholic or other toxic psychoses, drug intoxication, comatose conditions, circulatory collapse, CNS depression of any cause, impaired bone marrow function, history of toxic or idiosyncratic granulocytopenia/agranulocytosis (with the exception of granulocytopenia/agranulocytosis from previous chemotherapy), severe renal or cardiac disorders, active liver disease associated with nausea, anorexia or jaundice, progressive liver disease, hepatic failure, and paralytic ileus. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Risk of agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia, thromboembolism, cardiovascular disorder, MI, QT interval prolongation, hyperglycemia, metabolic changes, dyslipidemia, weight gain, seizures, fever, anticholinergic effects. Monitoring of WBC counts and absolute neutrophil count; 10 days prior to starting treatment, weekly monitoring for 18 weeks, and thereafter at least every 4 weeks throughout treatment and 4 weeks after complete discontinuation. Women of child-bearing potential. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Tachycardia, constipation, hypersalivation, drowsiness, sedation, dizziness, leukopenia, decreased WBC, neutropenia, eosinophilia, leukocytosis, weight gain, dysarthria, blurred vision, syncope, postural hypotension, hypertension, nausea, vomiting, dry mouth, headache, seizures, convulsions, myoclonic jerks, extrapyramidal symptoms, akathisia, tremor, rigidity, elevated liver enzymes, urinary retention or incontinence, benign hyperthermia, disturbances in sweating, temperature regulation, fatigue.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions:
Lithium, alcohol, MAO inhibitors, narcotics, antihistamines, benzodiazepines, carbamazepine,
phenytoin, rifampicin, cimetidine, erythromycin, fluvoxamine, perazine, ciprofloxacin, oral contraceptives, SSRIs (e.g. paroxetine, sertraline, fluoxetine, citalopram), omeprazole, CYP 450 inhibitors or inducers.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adult patients who have undergone elective hip or knee replacement surgery. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE); prevention of recurrent DVT and PE. Reduce the risk of stroke, systemic embolism, and death in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation with one or more risk factors.
flattened_sections.dose: Prevention of VTE – Elective hip or knee replacement surgery: 2.5 mg twice daily, taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. Duration of treatment for patients undergoing hip replacement surgery: 32 to 38 days; knee replacement surgery: 10-14 days. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism – NVAF: 5 mg twice daily. In patients with at least 2 of the following characteristics: age ≥80 yrs, BW ≤60 kg, or serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL (133 micromole/L): 2.5 mg twice daily. Treatment of DVT and PE: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE: 2.5 mg twice daily after at least 6 months of treatment for DVT or PE. Cardioversion - For patients initiating treatment with apixaban: 5 single doses of 5 mg twice daily before cardioversion. Dose reduction to 2.5 mg twice daily. If cardioversion is required before 5 doses of apixaban can be administered, give 10 mg loading dose then 5 mg twice daily. Dose reduction to 5 mg loading dose followed by 2.5 mg twice. Loading dose to be given at least 2 hrs before cardioversion.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Increased risk of hemorrhage, bleeding. Discontinue prior to elective surgery or invasive procedures places patients at an increased risk of thrombosis. Renal Impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min) or undergoing dialysis; mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B). Post-op use of indwelling epidural catheters or concomitant use of medicinal products affecting homeostasis. Risk of developing an epidural or spinal hematoma which can result in long-term or permanent paralysis. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Anemia, hemorrhage, contusion, epistaxis, hematuria, hematoma, gingival bleeding, menorrhagia.

flattened_sections.dose: Patients >71 kg: 5 tabs; 55-70 kg: 4 tabs; 40-54 kg: 3 tabs. Category I: Given daily during the initial phase (8 weeks) of treatment. If sputum is smear-positive, continue treatment for 4 weeks. Category II: Given daily during the initial phase (12 weeks) of treatment. flattened_sections.precautions: May produce decreases in visual acuity due to optic/retrobulbar neuritis. Not for treatment of latent TB infection.  Patients with pre-existing liver diseases or at increased risk for drug-related hepatitis. Discontinue pyrazinamide if signs of hepatocellular damage appear. Empiric treatment including initial monotherapy for presumed bacterial infections in host-compromised neutropenic patients. Effective in patients with cystic fibrosis and chronic LRTI either monotherapy or in combination with other antibacterial agents.
flattened_sections.dose: IV bolus inj over approx 5 mins or IV infusion over approx 15-30 mins. flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of symptoms of Parkinson’s disease (e.g. stiffness, trembling, and diminished movement or motionless) and movement disorders similar to Parkinson’s disease caused by certain drugs (neuroleptics and drugs with similar mechanism of action), and extrapyramidal symptoms (e.g. early dyskinesia, akathisia, and parkinsonism).
flattened_sections.dose: Adults: 100 mg once daily for first 4-7 days, followed by once-weekly increase until maintenance dose is reached. Usual effective dose: 200-600 mg once daily. Elderly - States of agitation and confusion or delirious syndromes: Lower dose. Previously treated with amantadine infusion soln: Can start with higher dose. Renal impairment – GFR 80-60 mL/min: 100 mg every 12 hrs; 60-50 mL/min: 200 mg and 100 mg (alternate days); 50-30 mL/min: 100 mg once daily; 30-20 mL/min: 200 mg twice a week; 20-10 mL/min: 100 mg thrice a week; < 10 and hemodialysis patients: 200 mg and 100 mg once a week or once every 2 weeks. Taken with little liquid in the morning and afternoon. Do not take the last daily dose later than 4 pm.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe decompensated heart failure (NYHA class IV). Cardiomyopathies. Myocarditis. 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block. Existing bradycardia < 55 beats/min. Known prolonged QT interval (Bazett QTc >420 ms) or discernible U-waves or congenital QT syndrome in the family anamnesis. History of serious ventricular arrhythmias (e.g. torsade de pointes). Influenza virus A infection. Rare hereditary galactose intolerance. Coadministration with budipine or other QT prolonging drugs. Reduced levels of potassium or magnesium in blood.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt discontinuation. Patients with renal insufficiency, prostatic hypertrophy, narrow-angle glaucoma, risks of electrolyte imbalances, cardiac pacemakers. Record ECG (50 mm/s) prior and 1 and 3 weeks after administration, prior and 2 weeks after any subsequent dose increase, and at least once a year. Manually determine the Bazett frequency-corrected QT time. Discontinue in patients with baseline >420 msQTc values, increase of >60 ms or >480 ms QTc during treatment, and discernible U waves; palpitations, dizziness, or syncope. Give amantadine infusion if acute worsening of parkinsonian symptoms (e.g. akinetic crisis) occurs. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Planning of pregnancy. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Dizziness, sleep disturbances, motor and psychiatric agitation, paranoid exogenous psychoses accompanied by visual hallucinations (elderly), urinary retention in case of prostatic hypertrophy, livedo reticularis sometimes associated with lower-leg and ankle edema, nausea, dry mouth, orthostatic dysregulation.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: QT prolonging drugs, anticholinergics, indirectly CNS -active sympathomimetics, alcohol, memantine, triamterene/HCTZ diuretics.

indication_long: Treatment of hypertension (HTN), coronary hea...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of hypertension (HTN), coronary heart disease (angina pectoris), stable chronic heart failure (CHF) with reduced systolic left ventricular function. In addition to ACE inhibitors, diuretics, and optionally cardiac glycosides.
flattened_sections.dose: HTN or angina pectoris: 5 mg once daily, may be increased to 10 mg once daily. Max 20 mg; Severe renal or hepatic impairment: Max 10 mg once daily. Stable CHF - Titration phase: Initially 1.25 mg once daily, increased to 2.5 mg, 3.75 mg, 5 mg, 7.5 mg, and 10 mg once daily in ≥2-week intervals. Max 10 mg. Taken in the morning.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Acute heart failure or during episodes of heart failure decompensation requiring IV inotropic therapy. Cardiogenic shock. 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block. Sick sinus syndrome. SA block. Symptomatic bradycardia or hypotension. Severe bronchial asthma and COPD. Severe forms of peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD) or Raynaud’s syndrome. Untreated pheochromocytoma. Metabolic acidosis.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt withdrawal, especially in patients with IHD. Patients with bronchospasm; DM showing large fluctuation in blood glucose values; strict fasting; ongoing desensitization therapy; 1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block; Prinzmetal’s angina; PAOD; present or history of psoriasis; undergoing general anesthesia. No therapeutic experience in CHF patients with type I DM, severe renal or hepatic impairment, restrictive cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, hemodynamically significant organic valvular disease, MI within 3 months. May mask symptoms of thyrotoxicosis and hypoglycemia. Positive anti-doping tests. Perform close monitoring of vital signs and symptoms of worsening heart failure during titration phase. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: CHF: Bradycardia, worsening of pre-existing heart failure, asthenia. Dizziness, headache, feeling of coldness or numbness in extremities, hypotension, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, fatigue.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Class-I and III antiarrhythmic agents, verapamil, centrally-acting antihypertensives, dihydropyridine CCBs, parasympathomimetic, topical beta-blockers, insulin, oral antidiabetics, anesthetics, digitalis glycosides, NSAIDs, beta-sympathomimetics, sympathomimetics that activate both beta- and alpha-adrenoreceptors, mefloquine, MAOI (except MAO-B inhibitors).

flattened_sections.indications: Used for superficial mucosal (oropharyngeal, oesophageal, or vaginal) candidiasis and for fungal skin infections. For systemic infections including systemic candidiasis, coccidioidomycosis, cryptococcosis, and has been tried in blastomycosis, histoplasmosis, sporotrichosis.
flattened_sections.dose: Superficial mucosal candidiasis: Usual dose 50 mg daily, may be given 100 mg if necessary for 7-14 days, for atrophic oral candidiasis associated with denture 14 days, and for other mucosal candida infections including esophagitis 14-30 days. Genital candidiasis (vaginal candidiasis or candida balinitis): 150 mg as a single dose. Infections of the skin: 50 mg daily for up to 6 weeks. Systemic candidiasis, cryptococcal meningitis and other cryptococcal infections: Initial dose 400 mg, followed by 200 mg to 400 mg daily for at least 6-8 weeks. Immunocompromised patients at risk of fungal infections: Prophylaxis 50 mg to 400 mg daily Renal Impairment- Creatinine clearance >50 mL/min:100 % of the standard recommended dose. CC < 50 mL/min (not on dialysis): 50% of the standard recommended dose. Patients on regular haemodialysis: 100% of the standard recommended dose after each dialysis session. No dosage adjustment is needed in patients with renal impairment given single-dose therapy.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Cisapride, terfenadine, astemizole, pimozide, quinidine. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with impaired hepatic or renal function, AIDS or malignancy, proarrhythmic conditions.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, flatulence, nausea and vomiting, taste disturbance, headache, dizziness, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, hyperlipidemia, increased liver enzymes, TEN, SJS, rash, dyspepsia, hepatic disorders, angioedema, anaphylaxis, alopecia, hypokalemia, prolonged QT interval, torsades de pointes.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Rifampicin, HCTZ, drugs metabolized by CYP450, CYP3A4, CYP2C9. Selective COX-2 inhibitors, terfenadine, astemizole, cisapride, amitriptyline, theophylline, contraceptive steroids.

flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to single functioning kidney; recent kidney transplant; vascular tone and renal function depend on RAAS activity; suffering from aortic or mitral stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; heart failure; hepatic impairment; DM and additional CV risk; ischemic cardiomyopathy or CV disease. Not recommended in patients with primary aldosteronism. Correct vol and/or sodium depletion prior to therapy. Monitor BP in the prevention of CV morbidity and mortality; potassium and serum Cr periodically in patients with renal impairment. Black population. Childn < 18 yrs.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE in adults; stroke and systemic embolism in adults with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), with one or more risk factors, e.g., prior stroke or transient ischemic attack, elderly ≥75 yrs, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class ≥II), and patients unstable for warfarin.
flattened_sections.dose: Treatment of DVT and PE: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE: 2.5 mg twice daily after at least 6 months of treatment. Prevention of VTE - Elective hip or knee replacement surgery: 2.5 mg twice daily. Patients with known sulfonamide hypersensitivity, active peptic ulceration or GI bleeding, asthma urticaria or allergic-type reaction after taking ASA or NSAIDs, including other COX-2 inhibitors. Peri-op pain of CABG surgery. Congestive heart failure (NYHA II-IV). Established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease and/or cerebrovascular disease.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Upper and lower GI complications, concomitant NSAID use. Increased risk of serious CV thrombotic events, MI, and stroke. Patients with pre-existing CHF or HTN, with compromised cardiac function, pre-existing edema, or other conditions pre-disposing to, or worsened by, fluid retention, renal toxicity, dehydration, severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class B). CYP2D6 inhibitors, CYP2C9 poor metabolizers. Serious skin reactions (e.g. exfoliative dermatitis, SJS and toxic epidermal necrolysis). Concurrent therapy with warfarin. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Elderly. May affect the ability of driving or operating machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.

flattened_sections.indications: Management of nausea and vomiting induced by cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Prevention and treatment of post-op nausea and vomiting (PONV). Management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) in childn ≥6 months, and for the prevention and treatment of PONV in childn ≥1 month.
flattened_sections.dose: Chemotherapy and radiotherapy induced nausea and vomiting (CINV and RINV) - Adults - Emotogenic chemotherapy and radiotherapy: 8 mg administered as a slow IV inj (in not <30 secs) or IM inj, immediately before treatment, followed by 8 mg orally every 12 hrs. Highly emetogenic chemotherapy: A single dose of 8 mg by slow IV inj (in not <30 secs) or IM inj immediately before chemotherapy, then followed by 2 further IV inj or IM doses of 8 mg, 4 hrs apart, or by a constant infusion of 1 mg/hr for up to 24 hrs. Max initial IV dose of 16 mg diluted in 50-100 mL of saline or other compatible infusion fluid and infused over <15 mins immediately before chemotherapy. May be enhanced by addition of single IV dose of dexamethasone sodium phosphate, 20 mg administered prior to chemotherapy. Childn ≥6 months and adolescents - CINV: Given by IV infusion diluted in 25-50 mL of saline or other compatible infusion fluid and infused over < 15 mins. Should be diluted in 5% dextrose or 0.9% NaCl. . Dosing by BSA: ≤0.6 m2: 5 mg/m2 + 2 mg syr every 12 hrs on 1st day, then 2 mg syr every 12 hrs on 2nd-6th day; 0.6 m2 to 1.2 m2: 5 mg/m2 IV + 4 mg syr or tab after 12 hrs on 1st day, then 4 mg syr or tab every 12 hrs on 2nd-6th day; >1.2 m2: 5 mg/m2 IV + 8 mg syr or tab after 12 hrs on 1st day, then 8 mg syr or tab every 12 hrs. The IV dose must not exceed 8 mg. Total dose over 24 hrs (given as divided dose) must not exceed 32 mg. Dosing by BW: ≤10 kg: Up to 3 doses of 0.15 mg/kg IV every 4 hrs on 1st day, then 2 mg syr every 12 hrs on 2nd-6th day; >10 kg: Up to 3 doses of 0.15 mg/kg IV every 4 hrs on 1st day, then 4 mg syr or tab every 12 hrs on 2nd-6th day. The IV dose must not exceed 8 mg. Total dose over 24 hrs (given as divided dose) must not exceed 32 mg. Post-operative nausea and vomiting - Adults: May be administered as a single dose of 4 mg given by IM or slow IV inj at induction of anesthesia. Childn ≥1 month and adolescents: For prevention and treatment after surgery, a single dose may be administered by slow IV (not < 30 secs) at dose 0.1 mg/kg up to max of 4 mg either prior to, at or after induction of anesthesia. Patients with hepatic impairment: Max dose of 8 mg.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with apomorphine.
flattened_sections.precautions: Hypersensitivity to other selective 5HT<sub>3</sub>  receptor antagonists. Patients with congenital long QT syndrome, who have or may develop prolongation of QT, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, bradyarrhythmias, are taking medicinal products that lead QT prolongation or electrolyte abnormalities, with sub-acute intestinal obstruction, with adenotonsillar surgery prevention of nausea and vomiting. Concomitant use with serotonergic drugs. Childn receiving ondansetron with hepatotoxic chemotherapeutic agents. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Headache, constipation, sensation of warmth or flushing, local IV injection site reactions.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, tramadol, apomorphine, SSRIs, SNRIs.

indication_long: Monotherapy or in combination with pegylated ...

flattened_sections.indications: Monotherapy or in combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or dexamethasone for the treatment of adult patients with progressive multiple myeloma who have received at least 1 prior therapy and who have undergone or are unsuitable for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. In combination with melphalan and prednisone indicated for the treatment of adult patients with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are not eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.  In combination with dexamethasone, or with dexamethasone and thalidomide indicated for the induction treatment of adult patients with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
flattened_sections.dose: IV/SC. Administered as a 3-5 secs IV bolus through a peripheral or central IV catheter followed by a flush with NaCl 9 mg/mL (0.9%) soln for inj. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Monotherapy: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8 and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. After confirmation of complete response: 2 cycles. Patients who do not achieve a complete remission receive a total of 8 cycles. At least 72 hours should elapse between consecutive doses. Dose adjustment during treatment and re-initiation of treatment for monotherapy: Re-initiated at 25% reduced dose (1.3 mg/m2 reduced to 1.5 mg/m2; 1.0 mg/m2 reduced to 0.7 mg/m2). Combination therapy with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is administered 30 mg/m2 on day 4 of treatment cycle as 1-hr IV infusion administered after the bortezomib inj. May be administer up to 8 cycles as long as patients have not progressed and tolerate the treatment. Combination with dexamethasone: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Dexamethasone is administered orally at 20 days on days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, and 12 of the bortezomib treatment cycle, patients achieving a response or a stable disease after 4 cycles of this combination therapy can continue to receive the same combination for a maximum of 4 additional cycles. Combination therapy with melphalan and prednisone: 6-week period treatment cycle. Cycles 1-4: Bortezomib administered twice weekly on days 1, 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, 29, and 32. Cycles 5-9: Bortezomib is administered once weekly on days 1, 8, 22 and 29. At least 72 hrs elapse between consecutive doses of Bortezomib. Melphan and prednisone both given orally on days 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the 1st week of each bortezomib treatment cycle. Untreated multiple myeloma patients eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (induction therapy) – Combination therapy with dexamethasone: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of bortezomib treatment cycle for 4 treatment cycles; Combination therapy with dexamethasone and thalidomide: 1.3 mg/m2 BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 28-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of bortezomib treatment cycle + thalidomide 50 mg orally on days 1-14 may be increased to 100 mg on days 15-28, may further increased to 200 mg daily from cycle 2 if tolerated. Hepatic impairment (moderate and severe): 0.7 mg/m2 in the 1st treatment cycle. Consider dose escalation to 1.0 mg/m2 or further dose reduction to 0.5 mg/m2 in subsequent cycles based on patient’s tolerability.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to active substance, boron. Acute diffuse infiltrative pulmonary and pericardial disease.
flattened_sections.precautions: Should not be administered intrathecally. Monitor patients who experience constipation. Hematological toxicity, HZV virus reactivation, HBV reactivation and infection, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, peripheral neuropathy, seizures, hypotension, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, heart failure, ECG investigations, pulmonary disorders, renal, and hepatic impairment, tumor lysis syndrome. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, fatigue, pyrexia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, neutropenia, peripheral neuropathy, headache, paresthesia, decreased appetite, dyspnea, rash, herpes zosters, myalgia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, ritonavir). Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, St. John’s Wort).

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

Initial treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer either in combination with an anthracycline or in combination with trastuzumab, or in patients over expressed HER-2 at a 3+ level for whom an anthracycline is not suitable. Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma who have failed prior liposomal anthracycline therapy.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: First-line treatment of ovarian cancer: 175 mg/m2 IV infusion over a period of 3 hrs or 135 mg/m2 IV infusion over a period of 24 hrs followed by 75 mg/m2 of cisplatin, therapy is repeated at 3-week interval. 2nd-line treatment of ovarian cancer: 175 mg/m2 over 3 hrs, with a 3 weeks interval between courses. Adjuvant chemotherapy in breast carcinoma: 175 mg/m2 over a period of 3 hrs every 3 weeks for 4 courses. Following AC therapy. 1st-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma with combination with doxorubicin (50 mg/m2): Recommended dose 220 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs, with a 3-week interval between courses, should be administered 24 hrs after doxorubicin. 1st-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma with combination with trastuzumab: Recommended dose 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hrs, with 3-week interval between courses, infusion may be started the day following the 1st dose of trastuzumab or immediately after the subsequent dose of trastuzumab. 2nd- line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma: 175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hrs, with a 3-week interval between courses. Advanced NSCLC: 175 mg/m2 administered 3 hrs followed by 80 mg/m2 of cisplatin, with a 3-week interval between courses. Treatment of AIDS-related KS: Recommended dose 100 mg/m2 3 hrs IV infusion every 2 weeks.

flattened_sections.indications: Management of bronchial asthma; seasonal allergic and allergic/non-allergic perennial rhinitis. Treatment and prevention of nasal polyps after polypectomy.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosage. Severe asthma: Divide total daily dose to be taken twice daily; Elderly and adults: 200-1,600 mcg daily as initial treatment, for severe asthma, and while reducing or discontinuing oral glucocorticoids; Childn >12 yrs: 200-800 mcg daily for less severe cases, may be increased to max 1,600 mcg daily during periods of severe asthma; ≤12 yrs: 200-800 mcg daily, may be increased to max 800 mcg daily during periods of severe asthma. Mild to moderate asthma - Elderly, adults, childn >12 yrs: 200-400 mcg for patients who have not previously received inhaled glucocorticoids. Max 800 mcg twice daily for patients already controlled on inhaled steroids; Childn ≤12 yrs: 200-400 mcg twice daily. Transfer patient to once daily dose taken at the same time each evening with same equiv total daily dose. Increased frequency of bronchodilator use or persistent respiratory symptoms: Administer dose twice daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Primary treatment of status asthmaticus or other acute episodes/exacerbations of asthma or in patients with moderate to severe bronchiectasis. Untreated active or quiescent pulmonary TB and untreated fungal, bacterial, or systemic viral infections.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not a treatment for acute asthmatic attack. Patients with excessive mucus secretion, on alternate-day prednisone regimens, hypothyroidism, cirrhosis. Concomitant aspirin in hypoprothrombinemia. Advise patient to rinse their mouth with water and spit out or brush their teeth after inhalation. May increase susceptibility to infections (e.g., Chickenpox, measles); risk of adrenal insufficiency and unmasking of allergic conditions when patients are transferred from systemic to inhalation therapy; pharyngeal and laryngeal candidiasis; pulmonary infiltrates with eosinophils. Immediately resume previously effective dosages of systemic steroids during periods of stress or severe asthmatic attack in patients withdrawn from systemic corticosteroids. Perform routine tests of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal-axis (HPA) function and hematological status periodically during long-term therapy. Discontinue slowly if systemic effects occur. Pregnancy Risk: Category B. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Ocular complications, reduced bone density, suppression of HPA responsiveness to stress, inhibition of growth velocity in childn, exacerbation of glaucoma, osteoporosis, fractures.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Systemic steroids, aspirin.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in combination with cisplatin as initial treatment or monotherapy after prior chemotherapy. In combination with cisplatin for treatment of patients with malignant pleural mesothelioma whose disease is unresectable or who are not candidates for curative surgery.
flattened_sections.dose: IV infusion. Combination with cisplatin: 500 mg/m2 over 10 mins on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, 30 mins before 2 hrs infusion of 75 mg/m2 cisplatin. Give appropriate hydration prior to and/or after receiving cisplatin. Monotherapy: 500 mg/m2 over 10 mins on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Pre-medication regimen: Low-dose oral folic acid (350-1000 mcg) or multivitamin with folic acid daily at least 5 daily doses for 7 days prior to 1st dose of treatment, continued throughout the therapy and for 21 days after last dose; 1,000 mcg vit B12 IM during the week prior to 1st dose of treatment and every 3 cycles thereafter; 4 mg oral dexamethasone 2x daily prior to, the same day and the day after pemetrexed.
flattened_sections.contraindications: History of severe hypersensitivity. Renal impairment (CrCl < 45 mL/min). Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Not a treatment for squamous cell non-small cell lung cancer. Coadministration with NSAIDs to patients with mild to moderate renal impairment (CrCl 45-79 mL/min). Patients should have ANC ≥1,500 cells/mm3, platelet count ≥100,000, and CrCl 45 mL/min prior to the start of new cycle. Bone marrow suppression, myelosuppression. Consider draining the effusion in patients with a third-space fluid collection prior to treatment. Monitor CBC (e.g., platelet counts) and renal function. Use effective contraceptives. Childn. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Monotherapy: Fatigue, nausea, anorexia. Combination with cisplatin: Vomiting, neutropenia, leukopenia, anemia, stomatitis/pharyngitis, thrombocytopenia, constipation.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Ibuprofen and other NSAIDs. Nephrotoxic drugs.
flattened_sections.packaging: Lyophilized powder for IV infusion 500 mg (P40,000.00).

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.indications: Infections caused by susceptible organisms: lower respiratory tract infections e.g. bronchitis and pneumonia; skin and soft tissue infections, acute otitis media, upper respiratory tract infections e.g. sinusitis and pharyngitis/tonsillitis. Treatment of sexually transmitted disease (STD) due to Chlamydia trachomatis and chancroid due to Haemophilus ducreyi and uncomplicated genital infections due to non-multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Prophylaxis against Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex (MAC) infection either alone or in combination with rifabutin, and treatment of disseminated MAC (DMAC) in combination with ethambutol in patients with advanced HIV. Treatment of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) caused by Legionella pneumophila and pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) caused by C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhea, Mycoplasma hominis in patients who require initial IV therapy.
flattened_sections.dose: Adults - Treatment of STDs caused by C. trachomatis and H. ducreyi: 1,000 mg single dose. For susceptible N. gonorrhoeae: 1,000 mg or 2,000 mg in combination with 250 mg or 500 mg ceftriaxone according to local clinical treatment guidelines. Prophylaxis against MAC infections in patients with HIV: 1,200 mg once per week. DMAC infections in patients with advanced HIV: 600 mg once a day. CAP: 500 mg IV single daily dose for 2 days, followed by 500 mg oral single daily dose for 7- to 10-day therapy. PID: 500 mg IV single dose for 1-2 days, followed by 250 mg oral single daily dose to complete 7-day therapy. Other infections: 500 mg single daily dose for 3 days (total dosage of 1,500 mg); can be given over 5 days with 500 mg given on day 1, then 250 mg daily on days 2 -5. IV infusion concentration and rate of either 1 mg/mL over 3 hrs, or 2 mg/mL over 1 hr. A 500 mg IV dose should be infused for minimum 1 hr duration. Childn - Any treatment: Total dose of 30 mg/kg, given as single daily dose of 10 mg/kg for 3 days, or given over 5 days with single dose of 10 mg/kg on day 1, then 5 mg/kg on days 2-5. Max total dose: 1,500 mg. Acute otitis media: 30 mg/kg as single dose. Pediatric Streptococcal pharyngitis: Single dose of 10 mg/kg or 20 mg/kg for 3 days. Max 500 mg/day. Susp - 3-day regimen - Childn >45 kg: Adult dose; 36-45 kg: 10 mL (400 mg); 26-35 kg: 7.5 mL (300 mg); 15-25 kg: 5 mL (200 mg); < 15 kg: 10 mg/kg. All doses given once daily for 3 days. 5-day regimen - Childn >45 kg: Adult dose; 36-45 kg: 10 mL (400 mg) on day 1, then 5 mL (200 mg) once daily on days 2-5; 26-35 kg: 7.5 mL (300 mg) on day 1, then 3.75 mL (150 mg) once daily on days 2-5; 15-25 kg: 5 mL (200 mg) on day 1, then 2.5 mL (100 mg) once daily on days 2-5; < 15 kg: 10 mg/kg on day 1, then 5 mg/kg once daily on days 2-5.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to azithromycin, erythromycin, any macrolide or ketolide antibiotic. Coadministration with ergot derivatives.
flattened_sections.precautions: Discontinue if allergic reaction, signs and symptoms of hepatitis occurs. Patients with significant hepatic disease, severe renal impairment (GFR < 10 mL/min), and diabetes; fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or saccharase-isomaltase deficiency. Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis (IHPS). Observe for signs of superinfection. Overgrowth of C. difficile including C. difficile-associated diarrhea. Patients with congenital or documented QT prolongation, electrolyte disturbance (e.g. hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia), bradycardia, cardiac arrhythmia or cardiac insufficiency; currently receiving drugs that prolong QT interval (e.g. Class IA and III antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, antidepressants, fluoroquinolones). Should be reconstituted and diluted as directed and administered as IV infusion over not < 60 mins. Do not administer as IV bolus or IM injection. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Transient episode of mild neutropenia; hearing impairment; nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loose stools, abdominal discomfort and flatulence; abnormal liver function; allergic skin reactions including rash and angioedema; local pain and inflammation at site of infusion. Moniliasis, vaginitis; thrombocytopenia; anorexia; aggressive reaction, nervousness, agitation, anxiety; dizziness, convulsions, headache, hyperactivity, hypoesthesia, paresthesia, somnolenece, syncope; deafness, tinnitus, vertigo; palpitations, arrhythmias; hypotension; dyspepsia, constipation, pseudomembranous colitis, pancreatitis; hepatitis and cholestatic jaundice; allergic reactions; arthralgia; interstitial nephritis, acute renal failure; asthenia, fatigue, malaise.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Antacids, cetirizine, didanosine (dideoxyinosine), digoxin and colchicine, ergot, zidovudine, atorvastatin, carbamazepine, cimetidine, coumarin-type oral anticoagulants, ciclosporin, efavirenz, fluconazole, indinavir, methylprednisolone, midazolam, nelfinavir, rifabutin, sildenafil, terfenadine, theophylline, triazolam, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole.
flattened_sections.packaging: Film-coated tablet 250 mg, 500 mg. Powder for oral suspension 200 mg/5 mL x 15 mL, 22.5 mL. Powder for IV infusion 500 mg.
