flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of stable chronic heart failure (CHF) with reduced systolic left ventricular function in addition to ACE inhibitors and diuretics, and optionally cardiac glycosides. 5 and 10 mg: Treatment of hypertension (HTN), coronary heart disease (angina pectoris).
flattened_sections.dose: HTN or angina pectoris: Initially 5 mg once daily. If necessary, increase to 10 mg once daily. Max 20 mg once daily. Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 20 mL/min): Do not exceed 10 mg/day. Stable CHF: Initially 1.25 mg once daily. May be increased to 2.5 mg, 3.75 mg, 5 mg, 7.5 mg and 10 mg once daily in intervals of 2 weeks or longer depending on individual tolerance. Max 10 mg once daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Acute heart failure or during episodes of heart failure decompensation requiring IV inotropic therapy, cardiogenic shock, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block without a pacemaker, sick sinus syndrome, SA block, symptomatic bradycardia, symptomatic hypotension, severe bronchial asthma, severe forms of PAOD or Raynaud’s syndrome, pheochromocytoma, metabolic acidosis.
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with heart failure, DM with extremely fluctuating blood glucose levels: Symptoms of markedly reduced blood glucose (hypoglycemia) e.g. tachycardia, palpitations or sweating can be masked, strict fasting, ongoing desensitization therapy, mild disturbances of AV conduction (1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block), Prinzmetal angina, PAOD, psoriasis or history of psoriasis; with pheochromocytoma. Increase sensitivity to allergens and severity of anaphylactic reactions. May mask symptoms of thyrotoxicosis. Administer only after alpha-receptor blockade in pheochromocytoma patients. If necessary to withdraw bisoprolol before surgery, it should be done gradually and completed about 48 hrs before anesthesia. Avoided in patients with obstructive airways diseases. No therapeutic experience in patients with type 1 DM, severely impaired renal or hepatic function, restrictive cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, hemodynamically significant organic valvular disease, or MI within the last 3 months. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Patients with CHF: Bradycardia, asthenia, fatigue. Worsening of pre-existing heart failure. Dizziness, headache. Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation. Feeling of coldness or numbness in the extremities, hypotension.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Calcium antagonists, class I and III antiarrhythmic agents, rifampicin, insulin or hypoglycemic agents, anesthetic agents. Centrally acting antihypertensive drugs, cardiac glycosides, NSAIDs, mefloquine, MAOIs (except MAO-B), beta-sympathomimetics, sympathomimetic drugs that activate both alpha & beta-adrenoceptors topical beta blockers, parasympathomimetic drugs, non-selective beta-blockers, and ergotamine derivatives, antihypertensive agents, other drugs with BP lowering potential (e.g. TCA, barbiturates, phenothiazines).

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of patients with advanced colorectal cancer. In combination with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and folinic acid (FA) in patients with no prior chemotherapy for advanced cancer. Monotherapy if treatment regimen containing 5-FU has failed. In combination with cetuximab for treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (KRAS wild-type) with expression of epidermal growth factor receptor without prior treatment for metastatic disease or after failure of irinotecan-containing cytotoxic therapy. In combination with 5-FU, FA, and bevacizumab as 1<sup>st</sup> line treatment for colon or rectum metastatic carcinoma. In combination with capecitabine with or without bevacizumab as 1<sup>st</sup> line treatment for metastatic colorectal carcinoma.
flattened_sections.dose: IV infusion. Infuse the diluted infusion solution into a peripheral or central vein. Adults - Monotherapy (previously treated patients): 350 mg/m2 over 30-90 mins every 3 weeks; Hepatic impairment (bilirubin 1.5-3x the ULN): 200 mg/m2. pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

As adjunct to valproate or lithium in the treatment of manic or mixed episodes in adults. For preventing recurrence of manic, mixed, or depressive episodes. flattened_sections.dose: Administered once a day. Schizophrenia - Adults ≥18 yrs: Initially, 5-10 mg/day, with target dose of 10 mg/day within several days, adjust dose by 5 mg/day at not < 1 week intervals if needed; Maintenance treatment: Reassessment is needed; 10-20 mg/day in patients stable on olanzapine for approx 8 weeks. Adolescents 13-17 yrs: Initially, 2.5 or 5 mg, with target dose of 10 mg/day, adjust dose by 2.5 or 5 mg if needed. Bipolar I disorder (manic or mixed episodes) - Adults ≥18 yrs - Monotherapy: Initially 10 or 15 mg/day, and adjust dose by 5 mg/day at intervals not <24 hrs if indicated. As adjunct to lithium or valproate: Initially 10 mg/day. Prevention of bipolar I disorder recurrence: 10 mg/day, subsequent adjustment of daily dose should be within 5-20 mg/day. Adolescents 13-17 yrs: Initially 2.5 or 5 mg/day with a target dose of 10 mg/day, adjust dose by 2.5 or 5 mg. Depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder - Adults ≥18 yrs: Olanzapine 5 mg and fluoxetine 20 mg once a day in the evening. Adjust dose within ranges of olanzapine 5-12.5 mg and fluoxetine 20-50 mg. Childn and adolescents 10-17 yrs: Olanzapine 2.5 mg and fluoxetine 20 mg once a day in the evening. Treatment-resistant depression - Adults ≥18 yrs: Initially, olanzapine 5 mg and fluoxetine 20 mg once a day in the evening. Adjust dose within ranges of olanzapine 5-20 mg and fluoxetine 20-50 mg. Elderly ≥65 yrs, debilitated patients, patients with hepatic/renal impairment or a predisposition to hypotensive reaction: 5 mg/day starting dose.

brand_info.title: Indications
brand_info.content: Acute and maintenance treatment of schizophrenia and related psychoses in adults and adolescents 13-17 yrs. Bipolar I disorder (manic or mixed episodes): As monotherapy for acute and maintenance treatment of manic or mixed episodes in adults and adolescents 13-17 yrs. As adjunct to valproate or lithium in the treatment of manic or mixed episodes in adults. For preventing recurrence of manic, mixed, or depressive episodes. In combination with fluoxetine: Acute treatment of depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adults and childn 10-17 yrs; treatment-resistant depression in adults.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: Administered once a day. Schizophrenia - Adults ≥18 yrs: Initially, 5-10 mg/day, with target dose of 10 mg/day within several days, adjust dose by 5 mg/day at not < 1 week intervals if needed; Maintenance treatment: Reassessment is needed; 10-20 mg/day in patients stable on olanzapine for approx 8 weeks. Adolescents 13-17 yrs: Initially, 2.5 or 5 mg, with target dose of 10 mg/day, adjust dose by 2.5 or 5 mg if needed. Bipolar I disorder (manic or mixed episodes) - Adults ≥18 yrs - Monotherapy: Initially 10 or 15 mg/day, and adjust dose by 5 mg/day at intervals not <24 hrs if indicated. As adjunct to lithium or valproate: Initially 10 mg/day. Prevention of bipolar I disorder recurrence: 10 mg/day, subsequent adjustment of daily dose should be within 5-20 mg/day. Adolescents 13-17 yrs: Initially 2.5 or 5 mg/day with a target dose of 10 mg/day, adjust dose by 2.5 or 5 mg. Depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder - Adults ≥18 yrs: Olanzapine 5 mg and fluoxetine 20 mg once a day in the evening. Adjust dose within ranges of olanzapine 5-12.5 mg and fluoxetine 20-50 mg. Childn and adolescents 10-17 yrs: Olanzapine 2.5 mg and fluoxetine 20 mg once a day in the evening. Treatment-resistant depression - Adults ≥18 yrs: Initially, olanzapine 5 mg and fluoxetine 20 mg once a day in the evening. Adjust dose within ranges of olanzapine 5-20 mg and fluoxetine 20-50 mg. Elderly ≥65 yrs, debilitated patients, patients with hepatic/renal impairment or a predisposition to hypotensive reaction: 5 mg/day starting dose.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Patients with known risk of narrow-angle glaucoma.

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drug, NMS, weight gain, falls that may lead to fracture and other injuries, disruption of body temperature regulation. CV, cerebrovascular, endocrine and metabolic, hematologic, hepatic, nervous system, and respiratory effects. Patients with concomitant illness, seizures and suicidal behavior. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn <18 yrs. Elderly ≥65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.

flattened_sections.indications: Contraceptive. For women who experience hormone-related fluid retention and resulting symptoms. Treatment of moderate acne vulgaris, symptoms of premenstrual dysphoric disorder, and dysmenorrhea.
flattened_sections.dose: Take one tab daily at the same time for 24 consecutive days, followed by 4 treatment free days. Start subsequent pack after 7-day tab-free interval. No preceding hormonal contraceptive use: Start on day 1 of menstrual bleeding. May start on days 2-5 but a barrier method is recommended during the first cycle. Changing from combined hormonal contraceptive (COC), vaginal ring, or transdermal patch: Start on the day after last tab of previous COC or on the day of removal of the last ring or patch of cycle pack. Changing from progestogen-only-method or progestogen-releasing intrauterine system: May switch any day with additional use of barrier method for first 7 days of tablet-taking. Following 1st trimester abortion: May start immediately. Following delivery or 2nd trimester abortion: Start at day 21-28. Use additional barrier method for the first 7 days of tablet-taking when starting later.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Presence or history of venous or arterial thrombotic/thromboembolic event (e.g., DVT, pulmonary embolism, MI) or cerebrovascular accident. Presence or history of prodrome of thrombosis (e.g., TIA, angina pectoris). High risk of venous or arterial thrombosis. History of migraine with focal neurological symptoms. DM with vascular involvement. Severe hepatic disease with persistent abnormal liver function. Severe renal insufficiency or acute renal failure. Presence or history of liver tumors (benign or malignant). Known or suspected sex-steroid influenced malignancies (e.g., of genital organs or breasts). Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Known or suspected pregnancy. Rare hereditary galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose galactose malabsorption.
flattened_sections.precautions: Increased risk of arterial and venous thrombotic and thromboembolic diseases (e.g., MI, DVT, pulmonary embolism, cerebrovascular accidents); DM, SLE, hemolytic uremic syndrome, chronic inflammatory bowel disease (e.g., Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis), sickle cell disease; benign or malignant liver tumors; chloasma; spotting or breakthrough bleeding. May increase risk of cervical or breast cancer. Patients with renal impairment or present or history of hypertriglyceridemia; hereditary angioedema. Discontinue if migraine frequency or severity increases; HTN or acute/chronic liver function disturbances occur; cholestatic jaundice recurs. Avoid sun or UV exposure in women prone to chloasma. Lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Emotional lability, depression/depressive mood, migraine, nausea, breast pain, unscheduled uterine bleeding, genital tract bleeding.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Enzyme inducers (e.g., phenytoin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampicin, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, felbamate, griseofulvin, St. John’s wort), HIV/HCV protease inhibitors, non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, ciclosporin, lamotrigine, angiotensin-II receptor antagonists, potassium-sparing diuretics, aldosterone antagonists.

flattened_sections.indications: Prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adult patients undergoing elective hip or knee replacement surgery. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) with one or more risk factors. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and for the prevention of recurrent DVT and PE.
flattened_sections.dose: Prevention of VTE after hip or knee replacement surgery: 2.5 mg twice daily starting 12-24 hours after surgery. Treatment duration- Knee replacement surgery: 10-14 days. Hip replacement surgery: 32-38 days. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in NVAF: 5 mg twice daily; elderly ≥80 yrs, BW ≤60 kg, serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL: 2.5 mg twice daily. Treatment of DVT and PE: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE: 2.5 mg twice daily after at least 6 months of treatment. Taken with or without food. Tabs may be crushed and suspended in water, D5W, or apple juice or mixed with applesauce and promptly administered orally.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active bleeding.
flattened_sections.precautions: Risk of bleeding including serious and potentially fatal hemorrhage. Patients with severe hepatic impairment, hepatic disease; associated with coagulopathy; renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min) or undergoing dialysis. Discontinue prior surgery or invasive procedure and restarted once adequate hemostasis is achieved. Patients with prosthetic heart valve or antiphospholipid syndrome. Switching from to or from other anticoagulants. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Anemia, hemorrhage, nausea, confusion.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir), inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John’s wort). Anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, NSAIDs.

flattened_sections.indications: Adjunct to diet for treatment of elevated total-C, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and triglycerides and to increase HDL-C in primary hypercholesterolemia, combined hyperlipidemia, elevated serum triglyceride levels, and dysbetalipoproteinemia not adequately controlled by diet. Reduction of total-C and LDL-C in homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Reduces risk of fatal CHD and non-fatal MI, stroke, revascularization procedures, and angina pectoris in patients without clinically evident CV disease, with or without dyslipidemia, but with multiple risk factors for CHD; non-fatal MI, fatal and non-fatal stroke, revascularization procedures, hospitalization for CHF, and angina in patients with CHD; CV disease in patients with diabetes with moderately decreased eGFR; major CV events (e.g., stroke) in patients with CHD and CKD not requiring dialysis. Reduces rate of GFR decline and CKD progression in patients with CHD and/or diabetes with microalbuminuria. Adjunct to diet to reduce total-C, LDL-C, and apolipoprotein B levels in childn 10–17 yrs with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia and persistently elevated LDL-C (≥160 or ≥190 mg/dL) despite adequate diet therapy.
flattened_sections.dose: Primary hypercholesterolemia and combined hyperlipidemia: 10 mg once daily. Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: 80 mg. Severe dyslipidemia in childn ≥10 yrs: Initially 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 80 mg once daily. In combination with cyclosporine, telaprevir, tipranavir/ritonavir, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: Max 10 mg.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistent serum transaminase elevations >3x ULN. Women of childbearing potential not using adequate contraception. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with heavy alcohol use and/or have history of liver disease; history of renal impairment. Myalgia, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, rhabdomyolysis with acute renal failure secondary to myoglobinuria, hemorrhagic stroke, increased HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels. Perform liver function tests before initiation of therapy and periodically thereafter. Reduce dose or discontinue if ALT/AST persist >3x ULN. Discontinue if markedly elevated CPK levels occur, myopathy is diagnosed or suspected, or if risk factors for renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis are present.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nasopharyngitis, hyperglycemia, pharyngolaryngeal pain, epistaxis, diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea, flatulence, arthralgia, pain in extremity, musculoskeletal pain, muscle spasms, myalgia, joint swelling, abnormal liver function test, increased blood creatine phosphokinase, nightmare, blurred vision, tinnitus, abdominal discomfort, eructation, hepatitis, cholestasis, urticaria, muscle fatigue, neck pain, malaise, pyrexia, positive WBC urine.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of pulmonary and extrapulmonary aspergillosis in intolerant and refractory to amphotericin B therapy, and blastomycosis. Histoplasmosis (e.g., chronic cavitary pulmonary disease and disseminated, non-meningeal histoplasmosis). Onchomycosis of the toenail, with or without fingernail involvement due to dermatophytes, and fingernail in non-immunocompromised adults. Taken with meal.
flattened_sections.dose: Blastomycosis and histoplasmosis: 200 mg once daily, may be increased in 100 mg-increments to max 400 mg if no obvious improvement or there is evidence of progressive fungal disease. Doses >200 mg/day in two divided doses. Aspergillosis: 200-400 mg daily. Life-threatening situations: Loading dose of 200 mg thrice daily for the first 3 days, continued for a minimum of 3 months. Onchomycosis - Toenails with or without fingernail involvement: 200 mg once daily for 12 consecutive weeks; Fingernails: 2 treatment pulses each consist of 200 mg twice daily for 1 week. The pulses are separated by a 3-week period without Funguard.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Present or history of CHF. Coadministration with CYP3A4 substrates; colchicine, fesoterodine, and solifenacin in varying degrees of renal or hepatic impairment; eliglustat in poor or intermediate CYP2D6 metabolizers and taking strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors; venetoclax in chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic leukemia.

Life-threatening cardiac dysrhythmias and/or sudden death in coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors. Transient or permanent hearing loss. Discontinue if signs and symptoms of liver disease or neuropathy appear. Monitor liver function. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Elderly ≥65 yrs. Fertility. Pregnancy and lactation.

indication_long: Treatment of acute ischemic stroke within 4.5...

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of acute ischemic stroke within 4.5 hrs of symptom onset and after exclusion of intracranial hemorrhage.
flattened_sections.dose: ≥90 kg: 25 mg (5,000 U); ≥80 to < 90 kg: 22.5 mg (4,500 U); ≥70 to < 80 kg: 20 mg (4,000 U); ≥60 to < 70 kg: 17.5 mg (3,500 U); < 60 kg: 15 mg (3,000 U). Given as single IV bolus over approx 5-10 secs.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Significant bleeding disorder (present or within past 6 months). With effective anticoagulation (e.g., INR >1.3). History or suspected intracranial hemorrhage. Symptoms suggestive of subarachnoid hemorrhage, even with normal CT-scan. Severe stroke (e.g., NIHSS >25). Acute ischemic stroke without disabling neurological deficit, or symptoms rapidly improving before start of inj. History of CNS damage (e.g., neoplasm, aneurysm, intracranial or spinal surgery). Hemorrhagic diathesis. Severe uncontrolled arterial HTN. Major surgery, biopsy of parenchymal organ, or significant trauma within past 2 months. Recent head or cranium trauma. Prolonged CPR (>2 mins) within past 2 weeks. Acute pericarditis and/or subacute bacterial endocarditis. Acute pancreatitis. Severe hepatic dysfunction (e.g., HF, cirrhosis, portal HTN, and active hepatitis). Active peptic ulceration. Arterial aneurysm and arterial/venous malformation. Neoplasm with increased bleeding risk. Symptoms of ischemic attack beginning >4.5 hrs before inj or unknown onset time. Seizure at onset of stroke. Administration of heparin within previous 48 hrs and thromboplastin time exceeding the ULN for laboratory. History of prior stroke and concomitant diabetes. Prior stroke within last 3 months. Platelet count < 100,000/mm<sup>3</sup>. >185 mmHg SBP or >110 mmHg DBP, or aggressive management (IV pharmacotherapy) to reduce BP. Blood glucose < 50 mg/dL or >400 mg/dL (< 2.8 mM or >22.2 mM).
flattened_sections.precautions: Avoid administration of IV heparin or platelet aggregation inhibitors (e.g., aspirin) in the first 24 hrs after treatment. Bleeding. Cerebral edema. Hypersensitivity (e.g., angioedema). Discontinue concomitant heparin immediately if serious bleeding occurs. Consider protamine if heparin was given within 4 hrs before bleeding. Recent IM inj or small recent traumas, puncture of major vessels or cardiac massage for resuscitation. Conditions with increased hemorrhage risk. Patients receiving anticoagulants. Monitor BP for 24 hrs after treatment. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly >80 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.

brand_info.title: Indications
brand_info.content: Treatment of acute ischemic stroke within 4.5 hrs of symptom onset and after exclusion of intracranial hemorrhage.

brand_info.title: Dose
brand_info.content: ≥90 kg: 25 mg (5,000 U); ≥80 to < 90 kg: 22.5 mg (4,500 U); ≥70 to < 80 kg: 20 mg (4,000 U); ≥60 to < 70 kg: 17.5 mg (3,500 U); < 60 kg: 15 mg (3,000 U). Given as single IV bolus over approx 5-10 secs.

brand_info.title: Contraindications
brand_info.content: Hypersensitivity. Significant bleeding disorder (present or within past 6 months). With effective anticoagulation (e.g., INR >1.3). History or suspected intracranial hemorrhage. Symptoms suggestive of subarachnoid hemorrhage, even with normal CT-scan. Severe stroke (e.g., NIHSS >25). Acute ischemic stroke without disabling neurological deficit, or symptoms rapidly improving before start of inj. History of CNS damage (e.g., neoplasm, aneurysm, intracranial or spinal surgery). Hemorrhagic diathesis. Severe uncontrolled arterial HTN. Major surgery, biopsy of parenchymal organ, or significant trauma within past 2 months. Recent head or cranium trauma. Prolonged CPR (>2 mins) within past 2 weeks. Acute pericarditis and/or subacute bacterial endocarditis. Acute pancreatitis. Severe hepatic dysfunction (e.g., HF, cirrhosis, portal HTN, and active hepatitis). Active peptic ulceration. Arterial aneurysm and arterial/venous malformation. Neoplasm with increased bleeding risk. Symptoms of ischemic attack beginning >4.5 hrs before inj or unknown onset time. Seizure at onset of stroke. Administration of heparin within previous 48 hrs and thromboplastin time exceeding the ULN for laboratory. History of prior stroke and concomitant diabetes. Prior stroke within last 3 months. Platelet count < 100,000/mm<sup>3</sup>. >185 mmHg SBP or >110 mmHg DBP, or aggressive management (IV pharmacotherapy) to reduce BP. Blood glucose < 50 mg/dL or >400 mg/dL (< 2.8 mM or >22.2 mM).

brand_info.title: Precautions
brand_info.content: Avoid administration of IV heparin or platelet aggregation inhibitors (e.g., aspirin) in the first 24 hrs after treatment. Bleeding. Cerebral edema. Hypersensitivity (e.g., angioedema). Discontinue concomitant heparin immediately if serious bleeding occurs. Consider protamine if heparin was given within 4 hrs before bleeding. Recent IM inj or small recent traumas, puncture of major vessels or cardiac massage for resuscitation. Conditions with increased hemorrhage risk. Patients receiving anticoagulants. Monitor BP for 24 hrs after treatment. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly >80 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.

brand_info.title: Side Effects
brand_info.content: Vascular, GI (e.g., hematemesis, melena, gastric, gastric ulcer, rectal, and mouth hemorrhage), urogenital (e.g., hematuria, urinary tract hemorrhage), inj/puncture site, and Intracranial (e.g., cerebral hemorrhage or hematoma, hemorrhagic stroke, hemorrhagic transformation stroke, intracranial hematoma, subarachnoid hemorrhage) hemorrhage, somnolence, aphasia, hemiparesis, convulsion, epistaxis, ecchymosis.

brand_info.title: Drug Interactions

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

indication_long: Treatment of type 2 DM in adults as 2nd

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of type 2 DM in adults as 2<sup>nd</sup> line therapy, when diet, exercise and initial treatment with metformin or glibenclamide (or another sulfonylurea) do not result in adequate glycemic control, and as replacement for previous treatment with metformin and glibenclamide in patients whose glycemia is stable and controlled.
flattened_sections.dose: Adult Initial treatment: Initially 1 tab of 500 mg/2.5 mg or 500 mg/5 mg once daily. Initial dose must not exceed the daily doses of glibenclamide (or equiv dose of another sulfonylurea) or metformin already being taken alone. As replacement for previous combination therapy with metformin and sulfonylurea: Initial dose must not exceed the daily dose of glibenclamide (or equiv dose of another sulfonylurea) and metformin already being taken. Increase dose in increments of not >500 mg/5 mg daily every 2 weeks or longer. Max2,000 mg/20 mg daily. Elderly: Start with lowest available and increase gradually if necessary. Do not titrate to max dose. Debilitated and malnourished patients: Do not titrate to max dose. Renal impairment CrCl30-59 mL/min or eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m2: Max metformin 1,000 mg daily. Closely monitor renal function every 3-6 months. Take with food.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Metabolic acidosis (e.g., lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis), diabetic pre-coma. Severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min or eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m<sup>2</sup>). Kidney insufficiency. Acute conditions with potential to alter renal function e.g. dehydration, severe infection, CV collapse (shock). Acute or chronic disease which may cause hypoxia e.g. cardiac or respiratory failure, recent MI, CV collapse/shock. Liver insufficiency, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Porphyria. Miconazole even for local use. Congenital galactosemia, glucose and galactose malabsorption syndrome or lactase deficiency.  Congenital galactosemia, glucose and galactose malabsorption syndrome, and lactase deficiency. Coadministration with miconazole or iodinated contrast media. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Lactic acidosis. Not recommended in patients with known mitochondrial diseases e.g., Mitochondrial Encephalopathy with Lactic Acidosis, and Stroke‑like episodes (MELAS) syndrome and Maternal inherited diabetes and deafness (MIDD).  Discontinue immediately in case of signs and symptoms suggestive of MELAS syndrome or MIDD after metformin administration. Hypoglycemia. Blood sugar imbalance. May reduce vit B<sub>12</sub> levels. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, infectious diseases, heart failure, and GCPD deficiency. Monitor renal function at least every 3-6 months in patients with CrCl 45-59 mL/min or eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> and in elderly patients; at least every 3 months in patients with CrCl 30-44 mL/min or eGFR 30-44 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Discontinue treatment 48 hrs before or from the time of IV administration of iodinated contrast media; 48 hrs before elective surgery. May be reinstituted after 48 hrs if renal function is stable. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Elderly ≥65 yrs.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, taste disturbance. Transient visual disturbances may occur at the start of treatment due to a decrease in glycemia levels. Vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Glucocorticoids, tetracosactides, beta-3-agonists, danazol, chlorpromazine, diuretics especially loop diuretics. Glibenclamide: Alcohol, phenylbutazone, bosentan, beta-blockers, clonidine, reserpine, guanethidine, sympathomimetics, fluconazole, desmopressin, colesevelam, ARBs (e.g., captopril, enalapril). Metformin: OCT1 inhibitors (e.g., verapamil) and inducers (e.g., rifampicin), OCT2 inhibitors (e.g., cimetidine, dolutegravir, crizotinib, olaparib, daclatasvir, vandetanib).
flattened_sections.packaging: Film-coated tablet 500 mg/5 mg, 500 mg/2.5 mg.

pregnancy_risk.header: Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:

categories.title: A
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb.

categories.title: B
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any.

categories.title: C
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks.

categories.title: D
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks.

categories.title: X
categories.content: Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits.

flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Anticoagulants, other fibrates and HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, ciclosporin, glitazones. Drugs metabolized by CYP2C19, CYP2A6, and CYP2C9 with a narrow therapeutic index.

flattened_sections.dose: 1 tab daily for 28 days starting from the 1<sup>st</sup> day of menstrual bleeding.

HCV medicinal products (e.g. boceprevir, telaprevir). Strong (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) or moderate (e.g. fluconazole, diltiazem, erythromycin) CYP3A4 inhibitors. Medical charcoal. Ciclosporin. Lamotrigine.

data.description: A rapid test based on unique and highly specific monoclonal antibodies that bind to the phosphorylated form of insulin-like growth factor binding protein-1 (phlGFBP-1). Reliable test for quickly and easily detecting premature rupture of fetal membranes in all patients.
data.directions: Take a vaginal fluid sample with polyester swab from the posterior fornix of the vagina or from the cervix if no fluid is visible, by leaving the swab in the vagina for 10-15 seconds. This allows the swab to absorb sufficient amount of specimen. Place the polyester swab in the specimen extraction solution provided and swirl it around vigorously for 10 seconds. After extraction, dip the yellow area of the dipstick into the solution and hold it there until the liquid front reaches the result area. Then remove the dipstick from the solution and place it in a horizontal position. A positive result can be seen if 2 lines, a control line and a test line, appear in the result area. If, after 5 mins, only the control line has appeared, the test result is negative. Disregard positive result if the test line appeared beyond 5 mins.
data.uses: Identifies cause of preterm births and major cause of maternal and fetal morbidity. Correct diagnosis is important to guide treatment and to minimize complications. However, symptoms differ between patients, which makes diagnosis challenging.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of advanced colorectal carcinoma, alone or in combination with leucovorin. As an adjunct to surgery in women with breast cancer, in combination chemotherapy. Management of gastric, primary hepatic, pancreatic, uterine (particularly cervical), ovarian, and bladder cancer.
flattened_sections.dose: IV injection: Initially 12 mg/kg once a day for 4 consecutive days, then 6 mg/kg on days 6, 8, 10, and 12 unless toxic reaction occurs before then; no therapy on days 5, 7, 9, and 11. Discontinue on day 12 even if no toxicity occurs. Alternatively, 15 mg/kg as single IV injection once a week throughout the course. Max 800 mg/day. IV infusion: 15 mg/kg (but not >1 g per infusion) diluted in 500 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride or 5% dextrose given once daily at a rate of 40 drops/min over 4 hrs. Infusion may be repeated on successive days until first GI or hematological side effects appear or a total of 12-15 g has been given. Alternatively, daily dose may be infused over 30-60 mins or given as continuous IV infusion over 24 hrs. Intra-arterial infusion: 5-7.5 mg/kg/day administered as a 24-hr continuous drip infusion. Maintenance therapy: Repeat initial therapy at intervals of 30 days after the last dose of the previous course. Alternatively, 10-15 mg/kg once a week when toxicity from the initial course of therapy has subsided. Max 1 g weekly. Combination therapy with leucovorin: 9-10 mg/kg for 5 days after leucovorin 5-12 mg/kg for 5 days. Repeat course every 4 weeks. For poor-risk patients - IV injection: Initially 6 mg/kg once a day for 3 days, then 3 mg/kg is given on days 5, 7, and 9 unless toxic reaction occurs before then. Repeat course every 30 days. Max 400 mg/day. IV infusion: 6 mg/kg given once a day over 4 hrs, until toxicity is observed.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Poor nutritional state, dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency, depressed bone marrow function, potentially serious infection, management of non-malignant disease. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Discontinue promptly following any signs of toxicity (e.g. stomatitis, esopharyngitis, leukocyte count <3,500/mm3, platelet count <100,000 mm3, granulocyte count <1,500/mm3, intractable vomiting, diarrhea or frequent LBM, hemorrhage, nervous system toxicity. Should not be readministered after a documented CV reaction (e.g. arrhythmia, angina, ST segment changes) or severe neurological toxicity. Patients with heart disease who experience chest pain during treatment course. Patients who undergone recent major surgery (within previous 30 days); have previously received high-dose irradiation therapy to bone marrow-bearing areas or alkylating agents; widespread metastatic involvement of bone marrow. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Elderly ≥70 yrs. Women. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Nucleoside analogs (e.g. brivudin, sorivudine), cimetidine, clozapine, interferon alfa-2b, leucovorin, levamisole, methotrexate, metronidazole, mitomycin, phenytoin, sorafenib, warfarin. Increase in or false positive in tests for bilirubin (icteric index) and 5-hydroxyindole acetic acid in urine. Diagnostic tests of thyroid function. Incompatibilities: Carboplatin, cisplatin, cytarabine, diazepam, doxorubicin and other anthracyclines, leucovorin, methotrexate, filgrastim, gallium nitrate, metoclopramide, morphine, ondansetron, parenteral nutrition, and vinorelbine.

flattened_sections.dose: Advanced colorectal cancer in combination with 5-FU - Bimonthly regimen: 200 mg/m2 IV infusion over 2 hrs, followed by IV bolus injection of 5-FU 400 mg/m2 and 22-hr infusion of 5-FU 600 mg/m2 for 2 consecutive days, every 2 weeks on days 1 and 2. Weekly regimen: 20 mg/m2 by IV bolus injection or 200-500 mg/m2 as IV infusion over 2 hrs plus IV bolus injection of 5-FU 500 mg/m2 in the middle or end of folinic acid infusion. Monthly regimen: 20 mg/m2 as IV bolus injection or 200-500 mg/m2 as IV infusion over 2 hrs immediately followed by IV bolus injection of 5-FU 425 or 370 mg/m2 during 5 consecutive days. Folinic acid rescue after chemotherapy with >500 mg/m2 methotrexate: Start rescue therapy within 24 hrs of methotrexate administration. Dosage schedule: 10 mg/m2 parenterally followed by 10 mg/m2 orally (if there is adequate GI function) every 6 hrs until serum methotrexate concentration has declined to <10-8 M. If at 24 hrs after methotrexate administration, serum creatinine has increased to ≥50% or the serum creatinine is >5x10-6 M, or if at 48 hrs after methotrexate administration, the serum methotrexate concentration is <9x10-7 M: May increase to 100 mg/m2 every 3 hrs until serum methotrexate >10-8M. Antidote to methotrexate toxicity: Up to 75 mg IV infusion within 12 hrs followed by 12 mg IM every 6 hrs for 4 doses. When average methotrexate doses appear to have an adverse effect: 6-12 mg IM every 6 hrs for 4 doses. Antidote to trimetrexate toxicity: 20 mg/m2 every 6 hrs, should be given orally or IV (over 5-10 mins) and continued for at least 72 hrs after last trimetrexate dose. Total daily dose: 80 mg/m2. Recommended course: 21 days trimetrexate therapy and 24 days folinic acid. Overdosage with trimetrexate >90 mg/m2 without concomitant folinic acid: 40 mg/m2 IV every 6 hrs for 3 days. Antidote to pyrimethamine toxicity: 3-9 mg per day IM for 3 days or until platelet and leukocyte counts reach safe levels. Antidote to trimethoprim toxicity: 3-10 mg per day until recovery of blood cell counts. Megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency: Up to 1 mg IM daily.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not to be used for treatment of undiagnosed anemia, pernicious anemia, vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency or other megaloblastic anemias secondary to vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiency. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not administer intrathecally. Do not mix with 5-FU in same IV injection or infusion. Administration of folinic acid after methotrexate in patients with aciduria, ascites, dehydration, GI obstruction, pleural or peritoneal effusions. Patients with renal impairment; advanced colorectal cancer when used in combination with 5-FU. Concomitant administration of folinic acid and 5-FU in elderly or debilitated patients; anticonvulsant therapy in childn. Lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, severe mucosal toxicity, diarrhea, dehydration. With 5-FU: leukopenia, diarrhea, stomatitis, lethargy, malaise, fatigue, alopecia, dermatitis, anorexia.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Folic acid antagonists, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, fluoropyrimidines, anticonvulsants, direct or indirect DNA synthesis inhibitors, glucarpidase. Incompatibilities: Droperidol, 5-FU, foscarnet, methotrexate.

flattened_sections.indications: Initial treatment of advanced epithelial ovarian cancer in established combinations with other approved chemotherapeutic agents. Palliative treatment of epithelial ovarian cancer, refractory to standard chemotherapy with or without cisplatin. Treatment of small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC).
flattened_sections.dose: Monotherapy - Initial dosing - Previously treated recurrent ovarian carcinoma: 360 mg/m2. Previously treated or have poor performance status: 300-320 mg/m2. Previously untreated: 400 mg/m2. Administer by IV infusion over 15-60 mins on day 1, every 4 weeks. Combination therapy with cyclophosphamide - Initial dosing - Treatment of advanced ovarian cancer for previously untreated patients: 300 mg/m2; cyclophosphamide dose: 600 mg/m2. Administer by IV infusion over 15-60 mins on day 1, every 4 weeks for 6 cycles. Dosage adjustments based on hematologic nadir from prior course - Platelets >100,000 cells/m2 and neutrophils >2,000 cells/m2: 125%. Platelets >50,000-100,000 cells/m2 and neutrophils 500-2,000 cells/m2: 100% from prior course. Platelets <50,000 cells/m2 and neutrophils <500 cells/m2: 75% from prior course. Renal impairment - CrCl 41-59 mL/min: 250 mg/m2; 16-40 mL/min: 200 mg/m2. Do not repeat intermittent courses until neutrophil count is at least 2,000 cells/mm3 and platelet count is at least 100,000 cells/mm3.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to carboplatin, cisplatin or other platinum-containing compounds, mannitol. Pre-existing severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) without risk-benefit ratio assessment; severe myelosuppression; significant bleeding, bleeding tumors. Concomitant use with yellow fever vaccine. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not use needles or IV sets containing aluminum parts. Patients at risk for myelosuppression. Patients previously on antineoplastic therapy (especially cisplatin-containing regimen); concurrent use of radiation or emetogenic therapy. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Childn. Pregnancy Risk: Category D.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Myelosuppression. GI effects. Pain and asthenia. Peripheral neuropathy. Ototoxicity and other sensory abnormalities. Carcinogenicity, mutagenicity and fertility impairment.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of bleeding episodes and peri-op management in adults and childn with hemophilia A or B with inhibitors, congenital Factor VII (FVII) deficiency, and Glanzmann’s thrombasthenia with refractoriness to platelet transfusions, with or without antibodies to platelets. Treatment of bleeding episodes and peri-op management in adults with acquired hemophilia. Treatment of severe postpartum hemorrhage when uterotonics are insufficient to achieve hemostasis.
flattened_sections.dose: Congenital hemophilia A or B with inhibitors - Acute bleeding episodes - Hemostatic: 90 mcg/kg every 2 hrs, adjust until hemostasis is achieved; Post-hemostatic: 90 mcg/kg every 3-6 hrs for severe bleeds until hemostasis is achieved. Peri-op management - Minor surgery - Initial: 90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2 hrs for the duration of the surgery. Post-surgical: 90 mcg/kg every 2 hrs for 48 hrs then every 2-6 hrs until healing occurs. Major surgery - Initial: 90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2 hrs for the duration of the surgery, additional bolus doses can be given. Post-surgical: 90 mcg/kg every 2 hrs for 5 days then every 4 hrs or by continuous infusion at 50 mcg/ kg/hr until healing occurs. Acquired Hemophilia - Acute bleeding episodes: 70-90 mcg/kg every 2-3 hrs until hemostasis is achieved. Peri-op management: 70-90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2-3 hrs for the duration of the surgery and until hemostasis is achieved. Congenital Factor VII Deficiency - Acute bleeding episodes: 15-30 mcg/kg every 4-6 hours until hemostasis is achieved. Peri-op management: 15-30 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 4-6 hrs for the duration of the surgery and until hemostasis is achieved. Glanzmann’s thrombasthenia - Acute bleeding episodes: 90 mcg/kg every 2-6 hrs until hemostasis is achieved. Severe postpartum hemorrhage: 60-90 mcg/kg BW IV bolus; in case of insufficient hemostatic response, 2nd dose can be administered after 30 mins. Peri-op management - Initial: 90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2 hrs for the duration of the procedure. Post-surgical: 90 mcg/kg every 2-6 hrs to prevent post-op bleeding.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: May cause serious arterial and venous thrombotic events. Monitor signs or symptoms of activation of coagulation system or thrombosis. Patients with known hypersensitivity to mouse, hamster, or bovine proteins; with congenital hemophilia receiving concomitant treatment with aPCCs; older patients with acquired hemophilia and receiving other hemostatic agents; with a history of cardiac, vascular disease or predisposed to thrombotic events.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Thrombotic events e.g. VTE, DVT; anaphylactic shock, rash, pruritus, urticaria; pyrexia, headache, nausea, dyspnea.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Prothrombin complex concentrates (activated or not). Antifibrinolytics; rFXIII.

Major surgery - Initial: 90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2 hrs for the duration of the surgery, additional bolus doses can be given. Post-surgical: 90 mcg/kg every 2 hrs for 5 days then every 4 hrs or by continuous infusion at 50 mcg/ kg/hr until healing occurs. Acquired Hemophilia - Acute bleeding episodes: 70-90 mcg/kg every 2-3 hrs until hemostasis is achieved. Peri-op management: 70-90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2-3 hrs for the duration of the surgery and until hemostasis is achieved. Congenital Factor VII Deficiency - Acute bleeding episodes: 15-30 mcg/kg every 4-6 hours until hemostasis is achieved. Peri-op management: 15-30 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 4-6 hrs for the duration of the surgery and until hemostasis is achieved. Glanzmann’s thrombasthenia - Acute bleeding episodes: 90 mcg/kg every 2-6 hrs until hemostasis is achieved. Severe postpartum hemorrhage: 60-90 mcg/kg BW IV bolus; in case of insufficient hemostatic response, 2nd dose can be administered after 30 mins. Peri-op management - Initial: 90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2 hrs for the duration of the procedure. Post-surgical: 90 mcg/kg every 2-6 hrs to prevent post-op bleeding.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of schizophrenia. Acute treatment of manic and mixed episodes associated with bipolar disorder and maintenance therapy for bipolar I disorder, both as monotherapy and as adjunct to lithium or valproate. Adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD). Treatment of irritability associated with autistic disorder, Tourette’s disorder. Special considerations in treating childn with schizophrenia, bipolar I disorder, and irritability associated with autistic disorder.
flattened_sections.dose: Schizophrenia - Adults: 10 or 15 mg/day once daily. Dose range 10-30 mg/day. Adolescents: 10 mg/day, initially 2 mg/day, titrate to 5 mg/day after 2 days and then 10 mg/day after 2 additional days. Adjust dose further by 5 mg increments up to max 30 mg/day. Bipolar I disorder - Adults - Monotherapy: 15 mg once daily. Adjunctive treatment with lithium or valproate: 10-15 mg once daily. Adjust dose further by 5 mg increments up to max 30 mg/day. Childn 10-17 yrs: Initially 2 mg/day, titrate to 5 mg/day after 2 days and then 10 mg/day after 2 additional days. Adjunctive treatment of MDD - Adults: Initially 2-5 mg/day. Dose range 2-15 mg/day. Adjust dose gradually up to 5 mg/day at intervals of not < 1 week. Irritability associated with autistic disorder - Childn 6-17 yrs: 5-15 mg/day. Initially 2 mg/day, increase to 5 mg/day and then 10 or 15 mg/day. Adjust dose gradually up to 5 mg/day at intervals of not < 1 week. Tourette’s disorder - Childn 6-18 yrs: 5-20 mg/day; Patients weighing < 50 kg: Initially 2 mg/day, then 5 mg/day after 2 days. May be increased to 10 mg/day; ≥50 kg: Initially 2 mg/day for 2 days, increased to 5 mg/day for 5 days, then 10 mg/day on day 8. Adjust dose gradually by 5 mg/day increments at intervals of not < 1 week. Max: 20 mg/day. Poor CYP2D6 metabolizers, patients taking concomitant CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 inhibitors or CYP3A4 inducers: Adjust dose except when used as adjunctive treatment of MDD.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Oral soln is not approved for MDD. Patients with dementia-related psychosis; worsening and/or emergence of suicidal ideation and behavior. NMS, tardive dyskinesia, hyperglycemia, DM, dyslipidemia, weight gain, compulsive behaviors, orthostatic hypotension, fall-related injury, leukopenia, neutropenia, and agranulocytosis. Patients with history of seizures, at risk for aspiration. Disruption of body temp regulation. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, headache, constipation, dizziness, akathisia, anxiety, insomnia, and restlessness. Somnolence, extrapyramidal disorder, fatigue, increased appetite, nasopharyngitis, and weight increased.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. itraconazole, clarithromycin) or strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g. quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine), strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, rifampin), antihypertensive drugs, benzodiazepines e.g. lorazepam.

indication_long: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia.

flattened_sections.indications: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia.
flattened_sections.dose: IV/SC only. Patients on low-dose chemotherapy or with non-serious marrow depression estimated damage: 1.25 mcg/kg/day. Patients with high-intensity chemotherapy or obvious decline of granulocytes: 2.5 mcg/kg/day for 7 days. Patients with neutrophilic granulocytes < 1x109/L after chemotherapy: 5 mcg/kg/day.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to filgrastim, E. coli-derived proteins. Increased dose of cytotoxic chemotherapy beyond established dosage regimens. Severe congenital neutropenia (Kostmann’s syndrome) with abnormal cytogenetics. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.precautions: Do not dilute using saline solutions. Obtain CBC and platelet count before instituting treatment. Concomitant use with cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Do not administer 24 hrs before to 24 hrs after cytotoxic chemotherapy. Patients with sickle cell disorders, chronic myeloid leukemia, myelodysplasia; preexisting cardiac conditions (MI, arrhythmia); infections causing myelosuppression. Risk for splenomegaly and splenic rupture, thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, cutaneous vasculitis, ARDS, osteoporosis. May cause transient positive bone imaging changes. Childn <18 yrs. Lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category C.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Musculoskeletal pain. Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, mucosal inflammation, constipation and diarrhea. Sickle cell crisis. Leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia. Increased gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase, ALP, LDH, and uric acid. Headache, anorexia. Cough, pharyngolaryngeal pain. Alopecia, skin rash. Erythema, swelling or pruritus at site of injection. Fatigue and generalized weakness.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Drugs that potentiate neutrophil release e.g. lithium.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, complicated urinary tract infections (UTI) including pyelonephritis, soft tissue infections (e.g. cellulitis, erysipelas, wound infections), and intra-abdominal infections in adults and childn, including neonates (from birth). Prophylaxis against gastrointestinal (GI) (including esophageal), orthopedic, cardiovascular (CV), and gynecological surgery (including caesarian section) infections.
flattened_sections.dose: Administered via deep IM injection, IV injection for 3-5 mins, or IV drip or infusion for 30-60 mins. Adults and childn ≥40 kg - CAP, acute exacerbations or chronic bronchitis, soft tissue infections (e.g. cellulitis, erysipelas, wound infections): 750 mg IV or IM every 8 hrs; Complicated UTI including pyelonephritis: 1.5 g every 8 hrs IV or IM; Severe infections: 750 mg IV every 6 hrs or 1.5 g IV every 8 hrs; Surgical prophylaxis for GI, gynecological surgery (including caesarian section), and orthopedic operations: 1.5 g with induction of anesthesia, may be supplemented with 750 mg IM after 8 hrs and 16 hrs; Surgical prophylaxis for CV and esophageal operations: 1.5 g with induction of anesthesia, followed by 750 mg IM every 8 hrs for 24 hrs. CAP, complicated UTI including pyelonephritis, soft tissue infections (e.g. cellulitis, erysipelas, wound infections), intra-abdominal infections - Childn < 40 kg, toddlers, and infants >3 weeks: 30-100 mg/kg/day IV in 3-4 divided doses. 60 mg/kg/day is appropriate for most infections; Infants 0-3 weeks: 30-100 mg/kg/day IV in 2-3 divided doses. Patients with renal impairment - CrCl 10-20 mL/min, renal failure on continuous arteriovenous hemodialysis in intensive therapy units: 750 mg twice daily; < 10 mL/min: 750 mg once daily. In patients on hemodialysis: Additional 750 mg IV or IM after each dialysis session. Can be incorporated into the peritoneal dialysis fluid (usually 250 mg for every 2 L of dialysis fluid).
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Cross-sensitivity with other beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g. penicillins, monobactams, carbapenems).
flattened_sections.precautions: Not indicated for infections caused by G(-) non-fermenting bacteria. Patients with renal impairment, history of non-severe hypersensitivity to other beta-lactam antibiotics; on a controlled sodium diet. Concomitant use with potent diuretics (e.g. furosemide) or aminoglycosides. Antibiotic-associated pseudomembranous colitis may develop. Overgrowth of Candida or other non-susceptible organisms during prolonged use. Monitor renal function of elderly patients and those with pre-existing renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Neutropenia, eosinophilia, decreased Hgb; transient rise in liver enzymes; injection site reactions (e.g. pain, thrombophlebitis).
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Estrogen, oral contraceptives; probenecid; potent diuretics (e.g. furosemide), aminoglycosides; oral anticoagulants. False positive Coomb’s test. May interfere with copper reduction methods (e.g. Benedict’s and Fehling’s soln, Clinitest). False negative ferricyanide test.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of severe bacterial infections sensitive to cefotaxime, especially septicemia, endocarditis, and meningitis, except those due to Listeria monocytogenes. Prophylaxis of endoscopic prostate resection.
flattened_sections.dose: Administered via deep IM injection, IV injection, or IV infusion for 20-60 mins. Adults - Usual dose: 3 g/day, may be increased up to 12 g depending on the severity of infection; Urinary tract infections: 2 g/day; Prophylaxis of endoscopic prostate resection: 1 g IV on anesthetic induction; Meningitis: 200-300 mg/kg/day. Max 24 g/day. Childn, infants, and full-term neonates: 50 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses via IV injection, may be increased up to 200 mg/kg/day depending on the severity of infection. Premature neonates: 50 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses via IV injection, may be increased to 100 mg/kg/day in severe infections. Pneumococcal meningitis - Adults, childn, and infants >3 months: 50-75 mg/kg IV infusion for 20 mins every 6 hrs within first 48-72 hrs (i.e. 200-300 mg/kg/day), followed by vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV infusion for 60 mins (i.e. 60 mg/kg/day) in adults in case of signs of severity or in the presence of reduced-penicillin sensitivity pneumococcus risk factors. May be continued for >48-72 hrs depending on the MIC of the isolated pneumococcus strain. Patients with renal impairment: CrCl ≤5 mL/min: Reduce dose by 50%. In patients undergoing hemodialysis: Administer an additional 1 g IV injection at the end of each dialysis session and every 24 hrs.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
flattened_sections.precautions: Cross-sensitivity with penicillins and other cephalosporins. Patients with renal impairment; on a strict low sodium diet. Concomitant use with potentially nephrotoxic antibiotics (e.g. aminoglycosides) or diuretics (e.g. furosemide, ethacrynic acid).
flattened_sections.side_effects: Cutaneous, digestive, hematological, hepatic, and nephrotoxic reactions. Metabolic encephalopathies. Venous inflammation. IM injection site pain.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Oral anticoagulants. False positive Coomb’s test; test for glucose when using reducing substances.

flattened_sections.dose: Adults and adolescents >13 yrs – Pharyngitis/tonsillitis, acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis: 250 mg twice daily for 10 days. Secondary bacterial infections of acute bronchitis: 250 or 500 mg twice daily for 5-10 days. Uncomplicated UTI: 250 mg twice daily for 7-10 days. Acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections: 250 or 500 mg twice daily for 10 days. Early Lyme disease: 500 mg twice daily for 20 days. Uncomplicated gonorrhea: 1 g once daily as single dose. Childn (who can swallow tabs whole) – Acute otitis media, acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis: 250 mg twice daily for 10 days. Patients with renal impairment – (CrCl 10- < 30 mL/min): Standard individual dose given every 24 hrs; < 10 mL/min (without hemodialysis): Standard individual dose given every 48 hrs; Hemodialysis: A single additional standard dose given at the end of each dialysis.

flattened_sections.precautions: Renal or hepatic impairment. Cross-hypersensitivity. Overgrowth of non-susceptible microorganism (Candida, Enterococci, Clostridium difficile). Superinfection. Discontinue use if CDAD is suspected or confirmed. Concurrent treatment of potent diuretics. Individuals with history of colitis. Monitor prothrombin time in patients at risk and administered exogenous Vitamin K. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy Risk: Category B.

Glucose oxidase or hexokinase method to determine blood/plasma glucose levels.

indication_long: Initial therapy in patients with type 2 diabe...

flattened_sections.indications: Initial therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) to improve glycemic control when diet and exercise do not provide adequate glycemic control. Adjunct to diet and exercise: (1) In patients with inadequately controlled type 2 DM on metformin or sitagliptin (alone or in combination); (2) as part of triple combination therapy with a sulfonylurea or PPAR-gamma agonist (e.g. thiazolidinediones) in patients inadequately controlled with any 2 of 3 drugs (metformin, sitagliptin, or sulfonylurea/PPAR-gama agonist); or (3) in combination with insulin.
flattened_sections.dose: Individualized dosage. Taken with food. Initial therapy: 50 mg sitagliptin/500 mg metformin tab 2x daily, may be titrated gradually up to 2,000 mg metformin daily. Inadequately controlled on metformin monotherapy: 50 mg sitagliptin 2x daily with dose of metformin already taken; on sitagliptin monotherapy: Initially 50 mg/500 mg 2x daily, may be titrated up to 50 mg/1 g 2x daily. As part of combination therapy with a sulfonylurea, thiazolidinedione or insulin: 50 mg sitagliptin 2x daily with metformin dose based on current dose and glycemic control level. Switching from co-administration of sitagliptin and metformin as separate tabs: Initiate dose of sitagliptin and metformin already being taken.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis (e.g. diabetic ketoacidosis) with or without coma. Type 1 DM. Hepatic disease. Lactation.
flattened_sections.precautions: Switching from other oral hypoglycemics. Patients exposed to stress, with excessive alcohol intake, risks for hypoglycemia, previously controlled DM developing laboratory abnormalities. Not recommended for patients with eGFR < 45-30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Concomitant use of cationic drugs. May require lower sulfonylurea or insulin doses to reduce risk of hypoglycemia. Discontinue prior to or at the time of iodinated contrast imaging in patients with eGFR ≥30-< 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>, history of liver disease, alcoholism, heart failure, or IV/intra-arterial administration of iodinated contrast, until eGFR has been re-evaluated 48 hrs after and found acceptable; pancreatitis; bullous pemphigoid; condition associated with hypoxemia, dehydration, or sepsis; suspected lactic acidosis; surgical procedures until resumption of oral intake and renal function is stable. Assess renal function prior to initiation of therapy and periodically thereafter. Monitor vit B<sub>12</sub> levels at 2-3 yr intervals in patients with inadequate vit B<sub>12</sub> or calcium intake or absorption. Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, headache, hypoglycemia, abdominal pain, acute pancreatitis, worsening renal function, URTI, fungal skin infection, peripheral edema, nasopharyngitis, constipation, arthralgia, myalgia, pain in extremity and back.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Nifedipine, ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine, thiazide and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid drugs, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, CCBs, isoniazid.
flattened_sections.packaging: Film-coated tablet 50 mg/500 mg (P30.31), 50 mg/850 mg (P32.14), 50 mg/1,000 mg (P32.55).

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa and other susceptible bacteria; used in immunocompromised or neutropenic patients; for biliary tract (cholangitis), lower (cystic fibrosis) and upper (otitis media) respiratory tract, skin (burns, ecthyma gangrenosum, ulceration), urinary tract, bone and joint, gynecological including postpartum endometritis and pelvic inflammatory disease, and intra-abdominal infections; surgical infection prophylaxis, septicemia.
flattened_sections.dose: Administered by slow IV injection over 3-5 mins and by IV infusion over 20-40 mins. Adults - Serious or complicated infections: 200-300 mg/kg daily in divided doses. Usual dose: 4 g every 6-8 hrs. Life-threatening infections caused by Klebsiella spp. or Pseudomonas: Not < 16 g daily. Max 24 g/day. Mild or uncomplicated infections: 100-150 mg/kg daily. Usual dose: 2 g every 6-8 hrs, or 4 g every 12 hrs IV. Prophylaxis during surgery: 2 g before procedure or when the umbilical cord is clamped in cesarean section, followed by at least 2 doses of 2 g at intervals of 4-6 hrs within 24 hrs of procedure. Renal impairment - CrCl 20-80 mL/min: 12 g/1.5 g per day in divided doses or 4 g/500 mg every 8 hrs; <20 mL/min: 8 g/1 g per day in divided doses or 4 g/500 mg every 12 hrs. Hemodialysis - All indications: Max 2.25 g every 12 hrs (every 8 hrs for nosocomial pneumonia), and additional 0.75 g after each dialysis period. Childn 1 month-12 yrs: 100-300 mg/kg daily in 3 or 4 divided doses; Neonates >7 days or weighing >2 kg: 300 mg/kg daily in 3-4 divided doses; <7 days or weighing <2 kg: 150 mg/kg daily in 3 divided doses.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. History of hypersensitivity to penicillins, cephalosporins, beta-lactamase inhibitors.
flattened_sections.precautions: Discontinue if serious hypersensitivity reactions and bleeding manifestations occur. Prolonged use may lead to superinfection, leukopenia, and neutropenia. Assess organ system functions (e.g. renal, hepatic, hematopoietic) periodically. Fever and rash in cystic fibrosis patients. Patients with low potassium reserves. Evaluate patients with gonorrhea for syphilis before initiating treatment. Pregnancy and lactation.
flattened_sections.side_effects: Nausea, indigestion, vomiting and diarrhea, constipation, rash, itchy or red skin, urticaria, difficulty sleeping, headache, dizziness and superinfection.
flattened_sections.drug_interactions: Probenecid, aminoglycosides, vecuronium, anticoagulants, methotrexate. Incompatibilities: Other antibiotics, Lactated Ringer’s soln, solns containing only sodium bicarbonate or alkaline solns, blood products, or albumin hydrolysates.

flattened_sections.indications: Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). Prevention of type 2 DM in patients with pre-diabetes and at least 1 additional risk factor in whom lifestyle modifications alone have not reached adequate glycemic control. 1<sup>st</sup> line therapy in overweight type 2 DM adult patients. Ovulation stimulation to support conception in women with PCOS.
flattened_sections.dose: Monotherapy and combination with other oral antidiabetic agents: Initially 500 or 750 mg once daily with the evening meal. Maintenance: 1 g for patients treated with 1 g or 2 g metformin. Dose adjustment based on blood glucose measurements is recommended after 10-15 days. Recommended dose of 750 mg tab: 2 tabs once daily, may be increased to a max dose of 3 tabs daily. Max recommended dose of 4 tabs of 500 mg or 2 tabs of 1 g daily. Combination w/ insulin: Initially 500 mg or 750 mg once daily. Ovulation stimulation to support conception in women with PCOS: 1,500-2000 mg once daily for at least 6 months. Max 2,000 mg once daily with the evening meal. Monotherapy for prediabetes: 1,000-1,500 mg once daily. Moderate renal impairment stage 3 (CrCl 30-59 mL/min or eGFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73 m2): Initially 500 mg or 850 mg daily. Max 1,000 mg. Always take with food. Slow increase of dose may improve GI tolerability.
flattened_sections.contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Any type of metabolic acidosis (e.g., lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis), diabetic pre-coma, severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min or eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), dehydration, severe infection or shock, diseases that may cause tissue hypoxia (unstable CHF, respiratory failure, recent MI or shock), hepatic insufficiency, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Intravascular administration of iodinated contrast materials. Discontinue 48 hrs prior to elective major surgical interventions and may not be reinstituted until 48 hrs afterwards. Coadministration with iodinated contrast media.
flattened_sections.precautions: Lactic acidosis. Not recommended in patients with  mitochondrial diseases e.g., Mitochondrial Encephalopathy with Lactic Acidosis, and Stroke‑like episodes (MELAS) syndrome and Maternal inherited diabetes and deafness (MIDD).
